category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Region Restrictions and Exceptions
prompt: Members of multiple OUs must be prevented from creating regional resources in unapproved Regions, while retaining local IAM administrator permissions in each account. Some global operations, such as IAM operations, must remain available. Which centralized control should be used?

choices.text: Use AWS Config to detect unapproved Regions
choices.explanation: This detects activity after the fact and does not reject creation requests.

choices.text: Use an SCP with a Deny based on conditions such as aws:RequestedRegion, with exceptions for required global service actions
choices.explanation: It can be applied at the organizational unit level as a boundary on IAM permissions.

choices.text: Manually create IAM groups for users in every account
choices.explanation: This does not centrally control other principals that may be created in member accounts.

choices.text: Enforce an approved Region list with a tag policy
choices.explanation: Tag rules do not control API authorization for Regions.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: It can be applied at the organizational unit level as a boundary on IAM permissions.
learning.concept: SCPs do not grant permissions. Also review global service APIs and cross-Region side effects.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Maintaining Writes During Migration
prompt: A 30 TB on-premises database is being migrated to AWS. Compatibility has been validated, and change logging is enabled on the source. Writes must continue during the initial copy, with only a brief pause at cutover until replica lag converges. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Restore only the initial snapshot
choices.explanation: Changes made after the snapshot is taken are not applied automatically.

choices.text: Combine AWS DMS full load with CDC
choices.explanation: Source changes can continue to be replicated after the initial transfer.

choices.text: Export all data at the end of the business day and transfer it to AWS
choices.explanation: Updates are not tracked during the lengthy initial copy.

choices.text: Switch to the new database, then copy the old database's configuration
choices.explanation: This does not carry over the data or its latest changes.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: Source changes can continue to be replicated after the initial transfer.
learning.concept: Check CDC latency and the target database's logging configuration, and validate data consistency for the changes before cutover.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Hybrid DNS
prompt: Several on-premises sites connect to a shared services VPC through Direct Connect. They need to resolve only the VPC's private hosted zone names from on-premises DNS, and resolution must continue if one of the two Availability Zones goes down.

choices.text: Configure conditional forwarding from the corporate DNS servers to a Resolver inbound endpoint
choices.explanation: This lets on-premises queries enter the VPC-side Resolver.

choices.text: Create only a Resolver outbound endpoint
choices.explanation: This is used for queries going from the VPC to external DNS servers.

choices.text: Put the private records in the on-premises public DNS
choices.explanation: The names would be public, and this would not resolve them through the private hosted zone.

choices.text: Have the sites query the VPC's AmazonProvidedDNS address directly
choices.explanation: This does not replace an inbound endpoint for receiving private DNS queries from outside the VPC.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This lets on-premises queries enter the VPC-side Resolver.
learning.concept: Determine inbound and outbound direction from the VPC-side Resolver's perspective. DNS forwarding ports and routing are also required.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Low RTO and Standby Cost
prompt: A small execution environment runs continuously in the DR Region, and test requests are sent to it periodically. Normal customer traffic is handled only by the primary environment; during an outage, the DR environment is scaled up to the required capacity. Which DR strategy does this describe?

choices.text: Pilot light
choices.explanation: This strategy keeps core components in place, but differs from maintaining a running, scaled-down version of the application.

choices.text: Multi-Region active-active
choices.explanation: This is not a configuration that keeps the DR environment scaled down to reduce overall costs.

choices.text: Warm standby
choices.explanation: A scaled-down version of the application and its data is maintained in the DR environment and scaled up when needed.

choices.text: Backup and restore only
choices.explanation: The DR environment is restored and prepared to run only after an outage.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: A scaled-down version of the application and its data is maintained in the DR environment and scaled up when needed.
learning.concept: RTO is the target recovery time; RPO is the acceptable time window for data loss. Replication and failover must be measured even when using the same strategy.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Account Separation
prompt: Users across 60 accounts sign in through the corporate identity provider. Account access and job permissions must be centrally configured according to each user's assigned group, without distributing long-term keys for each account.

choices.text: Manage account assignments and permission sets with IAM Identity Center
choices.explanation: Temporary access to multiple accounts can be assigned to users or groups.

choices.text: Manually create an IAM user with the same name in every account
choices.explanation: Long-term credentials still have to be managed separately for each account.

choices.text: Share the production root user's keys among all staff
choices.explanation: This provides neither individual auditing nor per-user permission management, and uses long-term credentials.

choices.text: Create a separate SAML provider and role in each account, and manage group assignments separately
choices.explanation: This allows temporary access, but account assignments are not centralized.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: Temporary access to multiple accounts can be assigned to users or groups.
learning.concept: Design identity federation and least privilege for each account as separate concerns.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Connecting Services with Overlapping Addresses
prompt: A business acquisition has resulted in overlapping CIDR blocks. The environments must be integrated quickly. The provider side can be limited to a TCP service behind an NLB, neither side can renumber its addresses, and broad routing between the VPCs must not be exposed.

choices.text: Propagate all VPC routes to the TGW as-is in both directions
choices.explanation: Overlapping address ranges cannot be distinguished when used simultaneously.

choices.text: Peer the VPCs while their CIDRs overlap
choices.explanation: VPCs with overlapping CIDRs cannot be peered.

choices.text: Distribute static routes for the same address range to both VPCs
choices.explanation: This does not resolve which VPC to select for the same CIDR or limit access to the service.

choices.text: Use an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service
choices.explanation: This creates a service entry point for the consumer without routing the entire provider VPC.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This creates a service entry point for the consumer without routing the entire provider VPC.
learning.concept: Publishing an individual service and connecting entire networks are different requirements. PrivateLink is an option for private connectivity to a single service.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Generative AI Data Processing Within a Region
prompt: Policy requires inference on input data to be confined to a single Region. Two accounts must invoke a model available only in that Region without using the internet. The calling identity for each account must be distinguishable during audits.

choices.text: Call a public endpoint using a single shared key
choices.explanation: The callers cannot be distinguished, and there is no private network path.

choices.text: Share a geography-based cross-Region inference profile
choices.explanation: Processing may be routed outside the specified Region, even within the same geographic area.

choices.text: Call the regional model through each VPC's NAT gateway
choices.explanation: The inference destination can be limited, but this does not meet the private network path requirement.

choices.text: Call the regional model through a Bedrock Runtime interface endpoint in each VPC, using a separate role for each account
choices.explanation: This limits the network path and processing location while separating the identities.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This limits the network path and processing location while separating the identities.
learning.concept: Check the Region of the API endpoint separately from the destinations to which an inference profile can route processing.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Automated Deployment After Migration
prompt: An application migrated from on premises requires the same monitoring configuration in 40 accounts. The configuration must also be managed for accounts created in the target OU in the future, without manually placing a deployment role in each account.

choices.text: Use trusted access with Organizations and automatic deployment of service-managed StackSets to the OU
choices.explanation: This automatically accounts for newly added accounts.

choices.text: Use an AWS Config aggregator to track new accounts
choices.explanation: It provides visibility but does not deploy the monitoring configuration.

choices.text: Use self-managed StackSets and create execution roles in each account
choices.explanation: Roles must also be prepared in accounts created later.

choices.text: Create a single CloudFormation stack in the monitoring account
choices.explanation: A stack does not automatically deploy resources to other accounts.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This automatically accounts for newly added accounts.
learning.concept: Distinguish mechanisms that create configuration across multiple accounts from those that aggregate configuration already created.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Multi-Account API Connectivity
prompt: HTTP services run in three VPCs in an organization. The consumer and provider accounts are different, and some CIDR blocks overlap. Access must be controlled with IAM authentication for each consumer, and you want to avoid creating a separate NLB for each consumer. Which architecture is appropriate?

choices.text: Only consolidate VPC routing through a Transit Gateway
choices.explanation: This does not provide service-level IAM authentication or resolve overlapping CIDRs.

choices.text: Register the services in a shared services network with VPC Lattice, associate the consumer VPCs, and configure an AWS_IAM authentication policy
choices.explanation: This provides service-level reachability and IAM authentication without relying on IP routing between VPCs.

choices.text: Expose all applications through internet-facing ALBs and restrict access only by source IP
choices.explanation: IP restrictions do not authenticate individual IAM principals.

choices.text: Connect everything with VPC peering and add each peer's CIDR to the routes in every VPC
choices.explanation: VPC peering cannot resolve overlapping address ranges, and IAM-based service authentication would still need to be configured separately.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This provides service-level reachability and IAM authentication without relying on IP routing between VPCs.
learning.concept: A shared services network brings together service discovery and authorization. PrivateLink is also applicable when publishing only a single TCP service.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Long-Running Approval Workflow
prompt: Vendor onboarding proceeds through identity verification, approver sign-off, and payee registration, in that order. Verification may take up to five days, and the workflow must retain the state of each step and branch on failures. Which design avoids running Lambda while the workflow is waiting?

choices.text: Increase the Lambda timeout and poll until approval is granted
choices.explanation: This cannot support a wait that exceeds Lambda’s maximum execution time.

choices.text: Configure callback waits for each approver in Step Functions Express
choices.explanation: Express workflows do not support this callback integration pattern, and their maximum execution time also does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Set the SQS DelaySeconds value to five days
choices.explanation: SQS delay settings do not support a five-day delay, and they do not represent approval state transitions.

choices.text: Use Step Functions Standard with task tokens to wait for approval, and branch on failures with Retry and Catch
choices.explanation: It manages long waits and callbacks and provides execution history.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: It manages long waits and callbacks and provides execution history.
learning.concept: Separate waiting from execution, and protect retries that cause side effects with idempotency keys in external systems.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Reprocessing Business Events and Low-Latency Aggregation
prompt: Fraud detection and aggregation must process the same order events within seconds of their arrival. Even if the detection logic is corrected the following week, it must be possible to replay the most recent seven days from an independent position while aggregation continues reading as usual.

choices.text: Subscribe both consumers directly to an SNS standard topic, and do not retain the events after delivery
choices.explanation: This separates delivery, but does not retain a source for reprocessing a week of events.

choices.text: Set the Kinesis Data Streams retention period to more than seven days and manage each processor as an independent consumer
choices.explanation: Each consumer maintains its own read position and can reread events independently within the retention period.

choices.text: Share one standard SQS queue between the two processors and delete each message after successful processing
choices.explanation: The consumers compete for messages, and deleted events cannot be reread later.

choices.text: Batch orders to S3 nightly and run fraud detection as a daily batch job
choices.explanation: Reprocessing is possible, but low-latency detection is not.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: Each consumer maintains its own read position and can reread events independently within the retention period.
learning.concept: Design for independent subscriptions and durable retention, and make processing idempotent when the same events are replayed.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Delegated Administration and Audit Log Retention
prompt: Management events from 80 accounts must be collected in a logging account that application developers do not administer. The collection must automatically include new accounts, and saved log versions must not be deletable during a defined retention period. Which two options should be combined?

choices.text: View only the event history separately in each member account
choices.explanation: This does not provide centralized storage or long-term retention.

choices.text: Only transition the S3 storage class to Glacier
choices.explanation: This changes storage costs but does not prevent deletion.

choices.text: Enable versioning on the central bucket and apply Object Lock compliance-mode retention
choices.explanation: This prevents deletion of protected versions and shortening their retention period while the retention period is in effect.

choices.text: Configure CloudTrail log file validation without retention
choices.explanation: This can help detect tampering, but does not prevent deletion.

choices.text: Create an organization trail in CloudTrail across multiple Regions and deliver logs to the central logging bucket
choices.explanation: This automatically includes new member accounts and centralizes management events.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This automatically includes new member accounts and centralizes management events. It also prevents deletion of protected versions and shortening their retention period while the retention period is in effect.
learning.concept: Design trail aggregation and protection against changes at the storage destination separately.

versionLabel: Original Practice Exam — Expanded Edition, November 2026

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Cross-Account Delegation for SaaS Auditing
prompt: A multitenant audit SaaS reads configuration settings in customer environments. Even if Customer A learns Customer B’s role ARN, the SaaS must not be able to act on Customer B’s permissions on Customer A’s behalf.

choices.text: Require the SaaS principal and a unique ExternalId issued by the SaaS for each customer in the trust policy
choices.explanation: The SaaS supplies the ID associated with the authenticated tenant, so knowing another customer’s ARN alone does not satisfy the condition.

choices.text: Use the same ExternalId for every customer
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish an assume-role request for another tenant.

choices.text: Trust the SaaS AWS account and treat customer role ARNs as secret
choices.explanation: This does not prevent confusion if an ARN becomes known.

choices.text: Set the session duration to the shortest possible value
choices.explanation: This does not prevent the wrong permissions from being issued in the first place.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: The SaaS supplies the ID associated with the authenticated tenant, so knowing another customer’s ARN alone does not satisfy the condition.
learning.concept: For third-party delegation, design STS permissions and trust conditions that prevent customer mix-ups as separate controls.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Reading encrypted logs in another account
prompt: Central S3 audit logs use a customer managed KMS key owned by the logging account. The analytics role already has permission to call GetObject. The analyst should be allowed to decrypt the logs only.

choices.text: Allow the external role to decrypt in the key policy, and allow the analytics account role to call kms:Decrypt on the key
choices.explanation: Using a key across accounts requires permission on both the key side and the caller side.

choices.text: Only allow kms:Decrypt for the analytics role
choices.explanation: The key owner's side has not authorized external use.

choices.text: Add kms:Decrypt to the S3 bucket policy
choices.explanation: A bucket policy does not authorize use of a KMS key.

choices.text: Enable automatic key rotation without changing KMS permissions
choices.explanation: Rotating key material does not grant decrypt permission.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: Using a key across accounts requires permission on both the key side and the caller side.
learning.concept: For SSE-KMS reads, evaluate S3 and KMS permissions separately, and do not grant unnecessary encryption or management actions.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Preventing S3 access through unintended paths
prompt: Managed EC2 instances access shared S3 data. Keep the application permissions in place while limiting use of the bucket to a specified gateway endpoint. Deny requests even when they are authenticated through another path. There is no need to exclude requests made by AWS services on behalf of the caller.

choices.text: Use an explicit Deny in the bucket policy with an aws:SourceVpce condition that denies access unless the endpoint ID matches the specified endpoint
choices.explanation: A bucket-level Deny also applies to authenticated requests coming through another path.

choices.text: Allow only that bucket in the specified endpoint's policy
choices.explanation: This can restrict requests traversing the endpoint, but it does not control requests to the bucket through another path.

choices.text: Require TLS when accessing the bucket
choices.explanation: This encrypts the connection but does not identify the endpoint.

choices.text: Enable S3 access logging
choices.explanation: This supports after-the-fact investigation but does not deny requests.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: A bucket-level Deny also applies to authenticated requests coming through another path.
learning.concept: A Deny based on access path may also affect tools such as the console. Check the intended path and operational exceptions first.

category: コスト最適化
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Maintaining discounts as compute platforms change
prompt: Three departments are gradually migrating from EC2 to Fargate and Lambda. The minimum hourly spend over the year is predictable. Which approach commits only to that minimum and remains applicable after the migration?

choices.text: Apply Compute Savings Plans to the stable baseline
choices.explanation: The hourly usage commitment can apply across eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage.

choices.text: Purchase EC2 On-Demand Capacity Reservations
choices.explanation: These reserve capacity; they are not a discount approach that spans the migration targets.

choices.text: Concentrate on EC2 Instance Savings Plans
choices.explanation: These cover a specific EC2 family and Region and do not carry over to Fargate or Lambda.

choices.text: Purchase Compute Savings Plans up to the variable peak
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to avoid overcommitting.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: The hourly usage commitment can apply across eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage.
learning.concept: Consider discount flexibility separately from the risk of unused commitment; handle the baseline and variable usage separately.

category: コスト最適化
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Long-term retention that meets the retrieval deadline
prompt: Invoice PDFs are accessed frequently until 90 days after creation. After that, they are needed only for a few audits per year and must be retained for seven years. Each audit request must be fulfilled within 24 hours. Each PDF is at least 10 MiB, and four hours are available for work after restoration. Which storage class has the lowest cost?

choices.text: Keep the files in S3 Standard for the entire period
choices.explanation: It allows immediate reads, but storage costs are high for long-term retention with infrequent access.

choices.text: Transition to Deep Archive after 90 days and use bulk retrieval
choices.explanation: Bulk retrieval typically takes up to 48 hours, which does not meet the deadline.

choices.text: Transition to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days and use expedited retrieval for every audit
choices.explanation: The wait is shorter, but storage and retrieval cost more for responsiveness that the conditions do not require.

choices.text: Transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days and use standard retrieval for audits
choices.explanation: Standard retrieval typically takes within 12 hours and lowers the unit cost of long-term storage.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: Standard retrieval typically takes within 12 hours and lowers the unit cost of long-term storage.
learning.concept: When choosing an archive class, compare not only storage cost but also retrieval tier, restoration deadline, and minimum storage duration.

category: コスト最適化
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Lowering private data transfer processing costs
prompt: Many VPCs send large volumes of data to S3 in the same Region through a centralized NAT gateway and Transit Gateway. All traffic originates from EC2 instances inside the VPCs. The traffic must remain off the internet, and you want to avoid processing charges from both devices for transfers to S3.

choices.text: Add a centralized NAT gateway for each source VPC
choices.explanation: This avoids Transit Gateway processing charges, but NAT data processing charges remain.

choices.text: Create an S3 interface endpoint only in the central VPC
choices.explanation: Transit Gateway processing charges for traffic to the central VPC and endpoint processing charges remain.

choices.text: Create an S3 gateway endpoint in each source VPC and associate it with the route tables for the relevant subnets
choices.explanation: Traffic to S3 bypasses the centralized NAT gateway and Transit Gateway, and the gateway endpoint itself has no processing charge.

choices.text: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration
choices.explanation: It accelerates requests and has a different pricing model; it does not eliminate the processing charges on the specified path.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: Traffic to S3 bypasses the centralized NAT gateway and Transit Gateway, and the gateway endpoint itself has no processing charge.
learning.concept: Using a private network and avoiding charges are separate concerns. Check the charges at every hop from source to destination.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Resuming writes during a Region outage
prompt: A business application uses Amazon Aurora and must resume writes within a few minutes from a database that is already available in a remote Region, even during a Regional outage. The application can execute the formal failover procedure and update its connection target, and the business can tolerate a small amount of data loss due to asynchronous replication.

choices.text: Set up a secondary Region with Aurora Global Database and rehearse a managed failover during an outage
choices.explanation: This provides cross-Region replication and the ability to promote the secondary for recovery writes.

choices.text: Use Route 53 to redirect traffic to the application in another Region
choices.explanation: This can redirect traffic, but it does not promote an available database.

choices.text: Copy Aurora snapshots to another Region every hour
choices.explanation: Restoring a snapshot creates a new database, making it difficult to meet a recovery target of a few minutes; the replication interval is also long.

choices.text: Add only an Aurora Replica in another Availability Zone in the same Region
choices.explanation: This can help with an Availability Zone outage, but it does not provide a database in a remote Region.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This provides cross-Region replication and the ability to promote the secondary for recovery writes.
learning.concept: Separate RPO from RTO: measure replication lag and the promotion of the recovery environment and connection cutover independently.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Canary deployment with automatic rollback
prompt: You want to route only 10% of production traffic to a new Lambda version initially, then shift all traffic to it only if it passes a five-minute monitoring period. If an error alarm triggers, the deployment must automatically roll back to the previous version.

choices.text: Shift all traffic to the new version, then manually roll back to the previous version
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to start with only 10% of traffic.

choices.text: Limit the new version's reserved concurrency to 10%
choices.explanation: Reserved concurrency does not split requests between the old and new versions at a specified ratio.

choices.text: Use a Lambda canary deployment with CodeDeploy and CloudWatch alarms, and enable automatic rollback
choices.explanation: A single deployment can manage both the gradual traffic shift and monitoring-based rollback.

choices.text: Manually adjust a weighted alias and send an email only if errors occur
choices.explanation: This supports a partial traffic shift but does not provide automatic rollback.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: A single deployment can manage both the gradual traffic shift and monitoring-based rollback.
learning.concept: For a gradual rollout, verify the monitoring evaluation period and traffic sample size, then rehearse stopping and rollback.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Automatically remediating configuration drift across an organization
prompt: Security controls must continuously detect resources whose required settings were removed after a team created them, then restore those settings using an approved procedure. You also need to retain evidence of each resource's noncompliance determination.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to capture API events only when resources are created
choices.explanation: This does not cover existing resources or drift after creation, and compliance evaluation would also be needed separately.

choices.text: Create only an AWS Config aggregator
choices.explanation: An aggregator can provide a consolidated view, but it does not by itself run rules for managed resources or perform automatic remediation.

choices.text: Use an SCP only to deny the API calls expected to cause changes
choices.explanation: This can prevent changes in advance, but it does not remediate existing drift that has already been detected.

choices.text: Detect drift with an AWS Config rule and configure a remediation action using Systems Manager Automation
choices.explanation: This records configuration evaluations based on resource state and can run a predefined procedure when a resource is noncompliant.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This records configuration evaluations based on resource state and can run a predefined procedure when a resource is noncompliant.
learning.concept: Combine preventive controls with detection and remediation, and limit permissions and rule scope to reduce the risk of unintended changes.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Centralizing distributed monitoring
prompt: Services run across 40 accounts in the same Region. SREs want to investigate metrics, logs, and traces together in CloudWatch from a central monitoring account, without managing replicated copies of each account’s monitoring data.

choices.text: Collect API events from all accounts using a CloudTrail organization trail
choices.explanation: This audits management events; it does not bring application metrics or traces together.

choices.text: Deploy the same CloudWatch dashboards in every account
choices.explanation: This standardizes views, but does not support the requirement to investigate data centrally from one account.

choices.text: Deliver all VPC Flow Logs to S3
choices.explanation: Network records can be aggregated, but this does not meet all the application monitoring requirements.

choices.text: Create a sink in the monitoring account with CloudWatch cross-account observability, and configure links from the source accounts
choices.explanation: This allows supported monitoring data to be viewed centrally and analyzed across accounts.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This allows supported monitoring data to be viewed centrally and analyzed across accounts.
learning.concept: Separate the monitoring account from the accounts that generate the data, and check the boundaries for Region, data type, and sharing permissions.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Waiting for an external process to complete
prompt: An order workflow requests inventory reservation from an external system. The result arrives by webhook several hours later. Which design correlates the request with its completion and starts the next step without keeping a worker waiting?

choices.text: Keep a Lambda function open while waiting for the notification
choices.explanation: The wait can exceed the execution time limit and unnecessarily consume execution time.

choices.text: Keep an Express execution running for several hours
choices.explanation: This exceeds the maximum execution time.

choices.text: Use a callback task in Step Functions Standard, manage the task token, accept an authenticated notification, and report completion
choices.explanation: This correlates the external event with the task that issued the request and allows processing to continue.

choices.text: Use an SNS notification with no correlation ID to start the next step
choices.explanation: This cannot identify which order should proceed.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This correlates the external event with the task that issued the request and allows processing to continue.
learning.concept: Manage task tokens in a secure backend, and verify the external notification’s authentication and correlation ID.

title: Validating dependencies across migration waves
prompt: Several systems acquired from another company cannot all be shut down at a fixed time. Dependencies between applications are undocumented, and rollback is required. What is the best preparation for migrating to AWS while keeping the business running?

choices.text: Switch everything over at once during a period of low user activity
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement that everything cannot be shut down at once and creates a large potential impact.

choices.text: Observe communication dependencies only after migration
choices.explanation: This does not verify required connectivity before cutover.

choices.text: Use observations of communications and assets to identify dependencies, then define migration waves and rollback conditions for each unit that will cut over together
choices.explanation: This identifies dependencies that a partial migration could disrupt and allows testing and cutover to be staged.

choices.text: Divide the systems into groups of equal size based only on the number of running instances
choices.explanation: Components with strong dependencies could end up in separate groups.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This identifies dependencies that a partial migration could disrupt and allows testing and cutover to be staged.
learning.concept: Define migration waves based on business dependencies and rollback feasibility, rather than size.

title: Separating departmental costs from shared costs

Finance wants to retain each product’s direct costs while allocating shared network costs among products according to their proportions. It is sufficient for the allocation results to be available on the Cost Categories details page; there is no need to change amounts on invoices or in Cost Explorer.

choices.text: Physically duplicate the shared VPC resources for each department
choices.explanation: This changes the architecture to enable allocation and could also increase shared infrastructure costs.

choices.text: Combine all costs into a fixed budget in the management account
choices.explanation: This supports budget monitoring but does not express an allocation among products.

choices.text: Classify costs in AWS Cost Categories using accounts or activated cost allocation tags, and apply a split charge rule to shared costs
choices.explanation: This defines direct cost attribution and shared cost allocation for billing analysis.

choices.text: Apply a single product tag only to the shared network
choices.explanation: This attributes the entire cost to one product rather than allocating it according to proportions.

title: Auditing Manual Changes to a Production Stack
prompt: The operations team manually changed some settings managed by CloudFormation during an emergency. For supported explicitly declared properties, they want to identify the differences between the actual values and the managed definition before deciding how to remediate them.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to find only who made the changes
choices.explanation: This can trace the cause of the changes, but it does not provide a side-by-side inventory of the current state and expected values.

choices.text: Re-create the stack without reviewing the template
choices.explanation: This affects the configuration and state before the differences have been analyzed.

choices.text: Create a change set from the same template and do nothing else
choices.explanation: A standard change set checks for changes to the definition; it is not a complete inventory of drift in all actual settings.

choices.text: Run drift detection for the stack and review the resources that changed and their differences
choices.explanation: This lets you check differences between the expected values declared in the template for managed resources and their actual settings.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド

learning.reason: This lets you check differences between the expected values declared in the template for managed resources and their actual settings.
learning.concept: Treat drift detection, auditing the cause of changes, and remediation as separate phases.

category: コスト最適化
title: Separating Performance Settings from Capacity
prompt: Image-processing workers store temporary data on the EBS volume attached to each EC2 instance. Measurements show that each 2 TiB volume needs 5,000 IOPS and 350 MiB/s. The team wants to retain SSD storage and adjust IOPS and throughput independently in the future. Which configuration meets these needs using general purpose SSD pricing without provisioning more capacity than necessary?

choices.text: Keep gp2 and increase only the volume capacity to get the required throughput
choices.explanation: With gp2, capacity and performance are related, and its throughput limit is below 350 MiB/s.

choices.text: Switch to gp3 and specify 5,000 IOPS and 350 MiB/s while keeping the volume at 2 TiB
choices.explanation: You can provision IOPS and throughput independently without increasing capacity.

choices.text: Switch to io2 Block Express and specify 2 TiB and 5,000 IOPS
choices.explanation: Its performance may fit, but it uses a Provisioned IOPS SSD pricing model and does not meet the requirement to choose general purpose SSD pricing.

choices.text: Switch to st1 and distribute the data across multiple volumes
choices.explanation: This is a throughput-optimized HDD and does not meet the requirement to retain SSD storage.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Keep capacity unchanged and adjust the required IOPS and throughput independently.
learning.concept: Additional performance charges apply when gp3 settings exceed its included baseline. Measure both EBS and EC2 limits in advance.

category: コスト最適化
title: Large Inference Inputs and Idle Costs
prompt: Images totaling 600 MB are analyzed only a few times a day. Each inference takes about 12 minutes. The caller only needs to retrieve the result from S3, and the team wants the number of inference instances to be zero during periods with no requests. Which configuration preserves the existing SageMaker AI model and endpoint for accepting requests?

choices.text: Use SageMaker real-time inference and keep one instance running at all times
choices.explanation: Inference capacity would not fall to zero while idle, and this mode does not meet the requirements for processing a large input in this way.

choices.text: Use SageMaker Serverless Inference and run each request synchronously
choices.explanation: This can help reduce idle costs, but it does not meet the payload and processing-time requirements.

choices.text: Use SageMaker Batch Transform to process multiple inputs together on a schedule
choices.explanation: This suits large-scale offline inference, but does not preserve the existing endpoint contract for accepting individual requests.

choices.text: Use SageMaker Asynchronous Inference with S3 input and output, and scale to zero based on the queue
choices.explanation: This combines long-running, large-payload asynchronous processing with inference capacity that is available only when needed.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The solution must handle large inputs and long processing times, and scale inference capacity to zero when the queue is empty.
learning.concept: Compare SageMaker inference modes by payload limits, response time, invocation pattern, and idle capacity.

category: コスト最適化
title: Month-End Queueing and Fixed Costs
prompt: On a provisioned Redshift cluster, the number of concurrent eligible BI queries surges for a few hours at month-end. The current number of nodes is sufficient under normal conditions. Which approach adds concurrent processing capacity only during peak periods while preserving the connection target and data?

choices.text: Enable Concurrency Scaling for the relevant WLM queue, and configure usage limits and notifications
choices.explanation: Eligible queries can be routed to additional capacity to handle sudden concurrency.

choices.text: Permanently increase the RA3 node count to the level needed at month-end
choices.explanation: The added capacity would also incur costs under normal conditions, contrary to the requirement to scale only for peak periods.

choices.text: Only increase the concurrency setting in WLM
choices.explanation: This shares existing capacity among more queries; it does not add cluster capacity.

choices.text: Delete older tables and keep the cluster the same size
choices.explanation: This does not address the cause of concurrency queuing and does not preserve the existing data.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Keep the current connection and normal-period capacity while handling peak load in the target queue with additional capacity.
learning.concept: WLM concurrency settings and Concurrency Scaling serve different functions. Check eligible queries, saved credits, and limits on additional charges.

category: コスト最適化
title: Unpredictable Access Patterns
prompt: A public data S3 bucket contains mostly objects of 1 MB or larger. Even old objects can receive sudden access, and when they will be accessed cannot be predicted. You must maintain millisecond-level access to all data without restoring it first, while automatically moving only infrequently accessed data to a lower-cost tier. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Move all data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days.
choices.explanation: This moves data based only on age and normally requires a restore operation before retrieval.

choices.text: Move data to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and keep it there.
choices.explanation: The data remains directly accessible, but age-based movement does not reflect actual usage or automatically respond if access increases again.

choices.text: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering without enabling any optional asynchronous archive tiers.
choices.explanation: It can automatically move objects among directly accessible tiers based on actual access patterns.

choices.text: Keep the data in S3 Standard and add an application-side cache.
choices.explanation: This helps with frequently accessed data, but does not automatically lower storage costs for infrequently accessed objects.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Use each object's actual access history instead of a fixed age-based transition, and do not select an option that requires restoration.
learning.concept: Distinguish Intelligent-Tiering's automatic access tiers from asynchronous archive tiers that must be explicitly enabled.

category: コスト最適化
title: Shared Files and Performance on Reuse
prompt: Workers in multiple Availability Zones in a rendering environment access the same Amazon EFS paths through POSIX. Many assets are not accessed for six months, but files reused in production should handle repeated reads with low latency after the first access. Which approach reduces storage costs without changing the application or file paths?

choices.text: Move the data to an S3 infrequent-access storage class and have the application reference object keys.
choices.explanation: This requires changing the existing POSIX-path interface.

choices.text: Configure Amazon EFS lifecycle management to move files to an infrequent-access tier and to move them to Standard on first access.
choices.explanation: This separates tiers within the same file system and can return reused files to the low-latency tier.

choices.text: Attach general-purpose SSD EBS volumes to each EC2 instance and synchronize the files regularly.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the semantics and operations of sharing the same files across multiple Availability Zones.

choices.text: Create a new EFS One Zone file system and keep all files in Standard at all times.
choices.explanation: This violates the multiple Availability Zone requirement and does not tier data based on access frequency.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Use both EFS's transparent tiering and the setting that returns files to Standard after access.
learning.concept: EFS tiering takes place within the same file system. Account for first-access latency and access charges for files in the infrequent-access tier.

category: コスト最適化
title: Detecting Anomalies in Variable Billing
prompt: Daily usage costs vary by day of the week and by campaign for each department. You want to be notified of deviations from normal patterns before a fixed monthly budget is exceeded. The development team wants to use cost data from AWS and inspect the services or accounts that contributed to detected anomalies. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Set a fixed amount in monthly AWS Budgets and notify only when actual costs reach 80%.
choices.explanation: This tracks progress toward a fixed budget, but does not detect deviations from normal patterns or identify their causes.

choices.text: Plot the daily total from the CUR on a dashboard and have an owner review it manually.
choices.explanation: This provides detailed data, but does not provide automatic anomaly detection or notifications.

choices.text: Apply the same fixed threshold to the usage counts of each service in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: Usage-count metrics do not provide a basis for actual billed costs that reflects discounts and pricing models.

choices.text: Configure monitors and notifications in AWS Cost Anomaly Detection, then inspect the possible causes.
choices.explanation: It detects deviations based on usage history and lets you inspect accounts and other contributors to an anomaly.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The requirement calls for history-based anomaly detection and possible causes in addition to comparison against a fixed limit.
learning.concept: Billing data takes time to ingest. Do not treat anomaly-detection notifications as real-time request blocking.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Initial Setup for New Accounts
prompt: Many development accounts are added by designated OU in AWS Organizations. Whenever a new account enters a target OU, you want to automatically apply a CloudFormation template containing a common IAM role and monitoring definitions to selected Regions. Manually placing an execution role in each account is not an option. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Create execution roles for self-managed StackSets in each account and deploy manually.
choices.explanation: This requires role configuration and a separate launch for each account.

choices.text: Configure trusted access with Organizations, target the OU with service-managed StackSets, and enable automatic deployments.
choices.explanation: This can automate deployment to specified Regions for accounts that enter the target OU.

choices.text: Add only an IAM SCP to the organization root.
choices.explanation: An SCP controls permission boundaries; it does not create CloudFormation resources.

choices.text: Collect inventory for the target OU with AWS Config aggregation and manually deploy the monitoring role.
choices.explanation: This provides visibility, but does not meet the requirement for automatic deployment from a template.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Combine service-managed permissions targeting an OU with automatic deployment when accounts are added.
learning.concept: Operationally decide whether stacks should be retained or deleted when an account is removed from an OU.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Notify Only for Correlated Failures
prompt: A payment API is monitored separately for error rate and latency. You want to retain each alarm's state transitions for investigation, but page the on-call engineer only when both alarms are in the ALARM state. You can modify the two existing alarms, and they are configured in the same account and Region. Which approach meets this requirement without adding new notification decision code?

choices.text: Configure both existing alarms to notify the same SNS topic directly
choices.explanation: A notification would arrive even if either alarm entered ALARM on its own.

choices.text: Add an SNS action to only one alarm and retain the other for history
choices.explanation: The notification would depend on only one alarm's state, so it would not enforce an AND condition.

choices.text: Average both values and replace them with a single standard alarm
choices.explanation: This would combine metrics with different units and lose the independent alarm states and correlation condition.

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch composite alarm that ANDs the ALARM states of the existing alarms, and configure only that alarm to send notifications
choices.explanation: It evaluates the shared condition while retaining the child alarm states, limiting notifications to the on-call engineer.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Combine an AND condition over the states of the two existing alarms into one alarm, and configure the notification target on the composite alarm.
learning.concept: A composite alarm evaluates child alarm states; it does not average metric values or evaluate whether thresholds were crossed simultaneously on the same data point.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Stop Condition for Resilience Testing
prompt: You are running a short resilience test with AWS Fault Injection Service against part of a production service. If the user-facing error rate exceeds an acceptable threshold, you want the experiment to stop without waiting for an operator. Which two actions should you combine to make the stop decision and experiment targets clear with minimal additional operational effort?

choices.text: Shorten the experiment duration and wait until the scheduled end time even if an alarm fires
choices.explanation: This does not stop the experiment immediately when user impact occurs, even if it is still within the specified duration.

choices.text: Configure a CloudWatch alarm for the user-facing error rate
choices.explanation: This makes the threshold breach available for a stop condition to reference.

choices.text: Do not specify experiment targets; use CloudTrail only to review the affected operations afterward
choices.explanation: This neither clarifies the targets nor provides an automated decision based on customer errors.

choices.text: Register that alarm as a stop condition in the experiment template and explicitly specify the targets
choices.explanation: FIS can initiate stopping the experiment based on the alarm state.

choices.text: Ask the recipients of SNS email notifications to use the console during an incident
choices.explanation: This requires an operator to respond and is not an automatic stop.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Create a CloudWatch alarm from observed application data, then connect that alarm to a stop condition in the experiment template.
learning.concept: A stop condition controls stopping the experiment. Whether each component recovered afterward must be checked separately.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Detect Failures in the User Journey First
prompt: A customer portal is delivered through CloudFront. The backend health checks are passing, but an incident caused the flow to fail after users signed in and while they were opening the settings page in a browser. You want to periodically verify the entire sequence with a dedicated test account, including at night when no real users are accessing the service. Which approach is suitable?

choices.text: Monitor only the CloudFront 4xx rate and react to production traffic
choices.explanation: This does not generate activity when there is no traffic or verify page navigation.

choices.text: Run the existing ALB target health check every minute
choices.explanation: A single health endpoint does not verify the settings page after sign-in.

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch Synthetics browser Canary to run the sequence periodically and notify on failure with an alarm
choices.explanation: It can verify the specified user journey even when traffic is low.

choices.text: Use only CloudWatch RUM to record real-user activity
choices.explanation: This helps diagnose real usage, but does not generate periodic interactions when no one is accessing the service.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Periodically interact with the pages in the same order as a user would and verify the result, rather than checking only component responses.
learning.concept: Application health and successful completion of an authenticated business flow in a browser are different things to observe.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Track Failures in Large-Scale Processing
prompt: A Step Functions Distributed Map processes a large number of records in S3. Operators want to review not only the aggregate for the parent execution, but also the Map Run's success and failure counts and the status of child workflows, so they can identify executions to rerun. Which approach provides detailed information while preserving the original workflow configuration?

choices.text: Inspect the Step Functions Map Run details or call DescribeMapRun, then investigate the relevant child executions from the list
choices.explanation: This lets you track counts at the Map Run level and identify which child workflows are involved.

choices.text: Look at the parent execution's total processing time and infer the number of failures from the duration
choices.explanation: Processing time does not identify causes or counts and does not correspond to the status of child executions.

choices.text: Treat the total number of S3 objects as the number of successful child workflows
choices.explanation: The input count does not necessarily equal the success count and does not represent the processing results.

choices.text: Track the parent execution start events in CloudTrail and treat the number of starts as the number of failures
choices.explanation: This confuses API audit records with item-level and child-execution status in a Map Run.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Distributed Map has a Map Run as an observability unit distinct from the parent execution, and it exposes child execution status.
learning.concept: Use CloudWatch metrics for detection, and Map Run details or execution history to determine which processing runs failed.

category: コスト最適化
title: Unexpected Scans in Departmental Analytics
prompt: Each department queries a shared S3 data lake with Athena. If an inexperienced user forgets to specify a partition predicate, a single query can scan a large amount of data. The goal is to automatically stop an individual query that exceeds its department's limit, rather than merely sending a notification at month end. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Set a shared monthly AWS Budgets budget for all departments and send an email when it is exceeded
choices.explanation: This provides an after-the-fact notification and does not stop an individual query that is running.

choices.text: Create only a workgroup-level aggregated data usage alarm
choices.explanation: This tracks aggregate usage but does not cancel an individual query at a specified limit.

choices.text: Use a separate Athena workgroup for each department and set a per-query data usage limit for each workgroup
choices.explanation: This applies department-specific limits and can cancel an individual query that exceeds its limit.

choices.text: Set a short lifecycle policy on the output S3 bucket
choices.explanation: This reduces the cost of storing query results; it does not control the amount of input data a query reads.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A billing alarm monitors usage after the fact. To control a running query, use a per-query limit on its workgroup.
learning.concept: Data usage thresholds can apply to individual queries or aggregate usage across a workgroup, with the latter used for notifications.

category: コスト最適化
title: Ingesting Logs That Are Rarely Queried
prompt: An application sends two types of logs to CloudWatch Logs. Keep the existing configuration for logs that require pattern detection and live investigation. A separate, high-volume set of diagnostic logs is kept almost exclusively for retention and is searched once a month with CloudWatch Logs Insights. Which configuration lowers the ingestion cost of the new diagnostic logs without disrupting existing operations?

choices.text: Send the diagnostic logs to the existing Standard log group and shorten the retention period
choices.explanation: This preserves existing features but does not lower the ingestion cost of the new diagnostic logs.

choices.text: Create a new Infrequent Access log group for diagnostic logs and keep the existing operational logs in Standard
choices.explanation: The diagnostic logs remain searchable with Logs Insights, allowing the required features to be separated while reducing ingestion costs.

choices.text: Change the existing log group to Infrequent Access and mix all logs together
choices.explanation: You cannot change the class of an existing group, and this would not preserve the live investigation features you need.

choices.text: Compress the logs, store them only in S3, and continue searching them with CloudWatch Logs Insights as before
choices.explanation: Storing the logs only in S3 does not preserve the specified CloudWatch Logs Insights search workflow.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Separate logs with different search frequencies and feature requirements into different log groups.
learning.concept: CloudWatch Logs classes offer different features. Choose the class when you create the log group.

category: コスト最適化
title: Nightly ETL That Can Wait to Start
prompt: A data team runs an AWS Glue 4.0 Spark job overnight. The job is supported with G.1X workers, and the inventory data only needs to be ready by the next morning, so some variation in start time is acceptable. Which option lowers the DPU execution rate while using the existing job and avoiding self-managed infrastructure?

choices.text: Change the job to the Glue Flex execution class and measure its runtime and completion deadline
choices.explanation: In a supported configuration, this can lower the rate when the team accepts variation in start and runtime.

choices.text: Replace the G.1X workers with larger Standard workers and run the job continuously for 24 hours
choices.explanation: This is not a setting that lowers the rate, and continuous operation is not required.

choices.text: Keep a Glue Development Endpoint running and manually execute the same processing every night
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to operate the same job and adds idle infrastructure and manual steps.

choices.text: Only reduce the frequency of Data Catalog crawlers
choices.explanation: This can affect crawler costs, but it does not change the DPU rate of the existing Spark job.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: For a supported Spark job that can tolerate a delayed start, selecting the Flex execution class can lower the processing rate.
learning.concept: Flex is suited to noncritical batch processing. For work that requires a precise start time, use another execution class and validate performance.

category: コスト最適化
title: Comparing Storage and Request Costs
prompt: A DynamoDB on-demand table stores historical billing statements. An internal estimate puts its current monthly Standard costs at $900 for storage and $100 for requests. With Standard-IA, storage is estimated at $400 with the same request volume costing $130. Which change lowers costs without moving the data, while preserving the query API and immediate reads?

choices.text: Only switch from on-demand to provisioned capacity to lower the Standard storage rate
choices.explanation: Changing the capacity mode does not lower this storage rate.

choices.text: Shorten the DynamoDB TTL to delete most of the data
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to retain the existing data.

choices.text: Move all historical data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
choices.explanation: This requires moving the data and does not preserve immediate reads through the DynamoDB API.

choices.text: Change the current table to DynamoDB Standard-IA
choices.explanation: Under the given estimates, the storage savings exceed the increased request cost. The table API can be preserved.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A DynamoDB table class affects both storage and request costs. The estimated total is $530, below the current $1,000.
learning.concept: Compare estimates for both storage and read/write volume instead of deciding based only on access frequency. Do not confuse DynamoDB table-class names with S3 storage classes.

category: コスト最適化
title: Cost of Additional Interruption-Tolerant Workers
prompt: ECS Linux workers retrieve work from SQS. At least two tasks must run on standard Fargate capacity, where they are less likely to be interrupted, while additional tasks added during queue peaks can tolerate interruptions to reduce costs. Which capacity strategy expresses this in a single ECS service?

choices.text: Specify only FARGATE_SPOT and set the ECS service desired task count to 2
choices.explanation: The minimum task count specifies the desired total number of running tasks; it does not reserve standard capacity.

choices.text: Set the FARGATE and FARGATE_SPOT weights equally and omit base
choices.explanation: The allocation is determined by a ratio, so this does not ensure at least two tasks on standard capacity.

choices.text: Set base to 2 for FARGATE and assign the weight for additional capacity only to FARGATE_SPOT
choices.explanation: This places the first two tasks on standard Fargate and lets the capacity strategy place any excess on Spot.

choices.text: Set ECS task scheduling to DAEMON and use FARGATE_SPOT
choices.explanation: DAEMON is not supported for ECS services on Fargate, so this cannot express the desired allocation.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Use FARGATE for the base capacity and specify FARGATE_SPOT for capacity allocated beyond that base.
learning.concept: Spot tasks can be interrupted. Design message redelivery and idempotent processing on the receiving side.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Preventing Configuration Changes on Peak Days
prompt: Several AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks update a running service. During freeze periods, such as the year-end shopping season, you want to determine whether updates are allowed using a single calendar, without editing dates scattered across all the runbooks. Outside the freeze period, the normal schedule should remain in effect. Which method is suitable?

choices.text: Register the freeze period in Systems Manager Change Calendar and have each runbook check the calendar state before making a change
choices.explanation: Each runbook can consult a centralized control to determine whether a change is allowed, separately from its schedule.

choices.text: Copy the freeze dates individually into each EventBridge Scheduler rule
choices.explanation: This requires modifying the schedules and does not make the decision from a single change calendar.

choices.text: Enable AWS Config configuration change notifications only on freeze dates
choices.explanation: This can notify you after a change, but it does not prevent an automation from making the change first.

choices.text: Manually delete the IAM role on the start date and recreate it when the period ends
choices.explanation: This requires a destructive operation on an existing role and is not calendar-based control.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Have the runbooks consult the same Change Calendar without changing their invocation schedules.
learning.concept: Check the Change Calendar state before processing, and do not proceed when it is CLOSED.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Bringing an Existing Physical Resource Under IaC Management
prompt: An existing S3 bucket contains a large number of contracts, and other systems refer to its unique bucket name. The bucket was created outside CloudFormation and does not currently belong to another stack. Which combination should you use to bring it under IaC management without replacing the same physical resource? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Create a new bucket with the same name in a normal stack update.
choices.explanation: A CloudFormation create operation does not adopt an existing bucket as a managed resource.

choices.text: Define the existing bucket as a resource in the template and specify a DeletionPolicy.
choices.explanation: The resource definition and a deletion policy are required for the resource to be included in a manual resource import.

choices.text: Move the bucket's data to another bucket and delete the original bucket.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirements to retain the physical bucket and preserve existing references to it.

choices.text: Run drift detection only on the current stack.
choices.explanation: Drift detection evaluates resources that are already managed; it does not bring new resources into a stack.

choices.text: Create an IMPORT change set that identifies the existing resource by bucket name, then execute it after review.
choices.explanation: This brings the physical resource under CloudFormation management without recreating it.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: To explicitly import an existing resource, associate its template definition with the identifier of the existing resource.
learning.concept: After import, drift detection compares declared values with the actual configuration. Management can begin without changing the bucket's data or the references used by its consumers.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Per-Request Investigation and Monitoring Costs
prompt: An API service emits latency using Embedded Metric Format and sets each request ID as a CloudWatch metric dimension. The cost of custom metrics has increased as the number of unique IDs grows. How should you change the setup to retain service- and operation-level alarms while enabling investigations by individual request ID?

choices.text: Keep every request ID as a dimension and shorten only the log retention period
choices.explanation: This can reduce log storage costs, but the problem of creating a separate metric for each request remains.

choices.text: Discard all service and operation information too, and aggregate everything into one metric
choices.explanation: This reduces the number of series but does not meet the requirement for service- and operation-level alarms.

choices.text: Limit metric dimensions to service and operation, and retain the request ID as a log attribute in the same event
choices.explanation: This preserves alarms with a small number of series and still allows searches by ID.

choices.text: Split each request ID into finer-grained values and set them as multiple dimensions
choices.explanation: The number of combinations would still be large, so this would not remove the cause of the problem.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Separate the low-cardinality attributes needed for alarms from the ID used only for individual record investigations.
learning.concept: In EMF, each dimension combination creates a separate metric series. Keep the request ID as a log property so it can be searched with tools such as Logs Insights.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Relationship Between Backlog and Worker Count
prompt: EC2 workers process video messages from an SQS queue in parallel. The processing rate of each worker is nearly constant, and the acceptable queue wait time is known. The current scaling policy uses the absolute queue depth, causing it to scale out or in excessively as the worker count changes. Which approach uses a metric that changes in proportion to the worker count for target tracking?

choices.text: Use ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible without normalization and keep the target at the same absolute value
choices.explanation: The wait time differs for the same queue depth with 2 workers versus 20, so this does not represent a condition that scales with the number of workers.

choices.text: Use the number of visible messages divided by the number of active workers, and set the target based on the acceptable wait time
choices.explanation: The backlog per worker changes in relation to capacity and can be used as a basis for determining the worker count.

choices.text: Use the number of seconds elapsed since the queue was created as the metric
choices.explanation: This does not represent processing demand, and changing the worker count does not improve the metric.

choices.text: Replace the queue with a FIFO queue and use a single group
choices.explanation: This limits parallelism and does not solve the problem of adjusting the active worker count to match the load.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Divide the number of messages waiting to be processed by the total number of workers, then set a target for the per-worker queue backlog.
learning.concept: Estimate the target from the acceptable wait time and the processing time per message, then use load testing to assess sudden increases in arrivals and delays in starting workers.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Gradually Changing a Configuration Without Redeploying
prompt: A service needs to switch an inventory API feature flag without a new service deployment. If a required field is missing from the configuration JSON, the configuration must be rejected before distribution. If an existing CloudWatch alarm goes off during a gradual rollout, the service must automatically revert to the previous configuration. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Use CodeDeploy to perform a blue/green deployment of the application binary
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to distribute only configuration values without redeploying the application.

choices.text: Replace the S3 object directly and enable versioning only
choices.explanation: The previous version is retained, but this does not provide automated gradual rollout, validation, or alarm-triggered rollback.

choices.text: Audit the configuration file after distribution using a Config rule
choices.explanation: Auditing can help operations, but it does not validate the JSON in advance or roll back configuration distribution.

choices.text: Configure AWS AppConfig with JSON schema validation, a gradual deployment strategy, and CloudWatch alarm monitoring
choices.explanation: This prevents invalid configuration from being distributed and can revert to the previous configuration if an issue occurs during rollout.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Configuration validity and health during distribution are evaluated separately.
learning.concept: AWS AppConfig can roll out validated configuration through a deployment strategy and roll back the deployment in response to an alarm. Also consider the interval at which clients retrieve configuration.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Distinguishing Management Operations from Data Access
prompt: An internal audit needs to identify the principals that changed an S3 bucket policy and called GetObject on a single bucket containing sensitive data. The existing CloudTrail trail already records management events. Which approach adds only the required records without collecting large volumes of access data from every bucket?

choices.text: Add CloudTrail data events for GetObject, scoped to objects in the target S3 bucket
choices.explanation: This supplements the existing management event records with only the required object reads.

choices.text: Switch to a multi-Region trail and collect management events only
choices.explanation: Adding Regions does not record the data events needed to capture object reads.

choices.text: Investigate using only CloudTrail Event history and make no additional configuration changes
choices.explanation: Event history does not automatically record or display the specified object reads.

choices.text: Check the total S3 request count metric in CloudWatch
choices.explanation: An aggregate metric cannot identify the principal or object for an individual request.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Operations on a bucket's configuration are management events, while operations on objects are data events.
learning.concept: Data events can be scoped to specific resources or actions. Also verify the trail's destination and the investigation team's access permissions.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Global TCP Failover with Fixed IP Addresses
prompt: Customers worldwide have already registered the destination IP addresses in their firewalls, so migrating to DNS names is not possible. The application accepts raw TCP traffic through Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in Tokyo and Virginia. Users should connect to the nearest healthy Region, and the solution should handle a Regional failure. Which architecture is most appropriate?

choices.text: Register each Region's NLB name in weighted Route 53 records
choices.explanation: This requires migrating to DNS names and does not address the constraint that customers allow only fixed IP addresses.

choices.text: Configure the NLB as an origin for a CloudFront distribution
choices.explanation: CloudFront does not provide the required raw TCP entry point or global TCP failover to NLBs.

choices.text: Register the two Regional NLBs as endpoints in an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator
choices.explanation: It provides fixed Anycast IP addresses and routes TCP traffic across Regions based on endpoint health and user location.

choices.text: Place a NAT Gateway behind each NLB
choices.explanation: A NAT Gateway is for outbound translation and does not provide a fixed global TCP entry point.

source.label: AWS Global Accelerator 開発者ガイド

learning.reason: AWS Global Accelerator provides fixed IP addresses and routes traffic based on health to endpoints in multiple Regions, including NLBs.
learning.concept: Distinguish CloudFront for static content delivery from Global Accelerator for TCP/UDP traffic received at fixed IP addresses.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Transparent Inspection Appliance
prompt: You want to inspect all IP traffic leaving multiple application VPCs for the internet using a fleet of third-party IDS/IPS appliances in a dedicated VPC. The appliances must scale horizontally, and return packets must reach the same appliance. The application-side proxy settings cannot be changed. Which architecture is best?

choices.text: Use Gateway Load Balancer and GWLB endpoints
choices.explanation: It acts as a transparent Layer 3 gateway, distributes traffic to virtual appliances, and provides flow stickiness.

choices.text: Register the IDS/IPS appliances as targets behind an Application Load Balancer
choices.explanation: An ALB is for HTTP(S) and does not transparently inspect arbitrary IP packets.

choices.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs
choices.explanation: Flow Logs record traffic; they do not inspect or block packets inline.

choices.text: Manually configure an appliance for each NAT Gateway
choices.explanation: This does not centrally provide transparent service insertion, flow preservation, and automatic scaling.

source.label: Gateway Load Balancer 開発者ガイド

learning.reason: GWLB combines transparent ingress and egress with load balancing across virtual appliances.
learning.concept: GWLB provides flow stickiness to appliances. If traffic traverses a Transit Gateway, also configure appliance mode on the inspection VPC attachment and routing for both directions.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Preventing IP Overlaps Across an Organization
prompt: You are consolidating more than 100 AWS accounts, including accounts from an acquisition. Each team has chosen VPC CIDRs independently. For future VPCs, you want to prevent overlaps and centrally track address usage across existing networks, on-premises networks, and future Regions. Which approach has the lowest operational overhead?

choices.text: Distribute a spreadsheet so each team can reserve CIDRs
choices.explanation: This provides neither allocation controls nor automatic detection, and is difficult to sustain at organizational scale.

choices.text: Create pools and scopes in Amazon VPC IPAM and share them with accounts
choices.explanation: This centralizes CIDR planning, allocation, and usage tracking across the organization.

choices.text: Use the same CIDR in every VPC and isolate them with Transit Gateway
choices.explanation: Overlapping CIDRs complicate connectivity and routing.

choices.text: Separate only the namespaces with Route 53 Resolver rules
choices.explanation: DNS rules do not manage IP address allocation or overlap.

source.label: Amazon VPC IPAM ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: VPC IPAM helps plan, track, and monitor IP addresses across AWS.
learning.concept: Design a hierarchy of CIDR pools and share them across accounts before the network grows.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Symmetric Paths for Centralized Stateful Inspection
prompt: You need to inspect traffic between many spoke VPCs connected through Transit Gateway using a central stateful firewall VPC. You use multiple appliances, and return packets must always follow the same appliance path. Which setting should you add?

choices.text: Enable IPv6 only in all spoke VPCs
choices.explanation: Changing the IP version does not guarantee symmetric paths.

choices.text: Configure Route 53 latency-based routing
choices.explanation: This selects DNS responses; it does not pin the packet return path.

choices.text: Add an Internet Gateway to each spoke
choices.explanation: This can bypass centralized inspection and expose traffic to the internet.

choices.text: Enable appliance mode on the Transit Gateway attachment to the inspection VPC
choices.explanation: This preserves symmetric flow routing, allowing stateful appliance inspection.

source.label: Transit Gateway 開発者ガイド

learning.reason: Appliance mode preserves the flow symmetry required for stateful inspection.
learning.concept: Appliance distribution through GWLB and attachment path control in TGW are complementary.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Local File Access at a Factory
prompt: Windows workstations at a factory need low-latency access to several terabytes of CAD deliverables through an SMB share. The authoritative data must be stored durably in S3, and the factory must also be able to access files updated in the cloud. Which architecture best minimizes changes to the workstations?

choices.text: Distribute S3 presigned URLs to each workstation
choices.explanation: This does not meet the SMB share requirement or preserve compatibility with existing applications.

choices.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway on premises and expose S3 as an SMB share
