choices.explanation: It provides an SMB/NFS share with a local cache and stores objects in S3.

choices.text: Attach EBS volumes directly to the workstations
choices.explanation: EBS is block storage for EC2 and cannot be provided directly to on-premises workstations.

choices.text: Copy all data every night with DataSync
choices.explanation: This does not provide the experience of continuous shared file access.

source.label: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: File Gateway provides cached file shares to on-premises SMB/NFS clients and stores the data in S3.
learning.concept: To access objects updated directly in S3, configure or trigger a metadata cache refresh. Verify the required propagation time and update paths; do not assume immediate bidirectional synchronization.

sourceLabel: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway User Guide

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Shared Linux and Windows Workspace
prompt: A video production team uses NFS on Linux rendering nodes and SMB on Windows editing workstations. Both must work with the same project hierarchy, ACLs, and files at the same time, and the team wants a managed, high-performance file system on AWS. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: Mount Amazon EFS on the Windows workstations over SMB
choices.explanation: EFS is an NFS file system, not a native SMB share.

choices.text: Mount S3 as a local disk on each operating system
choices.explanation: This does not meet the POSIX/SMB file semantics and ACL requirements.

choices.text: Mount FSx for Windows File Server on the Linux nodes over NFS
choices.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server is for SMB and does not provide the same volume over NFS.

choices.text: Use a multiprotocol volume in Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
choices.explanation: It can provide multiprotocol NFS and SMB access to the same data.

source.label: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: FSx for ONTAP supports multiprotocol SMB and NFS access to the same data.
learning.concept: Check protocol, ACL, and file-sharing compatibility before considering performance.

sourceLabel: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP User Guide

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: A Global Entry Point for Objects
prompt: A photo-sharing service stores images replicated across S3 buckets in two Regions. Users need to read and write through a single global name from the AWS network closest to them, using the active bucket selected by the operator. The application should not need logic to determine the Region. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on each bucket
choices.explanation: It does not provide a single multiregion entry point or route requests to the active bucket.

choices.text: Create a separate CloudFront distribution for each bucket
choices.explanation: The application or users would still need to choose the destination.

choices.text: Create buckets with the same name in different Regions
choices.explanation: S3 bucket names must be globally unique.

choices.text: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point and register both buckets
choices.explanation: It can route requests to S3 buckets in multiple Regions through a single global endpoint.

source.label: Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: A Multi-Region Access Point provides a single global endpoint for S3 buckets in multiple Regions.
learning.concept: This question asks for a global data-plane entry point that uses the active bucket; it does not assume automatic failover.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points User Guide

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Ultra-Low-Latency 5G Video Analysis
prompt: A port's autonomous guided vehicles send 5G video that must be analyzed in under 10 ms, which is not possible with a round trip to a metropolitan Region. AWS APIs or containers need to run near the edge of the mobile operator's 5G network. Where should the workload be deployed?

choices.text: Deploy the workload in an AWS Wavelength Zone
choices.explanation: It provides access to AWS services with ultra-low latency near the edge of a 5G network.

choices.text: Store the data in S3 Intelligent-Tiering in a distant Region
choices.explanation: Storage tiering does not reduce real-time inference latency.

choices.text: Use only a CloudFront edge location
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to place VPC workloads at the 5G edge.

choices.text: Purchase an EC2 Dedicated Host
choices.explanation: A Dedicated Host is a dedicated server in an AWS Region, not a workload placement option at a mobile operator's 5G edge.

source.label: AWS Wavelength 開発者ガイド

learning.reason: Wavelength Zones are AWS infrastructure for running ultra-low-latency applications within mobile operators' 5G networks.
learning.concept: Distinguish Local Zones near metropolitan areas, Wavelength near mobile operators' 5G networks, and Outposts at customer premises.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Low-Latency Rendering in a Metropolitan Area
prompt: Video editors are in a metropolitan area, and the round-trip latency to the nearest parent Region makes collaborative editing uncomfortable. They still want to use the parent Region for the control plane and many services. Which option is the best fit for running EC2/EBS near the metropolitan area without placing hardware at the customer's facility?

choices.text: Install an AWS Outposts rack in the editors' office
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the constraint that no rack should be installed at the customer's facility.

choices.text: Move the VPC to another Region
choices.explanation: This would compromise integration with the parent Region's services and does not guarantee proximity to the metropolitan area.

choices.text: Create a subnet in an AWS Local Zone and place the workload there
choices.explanation: Local Zones extend a parent Region with infrastructure near metropolitan areas, where low-latency workloads can run.

choices.text: Enable only S3 Cross-Region Replication
choices.explanation: Replicating data alone does not bring compute closer to users.

source.label: AWS Local Zones ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: Local Zones extend a parent Region and let you run low-latency workloads near metropolitan areas.
learning.concept: Choose between Outposts and Local Zones based on whether physical infrastructure must be located at the customer's premises.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: On-Premises Processing and Data Residency
prompt: A hospital needs to process imaging workloads on its premises, and regulations prohibit patient images from leaving the facility. The hospital wants to deploy AWS-managed compute and storage on-site while reusing as much as possible of its existing AWS VPC, IAM, APIs, and operating model. Which option is most appropriate?

choices.text: Extend the CloudFront cache duration
choices.explanation: This does not provide AWS compute on the hospital premises or meet the data residency requirement.

choices.text: Use Dedicated Instances in another Region
choices.explanation: Dedicated tenancy does not change the processing location: the instances still run in a Region, not on the hospital premises.

choices.text: Store the data directly in S3 Glacier Deep Archive
choices.explanation: This is archival storage and does not provide low-latency processing on the hospital premises.

choices.text: Deploy AWS Outposts at the hospital
choices.explanation: Outposts extends AWS infrastructure and services to on-premises locations, supporting local processing.

source.label: AWS Outposts ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: Outposts extends AWS infrastructure and services to on-premises locations.
learning.concept: Unlike Wavelength and Local Zones, Outposts places AWS services at the customer’s facility.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Static Content Origin Failure
prompt: A global product website is delivered through CloudFront. It normally retrieves images from a primary S3 origin. If the S3 origin in that Region becomes unavailable, the site must automatically fail over only cache-miss GET/HEAD requests to a replicated S3 bucket in another Region. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Configure primary and secondary S3 origins in a CloudFront origin group
choices.explanation: For specified HTTP status codes, CloudFront can fail over GET/HEAD requests to the secondary origin.

choices.text: Synchronize an S3 bucket to each CloudFront edge location
choices.explanation: Edge locations are not user-managed destinations for deploying S3 buckets.

choices.text: Set the CloudFront TTL to 0
choices.explanation: This only reduces caching; it does not provide a switch to another origin when the origin fails.

choices.text: Point Route 53 weighted records to the S3 bucket names
choices.explanation: This is not an automatic failover feature for requests CloudFront makes to its origins.

source.label: Amazon CloudFront 開発者ガイド

learning.reason: A CloudFront origin group can conditionally fail over to a secondary origin when the primary fails.
learning.concept: When designing origin failover, verify which methods are covered and whether the replicated data is consistent.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Consistent Segmentation Across Global Sites
prompt: An enterprise operates across multiple Regions, multiple AWS accounts, and dozens of branch networks. It wants to distribute consistent isolation policies among development, production, and shared services, while simplifying global WAN connectivity and routing from a central point. Which AWS service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Add a separate internet gateway to each VPC
choices.explanation: This does not provide private connectivity between sites or consistent segmentation.

choices.text: Define a global network and core network policy with AWS Cloud WAN
choices.explanation: A policy can manage a global network spanning Regions, accounts, and on-premises locations.

choices.text: Synchronize each branch directly with S3
choices.explanation: File transfer does not manage network connectivity or segmentation policies.

choices.text: Consolidate only the Route 53 public hosted zones
choices.explanation: DNS consolidation does not replace WAN connectivity and routing control.

source.label: AWS Cloud WAN ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: Cloud WAN centrally builds and manages global networks and lets you define segments through core network policies.
learning.concept: For connectivity spanning many Regions, sites, and accounts, also evaluate policy-driven global WAN services.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Shared POSIX Storage Resilient to an AZ Failure
prompt: Containerized research computing jobs concurrently read and write the same POSIX files from Linux workers in multiple AZs. They cannot tolerate losing access to the data because of a single-AZ failure, and the operations team does not want to manage file servers or replication. Which storage should they choose?

choices.text: Attach an EBS volume in one AZ to all workers
choices.explanation: EBS is scoped to an AZ and does not provide a shared file system without management.

choices.text: Replicate the data to each worker’s instance store
choices.explanation: This is local storage that can be lost if an instance fails and does not meet the shared consistency requirement.

choices.text: Mount an EFS Regional file system from multiple AZs
choices.explanation: EFS Regional stores data across multiple AZs in a Region and provides a shared NFS file system.

choices.text: Use S3 One Zone-IA as a POSIX file system
choices.explanation: This is single-AZ storage and does not meet the requirements for a shared POSIX file system.

source.label: Amazon EFS ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: EFS Regional is a managed NFS file system that stores data across multiple AZs.
learning.concept: Evaluate EFS Regional when shared POSIX access, multi-AZ resilience, and managed operations are all required.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Managed SFTP for Partners
prompt: Hundreds of trading partners cannot change their existing SFTP clients. Incoming files must be stored in S3, isolated in a logical directory for each partner, and identity management must use the enterprise’s existing IdP. Which option is best for avoiding server OS patching and SFTP daemon operations while providing only a private entry point inside a VPC?

choices.text: Install OpenSSH on EC2 and use cron to copy files to S3
choices.explanation: You would have to operate patching, availability, user isolation, and scaling yourself.

choices.text: Configure an AWS Transfer Family SFTP server with a VPC-hosted endpoint and an S3 backend
choices.explanation: It provides managed SFTP, a VPC endpoint, S3 storage, and custom IdP integration.

choices.text: Expose an SFTP port through API Gateway
choices.explanation: API Gateway does not terminate the SFTP protocol.

choices.text: Distribute CloudFront signed cookies to the partners
choices.explanation: This controls access to web delivery; it does not provide SFTP uploads.

source.label: AWS Transfer Family ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: Transfer Family provides managed file transfer protocols such as SFTP and can use S3 for storage.
learning.concept: When compatibility with an existing file transfer protocol is required, evaluate a managed transfer service before an HTTP API or self-managed SSH.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Organization-Wide Egress Filtering
prompt: You want to centrally control internet egress from private subnets across multiple accounts using an allowlist. You need stateful inspection and domain-based controls for TLS SNI and HTTP, and you want rules and policies automatically applied across the organization, including to new accounts. You do not want to operate the OS or clusters of a third-party firewall. Which architecture is the best fit?

choices.text: Write FQDN rules in the security groups of each EC2 instance
choices.explanation: Security groups do not provide domain-name-based egress filtering or TLS inspection.

choices.text: Store VPC Flow Logs in S3
choices.explanation: This provides retrospective visibility; it does not allow or block egress traffic.

choices.text: Deploy AWS Network Firewall in an inspection VPC and apply it across the organization using a centralized Firewall Manager Network Firewall policy
choices.explanation: Network Firewall provides stateful inspection and domain-based egress filtering, while Firewall Manager can apply a consistent Network Firewall policy to existing and new targets in AWS Organizations.

choices.text: Delete the routes to the internet gateway
choices.explanation: This stops all egress and cannot permit the required traffic based on an allowlist.

source.label: AWS Firewall Manager 開発者ガイド

learning.reason: Network Firewall provides managed stateful inspection and domain-based egress filtering, while Firewall Manager helps deploy consistent policies across AWS Organizations.
learning.concept: Domain-name allowlisting is different from decrypting TLS payloads. Configure the routes through the inspection VPC, the Firewall Manager policy scope, and automatic remediation as well.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Recovery Launch Target After Site Loss
prompt: A manufacturing plant has 120 on-premises Windows servers that must be recovered to AWS if the entire plant loses power or is lost. You want to keep normal EC2 costs low, while fixing the recovery subnet, IAM instance profile, and instance type to audited configurations. Which architecture is most appropriate?

choices.text: Create hourly AMIs with AWS Backup and launch them manually from the console after an outage
choices.explanation: AMI recovery is possible, but this does not provide continuous replication or standardized recovery launch configurations, leaving room for variation in manual settings.

choices.text: Configure continuous replication with Elastic Disaster Recovery, and preconfigure per-source-server launch settings and EC2 launch templates
choices.explanation: Correct. DRS continuously replicates from on-premises at low cost, and launch settings and launch templates can control network, size, and IAM settings for recovery and drill instances.

choices.text: Keep test instances running continuously with Application Migration Service
choices.explanation: MGN is a migration service, and keeping instances running continuously conflicts with the requirement to keep normal costs low.

choices.text: Create only an EC2 Auto Scaling group and copy the on-premises disks during an outage
choices.explanation: Auto Scaling does not provide block-level continuous replication or recovery point management for on-premises servers.

source.label: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery: 起動設定

learning.reason: Recovery from a site loss combines continuous replication with precontrolled launch configuration for recovery.
learning.concept: In disaster recovery, validate the recovery network, permissions, and capacity in advance, as well as the data.

sourceLabel: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery: Launch settings

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Final Synchronization for a Rehost Migration
prompt: You are rehosting 30 VMs for an internal portal to AWS. You want to run integration tests on AWS before cutover, while updates continue on the on-premises production environment during testing. At cutover, you want to launch new instances that include the latest changes. Which procedure is most appropriate?

choices.text: Run a test launch with AWS Application Migration Service, then launch cutover instances again during the cutover window
choices.explanation: Correct. MGN separates test and cutover launches. At cutover, it can launch new instances with data that has been continuously replicated up to that point.

choices.text: Reuse the test-launched instances by changing them to the production DNS names
choices.explanation: Source changes made after the test launch are not continuously applied to the test instances, so this cannot ensure cutover with the latest data.

choices.text: Replicate the entire VMs with AWS DMS and convert them to EC2 instances
choices.explanation: DMS is primarily a database migration service and is not suitable for rehosting VMs, including their operating systems.

choices.text: Use the same backup recovery point for testing and production
choices.explanation: Production updates made after testing would not be reflected in the cutover target.

source.label: AWS Application Migration Service ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: Do not repurpose the test copy for production; launch cutover instances with the final synchronized data at cutover.
learning.concept: For migration with continuous replication, distinguish test results from the final, synchronized production copy.

sourceLabel: AWS Application Migration Service User Guide

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: File synchronization without saturating bandwidth
prompt: The design department is migrating 18 TB of CAD data from on-premises NFS to Amazon S3. After the initial migration, it must synchronize nightly changes and limit network usage during business hours. The operations team wants to manage integrity verification and scheduled runs. Which service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Configure AWS DataSync locations, a task, and a nightly schedule
choices.explanation: Correct. DataSync automates transfers between NFS and S3 and can be configured with a schedule, bandwidth limits, and integrity verification.

choices.text: Ship a physical device every night to ingest the changes
choices.explanation: Physical transfer is unsuitable for nightly incremental synchronization and a short update cycle.

choices.text: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication to an on-premises NFS system
choices.explanation: S3 replication is a feature for replication between S3 buckets; NFS cannot be used as its direct source.

choices.text: Copy the data manually to Amazon EFS, then export it to S3
choices.explanation: This adds an intermediate storage location and manual work, and does not meet the incremental synchronization and bandwidth-limiting requirements in one managed workflow.

source.label: AWS DataSync ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: Manage online incremental transfers as operational tasks.
learning.concept: For initial transfers and recurring increments, assess data volume, effective bandwidth, and downtime constraints separately.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Large initial upload from a new customer’s field location
prompt: A video production company with AWS Enterprise Support needs to transfer 400 TB of initial video data to AWS from a filming location with limited connectivity. It is a new AWS customer and can bring its own storage to a secure facility near the location, where it can upload to S3 over a high-speed connection. Which option is most appropriate and currently available to new customers?

choices.text: Reserve an AWS Data Transfer Terminal, bring the company’s own devices, and upload over the high-speed connection
choices.explanation: Correct. AWS Data Transfer Terminal is a network-connected physical facility where customers bring their own devices. Enterprise Support customers can reserve it for large data transfers.

choices.text: Order a new AWS Snowball Edge device
choices.explanation: Snowball Edge is not available to new customers. AWS directs new customers to alternatives such as Data Transfer Terminal.

choices.text: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to exceed the filming location’s connection limit
choices.explanation: Route optimization may help, but it cannot exceed the site’s physical upload-bandwidth limit.

choices.text: Import the video directly as an EBS snapshot
choices.explanation: This is not a transfer feature for directly uploading video files as an EBS snapshot.

source.label: AWS Data Transfer Terminal ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: Choose a current alternative for large, offline-like transfers given that Snowball Edge is no longer available to new customers.
learning.concept: Data Transfer Terminal is for Enterprise Support customers; confirm facility, equipment, and reservation requirements in advance.

sourceLabel: AWS Data Transfer Terminal User Guide

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Transforming a heterogeneous database migration
prompt: An older commercial database is being migrated to Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition. Its schema includes proprietary stored procedures and dialect-specific SQL, and data changes must be kept in sync without stopping operations. Which combination best divides the conversion work and ongoing data transfer?

choices.text: Use DMS alone to fully automate stored-procedure conversion
choices.explanation: DMS is primarily for data transfer and does not guarantee complex heterogeneous database code conversion.

choices.text: Use Schema Conversion Tool to assess and convert the schema and code, and DMS for full load and CDC
choices.explanation: Correct. SCT can assess and convert schemas and code between heterogeneous engines, while DMS can perform change data capture after the initial load.

choices.text: Create an RDS cross-Region read replica
choices.explanation: This is a replication feature for supported, matching RDS engines; it cannot convert an on-premises commercial database to heterogeneous Aurora.

choices.text: Use AWS Backup to restore the source database directly to Aurora PostgreSQL
choices.explanation: Backup restoration does not convert a heterogeneous database schema or replicate ongoing changes.

source.label: AWS Schema Conversion Tool ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: For heterogeneous databases, design code and schema conversion separately from data replication.
learning.concept: CDC handles data changes. Assess support for SQL dialects and procedures in advance.

sourceLabel: AWS Schema Conversion Tool User Guide

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Encrypted backups to another account
prompt: EBS volumes in a production account are to be copied to a dedicated recovery account within Organizations. The EBS resources are not fully managed by AWS Backup. Which configuration is required on the destination side for the cross-account copy?

choices.text: Create a backup vault in the destination encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, and configure a vault policy that allows the copy
choices.explanation: Correct. For cross-account copying of resources that are not fully managed, the destination vault needs a customer managed key and permission to allow the copy.

choices.text: Use the destination’s default backup vault
choices.explanation: The default vault cannot be used as the destination for cross-account copies.

choices.text: Share the source’s AWS managed KMS key with the destination
choices.explanation: The key policy for an AWS managed key cannot be modified for sharing.

choices.text: Restore directly from the source account to the destination
choices.explanation: With AWS Backup, first copy the recovery point to a vault in the destination account, then restore it there.

source.label: AWS Backup: クロスアカウントバックアップ

learning.reason: Design for the destination account’s ownership, encryption key, and vault policy.
learning.concept: Which keys can be used for cross-account copying depends on whether the resource is fully managed.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Reassessing RTO and RPO After a Change
prompt: A payment application must continue to meet an RTO of 30 minutes and an RPO of 5 minutes after deployment. After an infrastructure change, you want a single assessment result that identifies components that fall short of these targets and the CloudWatch alarms, SOPs, and tests needed. Which operational approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use AWS Config rules alone to calculate RTO and RPO
choices.explanation: Config is useful for checking configuration compliance, but it does not independently assess estimated RTO and RPO for the entire application or recommend recovery procedures.

choices.text: Compare only CPU utilization in CloudWatch
choices.explanation: CPU utilization alone cannot assess RPO, recovery time, dependencies, or whether procedures can be carried out.

choices.text: Publish a new version of the application in Resilience Hub and run a resilience assessment
choices.explanation: Correct. Resilience Hub assesses estimated RTO and RPO against policies and provides recommendations for alarms, SOPs, and tests.

choices.text: Defer the assessment until the annual manual DR exercise
choices.explanation: This can leave configuration drift after a change undetected for an extended period.

source.label: AWS Resilience Hub: 評価レポート

learning.reason: Reassess deviations from targets whenever the configuration changes.
learning.concept: Setting RTO and RPO targets is not enough; the application configuration must be validated against them continuously.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Safe Operation of a Two-Region Failover
prompt: An order API is deployed independently in two Regions. During a major disruption, you want to stop DNS traffic to one Region and switch to the other within predefined safety rules. You want to avoid manual DNS edits and prevent accidentally stopping traffic to both Regions. Which service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use routing controls and safety rules in Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)
choices.explanation: Correct. ARC routing controls work with Route 53 health checks to control traffic between Regions, and safety rules can prevent dangerous state transitions.

choices.text: Delete the Route 53 hosted zone and create a new one in the other Region
choices.explanation: This is destructive and provides neither an immediate switch nor safe state control.

choices.text: Delete the ALB in each Region simultaneously, then recreate it only in the healthy Region
choices.explanation: Deleting and recreating load balancers is destructive and does not provide a DNS-level switch.

choices.text: Copy the Global Accelerator static IP to each Region
choices.explanation: Static IPs cannot be copied this way, and this approach does not meet the safety-rule requirement.

source.label: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC): Routing control

learning.reason: Operate regional failover with explicit switch states and safety guardrails instead of manual DNS edits.
learning.concept: The current name is Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC).

sourceLabel: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC): Routing control

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Shifting Traffic Away from a Single AZ
prompt: A service is deployed in three AZs behind an Application Load Balancer in a single Region. A network issue is suspected in one AZ, and you want to temporarily stop sending new traffic only to that AZ while continuing to serve requests in the other AZs. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Delete the subnet in the affected AZ
choices.explanation: This is a destructive operation that can remove dependent resources, not a temporary way to shift traffic away.

choices.text: Set the Auto Scaling minimum capacity to zero in all AZs
choices.explanation: This would also remove capacity from healthy AZs.

choices.text: Disable health checks and rely only on client retries
choices.explanation: This does not prevent traffic from being routed to the affected AZ.

choices.text: Use zonal shift in Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)
choices.explanation: Correct. ARC zonal shift temporarily shifts traffic for supported resources away from a specified AZ to healthy AZs in the same Region.

source.label: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC): Zonal shift

learning.reason: Isolate the impact at the AZ level to match the failure domain.
learning.concept: Zonal shift is temporary; confirm that the resource is supported and that the healthy AZs have sufficient capacity.

sourceLabel: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC): Zonal shift

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Regional Switch for Planned Maintenance
prompt: A global ordering system uses Aurora Global Database. Before planned maintenance in the primary Region, you want to move writes to another Region. You need to confirm synchronization before the switch, avoid data loss, and minimize application changes. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Perform a managed switchover of the Aurora Global Database
choices.explanation: Correct. Use a managed switchover for a planned regional transition; it promotes the secondary to the new writable primary.

choices.text: Delete the secondary cluster and create an empty cluster
choices.explanation: This conflicts with data protection and a fast switch, and does not provide a write target.

choices.text: Create an independent cluster and run periodic S3 exports
choices.explanation: Manual exports are unlikely to meet a low RPO and a short switchover time.

choices.text: Promote a Multi-AZ standby to another Region
choices.explanation: A Multi-AZ standby is a high-availability feature within the same Region.

source.label: Amazon Aurora: Aurora Global Database

learning.reason: Distinguish a planned switchover from failover during a disruption.
learning.concept: For planned maintenance, use a switchover that can verify synchronization; use a different recovery procedure during a disruption.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Replicating Existing Objects
prompt: An S3 bucket in the Tokyo Region must be replicated to the Osaka Region. Versioning is enabled, and replication must cover not only objects added in the future but also the 800 million objects that already exist. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Configure only a replication rule and wait for existing objects to be replicated
choices.explanation: Standard replication configuration does not automatically replicate objects created before the rule was set up.

choices.text: Disable versioning before configuring replication
choices.explanation: S3 replication requires versioning on both the source and destination buckets.

choices.text: Configure a replication rule and run S3 Batch Replication for existing objects
choices.explanation: Correct. Ongoing replication applies to new objects, and Batch Replication can be used for existing objects.

choices.text: Use a Lifecycle rule to move objects to another Region
choices.explanation: Lifecycle manages storage-class transitions and expiration within a bucket; it does not perform cross-Region replication.

source.label: Amazon S3: Batch Replication

learning.reason: Separate ongoing replication for new data from backfilling existing data.
learning.concept: Objects that predate activation of the configuration require an explicit backfill operation.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Regularly Verifying Recoverability
prompt: A medical appointment system takes daily backups with AWS Backup. An audit requires periodic proof not only that backup jobs succeeded, but also that the backups can be restored to an isolated environment and pass application checks after startup. Which approach is most appropriate while minimizing manual effort?

choices.text: Set CloudWatch alarms only on backup-success metrics
choices.explanation: Successful backup creation does not prove that the restored workload is usable.

choices.text: Configure an AWS Backup restore testing plan to perform periodic restores to an isolated environment and validate them
choices.explanation: Use a restore testing plan to restore regularly into an isolated environment. Send the completion event through EventBridge to a validation workflow, such as Lambda, to test the application. Record the validation result with PutRestoreValidationResult and retain the validation logs.

choices.text: Restore to the production database monthly and overwrite the original database
choices.explanation: Overwriting production is high risk and conflicts with safe validation in an isolated environment.

choices.text: Delete older recovery points and keep only the latest one
choices.explanation: This does not verify recoverability and reduces retention and ransomware recovery capabilities.

source.label: AWS Backup: 復元テスト

learning.reason: Successful backups and a usable restored workload are separate things to verify.
learning.concept: Business continuity evidence should cover backup creation, restoration, health checks, and result retention.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Reprocessing Orders During an Outage
prompt: The order API processes payment requests asynchronously. If the downstream payment provider becomes temporarily unavailable, requests must not be lost and must be retried automatically after recovery. To avoid duplicate charges, failed requests must be isolated somewhere they can be investigated, and reprocessing must be controlled. Which architecture is most appropriate?

choices.text: Increase the API Gateway client timeout when the payment provider fails
choices.explanation: A long-running synchronous connection does not absorb the outage and still leaves request-loss and scaling problems.

choices.text: Record failed orders only in CloudWatch Logs and resend them manually
choices.explanation: Logs are not a reprocessing queue or failure-isolation mechanism, and manual work increases the risk of omissions and longer recovery times.

choices.text: Combine an SQS queue, a dead-letter queue, and idempotent payment processing
choices.explanation: Correct. SQS durably holds requests and can isolate failures in a DLQ. Designing the consumer to be idempotent helps prevent duplicate charges when messages are redelivered.

choices.text: Keep the database transaction open indefinitely when a payment fails
choices.explanation: Long-running transactions can cause locks or resource exhaustion and do not improve resilience to downstream outages.

source.label: Amazon SQS: デッドレターキュー

learning.reason: Absorb temporary downstream outages with a durable queue, failure isolation, retries, and idempotency.
learning.concept: At-least-once delivery can result in duplicates, so side-effecting operations need idempotency keys and state management.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Setting Permission Limits for Delegated Developers
prompt: Administrators in each development account are to be delegated the ability to create IAM roles. However, the roles they create must not exceed a defined set of permissions, and developers must be able to self-serve within that scope. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Require a permissions boundary on created roles and deny requests that omit or change the boundary
choices.explanation: A permissions boundary limits the maximum permissions that can be granted to a role while allowing delegation within that scope.

choices.text: Grant AdministratorAccess to all developers
choices.explanation: This does not meet the least-privilege or permission-limit requirements.

choices.text: Use tag policies to regulate role names
choices.explanation: Tag conventions do not restrict which APIs can be performed.

choices.text: List principals only in the trust policy
choices.explanation: A trust policy does not limit a role's maximum permissions.

source.label: AWS IAM: Permissions boundaries

learning.reason: A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions available to the delegated role.
learning.concept: An SCP sets an account-level maximum, while a permissions boundary sets a principal-level maximum; neither grants permissions by itself.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Analyzing unintended external access
prompt: A security team wants to continuously check whether S3 buckets, KMS keys, and IAM roles in its organization are exposed outside the organization through resource policies. Which service should it use to detect external access paths defined by policies without manually correlating access logs?

choices.text: Deliver CloudTrail logs to S3 and query all events with SQL
choices.explanation: This provides a record of past activity, but it does not continuously analyze external reachability from policies.

choices.text: Enable IAM Access Analyzer as an organization analyzer
choices.explanation: Access Analyzer analyzes resource policies and helps detect access that is reachable from outside or within the organization.

choices.text: Randomize all bucket names
choices.explanation: Making names difficult to guess does not prevent external access allowed by resource policies.

choices.text: Rotate every IAM user's access keys daily
choices.explanation: Credential rotation does not detect resource policies that expose resources to external principals.

source.label: AWS IAM: IAM Access Analyzer

learning.reason: An organization analyzer provides a centralized way to review external access resulting from policies.
learning.concept: Detecting reachability and reviewing actual access history are complementary. After detection, compare the finding with your intent and revise the policy as needed.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Account access based on job attributes
prompt: Across hundreds of AWS accounts, you want to automatically control access based on employees' department, project, and employment status. The HR directory is the authoritative source for these attributes, and you want to avoid managing IAM users in each account. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Create IAM users in each account and update them whenever an employee changes roles
choices.explanation: Attribute synchronization would be distributed, creating substantial operational overhead and a greater risk of gaps at this scale.

choices.text: Give everyone a shared administrator role
choices.explanation: This removes least-privilege access based on department and job function.

choices.text: Configure identity-provider attributes in Identity Center and assign attribute-based permission sets
choices.explanation: You can use attributes from an external identity source for ABAC and centrally manage assignments across accounts.

choices.text: Use tag policies alone to enforce employees' departments
choices.explanation: Tag policies standardize resource tags; they do not provide user authorization attributes.

source.label: AWS IAM Identity Center: Attributes for access control

learning.reason: Authoritative attributes from the identity provider can be linked to authorization.
learning.concept: With ABAC, clarify whether each policy evaluates principal, session, or resource attributes.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM Identity Center: Attributes for access control

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Encryption recovery during a Regional outage
prompt: The primary Region and DR Region handle the same encrypted data format. During a DR failover, you want to manage the related KMS keys across Regions. Which KMS feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Specify the ARN of a single-Region key in all DR services
choices.explanation: KMS keys are Regional resources, so a key in another Region does not become a local key there.

choices.text: Choose an AWS managed key in each Region to get the same key
choices.explanation: AWS managed keys in different Regions are separate keys.

choices.text: Export the key material daily and import it into the DR Region
choices.explanation: AWS KMS symmetric key material is not something you export for this purpose.

choices.text: Use a multi-Region KMS key with a primary key and replica keys
choices.explanation: The related primary and replica keys share the same key material and can be used in their respective Regions.

source.label: AWS KMS: マルチリージョンキー

learning.reason: Related keys can be used in each Region while retaining the same key material.
learning.concept: Manage key policies and each service's encryption settings separately for each Region.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Decryption with tenant boundaries
prompt: A shared service encrypts documents for many customers with the same symmetric KMS key. Decryption must be denied unless the customer ID and document ID match the values used during encryption. How can this be done without creating more keys for each customer?

choices.text: Include the customer ID and document ID in the encryption context, and use a kms:EncryptionContext condition to restrict which context values are authorized.
choices.explanation: KMS binds the encryption context to the ciphertext as additional authenticated data (AAD) and requires the same key-value pairs during decryption. Policy conditions restrict the context values that callers are allowed to use.

choices.text: Record the customer ID in the key description
choices.explanation: The description is not evaluated as an authorization condition.

choices.text: Put the customer ID only in the filename
choices.explanation: An object name is not a KMS decryption authorization condition.

choices.text: Create multiple aliases for the same key
choices.explanation: An alias is another name for a key; it does not enforce per-operation conditions.

source.label: AWS KMS: 暗号化コンテキスト

learning.reason: KMS authenticated encryption verifies that the encryption and decryption contexts match. Policy conditions restrict the context values callers are permitted to use.
learning.concept: The encryption context is not encrypted and is recorded in logs. Use only non-sensitive, publicly shareable identifiers; never include sensitive information.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Preventing Evidence Deletion During Retention
prompt: Audit logs must not be deleted, overwritten, or have their retention period shortened for seven years after they are recorded, even by administrators. Which configuration is most appropriate?

choices.text: Deny DeleteObject and make an exception for administrators
choices.explanation: The administrator exception and the possibility of policy changes do not satisfy the immutable-retention requirement.

choices.text: Enable versioning on the bucket and configure Object Lock in compliance mode with a seven-year retention period
choices.explanation: In compliance mode, objects cannot be deleted or have their retention period shortened during the retention period, even by the root user.

choices.text: Move the objects to Standard-IA immediately
choices.explanation: A storage class does not provide immutable retention.

choices.text: Send a notification through Config after deletion
choices.explanation: This detects deletion after the fact; it does not prevent it.

source.label: Amazon S3: Object Lock

learning.reason: Compliance mode prevents deletion and retention shortening while the retention period is in effect.
learning.concept: Object Lock requires versioning and should be distinguished from governance mode.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Making Centralized Backups Immutable
prompt: Recovery points are centralized in a dedicated backup account. You must ensure that, even during a ransomware compromise, organization administrators cannot delete them or shorten their retention after the configuration is finalized. Which feature is appropriate?

choices.text: Attach an S3 bucket policy to the vault
choices.explanation: An AWS Backup vault is not an S3 bucket.

choices.text: Require MFA only for administrators
choices.explanation: This does not make deletion by an authenticated administrator impossible.

choices.text: Configure Vault Lock in compliance mode and make the vault immutable after the grace period
choices.explanation: After the grace period ends, recovery points are protected from deletion or changes that violate the retention rules.

choices.text: Only copy backups to another Region
choices.explanation: This does not prevent deletion or retention changes in the destination vault.

source.label: AWS Backup: Vault Lock

learning.reason: Compliance mode prevents changes to retention rules after the configuration is finalized.
learning.concept: A separate account limits the scope of compromise, while Vault Lock ensures recovery-point immutability.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Continuously Discovering Sensitive Data in S3
prompt: You want to continuously identify data that appears to be personal information or credentials in files uploaded to S3 each day, and aggregate the findings without modifying the application. Which option is most appropriate?

choices.text: Generate only S3 Inventory reports
choices.explanation: Inventory does not detect sensitive data in object contents.

choices.text: Search only CloudTrail management events
choices.explanation: CloudTrail does not classify object contents.

choices.text: Apply Inspector directly to the S3 bucket
choices.explanation: Inspector is not a general-purpose service for classifying S3 content.

choices.text: Use Macie automated discovery or sensitive data discovery jobs
choices.explanation: Macie detects sensitive data in S3 objects and generates findings.

source.label: Amazon Macie: 機密データ検出

learning.reason: Macie analyzes S3 content as a managed detection service.
learning.concept: Design the scope, frequency, exclusions, and access permissions for discovery results.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Organization-Wide Security Standards
prompt: You want to apply the same Security Hub standards to all accounts across multiple Regions and enable additional standards for only some OUs. How can you avoid manually tracking account additions and removals?

choices.text: Enable the standards manually in each account and track them in a spreadsheet
choices.explanation: Tracking new accounts and changes this way is decentralized.

choices.text: Configure central configuration through the delegated administrator and associate policies with the organization, OUs, and accounts
choices.explanation: Configuration policies can consistently apply standards and controls across the organization hierarchy.

choices.text: Only aggregate findings in S3
choices.explanation: Aggregating findings does not apply standards consistently.

choices.text: Use an SCP to deny the Security Hub API
choices.explanation: This prevents evaluations from being enabled, contrary to the requirement.

source.label: AWS Security Hub: 中央設定

learning.reason: Central configuration supports applying standards and controls according to the organization hierarchy.
learning.concept: Finding aggregation, delegated administration, and enabling standards are separate configurations.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Onboarding Accounts for Threat Detection
prompt: You want threat detection to be enabled as soon as a new account joins your organization, with findings centrally managed in a dedicated security account. Which configuration is most appropriate?

choices.text: Distribute shared access keys to every account
choices.explanation: Long-term keys are unnecessary and do not ensure automatic onboarding.

choices.text: Store only CloudWatch Logs in a central bucket
choices.explanation: Aggregating logs alone does not provide GuardDuty threat detection.

choices.text: Designate the security account as the GuardDuty delegated administrator and enable automatic activation through Organizations integration
choices.explanation: The delegated administrator can manage organization member accounts and enable GuardDuty automatically.

choices.text: Log in monthly as the root user of the management account
choices.explanation: This conflicts with least privilege and automation.

source.label: Amazon GuardDuty: Organizations統合

learning.reason: Organizations integration and delegated administration enable centralized operation of threat detection.
learning.concept: Do not use the management account's powerful permissions for routine operations.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Reducing Unused Permissions
prompt: You want to reduce excessive permissions on an old IAM role based on actual usage. Static syntax checks alone are not enough. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Review IAM Access Analyzer's unused access analysis
choices.explanation: It can recommend unused service permissions and actions based on access activity.

choices.text: Format the JSON to reduce its line count
choices.explanation: Changing the formatting does not identify unused permissions.

choices.text: Replace every role with ReadOnlyAccess
choices.explanation: This could break required write operations.

choices.text: Disable CloudTrail
choices.explanation: This removes evidence of usage and undermines auditing.

source.label: AWS IAM: 未使用アクセスの削減

learning.reason: Actual usage can be used to review and reduce excessive permissions.
learning.concept: Check for legitimate but infrequent operations, and adopt recommendations only after change control and testing.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Preventing Noncompliant Resources Before Creation
prompt: In a governed OU, you want to prevent specific noncompliant resources from being created through IaC. Notifications after a violation are not enough. Which type of Control Tower control should you use?

choices.text: Enable only detective controls
choices.explanation: They evaluate existing resources; they do not prevent creation.

choices.text: Deliver CloudTrail logs to S3
choices.explanation: This records operations but does not reject creation requests.

choices.text: Enable proactive controls
choices.explanation: CloudFormation hooks can prevent the provisioning of noncompliant resources.

choices.text: Add tags to the stack
choices.explanation: Adding tags alone does not create a Control Tower control.

source.label: AWS Control Tower: コントロール

learning.reason: Proactive controls reject noncompliant configurations at creation time.
learning.concept: Preventive, proactive, and detective controls apply at different stages.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Attribute-Based Delegation for a Data Lake
prompt: You want to delegate access across multiple accounts in a data lake with thousands of tables and columns, based on sensitivity classification, region, and business unit. Which design avoids granting permissions individually for each table?

choices.text: Copy the tables to a public bucket
choices.explanation: This forfeits governance and does not provide column- or table-level authorization.

choices.text: Associate LF-Tags with Data Catalog resources and principals, then grant tag-based permissions
choices.explanation: Attribute matching can scale permissions across many catalog resources.

choices.text: Put the sensitivity classification only in the description field
choices.explanation: Description metadata is not evaluated as an authorization condition.

choices.text: Make all users data lake administrators
choices.explanation: This conflicts with least privilege and separation of duties.

source.label: AWS Lake Formation: LFタグ

learning.reason: LF-Tags enable permissions to be applied at scale based on attributes.
learning.concept: Design the tagging taxonomy and delegated administration first, and understand that assigning tags alone does not grant permissions.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Detecting tampering with audit logs
prompt: You want to periodically verify CloudTrail logs stored in S3 by comparing them with AWS-signed digests to detect changes or deletions after delivery. Which additional setting should you enable?

choices.text: Extend event history retention
choices.explanation: Event history does not provide cryptographic log integrity validation.

choices.text: Set CloudWatch Logs retention to indefinite
choices.explanation: Retention duration alone does not provide digest validation.

choices.text: Disable management events
choices.explanation: This does not validate integrity and would remove records that are important for auditing.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation
choices.explanation: The delivered digests can be used to detect changes to or deletion of log files.

source.label: AWS CloudTrail: ログファイル整合性検証

learning.reason: Signed digests make it possible to detect tampering with delivered logs.
learning.concept: Integrity validation does not replace immutable retention, so access controls and retention must be designed separately.

sourceLabel: AWS CloudTrail: Log file integrity validation

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Automatic rotation of application credentials
prompt: Multiple applications use RDS credentials. Which configuration best avoids placing plaintext credentials in code or deployment settings while supporting periodic rotation and failure tracking?

choices.text: Embed the password in an AMI and rebuild it every quarter
choices.explanation: This leaves copies of the credentials behind and does not provide secure rotation.

choices.text: Store the credentials in Secrets Manager, configure rotation, and retrieve them at runtime
choices.explanation: This combines secure storage and retrieval with rotation and monitoring.

choices.text: Store the plaintext value in CloudFormation Parameters
choices.explanation: This can expose the value in templates or history.

choices.text: Share a common long-term access key
choices.explanation: This does not solve database credential rotation and reduces traceability.

source.label: AWS Secrets Manager: ローテーション

learning.reason: Runtime retrieval and rotation avoid distributing plaintext credentials.
learning.concept: Design how clients reconnect and how they switch between old and new values.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Mitigating interception of EC2 credentials
prompt: You want to reduce the risk of temporary credentials being obtained from the instance metadata service through SSRF. Which setting rejects HTTP requests without a token while retaining the IAM role?

choices.text: Remove the instance profile and put access keys in environment variables
choices.explanation: This exposes long-term keys and reduces security.

choices.text: Allow HTTPS in the security group
choices.explanation: This does not control metadata requests originating inside the instance.

choices.text: Require IMDSv2 and a token
choices.explanation: This requires a session-oriented token and can reject IMDSv1-style requests.

choices.text: Replace the public IPv4 address with an Elastic IP
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to how the metadata service is accessed.

source.label: Amazon EC2: IMDSの設定

learning.reason: Requiring IMDSv2 rejects requests that do not include a token.
learning.concept: IMDSv2 is one layer of defense; input validation and a least-privilege role are also needed.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Automated collection of audit evidence
prompt: You want to periodically collect and review evidence for each control in an audit framework, based on service configurations and user actions across multiple accounts. Which central service can reduce the need to collect screenshots?

choices.text: Set a monthly budget in AWS Budgets
choices.explanation: Budgets is for cost management and does not collect audit evidence.

choices.text: Create a Route 53 health check
choices.explanation: This is for availability monitoring, not audit evidence collection.

choices.text: Save invoice PDFs
choices.explanation: Invoices do not cover compliance evidence for configurations and actions.

choices.text: Set up a framework and assessment in Audit Manager, then review automatically collected evidence
choices.explanation: It automatically collects evidence from AWS services and helps organize assessments mapped to controls.

source.label: AWS Audit Manager

learning.reason: Evidence collection and review can be structured around a framework.
learning.concept: Audit Manager does not automate passing an audit; the organization remains responsible for judging whether the evidence is appropriate.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Preventing S3 Data Exfiltration Outside the Organization
prompt: Restrict access to a sensitive S3 bucket to IAM principals in your organization and explicitly approved AWS service calls. Even if IAM permissions are inadvertently broadened, you want the bucket policy to deny principals outside your organization. Choose the two most appropriate measures.

choices.text: Use aws:PrincipalOrgID as a condition to deny access from outside your organization
choices.explanation: A resource policy can evaluate the requesting principal's organization ID to express an organizational boundary.

choices.text: Explicitly exempt legitimate service calls from the deny condition by using PrincipalIsAWSService and similar conditions
choices.explanation: This lets you intentionally distinguish legitimate service principals that do not have an organization ID.

choices.text: Randomize object keys
choices.explanation: Concealing names is not authorization.

choices.text: Allow S3:* for all roles
choices.explanation: This violates least privilege and does not create a resource-side deny.

choices.text: Export an Inventory report monthly
choices.explanation: This provides a retrospective listing and does not deny requests when they occur.

source.label: AWS IAM: グローバル条件キー

learning.reason: Combine an explicit deny based on organization ID with conditions that allow legitimate access through AWS services.
learning.concept: A data perimeter should not rely on identity policies alone; layer resource policies and organizational boundaries.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Reaching an Internal API from an Existing Distribution
prompt: Add a dynamic API to a site served through CloudFront. The ALB and ECS tasks are in private subnets in a supported Region, and only CloudFront should be able to call the API. Which configuration serves the API's GET and POST requests through the existing distribution without making the ALB public?

choices.text: Set only the internal ALB's private DNS name as a regular public custom origin
choices.explanation: Configuring a public custom origin by itself does not create a network path from CloudFront to a VPC private subnet.

choices.text: Configure the ALB as a CloudFront VPC origin and restrict origin access to a security group for CloudFront
choices.explanation: This creates a private connection between CloudFront and the internal ALB, which can be assigned to an API behavior in the existing distribution.

choices.text: Make the ALB internet-facing and inspect a dedicated HTTP header
choices.explanation: This may be an option for controlling access to a public ALB, but it violates the requirement to keep the ALB private.

choices.text: Move the API to an S3 static website endpoint and use OAC
choices.explanation: An S3 static website does not run a dynamic ECS API, and OAC cannot be used with a static website endpoint.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Choose an origin that the existing CloudFront distribution can use directly while keeping the internal ALB private.
learning.concept: Check the requirements for creating a VPC origin and the service-managed security group allowed at the origin. If caching personalized API responses, design the cache key and authorization separately.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Filtering by Department During Document Retrieval
prompt: An internal Bedrock Knowledge Base uses a shared vector store that supports metadata filtering. Each document is tagged with the department IDs allowed to view it, and only the authenticated application's backend can call the search API. How should you limit retrieval candidates to authorized departments so documents from other departments are not passed to the generative model?

choices.text: Add the department name to the prompt and tell the model not to include other departments' documents in its answer
choices.explanation: This may still pass search results from other departments to the generative model, so it does not isolate access at retrieval time.

choices.text: Set the model's temperature to 0 to reduce citations of documents from other departments
choices.explanation: The generation probability setting does not restrict which items are eligible for retrieval.

choices.text: Resolve the department IDs authorized for the authenticated principal on the server and apply them as a metadata filter for retrieval
choices.explanation: Only authorized candidates are included in the search results and passed to the generative model.

choices.text: Pass all search results to the model, then remove documents from other departments from the citation list after generation
choices.explanation: This does not constrain the model's input and information from other departments may appear in the final text.

source.label: AWS公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: The trusted caller should determine the condition before generating the prompt, at retrieval time.
learning.concept: The backend must always apply the metadata filter. Do not expose an API that lets users replace the authorization condition, and test for cross-department access.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Central Networking and Department Accounts
prompt: A network account and application accounts are in the same AWS Organizations organization. For strict access management, the network team must own the subnets and routes of one VPC. Departments must not add VPCs, and they want to use designated subnets while owning and paying for their EC2 and Lambda resources in their own accounts. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Share subnets from the VPC owner account with department accounts using AWS RAM
choices.explanation: Participants in a shared VPC can create resources owned by their own accounts in shared subnets of a centrally managed VPC.

choices.text: Create a cross-account IAM role in the central VPC and have departments use it to create EC2 and Lambda resources.
choices.explanation: Resources created with a role in the central account are owned and billed by the central account.

choices.text: Create a PrivateLink endpoint in each department VPC to connect to a service in the central VPC
choices.explanation: This can provide access to a central service, but it cannot place department compute resources in designated subnets in the central VPC.

choices.text: Create a dedicated VPC for each department and connect it to the central Transit Gateway
choices.explanation: This can use central routing, but requires each department to create and manage a VPC.

source.label: Amazon VPC 共有VPCガイド

learning.reason: With VPC sharing, the owner manages the network, while participants can create resources owned by their own accounts in shared subnets.
learning.concept: Consider VPC sharing when account separation and centralized network ownership are both required.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Sharing resources with an OU
prompt: A central IPAM integrated with AWS Organizations must assign private CIDRs for VPCs to accounts newly added to the development OU. The IPAM home Region and the pool's locale are different. Which two settings should be configured to avoid enumerating accounts or requiring manual approval? Select two.

choices.text: Create a resource share in the pool's locale and make the development OU a principal.
choices.explanation: When the locale differs from the home Region, creating the share in the locale does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Enable sharing with AWS Organizations in AWS RAM.
choices.explanation: This is required before an organization or OU can be specified as a principal.

choices.text: Share the pool only with the network account and use an SCP to allow CIDR assignment in the development OU.
choices.explanation: An SCP sets permission boundaries. It does not grant the development OU access through a resource share.

choices.text: Limit the principals to the IDs of existing development accounts.
choices.explanation: Accounts created in the future are not included in the list of existing IDs.

choices.text: Create the resource share in the IPAM home Region, add the pool, and specify the development OU as a principal.
choices.explanation: The share is managed in the home Region, and accounts in the OU can use the pool.

source.label: Amazon VPC IPAM — AWS RAMでIPAMプールを共有

learning.reason: Enable sharing within the organization and specify the development OU as a principal for the share in the IPAM home Region.
learning.concept: The IPAM home Region is where the pool is managed; the locale indicates the Region where the pool is used.

sourceLabel: Amazon VPC IPAM — Share an IPAM pool using AWS RAM

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Concurrent updates across Regions
prompt: Inventory reservations are accepted in Northern Virginia and Ohio. When the same reservation item is changed concurrently in both Regions, the application must be able to detect the conflict and reassess the reservation rather than lose a successful update to a last-writer-wins overwrite. A reservation is contained in a single item. Which design meets this requirement while allowing writes in the remaining Region during a Regional outage?

choices.text: Use MREC and apply a condition expression with the same version number in each Region.
choices.explanation: The condition can be met in both Regions before replication occurs.

choices.text: Use MREC and serialize writes in each Region with TransactWriteItems.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB transactions are atomic only within the caller's Region.

choices.text: Use MREC and reconcile changes after they reach another Region through DynamoDB Streams.
choices.explanation: Detection occurs after a write succeeds, so it cannot protect the reservation from a conflicting update.

choices.text: Use MRSC and place a witness in the same US Region set as the two write Regions. Reassess when a condition fails or a conflict occurs.
choices.explanation: Conditional updates use the latest state, and a quorum can be maintained during an outage in one Region.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — グローバルテーブルの仕組み

learning.reason: MRSC replicates synchronously and evaluates condition expressions against the latest version. If the same item is being updated in another Region, DynamoDB returns ReplicatedWriteConflictException, allowing the application to reassess the state.
learning.concept: With MREC, condition expressions are evaluated against the local item and cannot prevent a conflict with a write that succeeds in another Region before replication.

sourceLabel: Amazon DynamoDB — How global tables work

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Redundancy across Direct Connect devices and locations
prompt: The on-premises-to-VPC path to the exchange must use Direct Connect exclusively. With redundant equipment, you want traffic to continue over the remaining physical paths if either one AWS-side device fails or one Direct Connect location fails. For the 99.99% SLA target model with maximum resiliency, which physical connection requirements must the design meet? Select two.

choices.text: Establish at least two dedicated connections at each location, terminating them on different AWS devices.
choices.explanation: This prevents a device failure from affecting every connection at that location.

choices.text: Consolidate all connections at each location into a LAG on the same AWS-side device.
choices.explanation: A LAG shares the device, making it a single point of failure.

choices.text: Create multiple private VIFs on a single physical connection.
choices.explanation: Splitting VIFs does not change the shared physical connection or location.

choices.text: Have dedicated connections at two or more physically independent Direct Connect locations.
choices.explanation: If an entire location is unavailable, communication can continue through another location.

choices.text: Replace the second path with a Site-to-Site VPN over the internet.
choices.explanation: This adds physical path diversity but violates the requirement that all paths use Direct Connect.

source.label: AWS Direct Connect — Resiliency Toolkit

learning.reason: For maximum resiliency, establish at least two dedicated connections at each of two or more locations, and terminate them on different AWS devices within each location.
learning.concept: Treat ports, devices, fiber paths, and locations as separate failure domains. A LAG can aggregate bandwidth, but its connections terminate on the same AWS device. Check the published conditions for SLA coverage as well, including an Enterprise Support plan and the Availability Zone configuration of endpoints.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Failing over event publishing during a Regional outage
prompt: A SaaS order service publishes through EventBridge PutEvents, and processing rules trigger orders. The same processing rules are configured on two event buses in different Regions. The design must automatically switch the destination when a primary-Region outage is detected, after a one-time configuration change to the publishing application, without custom rerouting logic in the application. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Configure an EventBridge archive in each Region and replay the secondary Region's archive when an outage is detected.
choices.explanation: An archive is for reprocessing events that have already been received. It does not switch the publishing destination.

choices.text: Associate the primary and secondary buses with an EventBridge global endpoint and a Route 53 health check, and specify that endpoint's ID when publishing.
choices.explanation: The publisher can keep using the same endpoint ID; the destination Region switches according to the health check.

choices.text: Have the publisher store both bus ARNs and retry to the secondary bus if the primary Region returns an error.
choices.explanation: This can work, but it requires the publisher to operate custom routing and retry logic.

choices.text: Forward all orders from a rule on the primary bus to the secondary bus.
choices.explanation: This can forward events already accepted, but the ingress does not switch when the primary Region cannot accept PutEvents calls.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge global endpoints ユーザーガイド

learning.reason: An EventBridge global endpoint switches the destination Region for events based on a health check.
learning.concept: Design event publishing failover together with idempotency on the event-processing side.

sourceLabel: Amazon EventBridge global endpoints User Guide

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Validate Recovery Plan Permissions and Configuration in Advance
prompt: A regional failover for a payment service proceeds in order: promote the Aurora Global Database, scale out the standby EC2 Auto Scaling group, and switch DNS. The audit team wants to continuously assess the recovery plan's execution role, the recovery group's maximum capacity, and database engine compatibility without actually failing over production. Which approach is best for a new failover plan?

choices.text: Restore Aurora with an AWS Backup restore test and assume that Auto Scaling and DNS will also switch over successfully.
choices.explanation: Validating a restore from backup does not assess promotion of a live replica or the full failover procedure.

choices.text: Periodically monitor the external user path with Route 53 health checks and CloudWatch Synthetics.
choices.explanation: This monitors normal response behavior, but does not assess the recovery plan's role or recovery-side capacity.

choices.text: Define the failover steps in ARC Region switch and monitor the plan's automated evaluation results.
choices.explanation: It can continuously evaluate engine compatibility, capacity, IAM permissions, and other factors for each execution block without a production failover.

choices.text: Use AWS Resilience Hub evaluation results to validate the recovery plan's execution role without any additional configuration.
choices.explanation: It can be used to assess RTO/RPO and resilience, but does not validate execution permissions for individual Region switch blocks.

source.label: Amazon Application Recovery Controller — Region switchの計画評価

learning.reason: ARC Region switch continuously evaluates each execution block and its related IAM permissions, warning about configuration that could prevent the plan from running.
learning.concept: Distinguish monitoring externally observable service failures from evaluating whether a specific recovery procedure is ready to run.

sourceLabel: Amazon Application Recovery Controller — Region switch plan evaluation

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Separate Read Denials from Write Boundaries
prompt: An operations role's identity policy allows GetObject and PutObject on the same S3 object. The role's permissions boundary allows only GetObject. The bucket policy explicitly denies GetObject for that role and does not allow PutObject. No other policies affect the decision. Select TWO correct outcomes.

choices.text: If the boundary is removed, both GetObject and PutObject succeed.
choices.explanation: Removing the boundary does not remove the bucket policy's explicit denial of GetObject.

choices.text: GetObject succeeds because the boundary allows it.
choices.explanation: A boundary does not override a denial and does not itself grant resource access.

choices.text: PutObject is denied because it is not allowed by the boundary applied to the role.
choices.explanation: Under these conditions, the effective permissions are the intersection of the identity-based allow and the boundary.

choices.text: PutObject succeeds because the bucket policy does not explicitly deny it.
choices.explanation: The absence of an explicit denial does not help when the permissions boundary does not allow the operation.

choices.text: GetObject is denied because the bucket policy explicitly denies it.
choices.explanation: An applicable explicit denial takes precedence over allows from the boundary and identity policy.

source.label: AWS IAM — ポリシー評価ロジック

learning.reason: GetObject is subject to an applicable explicit denial. Although the identity policy allows PutObject, the boundary does not allow it, and no other policy grants it.
learning.concept: Distinguish the precedence of explicit denials from a boundary that limits identity-based permissions.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Delegating KMS Permissions for an Individual Job
prompt: You need to grant a temporary IAM role used by a contractor permission to decrypt ciphertext for a specific job with an existing symmetric KMS key. The operations role cannot modify the key's existing policy, but it is authorized to delegate permissions. The delegation must be explicitly revocable when the job completes, and a short delay for the settings to propagate is acceptable. Which method is best?

choices.text: Create a Decrypt grant for the contractor role conditioned on the encryption context for the job, and call RevokeGrant when the job ends.
choices.explanation: This delegates a specific operation temporarily without changing the existing key policy.

choices.text: Add Decrypt permission for the contractor role to the key policy used by all jobs, then remove it after each job.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the operational constraint that the key policy cannot be modified.

choices.text: Disable the KMS key itself when the job ends.
choices.explanation: This does not end only the temporary delegation; it also prevents other workloads using the same key from decrypting.

choices.text: Give the contractor's account an alias with the same name as the key.
choices.explanation: An alias alone does not grant permission to the original key or provide the same key material.

source.label: AWS KMS — グラント

learning.reason: Use a KMS grant to delegate only Decrypt on the target key, and constrain it to the job with an EncryptionContext. Revoke the grant explicitly when the job completes.
learning.concept: KMS grants do not expire automatically, and revocation takes time to propagate. Plan which principal creates the grant and which principal revokes it.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Audit Logs for Bedrock Inference
prompt: An audit requirement calls for storing the text and binary images sent to and received from the Converse operation at the Amazon Bedrock bedrock-runtime endpoint. An encrypted S3 bucket is available in the same Region and account. Which configuration can audit the payloads without modifying the API callers?

choices.text: Configure only CloudWatch Logs as the destination for model invocation logging.
choices.explanation: Small bodies and metadata can be captured, but S3 is needed to deliver binary images and large bodies.

choices.text: Forward Bedrock operational metrics from CloudWatch Metric Streams to S3 through Firehose.
choices.explanation: This transfers aggregated values such as invocation counts and latency; it does not record input and output content.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail data events for Converse to save request and response bodies.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail can audit API operations, but this approach does not capture complete inference bodies and binary data.

choices.text: Enable text and image logging for Bedrock model invocation logging and set the audit S3 bucket as the destination.
choices.explanation: This can record the content of the targeted modalities for Converse, and S3 can deliver large data and binary images.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock: model invocation logging

learning.reason: For supported Bedrock Runtime APIs, invocation logging records inputs and outputs. S3 delivery is needed for images and large bodies.
learning.concept: When recording bodies, distinguish this from ordinary API auditing and manage access to sensitive information in logs and its retention period.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Organization-Wide Cost Allocation Tags
prompt: In the product OU of an AWS Organization, CostCenter tags on resources must use the spelling and values in the finance department’s list.
