Limit enforcement to resource types that support it, and reject updates that include noncompliant values. For now, existing creation paths that omit the tag must remain allowed. Which configuration under the OU is most appropriate?

choices.text: Apply an SCP that requires the CostCenter request tag to be present for all resource creation.
choices.explanation: This would block all creation paths that omit the tag, which must remain allowed for now. The tag’s presence alone also does not validate its value.

choices.text: Apply an Organizations tag policy that defines the allowed values to the product OU, and enable enforcement for the applicable resource types.
choices.explanation: This blocks noncompliant tag operations on the applicable resource types. It does not block every creation that omits the tag.

choices.text: Configure the allowed tag values in Cost Categories.
choices.explanation: Cost Categories can classify billing data, but they do not reject resource tag updates.

choices.text: Configure an allowed-value list in an AWS Config required-tags rule and remediate weekly.
choices.explanation: This can detect and remediate noncompliance after the fact, but it does not meet the requirement to reject tag values during an update.

source.label: AWS Organizations: タグポリシー

learning.reason: Enabling enforcement for the applicable resource types in a tag policy can reject noncompliant settings for the specified tag.
learning.concept: Design compliance for existing tags separately from requirements that the tag be present. Check behavior for resources without the tag and for unsupported resource types.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Resume by Resending Only the Parts Not Yet Uploaded After a Network Interruption
prompt: A production site must upload a 100 GiB video as a single S3 object. It must not resend parts that S3 accepted before a network interruption. Another worker may take over when the upload resumes, and the object must not be exposed to users while it is being transferred. Which implementation meets these requirements?

choices.text: Enable Transfer Acceleration and resume a single PutObject from the byte offset where it stopped.
choices.explanation: This can optimize the transfer path, but PutObject cannot resume from an offset, and 100 GiB exceeds the single-PUT size limit.

choices.text: Start an S3 multipart upload and share the upload ID, part numbers, and ETags. Send the completion request after all parts succeed.
choices.explanation: Workers can take over the same upload, retain successfully uploaded parts, and complete them as one object.

choices.text: Publish each part as a separate object in sequence and return all the keys in a manifest.
choices.explanation: This allows retries at the part level, but users would receive multiple S3 objects rather than one.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning and use Range to PutObject only the unsent range of the same object.
choices.explanation: Range is available for retrieving part of an existing object, but a regular PutObject cannot append a partial upload.

source.label: Amazon S3 — マルチパートアップロード

learning.reason: Recording the multipart upload ID, part numbers, and ETags lets another worker upload the remaining parts and then complete a single object.
learning.concept: Design the retry unit, completion process, and cost management with AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload when an upload is canceled.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Ensure Performance Immediately After Restore in an Alternate AZ
prompt: A media processing service starts workers in a standby AZ during an outage. It creates a processing volume from a regional EBS snapshot containing 300 GiB of shared data. In the alternate AZ, the service must be able to access all ranges randomly at normal performance within 30 seconds of startup, and it cannot keep a volume provisioned in the alternate AZ at all times. The capacity and performance are within the supported range for Fast Snapshot Restore. What should it do?

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore for the snapshot in the standby AZ in the account that will create the volume, and verify the create credits.
choices.explanation: This allows an initialized volume to be created in the target AZ. Keep the number of volumes created within the available credits.

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore only in the existing active AZ and reference the same snapshot from the standby AZ.
choices.explanation: Even within the same Region, FSR settings do not carry over to another AZ.

choices.text: Set the initialization rate to 300 MiB/s when creating the volume.
choices.explanation: Initializing all 300 GiB of snapshot data would take longer than 30 seconds.

choices.text: Increase gp3 IOPS and throughput, then initialize all blocks in the background after startup.
choices.explanation: Disk settings can increase normal I/O, but they do not guarantee that all blocks will be initialized within 30 seconds.

source.label: Amazon EBS — Fast Snapshot Restore

learning.reason: Preconfigure Fast Snapshot Restore for the combination of the snapshot and standby AZ in the account that will create the volume. Reserve the necessary create credits, and do not specify an initialization rate at creation.
learning.concept: FSR applies to a snapshot and AZ combination. An explicitly specified initialization rate takes precedence over FSR, and initialization time depends on the amount of snapshot data.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Resume from the Failure Point Using the Previous Definition
prompt: A Standard Workflow for order review failed two days ago because of a temporary outage in an external credit check. Before the failure, it had created a payment reservation, which must not be created again. The execution history has 500 events. The current production alias has switched to unapproved new logic, so this retry must use the original definition. Which operation meets these requirements?

choices.text: Pass the original input to the current production alias and start a new execution.
choices.explanation: The new definition would be associated with the execution, which would start from the first step.

choices.text: Start a new execution using the version ARN used at the time of failure.
choices.explanation: This lets you select the original definition, but a new execution starts from the first step.

choices.text: Redrive the failed execution by specifying its execution ARN.
choices.explanation: This resumes from the failure point using the original execution definition and does not rerun the payment reservation that already succeeded.

choices.text: Add Retry to the state machine, publish a new version, and apply it to the failed execution.
choices.explanation: A definition change does not apply to an execution that has already ended.

source.label: AWS Step Functions — 失敗した実行の再開

learning.reason: Redriving an eligible Standard Workflow execution uses its original input, definition, and execution ARN, preserves successful steps, and resumes at the failure point.
learning.concept: To determine whether Redrive applies, check the failure time, number of execution history events, and execution type. Starting an execution with a changed definition requires a new execution.

sourceLabel: AWS Step Functions — Redriving Failed Executions

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Delegate launch permissions by product
prompt: A finance team uses a shared Service Catalog portfolio to let each department launch an approved monitoring product in its own account. Developers can launch the product but cannot directly call CloudFormation or monitoring-resource creation APIs. Which configuration uses a dedicated role with the same name in each account without extending permissions to other products in the portfolio?

choices.text: Add permissions to create resources through CloudFormation and the target APIs to the portfolio user role.
choices.explanation: This allows the product to launch, but the same users can call the APIs directly without going through the product.

choices.text: Associate an IAM role ARN from the central management account with the entire portfolio.
choices.explanation: Launch constraints apply to a product and portfolio pair, so a role shared by all products does not provide the requested isolation.

choices.text: Set only a template constraint on the product to narrow the available parameter values.
choices.explanation: This controls parameters but does not configure the role assumed by the service at launch.

choices.text: Set a launch constraint on the target product and portfolio pair, specifying the same-named role in each account by its local name.
choices.explanation: At launch, Service Catalog uses the dedicated permissions, without granting users the usual resource-creation permissions.

source.label: AWS Service Catalog — 起動制約

learning.reason: Attach a launch constraint using the local role name to the product and portfolio pair. Service Catalog assumes the role in the target account, while users receive permissions to operate the product.
learning.concept: Distinguish portfolio access from the role that creates resources at launch. The local role name must match on both the constraint-creating and launch sides.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Start EC2 instances at each branch's local time
prompt: Development environments in the United States and Europe must start at 8:30 a.m. on weekdays and stop at 7 p.m., according to each location's local time. There are multiple IANA time zones, and the process of manually converting for daylight saving time to UTC is being retired. Apply the same operations to stopped EC2 instances, without keeping custom schedule-evaluation code running. Which design meets the requirements?

choices.text: Convert each branch's standard local time to UTC once and use an EventBridge scheduled rule.
choices.explanation: Because UTC is fixed, the local start time will shift after a daylight-saving transition.

choices.text: Specify start and stop cron expressions and an IANA time zone in EventBridge Scheduler, with the EC2 API as the target.
choices.explanation: This supports each branch's local time and daylight-saving changes, and the service can operate on stopped EC2 instances.

choices.text: Create a 24-hour rate schedule in EventBridge Scheduler and align only the first invocation to 8:30 a.m. local time.
choices.explanation: A 24-hour rate represents a fixed elapsed interval, so local time shifts around daylight-saving transitions and weekdays cannot be controlled.

choices.text: Configure local-time cron jobs on the EC2 instances for starting and stopping them.
choices.explanation: A stopped instance cannot run its own cron jobs, so it cannot start again this way.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler — スケジュール種別

learning.reason: Specify each branch's IANA time zone in the EventBridge Scheduler cron expressions, and use a least-privilege execution role to call the EC2 start and stop APIs.
learning.concept: Represent recurring fixed-time schedules with time-zone-aware cron expressions, distinguishing them from rate expressions that represent fixed intervals.

category: コスト最適化
title: Keep discounts active through a database migration
prompt: A payment company currently uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL in Ireland and plans to migrate to Aurora Serverless v2 in Ohio in four months. The hourly floor of eligible database usage spend will remain stable before and after the migration. The company wants to discount that stable usage with the same commitment before the migration and avoid upfront payment. Which purchase approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Purchase one year of RDS Reserved DB Instances in Ireland and transfer the reservation to Aurora Serverless v2 in Ohio after the migration.
choices.explanation: RDS Reserved DB Instance discounts depend on eligible attributes and cannot be transferred in this way to Aurora Serverless v2 in another Region.

choices.text: Purchase Compute Savings Plans for the stable spend and apply them to database compute usage at the source and destination.
choices.explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply to eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage; they do not discount usage from either database.

choices.text: Reserve Aurora provisioned DB instances in Ohio and apply the reservation to RDS in Ireland and ACU usage at the destination.
choices.explanation: A reservation for provisioned instances in Ohio cannot cover usage in Ireland or Serverless v2 ACU usage.

choices.text: Purchase a one-year Database Savings Plan sized to the stable hourly spend for eligible database usage, and pay on demand for usage above that amount.
choices.explanation: The same commitment can apply to eligible RDS and Aurora Serverless v2 usage before and after the migration, with no upfront payment.

source.label: AWS Database Savings Plans — 対象と料金

learning.reason: Set the one-year hourly commitment for a Database Savings Plan to the floor of eligible usage spend shared by both environments. The discount applies even as the eligible database service, Region, and deployment method change.
learning.concept: Before purchasing a commitment, check the hourly eligible spend. Usage above it is charged on demand, and unused commitment still incurs cost.

sourceLabel: AWS Database Savings Plans — Eligibility and pricing

category: コスト最適化
title: Separate routine database growth from bulk-migration capacity
prompt: The current RDS for PostgreSQL instance uses gp3 storage. Data normally grows gradually, but next month's bulk migration will ingest, in a short time, far more data than the currently available free space. The goal is to limit advance capacity allocation that is normally unnecessary while avoiding insufficient capacity during the bulk migration. Assuming the DB instance will remain in use, select two measures to take.

choices.text: Keep the allocated storage unchanged until just before the bulk migration, and start the migration assuming that storage autoscaling will keep up through multiple consecutive increases.
choices.explanation: Optimization after a previous change and limits on change frequency mean there is no guarantee that autoscaling will keep pace with the ingestion rate.

choices.text: Configure storage autoscaling with a maximum for routine growth, and monitor FreeStorageSpace.
choices.explanation: Autoscaling can handle growth within the expected range, while monitoring can detect low capacity or an approaching limit.

choices.text: Estimate the migration's data growth and working space, then increase allocated storage to the required capacity before starting.
choices.explanation: This avoids depending on autoscaling response time or whether consecutive changes are allowed for the rapid increase.

choices.text: Lower the maximum capacity so that the allocated storage of the same DB instance automatically shrinks after the migration.
choices.explanation: Lowering the maximum does not shrink storage that has already been allocated.

choices.text: Increase gp3 IOPS only during the bulk migration, without changing allocated storage.
choices.explanation: This may improve ingestion performance, but it does not increase the amount of data that can be stored.

source.label: Amazon RDS — ストレージの自動スケーリング

learning.reason: Use autoscaling with a limit and monitoring for routine growth. For the rapid increase during the bulk migration, estimate and allocate the required capacity before starting.
learning.concept: RDS storage autoscaling responds to low free space and has constraints between increases; it cannot reduce already allocated storage.

category: コスト最適化
title: Reduce Higher I/O Charges Without Changing the Configuration
prompt: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster has a steady, high volume of reads and writes. Keep the application, instance count, and capacity unchanged. A one-month estimate for comparison is as follows: with Standard, instances cost 1,600, storage 400, and I/O 1,100; with I/O-Optimized, instances cost 2,000, storage 480, and I/O 0. The units are the same, and all other costs remain unchanged. The current engine supports both configurations. What should you do if this workload continues?

choices.text: Keep Standard. The total for instances and storage, 2,000, is less than the 2,480 for I/O-Optimized.
choices.explanation: This leaves out Standard's I/O cost of 1,100.

choices.text: Change the cluster's storage configuration to I/O-Optimized. This reduces the current monthly total, including I/O, from 3,100 to 2,480.
choices.explanation: This meets the requirement based on a comparison of the same workload that includes instances, storage, and I/O.

choices.text: Keep the writer on Standard and change only the read replicas' storage configuration to I/O-Optimized.
choices.explanation: The storage configuration is set for the Aurora cluster as a whole.

choices.text: Even after changing to I/O-Optimized, the monthly cost will be 3,580 because the 1,100 charge for read and write I/O will still apply.
choices.explanation: I/O-Optimized does not add per-use charges for the cluster's read and write I/O.

source.label: Amazon Aurora — クラスターのストレージ構成

learning.reason: For the same workload, the monthly cost is 3,100 with Standard and 2,480 with I/O-Optimized. The latter is 620 less, even with its higher instance and storage costs.
learning.concept: When comparing Aurora pricing models, compare the total cost for the same workload, including cluster usage, storage, and read and write I/O.

category: コスト最適化
title: Receive Orders Promptly and Reduce Empty Requests
prompt: A retailer uses always-on workers to poll a single Standard queue. Orders arrive infrequently, and repeated empty ReceiveMessage calls are the main source of charges. The retailer wants to retrieve an order promptly when it arrives. The workers and queue must remain in place, and no fixed delay may be added between arrival and processing. The HTTP client's response timeout can be changed. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Set ReceiveMessage's WaitTimeSeconds to 20 seconds and set the HTTP response timeout to more than 20 seconds.
choices.explanation: When no message is available, the server waits and returns when one becomes available, reducing empty API calls.

choices.text: Keep short polling and pause the worker for 20 seconds after each empty receive response.
choices.explanation: This reduces the number of calls, but an order that arrives during the pause must wait until the next poll.

choices.text: Set ReceiveMessage's WaitTimeSeconds to 20 seconds and keep the existing 5-second HTTP response timeout.
choices.explanation: The client will time out first while the request is waiting, increasing errors and retries.

choices.text: Set the queue's Visibility Timeout to 20 seconds and call ReceiveMessage without waiting.
choices.explanation: Visibility timeout applies to messages that have been received, so it does not change how often empty responses occur.

source.label: Amazon SQS — ロングポーリングの設定

learning.reason: Use long polling with ReceiveMessage and set the HTTP timeout longer than the wait time. If a message is available, the request does not need to wait for the full limit.
learning.concept: The time to wait in a receive API call, the period for which a received message is hidden from other workers, and the time a queue delays delivery serve different purposes.

category: コスト最適化
title: Retain Images Tagged for Both Production and Development
prompt: In a single ECR repository, the same image digest may have tags that both start with prod- and ci-. Retain images with a prod- tag for 60 days after they are pushed, and make images with only a ci- tag eligible for deletion after 7 days from push. Use an ECR lifecycle policy without retagging images or adding scheduled code. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Set priority 1 for ci- at 7 days and priority 2 for prod- at 60 days.
choices.explanation: The rule with the lower priority number is applied first and could delete older images with both tags after 7 days.

choices.text: Configure both the prod- and ci- tag patterns in one rule and delete images 7 days after they are pushed.
choices.explanation: Multiple patterns in one rule select images that match all of them, which would include production images carrying both tags.

choices.text: Set priority 1 for prod- at 60 days and priority 2 for ci- at 7 days, using days since the images were pushed.
choices.explanation: An image that matches the higher-priority rule for its prod- tag is not deleted by the lower-priority ci- rule.

choices.text: Combine the rules and archive an image 7 days after the last time an image with a ci- tag was pulled.
choices.explanation: This is not the same as deleting an image 7 days after push, and it does not protect an image that also has a production tag.

source.label: Amazon ECR — ライフサイクルポリシーの例

learning.reason: Give the production tag rule higher priority. A lower-priority ci- rule cannot delete an image that matches both rules first.
learning.concept: ECR lifecycle rules act at the image level in priority order. When retaining deployment digests, inspect images with multiple tags in the preview.

category: コスト最適化
title: Allocate Shared EKS Node Costs by Pod Usage
prompt: Multiple departments in an organization share the EC2 nodes in one EKS cluster. Finance wants to use Pod CPU and memory resource requests as the allocation basis and process the billing line items exported to Amazon S3 with its existing Athena analysis. There is no budget to add dedicated nodes for departments and no staff to maintain allocation calculations. Select two AWS-side settings that are required.

choices.text: In the management account's Cost Management settings, enable split cost allocation data for Amazon EKS and select resource requests.
choices.explanation: This is a prerequisite for obtaining EKS workload details and AWS-managed allocation line items, and it lets you use CPU and memory as the basis.

choices.text: Activate department tags on EC2 nodes and group by Pod name in Cost Explorer.
choices.explanation: Node tags cannot distinguish Pods on the same node, and split cost allocation data is not available in Cost Explorer.

choices.text: Use Cost Categories to allocate node charges to departments at fixed proportions.
choices.explanation: Fixed proportions cannot use Pod resource requests that vary over time as the allocation basis.

choices.text: In CUR 2.0 Data Exports, enable split cost allocation data and resource IDs.
choices.explanation: This adds Pod-level split line items to the S3 export and lets the Athena processing identify resources.

choices.text: Enable only ECS split cost allocation data and leave the existing report's line items unchanged.
choices.explanation: Opting in for ECS does not apply to EKS, and allocation data must also be enabled in the export.

source.label: AWS Data Exports — 配分データの有効化

learning.reason: Opt in to EKS allocation data in Cost Management billing settings, then enable allocation data and resource IDs in the CUR 2.0 export.
learning.concept: Allocating costs among Pods that share nodes requires workload-level allocation line items rather than aggregated account or node tags.

sourceLabel: AWS Data Exports — Enabling Allocation Data

category: コスト最適化
title: Separate Daily Backups from Monthly Long-Term Retention
prompt: A company protects Amazon EBS volumes with AWS Backup. Daily recovery points from the most recent 30 days must be restorable quickly. Monthly recovery points must be retained for one year; after 30 days, restoration may take longer. Choose a configuration that reduces storage costs while preserving fast recovery for daily recovery points.

choices.text: Use the same rule for all daily and monthly recovery points, and move them to EBS archive the day after creation.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the recovery-time requirement for daily recovery points and is not suitable for the daily frequency.

choices.text: Keep daily recovery points warm for 30 days. Enable EBS archive in the monthly rule, move those points after 30 days, and delete them after one year.
choices.explanation: This preserves daily recovery times and keeps monthly recovery points in cold storage for at least 90 days, reducing long-term storage costs.

choices.text: Move monthly recovery points to cold storage after 30 days and delete them on day 60.
choices.explanation: This provides only 30 days in cold storage and does not meet the minimum cold-storage period or the one-year retention requirement.

choices.text: Copy monthly snapshots to S3 and use that bucket's S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition them to Glacier.
choices.explanation: EBS recovery points cannot be made restorable through AWS Backup by moving them to an arbitrary S3 bucket.

source.label: AWS Backup — バックアップルールとコールド保管

learning.reason: Keep the daily rule in warm storage and opt in to the supported EBS archive tier only for the monthly rule. Archive monthly recovery points after 30 warm days and retain them until the one-year retention deadline.
learning.concept: With EBS archive, a recovery point becomes a full snapshot and must remain in cold storage for at least 90 days. Consider daily and monthly frequencies separately in terms of recovery time and the cost of converting to full snapshots.

sourceLabel: AWS Backup — Backup Rules and Cold Storage

category: コスト最適化
title: Compare CPU Processing Speed and Execution Cost
prompt: After tuning memory for a Lambda image-conversion function, the average billable duration and p95 latency were 1.8 seconds and 2.1 seconds at 512 MB, 0.7 seconds and 0.9 seconds at 1,024 MB, 0.45 seconds and 0.6 seconds at 2,048 MB, and 0.3 seconds and 0.45 seconds at 4,096 MB. With the same architecture, equal request charges, and no cache or provisioned concurrency, which memory setting meets a p95 target of at most 1 second while minimizing average execution cost?

choices.text: Choose 512 MB.
choices.explanation: The average is 0.9 GB-seconds, and the 2.1-second p95 latency also misses the requirement.

choices.text: Choose 2,048 MB.
choices.explanation: The p95 meets the requirement, but 0.9 GB-seconds exceeds the 0.7 GB-seconds at 1,024 MB.

choices.text: Choose 1,024 MB.
choices.explanation: Its 0.9-second p95 meets the requirement, and its 0.7 GB-seconds is the lowest among the qualifying settings.

choices.text: Choose 4,096 MB.
choices.explanation: It responds fastest, but the product of memory and average duration is 1.2 GB-seconds.

source.label: AWS Lambda — 関数メモリの設定

learning.reason: The per-invocation GB-seconds for the three settings that meet the requirement are 0.7 at 1,024 MB, 0.9 at 2,048 MB, and 1.2 at 4,096 MB. The 1,024 MB setting is the lowest.
learning.concept: Lambda allocates more CPU as memory increases. More memory is not always cheaper; measure billed duration and request latency with the same input before deciding.

category: コスト最適化
title: Store Older Indexes at Lower Cost While Keeping Them Searchable
prompt: An operations company manages daily log indexes in OpenSearch Service. It continues writing to the current day's index, but indexes older than 7 days are immutable. The company must be able to search them for up to 120 days from its existing Dashboards without a restore operation. Supported instance types and dedicated master nodes are already configured, and added latency for searches of older data is acceptable. Which index lifecycle lowers costs?

choices.text: Keep only the current day's data in hot storage, and move indexes to cold storage after 7 days.
choices.explanation: Searching from cold storage first requires reconnecting the data to UltraWarm, which does not meet the requirement to search without a restore-like operation.

choices.text: Use hot storage for up to 7 days, then use Index State Management to move indexes to UltraWarm for searches through day 120.
choices.explanation: This separates indexes that are still being updated from read-only indexes while keeping them searchable from existing dashboards.

choices.text: Manually snapshot indexes after 7 days to S3 and delete them from the active domain.
choices.explanation: This can reduce storage costs, but a snapshot cannot be searched directly as an OpenSearch index.

choices.text: Move all indexes being ingested to UltraWarm and move only old indexes back to hot storage.
choices.explanation: UltraWarm indexes are read-only, so writes cannot continue to an index there.

source.label: Amazon OpenSearch Service — UltraWarmストレージ

learning.reason: Keep indexes that are still being written in hot storage, and move older read-only indexes to UltraWarm. UltraWarm indexes can be searched without restoring them.
learning.concept: When choosing an OpenSearch storage tier, consider separately whether individual documents can be updated, how quickly data must be searchable, and how long it must be retained.

category: コスト最適化
title: Estimate MSK Serverless Fixed Charges from Operating Hours
prompt: A company is evaluating a migration for a Kafka pipeline with irregular traffic. The required IAM authentication and throughput are supported by MSK Serverless. The estimate covers 720 operating hours in a month, with 40 partitions consistently present while the cluster is running. Costs for writes, reads, storage, and inter-Region transfer are estimated separately. How should the remaining fixed monthly charges be calculated?

choices.text: Multiply 720 cluster-hours and 28,800 partition-hours by their respective rates, then add the results.
choices.explanation: With Serverless, both the cluster and its existing partitions are subject to hourly charges.

choices.text: Calculate only the 720 hours for the running cluster. Partition costs are included in data input and output.
choices.explanation: Partitions are billed by time as a separate item from data transfer.

choices.text: Count the 40 partitions once, and assume the cluster is fully exempt from charges while idle.
choices.explanation: Partitions are billed by time, not by creation count, and maintaining a cluster incurs costs even when it is idle.

choices.text: Calculate only the 28,800 partition-hours, since cluster charges are included in the data storage rate.
choices.explanation: Cluster-hours are billed separately from storage.

source.label: Amazon MSK — Serverlessの料金項目

learning.reason: One cluster running for 720 hours contributes 720 cluster-hours. Forty partitions present for 720 hours each contribute 28,800 partition-hours; apply the respective rates to each.
learning.concept: Idle-time billing units differ among serverless products. Keep traffic-dependent charges separate from charges based on how long resources are maintained.

category: コスト最適化
title: Tiering a Cache with Mostly Infrequent Access
prompt: In node-based ElastiCache for Valkey 7.2, 90% of values are rarely read. Keep frequently read values at low latency, and retain the remaining values so they can still be retrieved with the same Valkey commands. Keys are much smaller than values, and a slight delay for infrequently accessed data is acceptable. Writes can be paused while a new cluster is launched from a backup. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Lower the memory limit of the existing cache and use allkeys-lru to evict infrequently accessed keys.
choices.explanation: This reduces memory use, but it does not meet the requirement to retain infrequently accessed values and retrieve them later by the same keys.

choices.text: Move to ElastiCache Serverless and explicitly assign some values to local SSD storage.
choices.explanation: Serverless does not let you specify node data tiering.

choices.text: Change only the node type of the existing non-tiered cluster in place to r7gd.
choices.explanation: Scaling an existing cluster across the disabled-to-enabled data-tiering boundary is not supported.

choices.text: Restore the backup to a new Valkey replication group that uses a supported node type, then switch clients when writes resume.
choices.explanation: Data tiering is available, moving infrequently used values to SSD while keeping them accessible through existing commands.

source.label: Amazon ElastiCache — データ階層化

learning.reason: Restore the existing non-tiered backup to a new replication group using a tiering-enabled node type. Distribute values between memory and local SSD while keeping keys in memory.
learning.concept: When moving to data tiering, check whether you can migrate by scaling the existing group or whether you need to restore from a backup.

category: コスト最適化
title: Evaluate Tiering for Small Audit Objects
prompt: Tens of millions of 8 KiB audit events are stored in an S3 general purpose bucket. A new lifecycle rule is intended to transition them to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days and retain them for seven years, but testing shows that the objects have not transitioned. Preserve event-level retrieval, and apply the change only if cost savings are confirmed. Which two items should you verify or address?

choices.text: Use a rule that targets only a prefix, since that removes the size minimum for a new configuration.
choices.explanation: A prefix filter does not override the default object-size behavior.

choices.text: Explicitly include a size filter in the lifecycle rule that covers the target events.
choices.explanation: This can make 8 KiB objects, which are excluded by default in a new configuration, eligible for transition.

choices.text: Combine the events into one archive object, delete the original files, and assume each record can still be retrieved individually by its former object key.
choices.explanation: With this design, events can no longer be retrieved by the same object keys.

choices.text: Compare measured samples and class pricing, including transition requests, per-object additional metadata, and retrieval costs.
choices.explanation: A comparison based only on the 8 KiB payload overlooks additional costs that scale with the number of objects.

choices.text: Enable versioning, which makes small objects eligible for transition under the standard settings.
choices.explanation: Enabling versioning alone does not remove the size restriction for a new lifecycle configuration.

source.label: Amazon S3 — ライフサイクル移行の考慮事項

learning.reason: An explicit size filter can override the default 128 KB minimum for small objects. Compare total costs between classes, including transition requests and additional metadata for each object.
learning.concept: The storage-rate savings that apply to large objects can be offset by per-object costs for small objects.

category: コスト最適化
title: Avoiding Idle Inference Compute Charges for Intermittent Requests
prompt: An internal inventory application uses a small CPU model in SageMaker AI for inference. Each request has an input of no more than 2 MB, inference takes a few seconds, and users need the prediction in the same HTTP response. The application often has no traffic for several hours, and cold starts are acceptable. GPU, dedicated placement in a VPC, and data capture are not required. Which approach avoids charges for inference compute resources while idle?

choices.text: Run batch transform jobs on a schedule and wait for the next job to finish for each new prediction.
choices.explanation: Compute can run only when needed, but this does not preserve a synchronous response for each input.

choices.text: Scale Asynchronous Inference to zero and have the current application treat the response body as the prediction.
choices.explanation: This can avoid idle costs, but asynchronous results are not returned as a direct synchronous response body.

choices.text: Use Serverless Inference without provisioned concurrency.
choices.explanation: It supports synchronous responses within the stated input and runtime limits, without ongoing charges for instances that are not running.

choices.text: Keep a real-time endpoint running with at least one instance.
choices.explanation: It supports synchronous responses, but incurs the cost of one instance even when there is no traffic.

source.label: Amazon SageMaker AI — 推論方式の選択

learning.reason: Intermittent traffic that needs synchronous responses within the size and duration limits fits Serverless Inference without provisioned concurrency.
learning.concept: Defining input size, synchronous response needs, cold-start tolerance, and network or monitoring constraints first makes inference options easier to compare.

sourceLabel: Amazon SageMaker AI — Choosing an inference option

category: コスト最適化
title: Independently Limiting Peak Compute Capacity and Monthly Usage
prompt: An analyst Redshift Serverless workgroup has a base capacity of 64 RPU and scales compute capacity as demand increases. Finance requires that capacity never exceed 256 RPU and that user queries stop for the rest of the month after usage reaches 800 RPU-hours. The same limits should not apply to other workgroups. Which two settings are required for this workgroup?

choices.text: Set the workgroup's Max capacity to 256 RPU.
choices.explanation: This sets the upper bound on the compute capacity that autoscaling can use at a given time.

choices.text: Set only the workgroup's Base capacity to 256 RPU.
choices.explanation: Setting the initial capacity does not cap autoscaling.

choices.text: Set Maximum RPU hours to 800 for the month and disable user queries when the limit is reached.
choices.explanation: This can stop queries according to the cumulative monthly limit for this workgroup only.

choices.text: Set Maximum RPU hours to 800 for the month and send only a notification when the limit is reached.
choices.explanation: This provides notice of the limit but does not stop user queries.

choices.text: Limit cross-Region data sharing to 800 GB.
choices.explanation: A data-sharing limit does not constrain overall query compute time or peak capacity.

source.label: Amazon Redshift — 計算容量と使用量の上限

learning.reason: Set Max capacity to 256 RPU and the monthly maximum RPU hours to 800, with user queries disabled when the limit is reached.
learning.concept: RPU measures compute capacity at a point in time; RPU-hours measure cumulative usage over a period. Limiting the former does not prevent the latter from growing with processing duration.

sourceLabel: Amazon Redshift — Compute capacity and usage limits

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Preserve Tenant-Scoped SQL and Foreign Keys
prompt: The billing service uses Aurora PostgreSQL to write each tenant's Invoice and InvoiceLine records in the same transaction. The primary keys of both tables and the foreign key from InvoiceLine to Invoice include tenant_id. Write volume is distributed across tenants, but the overall workload has reached the limit of a single writer. Choose a configuration that preserves the current foreign keys without implementing destination routing in the application.

choices.text: Shard Invoice by tenant_id and InvoiceLine by product ID, distributing each table independently.
choices.explanation: The parent and child are not colocated by the same key, so this does not meet the assumptions for foreign keys between existing sharded tables.

choices.text: Use Limitless Database to shard both tables by tenant_id and colocate them, then add the foreign key after conversion.
choices.explanation: The target rows and related rows reside on the same shard, preserving tenant-scoped SQL and foreign keys.

choices.text: Add Aurora Replicas to the existing cluster and distribute application writes to the reader endpoint.
choices.explanation: Ordinary Aurora Replicas do not act as write shards and cannot increase the writer's write capacity.

choices.text: Assign each tenant to a separate cluster and have one RDS Proxy choose the destination from tenant_id.
choices.explanation: RDS Proxy does not parse SQL to route tenants across multiple DB clusters.

source.label: Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless — 外部キーの制約

learning.reason: With Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless Database, the relevant referential constraint can be preserved when the foreign key includes the shard key and the parent and child tables are colocated using the same key.
learning.concept: Check how the shard key affects uniqueness, foreign keys, and joins. A tenant's primary write tables serve a different purpose from small, read-oriented reference tables.

sourceLabel: Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless — Foreign Key Limitations

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Publish Releases So Old and New Assets Remain Available Immediately
prompt: An educational site serves many images and CSS files through CloudFront. Browsers and corporate proxies also cache the files for 24 hours. Users who receive an update must fetch the new assets, while users still on the old release must continue using the old assets. It must also be possible to roll back to the immediately preceding release, and the distribution manifest is revalidated on every request. Which publishing approach should be used?

choices.text: Overwrite files at the same paths and invalidate the corresponding CloudFront objects each time.
choices.explanation: Even if the edge fetches the new content, invalidation does not clear same-path content already cached in browsers or proxies.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning and overwrite the same paths, with clients always requesting the original URLs.
choices.explanation: The origin retains previous versions, but clients use the same cache key and reference.

choices.text: Set only CloudFront's maximum TTL to zero for each release and overwrite the same paths.
choices.explanation: This cannot immediately replace same-URL caches already distributed downstream and does not suit parallel use of old and new releases.

choices.text: Place new files under versioned paths and update the manifest after validation. Retain the old files for rollback.
choices.explanation: The new and old URLs have different cache keys, allowing the reference to switch without disrupting users of the current release.

source.label: Amazon CloudFront — 無効化とバージョン付きファイル名

learning.reason: Keep versions side by side and switch only the version referenced by the manifest. Because the paths differ, users can receive the appropriate version even while intermediate caches still contain older responses.
learning.concept: CDN edge invalidations do not reach browser or corporate-proxy caches. Separate the lifetimes of long-lived assets and a small manifest that switches their references.

sourceLabel: Amazon CloudFront — Invalidations and Versioned File Names

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Resolve Offline Edit Conflicts by Field Type
prompt: An AWS AppSync API for inspectors uses a versioned DynamoDB data source. When an offline device returns an older version, the single approval status updated on the server while the device was editing must take precedence. Classification tags are stored as a DynamoDB String Set, and tags added by the device must be incorporated without duplicates. Arbitrary timestamp comparisons or custom merge code are not required. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Set conflict resolution to AUTOMERGE and keep classification tags as a DynamoDB Set.
choices.explanation: The scalar retains the server value, and the set is merged without duplicates.

choices.text: Set OPTIMISTIC_CONCURRENCY and do not retry or merge on the client.
choices.explanation: Changes from an older version are rejected, so tag additions are not incorporated either.

choices.text: Set AUTOMERGE and change the stored representation of classification tags to a DynamoDB List.
choices.explanation: A list appends values, so duplicate tags can remain.

choices.text: Disable conflict detection and replace all fields whenever the device's last-update timestamp is later.
choices.explanation: This may discard the server's approval status and tag additions from another device.

source.label: AWS AppSync — 競合検出と解決

learning.reason: Use VERSION-based conflict detection with AUTOMERGE. For a conflicting scalar, the server value is retained; for a DynamoDB Set, the values are merged as a union.
learning.concept: Although both may appear as GraphQL lists, a data-source List appends values, whereas a Set produces a deduplicated union.

sourceLabel: AWS AppSync — Conflict Detection and Resolution

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Querying Regular Partitions Without Registering Them in Advance
prompt: Every site writes log files each day to an S3 prefix with a predictable Region and date. Very few prefixes are missing, and queries are run only through Athena SQL. You want to keep the Glue Data Catalog table while avoiding daily partition additions and GetPartitions calls when queries start. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a Glue crawler to add new partitions every day, then prune partitions with date predicates.
choices.explanation: This narrows the data read, but it does not meet the requirement to avoid daily registration and GetPartitions.

choices.text: Create a Glue partition index and leave the partition registration process unchanged.
choices.explanation: This can make metadata lookups more efficient, but it does not eliminate partition registration.

choices.text: Configure date and Region projection and an S3 path template on the table.
choices.explanation: Athena can calculate candidate partitions at query time and avoid looking up individual Glue partitions.

choices.text: Load S3 Inventory into Glue to create an audit listing table, and do not register partitions in the original table.
choices.explanation: This provides an object listing, but it does not configure Athena to calculate the target partitions when querying the original log table.

source.label: Amazon Athena — パーティションプロジェクション

learning.reason: Configure the date range, Region values, and prefix template on the table so Athena can calculate candidates using partition projection.
learning.concept: Partition projection is used when Athena plans SQL queries. If many partitions are empty or other analytics engines also read the data, consider registered partitions.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Recomputing Corrected Aggregates Without Mixing Them Into Production Output
prompt: A Glue Spark job processes an append-only S3 input using job bookmarks and appends Parquet files to a production output location. Three runs contained a calculation error. You want to rerun that period with corrected logic and write validation output under a separate prefix. Keep the bookmark currently used by the scheduled job unchanged and retain the existing Parquet files. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Reset the current bookmark and let the scheduled job append directly to the production output location as usual.
choices.explanation: This loses the current processing position and mixes the recomputed output into production.

choices.text: Replay the data with bookmark Pause, specifying the runs before and after the target runs, and write to a validation prefix.
choices.explanation: This lets you specify run boundaries without updating the current state and keeps output validation independent.

choices.text: Rewind the bookmark, reuse the production output, and assume Glue will delete the files written before the update.
choices.explanation: This changes the processing position, and Glue bookmarks do not manage existing output files.

choices.text: Enable S3 versioning on the input bucket and configure the bookmark to restore each output file to a previous version.
choices.explanation: S3 versioning does not roll back job input state and the output set as a coordinated operation.

source.label: AWS Glue — ジョブブックマークと再処理

learning.reason: Use bookmark Pause mode to specify the target run boundaries and write validation output to a new prefix. Pause mode does not advance the bookmark.
learning.concept: Job bookmarks record input state. Rewind or Reset does not automatically clean up past output.

sourceLabel: AWS Glue — Job bookmarks and replay

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Synchronous Event Enrichment and Routing from a Queue
prompt: Send only high-value orders from SQS to an EventBridge bus for review. Before sending them, read customer attributes from DynamoDB and format each event so the review team has the information it needs in a single event. You want to avoid maintaining custom polling or Lambda functions. Retrieving the attributes takes little time. Which approach is possible?

choices.text: Specify DynamoDB GetItem directly as the enrichment target for Pipes, then send the event to the review bus.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB GetItem is not among the enrichment target types that can be specified directly.

choices.text: Specify Step Functions Standard as the enrichment target for Pipes and wait for the workflow's completion response.
choices.explanation: Step Functions can be used for Pipes enrichment only with the synchronously invocable Express type.

choices.text: Use only an input transformer in an EventBridge rule on the review bus to include the current values from DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: An input transformer changes values in an event; it does not read external data.

choices.text: Use Pipes to read from SQS, filter matching events, enrich them with an Express workflow, and set the review bus as the target.
choices.explanation: Pipes handles source polling and filtering, and the enrichment can return its result synchronously.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge Pipes — イベント補完

learning.reason: Use Pipes with SQS as the source to apply a filter, then look up DynamoDB data in a synchronously invoked Step Functions Express workflow and return the result. Send the enriched result to the target bus.
learning.concept: Pipes waits for the enrichment result, so the enrichment target must support synchronous invocation. Check the workflow type and which enrichment targets and final targets can be selected.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Automatically Deleting Large Volumes of One-Time Notifications After Execution
prompt: A SaaS application starts a notification task once at each customer’s scheduled time. The scheduling horizon is up to one year, and you do not want to run a custom worker during periods with no scheduled events. New schedules continue to be added during that period, and you also want to prevent completed schedules from continuing to consume the Region’s schedule quota. Completed appointments can already be tracked in the business database. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a one-time EventBridge Scheduler schedule for each appointment and set its after-completion action to DELETE.
choices.explanation: This provides managed execution at each individual time and frees quota after completion without manual cleanup.

choices.text: Create a one-time EventBridge Scheduler schedule and set its after-completion action to NONE.
choices.explanation: The completed definitions are not deleted, so the number of schedules accumulates as new appointments are added.

choices.text: Set an SQS message timer at booking time for up to one year and use it to start a worker.
choices.explanation: An individual SQS message delay cannot be set as far as one year in the future.

choices.text: Convert DynamoDB TTL deletion events into notification tasks.
choices.explanation: Deletion can be delayed after expiration, so this cannot schedule execution at the appointment time.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler — 実行済みスケジュールの削除

learning.reason: Create a one-time schedule for each appointment and set it to be deleted after completion when the schedule is created. Configure retries and a dead-letter queue to suit the required timing and operations.
learning.concept: The quota for registered Scheduler resources is separate from the quota for execution requests arriving at once. Automatic deletion prevents registered resources from accumulating.

sourceLabel: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler — Deleting completed schedules

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Testing New WAF Rules for False Positives
prompt: You are adding an AWS Managed Rules group containing multiple Block actions to the Web ACL for a public Application Load Balancer. Existing rules must retain their current blocking behavior. The added group must not block traffic for one week, and you want to measure individual matches even when a request that reaches the group matches multiple rules. Which configuration is best?

choices.text: Set only the added group’s return action to Count.
choices.explanation: When the first terminating rule matches, evaluation within the group stops, so later matches cannot all be measured.

choices.text: Set the Web ACL’s default action to Allow and leave the Block actions in the added group unchanged.
choices.explanation: Individual Block rules are evaluated first, so the default Allow action cannot prevent blocking during the trial.

choices.text: Override the action of each rule in the added group to Count.
choices.explanation: This makes the added rules non-terminating detections while preserving the blocking behavior of existing groups.

choices.text: Place a rule that allows all requests before the added rules.
choices.explanation: Allow terminates evaluation, so the added rules cannot be measured; it also affects subsequent existing blocking rules.

source.label: AWS WAF — ルールアクションの上書き

learning.reason: Apply a Count rule-action override to each rule in the added group. A match does not terminate evaluation there, so matches in later rules can also be observed.
learning.concept: Changing the group’s overall return action to Count does not change where evaluation of its internal rules stops. For impact analysis, target each rule.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Applying WAF When Accounts Join a Departmental OU
prompt: A company operates public ALBs across hundreds of AWS accounts managed by individual departments. The security team wants to automatically apply a shared AWS WAF group to new ALBs in the Product OU, including accounts that join the OU in the future, except for approved resources tagged as exceptions. Departments also operate their own rules in addition to the shared group. The prerequisites for Firewall Manager, such as AWS Config, are met. Which configuration should be selected in each Region?

choices.text: Have every departmental account’s ALBs directly reference a single regional Web ACL in the management account.
choices.explanation: Merely referencing a single Web ACL does not provide automatic cross-account management or exception handling.

choices.text: Use StackSets listing the current account IDs to distribute the same template.
choices.explanation: A fixed account list will not continuously cover accounts that join later or individual ALBs.

choices.text: Apply a Firewall Manager policy to the Product OU, but leave automatic remediation disabled and only monitor the list of violations.
choices.explanation: This can detect issues, but it will not automatically apply the shared group when an ALB is unprotected.

choices.text: Use a Firewall Manager WAF policy to select ALBs in the Product OU, exclude exception tags, and enable automatic remediation.
choices.explanation: The policy can apply protection according to its scope to accounts joining the OU and to new in-scope ALBs.

source.label: AWS Firewall Manager — ポリシースコープ

learning.reason: Limit a Firewall Manager regional WAF policy to ALBs in the Product OU, exclude resources with exception tags from its scope, and enable automatic remediation.
learning.concept: Design the organization policy scope, resource-tag scope, and automatic remediation separately. Set permissions so authorized approvers can change tag exceptions.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Controlling DNS Responses for Prohibited Names and Auditing Them
prompt: Private VPCs in the same Region use Route 53 VPC Resolver for name resolution. Queries for known prohibited domains must receive NXDOMAIN, and name resolution must be stopped before an application attempts to connect. For auditing, you must be able to identify the denied domains and the matching rules in query logs. Choose two required settings per VPC.

choices.text: Apply ALERT to the prohibited-name list in DNS Firewall to stop name resolution.
choices.explanation: ALERT generates logs, but DNS queries are allowed.

choices.text: Configure BLOCK rules for prohibited names to return NXDOMAIN, and associate the rule group with the VPC.
choices.explanation: This denies matching queries through the VPC Resolver and returns the specified response.

choices.text: Record only denials with VPC Flow Logs and retrieve the DNS Firewall rule ID and query name from them.
choices.explanation: VPC Flow Logs do not include the DNS Firewall rule ID or query name fields.

choices.text: Place a broad ALLOW rule at the highest priority, then list prohibited names in lower-priority BLOCK rules.
choices.explanation: When the higher-priority ALLOW rule matches, evaluation ends and the lower-priority block does not apply.

choices.text: In the same Region, add the VPC to the scope of Resolver query logging and configure an audit destination.
choices.explanation: This lets you inspect denied query names and the corresponding DNS Firewall fields.

source.label: Amazon Route 53 — DNS Firewallのルールアクション

learning.reason: Associate a rule group configured with BLOCK/NXDOMAIN for prohibited-name lists, and configure VPC Resolver query logging.
learning.concept: Use Resolver query logs to inspect DNS Firewall decisions. VPC Flow Logs record connection metadata, but they do not retain query names or DNS Firewall rule decisions.

sourceLabel: Amazon Route 53 — DNS Firewall rule actions

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Separating the Fargate Pod Execution Role from Application Permissions
prompt: All EKS Pods run on Fargate and use the same profile to pull images. Grant only the billing container read access to a specific S3 prefix. Other Pods must not be able to read it, and you want to avoid long-term access keys or adding EC2 nodes. How should credentials be provided?

choices.text: Create a service account dedicated to billing, and associate an S3 read role with it using OIDC and IAM roles for service accounts.
choices.explanation: The application in the target Pod can use temporary credentials for the dedicated role.

choices.text: Add S3 access to the Fargate profile’s Pod execution IAM role.
choices.explanation: The Pod execution role’s permissions are not passed to the container’s application.

choices.text: Place the EKS Pod Identity Agent on an EC2 node and distribute temporary credentials to the existing Fargate Pods.
choices.explanation: Fargate Pods are not supported targets for Pod Identity, and adding EC2 nodes does not change that.

choices.text: Specify the Kubernetes service account name directly as the Principal in the S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: That name is not an IAM principal used for AWS API authorization; the service account needs an associated IAM role.

source.label: Amazon EKS — Fargate Pod実行IAMロールとアプリ権限

learning.reason: Associate an IAM role through IRSA with the Kubernetes service account used only by billing. Scope the trust policy to that service account and grant the role only the required S3 permissions.
learning.concept: The Fargate Pod execution role is used by the infrastructure to start containers. Manage AWS API permissions for the container itself through its service account.

sourceLabel: Amazon EKS — Fargate Pod execution IAM role and application permissions

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Separate Log Access from Privileged Exceptions
prompt: Logs ingested into a CloudWatch Logs Standard log group in the future may contain payment card numbers. Operators should retain their existing ability to search the logs, but the numbers must not be displayed to them. Only auditors should be able to reveal the original values when needed, and an audit record of the number of detections is also required. Changes to the logger and an additional logging platform are not allowed. Select two required configurations.

choices.text: Configure a data protection policy with a payment card number data identifier, audit output, and masking.
choices.explanation: This detects matching new events and audits them while hiding the values during normal viewing.

choices.text: Grant decryption permissions for the KMS key only to auditors, and let operators view the same logs by field.
choices.explanation: KMS encryption at rest does not hide specific fields in a log message based on who is viewing it.

choices.text: Allow logs:Unmask only for the auditors’ role.
choices.explanation: Only authorized auditors can view the values before masking when needed.

choices.text: Configure a log metric filter and delete only the matching number strings from the original log events.
choices.explanation: A metric filter can aggregate detections, but it does not rewrite log events.

choices.text: Put a redaction expression in example Logs Insights queries and keep the IAM viewing permissions shared.
choices.explanation: This cannot enforce the same masking when a viewer uses another query or display method.

source.label: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — 機密ログの検出とマスキング

learning.reason: Configure the data identifier, audit, and masking in the log group’s data protection policy. Do not grant Unmask to regular operators; grant it only to auditors.
learning.concept: Post-ingestion log protection can separate viewing permissions. It does not apply retroactively to events ingested before the policy was configured, so distinguish those from the events in scope here.

sourceLabel: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — Detecting and masking sensitive log data

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Inspect Replacement Changes in Nested Stacks Before Applying Them
prompt: Updating a CloudFormation root stack may replace an RDS resource in a child stack it references. Before updating production, reviewers want to inspect changes to the root and child stacks as a single approval item. A replacement that depends on a parent output value may also be shown as conditional. Which procedure is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a change set for the root stack only and assume it will list every replacement in child stacks.
choices.explanation: Without including nested stacks, you cannot inspect changes at the child-resource level.

choices.text: Create a root change set that includes nested stacks, then inspect the child changes too. Investigate dependent outputs further when a replacement is conditional, and execute the update from the root after approval.
choices.explanation: This lets reviewers inspect root and child changes as one update and follows the execution procedure for nested change sets.

choices.text: Run drift detection to inspect replacement differences between the unapplied template and production.
choices.explanation: Drift detection compares the configuration expected by the stack with the running resources; it does not list replacements caused by unapplied changes.

choices.text: Create nested change sets, then execute each child change set individually in review order before applying the root.
choices.explanation: Nested change sets must be executed from the root. Updating production partway through also conflicts with the pre-approval requirement.

source.label: AWS CloudFormation — ネストされたスタックの変更セット

learning.reason: Create a root change set that includes nested stacks and expand it to inspect child changes. After review, execute the approved root change set.
learning.concept: Change sets help assess impact before an update, but they do not by themselves determine the result of dynamic references or whether execution will succeed.

sourceLabel: AWS CloudFormation — Change sets for nested stacks

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Capturing Delivery Failures and Function Execution Failures Separately
prompt: An EventBridge rule for operational automation invokes a Lambda function asynchronously. You want to capture both cases where a request is not accepted by Lambda because of a misconfigured invocation permission and where, after acceptance, the function fails and exhausts Lambda's retries. If execution fails, retain a record that includes the error response. Choose two required measures.

choices.text: Set only a retry count on the EventBridge target and assume EventBridge checks the return value of the completed function.
choices.explanation: After an asynchronous invocation is accepted, EventBridge does not wait for the function's execution result.

choices.text: Configure a Standard SQS DLQ in the same Region for the Lambda target of the EventBridge rule, and grant permission to deliver to it.
choices.explanation: EventBridge can capture events that it cannot deliver to the target.

choices.text: Only add SQS send permission to the Lambda execution role so that it automatically receives all failures.
choices.explanation: Permission is only a prerequisite for sending; an asynchronous failure destination must also be configured.

choices.text: Configure an OnFailure destination for Lambda's asynchronous invocation to receive records of failed processing.
choices.explanation: For failures after acceptance, this can receive an execution record containing the request and response.

choices.text: Configure only a Lambda asynchronous DLQ and use it to receive both calls EventBridge could not get accepted and Lambda error responses in the same format.
choices.explanation: Lambda's DLQ cannot receive events from invocations that Lambda did not accept, and it does not include detailed execution responses.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge — Lambdaターゲットへの非同期配信

learning.reason: Configure a target DLQ in EventBridge for events it cannot deliver. For failures after Lambda has accepted an event, use Lambda's asynchronous OnFailure destination to receive an execution record.
learning.concept: With asynchronous processing, delivery responsibility changes at each service boundary. Retries can deliver the same event more than once, so design the recovery path to avoid duplicating business side effects.

sourceLabel: Amazon EventBridge — Asynchronous Delivery to Lambda Targets

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Migrate Existing EDI While Preserving Signature Verification and Acknowledgments
prompt: A wholesaler is retiring its AS2 receiving server, which uses signatures and encryption. Trading partners can update the destination URL and certificates, but they cannot change from AS2. The company wants decrypted files stored in its own S3 bucket and a signed Message Disposition Notification (MDN) returned to the trading partner in the HTTP response. Which configuration meets these requirements without operating an AS2 server itself?

choices.text: Use a Transfer Family SFTP server, accept existing trading partner certificates as authentication keys, and send notifications through SNS after receipt.
choices.explanation: SFTP transfer acknowledgments and SNS notifications cannot return the signed MDN expected by an AS2 client.

choices.text: Configure an AS2-enabled server in Transfer Family with an S3 receiving destination, and set up the inbound agreement with the trading partner and the required certificates.
choices.explanation: This supports signature verification and decryption for inbound AS2, storage in S3, and a synchronous signed MDN.

choices.text: Create only an outbound AS2 connector in Transfer Family and configure trading partners to send data to it.
choices.explanation: A connector can send to an external AS2 destination, but it does not create an AS2 endpoint and agreement for receiving data.

choices.text: Connect HTTP POST directly to S3 through API Gateway and treat S3’s success response as the AS2 acknowledgment.
choices.explanation: The POST body could be stored, but this would not verify the AS2 signature or generate the corresponding MDN.

source.label: AWS Transfer Family — AS2メッセージの送受信

learning.reason: Configure an AS2-enabled Transfer Family server, profiles for the company and trading partner, certificates, and an inbound agreement. The receiving workflow decrypts and verifies the signature, stores the file in S3, and returns the MDN.
learning.concept: An AS2 agreement defines receiving-side protocol processing. An outbound connector, SFTP user authentication, and simple HTTP storage serve different roles.

sourceLabel: AWS Transfer Family — Sending and receiving AS2 messages

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Replace Tape Hardware While Preserving the Recovery Workflow
prompt: The on-premises backup product can use an iSCSI virtual tape library. You want to stop shipping physical tapes for long-term storage. During an audit, you must use the same backup product and barcodes to read stored tapes. You can allow time to prepare long-term data for recovery. Which architecture should you choose?

choices.text: Expose Amazon S3 File Gateway over SMB and connect the tape product using its existing iSCSI settings, without changing its configuration.
choices.explanation: File Gateway provides SMB or NFS file shares; it does not provide an iSCSI virtual tape library.

choices.text: Connect a Volume Gateway cached volume over iSCSI and use the block volume as a virtual tape changer.
choices.explanation: Although both use iSCSI, a volume and a virtual tape device are different.

choices.text: Use Tape Gateway virtual tapes and archive them after ejection. For recovery, return the tapes to the library and read them with the backup product.
choices.explanation: This preserves tape barcodes and existing iSCSI tape operations while eliminating physical media transport.

choices.text: Archive Tape Gateway tapes, then use GetObject on the stored S3 objects during recovery and pass them to the backup product.
choices.explanation: Archived tapes must be returned to the library through the console or API, then read through the existing tape interface.

source.label: AWS Storage Gateway — Tape Gatewayの概念

learning.reason: Use Tape Gateway as the product's iSCSI target, eject long-term tapes, and store them in the virtual tape shelf. Later, retrieve the required tapes to the library and read them.
learning.concept: Tapes in the tape shelf cannot be read directly. Include the archive pool and the retrieval process for tapes when needed in the recovery plan.

sourceLabel: AWS Storage Gateway — Tape Gateway Concepts

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Replace Capacity and Drain Work Before Spot Interruption
prompt: Spot workers in an Auto Scaling group can checkpoint jobs in progress in a short time. When you receive a notification indicating Spot interruption risk, you want to launch a replacement before the instance is terminated when possible, and drain work from the worker that is terminating. You want to continue using Spot and do not require a guarantee that early notification will always arrive. Which architecture should you choose?

choices.text: Enable Capacity Rebalancing and save a checkpoint with a termination lifecycle hook.
choices.explanation: This can attempt a replacement without waiting for a regular health check failure, and run drain logic at termination.

choices.text: Add only a termination lifecycle hook and rely on a regular health check failure to launch a replacement.
choices.explanation: This adds termination handling, but it does not attempt a replacement in response to a rebalance recommendation.

choices.text: Add only a launch lifecycle hook and save a checkpoint there for the instance that is about to terminate.
choices.explanation: A launch hook applies to a new instance, so it does not act on the worker that is about to terminate and needs to drain work.

choices.text: Set excess capacity and use average CPU-based scaling alone to reduce failures.
choices.explanation: Excess capacity may be available, but this does not proactively replace or drain a worker based on its individual Spot interruption risk.

source.label: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling — Capacity Rebalancing

learning.reason: Capacity Rebalancing can launch replacement candidates in response to a rebalance recommendation. A termination lifecycle hook can stop the worker from accepting new work and save state quickly.
learning.concept: Capacity Rebalancing creates an opportunity to act early, but does not guarantee replacement launch or advance notice. Design for jobs to be retried if draining does not finish in time.

sourceLabel: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling — Capacity Rebalancing

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Recover from a Host Failure with the Same Instance ID
prompt: A legacy license server runs on a single EBS-backed EC2 instance and must retain its instance ID and private IP address. Its current instance type supports EC2 automatic recovery, and it is acceptable to lose volatile memory on restart. OS process failures are monitored by a separate service. Which measure should you configure in advance for a physical host failure?

choices.text: Use Auto Scaling replacement and register an EC2 instance launched from the same launch template as the old instance.
choices.explanation: Even with the same template, a new instance receives a different instance ID.

choices.text: Use guest OS process monitoring to perform only a standard EC2 reboot.
choices.explanation: A standard reboot is not a recovery mechanism that moves the instance from a failed host to another host.

choices.text: Launch an AMI in a different Availability Zone and assign it the same private IP address and instance ID.
choices.explanation: A new instance cannot inherit the old instance ID, and a subnet does not span Availability Zones.

choices.text: Enable automatic recovery for the supported EC2 instance and recover it when a system status check fails.
choices.explanation: When moved to another host, the instance retains the required identifiers and EBS volumes, separating this recovery from guest OS issues.

source.label: Amazon EC2 — 基盤障害時の自動インスタンス復旧

learning.reason: For supported EC2 instances, automatic recovery attempts to move the instance to another host when a system status check fails. If successful, it retains the instance ID, IP address, and EBS volumes.
learning.concept: A system status check indicates an underlying host problem. An instance-level OS failure or an Availability Zone outage requires a different recovery approach.

sourceLabel: Amazon EC2 — Automatic Instance Recovery for Underlying Host Failures

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Switch the Cache Write Target After a Regional Outage
prompt: Applications run in two Regions in the same account. They use a node-based Valkey Global Datastore, with one Region as the write target under normal conditions and the other serving local reads. Loss of recent data due to asynchronous replication is acceptable. If the primary Region fails, you want to make the secondary the new write target by following a procedure. Which operating procedure is correct?

choices.text: Promote the secondary to primary and switch the application's write target.
choices.explanation: Run the AWS-managed procedure that makes the secondary writable, then connect the application to the new primary.

choices.text: Wait for the primary's Multi-AZ automatic failover to promote the other Region.
choices.explanation: Automatic failover within a Region does not promote another Region.

choices.text: Simply point the application's DNS for reads to the secondary and start writing to it.
choices.explanation: A secondary that has not been promoted cannot be used as a write target.

choices.text: Add nodes to the secondary and assume that this automatically adds a writable node.
choices.explanation: Scaling capacity within a Region does not change which Region is primary in the Global Datastore.

source.label: Amazon ElastiCache — Global Datastoreの制約

learning.reason: Cross-Region automatic failover does not occur, so explicitly promote the secondary and configure the application to use it as the new write target.
learning.concept: Automatic AZ failover within a Region differs from promotion between Regions. Because replication is asynchronous, also confirm that the remaining data is acceptable before resuming operations.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Recovering from replication failure caused by DDL during migration testing
prompt: A Blue/Green deployment using logical replication is being prepared for a major version upgrade of RDS for PostgreSQL. During synchronization, a new partition is added on the production Blue, and Green reports Replication degraded and cannot be switched over. Data accepted by Blue must remain the production source of truth, and writes must continue, including to the new partition. Which recovery procedure is required?

choices.text: Manually add the same partition to the current Green and switch over immediately while replication is degraded.
choices.explanation: Adding the partition manually does not clear the deployment's degraded state, and normal synchronization and switchover are not guaranteed.

choices.text: Only extend the switchover timeout and wait for degraded replication to recover.
choices.explanation: Adjusting the time limit does not fix DDL that is excluded from replication or the degraded state.

choices.text: Delete the Blue/Green deployment, including the old Green, and recreate it from the latest Blue. Disallow unsupported DDL during synchronization and switch over after validation.
choices.explanation: This is a supported procedure for rebuilding the test environment from the source of truth, including the existing partitions.

choices.text: Promote a Green read replica and use it as though it contained the same data as the original Blue.
choices.explanation: There is no guarantee that data written to Blue after replication degraded is present, so this does not meet the requirement to preserve the source of truth.

source.label: Amazon RDS — PostgreSQL Blue/Greenの論理複製制約

learning.reason: This form of DDL is not replicated from Blue to Green. Recreate the deployment, including the existing Green, and stop unsupported DDL on Blue until the next switchover while checking replication status.
learning.concept: A mechanism that reduces switchover time still constrains which changes are allowed during replication. Before a major version upgrade, check which DDL, extensions, and privilege changes are supported.

sourceLabel: Amazon RDS — PostgreSQL Blue/Green logical replication limitations

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Safely redrive failed messages at a controlled rate to a separate destination
prompt: A bug in a worker that aggregates equipment data has been fixed. You want to move the failed messages in an SQS Standard DLQ as-is to a separate queue for historical reprocessing, without mixing them into the queue currently handling the latest data. The destination database has little spare capacity, so you want to set a low maximum redrive rate for the initial run. The message bodies do not need to be transformed, and you want to reduce the amount of custom polling code. Which action should you choose?

choices.text: Redrive the DLQ to the live queue for the latest data at the system-optimized rate, distinguishing the messages only in the reprocessing worker.
choices.explanation: The messages would be mixed into the live queue for the latest data, and system-optimized redrive does not let you set a low maximum rate.

choices.text: Use DLQ redrive to specify a separate Standard queue and set a low custom maximum rate.
choices.explanation: This avoids the queue for new, latest data and limits the initial redrive rate.

choices.text: Make the reprocessing destination a FIFO queue and use built-in redrive from the Standard DLQ.
