choices.explanation: The source and destination queues for redrive must be the same queue type.

choices.text: Extend the DLQ visibility timeout and assume that messages will move slowly to a separate reprocessing queue.
choices.explanation: The visibility timeout controls when a received message becomes visible again; it does not move messages to another queue or limit the redrive rate.

source.label: Amazon SQS — DLQからのリドライブ

learning.reason: Choose a reprocessing Standard queue of the same type as the redrive destination and set a low custom maximum rate.
learning.concept: Built-in redrive can move messages to a queue of the same type. Separate processing is needed to filter or modify individual message bodies.

sourceLabel: Amazon SQS — Redriving messages from a DLQ

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Introducing shared short names and traffic monitoring across ECS clusters
prompt: Orders and inventory run on two ECS clusters in the same Region. Tasks are replaced frequently, and all callers are ECS services. Routing and ports between the VPCs are already available, and no external exposure is needed. In addition to service discovery by short name, the team wants traffic distribution, retries, and proxy metrics without application changes or custom sidecar management. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a Cloud Map private DNS namespace to return task IP addresses, and have the application use its existing DNS connections.
choices.explanation: This discovers tasks by name, but does not add ECS-managed proxy retries or traffic monitoring.

choices.text: Register each backend with an internal ALB and manage custom short names in Route 53.
choices.explanation: This provides routing and load balancing, but does not provide the shared namespace and per-task managed proxy configuration sought here.

choices.text: Configure inventory as both a Service Connect client and server, and orders as a client, in the same namespace; use the inventory client alias.
choices.explanation: ECS deploys proxies for both services and provides short names, traffic distribution, retries, and monitoring.

choices.text: Register HTTP services in VPC Lattice for a shared network, and have the application team operate the in-task traffic proxies.
choices.explanation: This allows services to be exposed across a broader scope, but adds an unnecessary exposure scope and self-managed proxy operations.

source.label: Amazon ECS — Service Connectの構成

learning.reason: Configure ECS Service Connect in the same Cloud Map namespace. Through ECS-managed task proxies, use name resolution, load balancing, retries, and metrics together.
learning.concept: Distinguish service discovery with Cloud Map alone from service-to-service communication managed by Service Connect. VPC reachability must be established separately.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Combining a required custom AMI at launch with dynamic node scaling
prompt: Analytics pods on Amazon EKS require a custom Linux AMI signed by the organization and a dedicated hardware driver that must be enabled when the OS starts from that image. Installing the driver later with a DaemonSet is not allowed. When pods cannot be scheduled, the team wants nodes that meet their CPU, memory, and instance type requirements to be selected automatically from multiple types. Which configuration should be chosen?

choices.text: Create a custom NodePool in EKS Auto Mode and specify a custom AMI ID in the NodePool.
choices.explanation: Auto Mode NodePools can constrain node characteristics, but they cannot specify a custom AMI.

choices.text: Use self-managed Karpenter with a custom AMI and compatible instance types to launch nodes for unscheduled pods.
choices.explanation: This supports both the approved image and instance selection.

choices.text: Use Auto Mode and install the dedicated driver at startup with a DaemonSet.
choices.explanation: Installing it later does not meet the image-signing and OS-startup requirements.

choices.text: Specify a custom AMI in a fixed-size managed node group and scale only the pods horizontally.
choices.explanation: An AMI can be selected, but a fixed number of nodes and pod-only horizontal scaling cannot add suitable nodes when capacity is insufficient.

source.label: Amazon EKS — Auto ModeのマネージドインスタンスとAMI

learning.reason: Use self-managed Karpenter on EC2 to configure allowed instance types and a custom AMI whose operation has been validated.
learning.concept: EKS Auto Mode handles node management but AWS selects the AMI. With a self-managed approach, you can manage the required image, but you also take responsibility for maintaining the controller and nodes.

sourceLabel: Amazon EKS — Auto Mode managed instances and AMIs

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Handle failures by percentage in a large S3 batch
prompt: The list of CSV records to process in S3 exceeds one million items each day and is too large to fit in the Step Functions state input. Validate each row individually with an external service that allows at most 200 concurrent requests. If failures and timeouts caused by malformed input and similar issues are no more than 0.5%, process the remaining items; if they exceed that percentage, fail the batch. Which two settings are required?

choices.text: Use a Distributed Map in the parent workflow and specify the S3 CSV as the ItemReader input.
choices.explanation: This processes a large dataset without loading it into the state input and passes one row at a time to child executions.

choices.text: Convert the entire S3 CSV into the parent input JSON and use an Inline Map.
choices.explanation: The data will not fit in the parent input, and an Inline Map is not suited to the required scale or execution history isolation.

choices.text: Make every child return success through Catch and use the Map's default failure settings.
choices.explanation: Treating failures as successes prevents the actual failure rate from being evaluated.

choices.text: Set MaxConcurrency to 200 and ToleratedFailurePercentage to 0.5.
choices.explanation: These settings express the downstream concurrency limit and the permitted failure and timeout rate across all items.

choices.text: Set ToleratedFailureCount to a fixed value of 5,000.
choices.explanation: When the total number of rows varies by day, a fixed count does not represent a 0.5% rate.

source.label: AWS Step Functions — Distributed Map

learning.reason: Read the S3 CSV with the Distributed Map ItemReader, then set MaxConcurrency to 200 and ToleratedFailurePercentage to 0.5.
learning.concept: Read inputs that exceed the state input limit from S3. Maximum concurrency controls simultaneous executions, while the tolerated failure percentage sets the permitted ratio of failures and timeouts.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Clean up stale connections without breaking reconnections
prompt: A delivery-notification API Gateway WebSocket API receives subscriptions from each connected device and stores them by connection ID. A device may go out of range without a disconnect event being delivered, so a later PostToConnection call can return GoneException. The same user may also have reconnected and subscribed under a different connection ID. Which handling stops retries to an invalid connection without breaking the current subscription when a notification fails?

choices.text: Keep retrying the same connection ID with exponential backoff until GoneException is resolved.
choices.explanation: Retrying an already-lost connection ID does not send the message to a new connection.

choices.text: Use the user ID as the key and cancel all subscriptions for that user.
choices.explanation: This would also delete the valid subscription on the reconnected device.

choices.text: Save the message in SQS and delete the invalid connection record only after a disconnect event arrives.
choices.explanation: A disconnect event may never arrive, so the invalid connection can remain indefinitely.

choices.text: Delete only the subscription record for the established connection ID that returned GoneException, then stop sending to that ID.
choices.explanation: This preserves a separate, newer connection ID and stops unnecessary retries to the stale connection.

source.label: Amazon API Gateway — 接続IDへのコールバック

learning.reason: When GoneException is returned for an established connection, delete only the record for that failed connection ID. Keep a different ID created by a new connection.
learning.concept: WebSocket disconnect notifications are best effort. Treat connection ID lifetime separately from user lifetime so that process retries do not remove a new connection.

sourceLabel: Amazon API Gateway — Callbacks to connection IDs

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Spread same-day writes and retrieve directly by reservation ID
prompt: A large number of reservations must be recorded in DynamoDB. Using the date as the partition key concentrated writes on the sale date. The application wants to use one GetItem call for an individual lookup when it knows the reservation date and reservation ID. A daily batch retrieves all reservations, but it can query each suffix in parallel and combine the results. Reservation IDs are well distributed. Which key design should you choose?

choices.text: Append a suffix derived from a hash of the reservation ID to the date, and use the reservation ID as the sort key.
choices.explanation: The key can be reconstructed from a known ID, and writes for the same day are spread across multiple values.

choices.text: Append a random suffix to the date that is assigned only at write time, and have the application call GetItem using only the reservation ID.
choices.explanation: The assigned value cannot be derived from the same ID, so an additional lookup is needed for a point read.

choices.text: Keep the date as the only partition key and switch the table to on-demand capacity.
choices.explanation: This changes table-level capacity management but does not spread traffic away from a single key.

choices.text: Use the reservation ID as the partition key, and run Scan on the table and filter the results for each daily batch.
choices.explanation: Individual lookups are possible, but the daily job cannot use targeted Query operations for each shard.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — 書き込みシャーディング

learning.reason: Use a partition key with a fixed-range hash suffix that can be calculated from the date and reservation ID. The individual lookup can calculate the same key, while the daily job queries every suffix.
learning.concept: Distinguish the write-spreading effect of a random suffix from the point-read convenience of a calculable suffix. In either design, listing a day requires combining results from the partitions.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Identify the index throttling base-table writes
prompt: A DynamoDB reservations table and its existing GSI use provisioned mode, and index-key distribution has been verified. During sales, PutItem calls to the base table fail. The exception is IndexWriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded, and ResourceArn identifies the search GSI rather than the reservations table. Base-table write capacity and account quotas are available. What should you do first while preserving the key design and query results?

choices.text: Increase only the provisioned write capacity of the base table.
choices.explanation: The exception identifies write capacity on the search GSI; increasing only the base-table capacity leaves the index bottleneck in place.

choices.text: Increase the provisioned read capacity of the search GSI.
choices.explanation: Write capacity for index updates is insufficient, so increasing read capacity will not resolve the issue.

choices.text: Increase the search GSI's provisioned write capacity and review its scaling settings.
choices.explanation: This addresses the GSI capacity shortage and can restore base-table writes that were throttled by backpressure.

choices.text: Switch the base-table client to strongly consistent reads.
choices.explanation: Changing read consistency does not increase the index's write capacity.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — GSIの書き込み制限

learning.reason: Increase the GSI's provisioned write capacity and review its scaling settings if needed. Writes to the base table can also be throttled by insufficient index capacity.
learning.concept: The remedies for write rejection differ depending on whether the cause is a hot key range, configured provisioned capacity, or an on-demand limit. Here, use both the exception reason and resource ARN to make the diagnosis.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Privately expose an API only to a VPC in another Region
prompt: A Tokyo business account owns an existing PrivateLink endpoint service that uses an NLB. The account wants to make it available additionally only to an analytics VPC in Ohio. The provider must not be relocated to another Region, the entire VPC must not be peered, and the consumer VPC must create a local interface endpoint. Select two configurations for a cross-Region PrivateLink setup.

choices.text: Change the consumer side to the Tokyo Region setting and specify Ohio subnets instead of Tokyo subnets.
choices.explanation: The VPC where the interface is created and the Region where the service is offered are specified separately in the request.

choices.text: On the provider side, add Ohio as a supported Region and authorize the analytics account as a principal. Allow vpce:AllowMultiRegion on the provider side.
choices.explanation: You can configure the consumer Region and the principals that are allowed to connect.

choices.text: Notify the consumer account of only the service name, and leave Tokyo as the only supported Region on the provider side.
choices.explanation: Selecting the Tokyo service on the consumer side is not sufficient if the provider has not made the service available in Ohio.

choices.text: In the analytics VPC in Ohio, create an interface endpoint with Tokyo as the service Region, and allow vpce:AllowMultiRegion for the operator role.
choices.explanation: This keeps the endpoint in the local Region while connecting it to a service in another Region.

choices.text: Add a route directly from Ohio to the Tokyo NLB to avoid configuring PrivateLink principals.
choices.explanation: Adding the service NLB to a VPC route table does not create an authorized PrivateLink interface connection.

source.label: Amazon VPC — PrivateLinkのリージョン間アクセス

learning.reason: On the provider side, add Ohio as a supported Region and authorize the consumer. On the consumer side, create an endpoint in the Ohio VPC with Tokyo specified as the service Region. The operator roles on both sides need permissions for cross-Region operations.
learning.concept: The Region where a service is offered and the Region where a consumer creates an interface endpoint can differ. PrivateLink does not expose the entire VPC network path.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Collect packets for investigation without changing the traffic path
prompt: An internal application running on supported EC2 instances needs packet-level investigation of TCP sessions that are already permitted. An analytics platform in the same VPC must be able to receive packets from a specific ENI, filtered by the source and destination ports. Avoid adding an agent to the application and avoid a design in which an analytics platform failure blocks the original traffic. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Add the source and destination ports and the action to a custom VPC Flow Logs format.
choices.explanation: Flow Logs are useful for investigating connections, but they do not provide the packets themselves.

choices.text: Use Traffic Mirroring on the target ENI, filter by port, and send the copies to an analysis appliance.
choices.explanation: This makes the target packets available for analysis without changing source software or the original traffic path.

choices.text: Route traffic from the target subnet through inline inspection behind a Gateway Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: This can inspect packets, but it places the inspection appliance in the original traffic path.

choices.text: Install a packet collection agent on the target EC2 instance and forward the collected data to a destination.
choices.explanation: Packet collection on the host is possible, but it does not meet the requirement to avoid adding an agent.

source.label: Amazon VPC — Traffic Mirroring

learning.reason: Associate the source ENI, a filter for the target ports, and the analytics platform as the target in a mirroring session. The copies can be sent without changing the original traffic path.
learning.concept: Flow Logs provide connection metadata; packet-level investigation requires a different observation method. In this design, distinguish inline inspection in the forwarding path from investigation outside that path.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Set up an independent organization investigation graph in another Region
prompt: The security team uses an Amazon Detective organization behavior graph in Tokyo. The team also wants to investigate relationships among users and resources in another U.S. Region, using accounts in the same AWS Organizations organization. Decide on the configuration before starting local data collection, and avoid performing routine investigations in the management account. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Send U.S. events directly to the API for the Tokyo graph and extend the geographic scope of that graph.
choices.explanation: Detective behavior graphs are Region-specific; there is no setting to extend one graph into another Region.

choices.text: Call the U.S. Region's Detective API and specify the name of the Tokyo investigation graph.
choices.explanation: The API for a Region can manage only the graph in that Region.

choices.text: Aggregate only the U.S. GuardDuty findings in Tokyo and configure Tokyo Detective to collect U.S. activity in the same graph.
choices.explanation: Aggregating findings alone does not configure a Detective graph and account data collection in another Region.

choices.text: Configure delegated administration and an organization behavior graph in the U.S. Region, then invite the target accounts to join.
choices.explanation: The security team can investigate the target organization's data in that Region using a Region-specific graph.

source.label: Amazon Detective — 組織ビヘイビアグラフとリージョン

learning.reason: Use delegated administration for the organization in the target Region and enable an organization behavior graph for the target accounts. Manage it in that Region separately from the existing Tokyo graph.
learning.concept: Organizations can group multiple accounts, but Detective behavior graphs are created separately in each Region.

sourceLabel: Amazon Detective — Organization behavior graphs and Regions

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restore a scheduled-for-deletion secret with the same ARN
prompt: Two days have passed since a 14-day recovery window was set for deletion of a production secret in Secrets Manager. The database password is still valid, but GetSecretValue fails after an application restart. The application must be restored immediately while retaining the secret's existing ARN as its reference. Which action should you choose?

choices.text: Run RestoreSecret on the original secret, then retrieve it again using the same ARN.
choices.explanation: During the recovery window, you can cancel the scheduled deletion and restore access to the existing secret.

choices.text: Specify AWSCURRENT in GetSecretValue and continue retrieving the value during the recovery window.
choices.explanation: A secret scheduled for deletion cannot be retrieved even during the recovery window.

choices.text: Create a separate new secret with the same name and password, then continue using the original ARN to retrieve it.
choices.explanation: A new resource does not inherit the original ARN.

choices.text: Update the database user's password and leave the secret scheduled for deletion.
choices.explanation: Changing the database alone does not clear the secret's deletion state.

source.label: AWS Secrets Manager — 削除予定と回復期間

learning.reason: Call RestoreSecret during the recovery window to cancel the scheduled deletion. The application can retrieve the value again using the same secret ARN.
learning.concept: The recovery window is the period in which scheduled deletion can be canceled. The value becomes unavailable starting when deletion is scheduled.

sourceLabel: AWS Secrets Manager — Scheduled deletion and recovery window

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Reuse ciphertext with expired imported key material
prompt: Symmetric key material generated in your own HSM was imported into a single-Region KMS key. Only one type of material is associated with this key. After the material expired, the key entered PendingImport, and existing data could no longer be decrypted. An external copy of the original material is retained. Which procedure lets you continue using the existing key ID and ciphertext as they are?

choices.text: Create a new AWS KMS-generated key with the same alias and retry decrypting the old ciphertext.
choices.explanation: An alias is a reference name; it does not carry over the previous key ID or key material.

choices.text: Unconditionally reuse the same import token as before expiration and send different random material to the existing key.
choices.explanation: You must reimport the same material that expired, and obtain new wrapping information for the import procedure.

choices.text: Obtain a new wrapping key and import token for the existing KMS key, then reimport the same key material that was retained.
choices.explanation: This restores the original material corresponding to the existing ciphertext to the same KMS key.

choices.text: Use EnableKey alone to change PendingImport back to Enabled without importing new key material.
choices.explanation: EnableKey cannot resolve a state in which the material is absent.

source.label: AWS KMS — インポート済みキーマテリアルの再投入

learning.reason: Obtain a new wrapping key and import token for the existing KMS key, then reimport the same key material used before.
learning.concept: Expiration of imported material differs from deletion of the KMS key itself. Restoring the material requires an external copy with identical contents.

sourceLabel: AWS KMS — Reimporting imported key material

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Protect a database from replacement while retaining the old storage resource
prompt: You want to prevent an update to a CloudFormation stack from accidentally changing the logical ID of a production RDS resource or replacing it. At the same time, you want to allow a planned replacement of an EBS volume and retain the old volume until cutover verification is complete. Choose two settings required within the scope of updating the stack.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain on the RDS resource and do not set a stack policy.
choices.explanation: This may retain the old database, but it does not prevent the stack itself from replacing or deleting the RDS resource.

choices.text: Use a stack policy to explicitly deny Update:Replace and Update:Delete for the target RDS resource.
choices.explanation: This prevents the targeted RDS resource from being replaced or deleted by a stack update.

choices.text: Deny replacement of the EBS volume in the stack policy to preserve the old volume.
choices.explanation: The old volume remains, but the planned replacement cannot be performed either.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain on the EBS resource.
choices.explanation: This allows replacement with a new volume while retaining the old volume after replacement.

choices.text: Set only DeletionPolicy to Retain on the EBS resource.
choices.explanation: DeletionPolicy handles cases such as removal from the stack; UpdateReplacePolicy is needed to retain the old resource during an update replacement.

source.label: AWS CloudFormation — スタックポリシーによる更新制御

learning.reason: Use a stack policy to deny Update:Replace and Update:Delete for RDS. Allow EBS replacement and use UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain to keep the old volume.
learning.concept: The policy that blocks operations during a stack update and the treatment of an old resource after replacement are configured separately. Deletion operations that are needed should be managed separately from ordinary stack updates.

sourceLabel: AWS CloudFormation — Controlling updates with stack policies

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Roll back ECS for both startup failures and application errors
prompt: An ECS rolling update has a previously completed deployment available. In this update, you want the new version to stop and roll back automatically both if new tasks cannot start and if the ALB health checks pass but the application error rate for the new revision rises sharply. A CloudWatch alarm that measures only the new revision can be configured. Which settings are appropriate?

choices.text: Use only the circuit breaker and automatic rollback.
choices.explanation: When ECS health checks pass, the circuit breaker alone does not inspect the application's own error rate.

choices.text: Configure the circuit breaker and a CloudWatch alarm for the application error rate, and enable automatic rollback for both.
choices.explanation: Task startup failures and abnormal business metrics can each be treated as deployment failures.

choices.text: Configure only the application error-rate alarm. Do not use the circuit breaker, and treat missing metrics as normal.
choices.explanation: If tasks do not start, the application metrics may not be emitted, so the deployment may not be automatically treated as failed.

choices.text: Shorten the ALB health-check interval and do not use ECS automatic rollback.
choices.explanation: Changing how quickly health is evaluated does not add application-error monitoring or automatic recovery to a previous revision.

source.label: Amazon ECS — ローリング更新時の失敗検知

learning.reason: Use the circuit breaker for startup and health failures, and a CloudWatch alarm for application errors that health checks do not detect. Enable rollback for both mechanisms.
learning.concept: ECS can combine multiple failure detection methods. A previously completed deployment is required as the recovery target for automatic rollback after a failed rolling update.

sourceLabel: Amazon ECS — Failure detection during rolling updates

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Limit account-region locations and instances separately during a bulk diagnosis
prompt: Use Systems Manager Automation to run the same diagnostic on target EC2 instances across five accounts and three Regions in each account. To avoid overloading the data platform, you want to run at most two account-Region combinations at a time, with at most four EC2 instances within each combination. The distribution roles are already configured. Which settings are appropriate?

choices.text: Set location concurrency to 4 and resource concurrency to 2.
choices.explanation: This allows up to four combinations to proceed, with two instances in each, exceeding the requested limit on combinations.

choices.text: Set resource concurrency to 8 and leave the location setting at its default.
choices.explanation: Up to eight instances could run in each combination, so this guarantees neither the per-combination limit of four nor a limit on the number of locations.

choices.text: Set the location error threshold to 2 and the resource error threshold to 4.
choices.explanation: These are stop conditions based on failures, not concurrency limits for normal execution.

choices.text: Set location concurrency to 2 and resource concurrency within each location to 4.
choices.explanation: This independently limits the number of combinations in progress and the number of EC2 instances running in each combination.

source.label: AWS Systems Manager — 複数アカウント・リージョンでの実行制御

learning.reason: Set Automation location concurrency to 2 and resource concurrency to 4.
learning.concept: Location rate control, which limits the breadth of execution, differs from resource rate control, which limits the number of instances within each location.

sourceLabel: AWS Systems Manager — Execution controls across multiple accounts and Regions

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Measure the failure rate for the version reached through the production alias
prompt: A Lambda prod alias routes 95% of its traffic to v18 and 5% to v19. Integration tests in development also invoke v19 directly. For an alarm used for automatic rollback, you want to measure the failure rate only for invocations that actually ran v19 through prod. Which monitoring approach should you use?

choices.text: Monitor Errors using only FunctionName and divide by all invocation counts.
choices.explanation: This combines aliases, versions, and direct invocations, so it cannot isolate the target.

choices.text: Specify only prod as the Resource and aggregate Errors and Invocations.
choices.explanation: This limits the data to production traffic, but does not distinguish v18 from v19.

choices.text: Aggregate Errors and Invocations for the time series with the prod alias and ExecutedVersion=v19.
choices.explanation: This limits the data by both the alias and the version that actually ran.

choices.text: Specify only the v19 version as the resource, without limiting the alias used for the invocation.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to limit the data to invocations through prod. Specifying only the resource also cannot identify the version actually selected after routing through an alias.

source.label: AWS Lambda — メトリクスのディメンション

learning.reason: Calculate the failure rate from the total Errors and Invocations for prod with ExecutedVersion=v19.
learning.concept: With a weighted alias, requests that specify the same alias can run different versions. Keep the metric dimensions aligned, and decide how to handle small samples and missing data.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Separate read bandwidth for two processes consuming the same shard
prompt: For each shard in a Kinesis Data Streams stream processing order events, fraud detection and analytics read the same complete set of records. Each needs processing capacity of 1.3 MB per second per shard, and neither the producer's partitioning nor the destination can be changed. Which configuration prevents analytics reprocessing from consuming fraud detection's read bandwidth?

choices.text: Use the same KCL application name for both processes and add more workers to each.
choices.explanation: Workers in the same application divide shard processing among themselves, so both processes cannot receive all records independently.

choices.text: Shorten the GetRecords polling interval for both shared-throughput consumers.
choices.explanation: They share the same shard read limit, which cannot meet the combined requirement of 2.6 MB per second.

choices.text: Register each process as a separate enhanced fan-out consumer and subscribe both to the same shard.
choices.explanation: Read capacity is independent for each consumer, so both can receive the required throughput from each shard.

choices.text: Register only one consumer for enhanced fan-out and have two independent processes share its ARN.
choices.explanation: Dedicated throughput is allocated per registered consumer; sharing one registration does not provide two independent capacity allocations.

source.label: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams — 専用帯域のコンシューマー

learning.reason: Register a separate enhanced fan-out consumer for each process. Each registered consumer can individually use up to 2 MB per second per shard.
learning.concept: Even when consumers receive the same records, shared and dedicated reads differ in the unit over which limits are shared.

sourceLabel: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams — Consumers with dedicated throughput

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Partition events by tenant and date at delivery time
prompt: An existing Amazon Data Firehose stream receives events as plain JSON. Dynamic partitioning is disabled, and the stream delivers data to S3 in ingestion-time order. Going forward, you want to route records based on each record's tenantId and eventDate. You will not move existing data or maintain Lambda functions or file-reorganization jobs. You can switch the destination. Which migration is appropriate?

choices.text: Update the existing stream and add partition-key macros while leaving dynamic partitioning disabled.
choices.explanation: The feature must be enabled when the stream is created; extraction macros cannot be used on a stream where it is disabled.

choices.text: Create a new Firehose stream with dynamic partitioning enabled, and configure an S3 prefix that extracts both keys from the JSON.
choices.explanation: Delivery destinations can then be selected from record contents, without a separate process to move objects after delivery.

choices.text: Put a date in the existing stream's S3 prefix using a time macro, and assume the same configuration will also extract tenantId.
choices.explanation: Time macros do not extract arbitrary JSON attributes from a record.

choices.text: Add partition names with a Glue crawler after delivery and leave the existing objects under their original prefixes.
choices.explanation: Catalog registration alone cannot split individual records into new S3 paths.

source.label: Amazon Data Firehose — 動的パーティション分割の有効化

learning.reason: Create a new stream for S3 with dynamic partitioning enabled, use inline extraction to get record values from JSON, and use them in the destination prefix. Switch the source to the new stream.
learning.concept: The arrival time used in Firehose S3 object names serves a different purpose from a business date inside a record. Dynamic partitioning cannot be enabled later on a stream that was created with it disabled.

sourceLabel: Amazon Data Firehose — Enabling dynamic partitioning

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Update an analytics table while auditing its pre-correction state
prompt: A sales ledger is stored in an analytics table on S3. When an order is canceled, update or delete the row with the matching order ID, without exposing analysts to an intermediate state during a single SQL statement. For a defined retention period, query the table as it existed before a correction, and use the same table from Athena and a compatible Spark engine. Avoid manually replacing files. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Manage an Iceberg v2 table in the Glue Data Catalog, update rows in Athena, and retain the snapshots needed for auditing.
choices.explanation: This provides table-level snapshot isolation and lets you query both current and prior states.

choices.text: Use a standard external Parquet table, enable S3 Versioning, and update multiple files with SQL.
choices.explanation: S3 object versions do not provide a consistent table state or row-level transactions.

choices.text: Partition the external table by date and append correction data to a separate file, without changing users' SQL.
choices.explanation: Existing rows would remain in query results, and this would not provide table management that automatically applies corrections and cancellations.

choices.text: Use Athena CTAS to write all rows, replacing the old S3 objects in place each time.
choices.explanation: This requires replacing everything and does not manage intermediate changes or historical states at the table level.

source.label: Amazon Athena — Icebergの行更新とスナップショット

learning.reason: Manage a compatible Iceberg v2 table in the Glue Data Catalog and process changes with Athena transactions. Row-level changes create new snapshots, and prior states can be queried while they are retained.
learning.concept: Object versioning and table snapshots operate at different levels. When multiple engines update a table, align the catalog, version, and locking method.

sourceLabel: Amazon Athena — Iceberg row updates and snapshots

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Protect Both Legacy Consumers and Long-Term Replay
prompt: Kafka-compatible stream events use three schema generations. Because consuming applications are updated team by team, older readers must be able to read new events, and newer readers must be able to replay every generation retained within the retention period. In Glue Schema Registry, the first version is the starting point for compatibility checks, and all retained generations are checked. Which mode should you choose?

choices.text: Choose BACKWARD_ALL.
choices.explanation: It covers reading all old data with a newer reader, but does not check whether older consumers can read newer data.

choices.text: Choose FORWARD_ALL.
choices.explanation: It covers reading new data with all older consumers, but does not check whether a newer reader can read all old data.

choices.text: Choose FULL.
choices.explanation: It checks both directions, but checking both directions against every earlier generation requires ALL.

choices.text: Choose FULL_ALL.
choices.explanation: This setting checks compatibility in both directions against all earlier versions in scope.

source.label: AWS Glue — スキーマ互換性モード

learning.reason: Configure FULL_ALL to check both forward and backward compatibility of the schema being registered against every earlier version in scope.
learning.concept: Backward compatibility means a newer reader can read old data; forward compatibility means an older reader can read new data. ALL indicates checks against multiple earlier versions.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Read the Latest Sales Data from Compute in Another Account
prompt: A central team will share only part of an encrypted Redshift sales table with an encrypted analytics cluster in another account. Analysts must read the latest data using their department's compute resources, without using the central team's administrative credentials or a separate copy in S3. The provider selects the account to authorize, and the consumer selects the namespace to which the authorization applies. Choose two required actions.

choices.text: On the provider side, create a datashare for the target objects and authorize the consumer account for read access.
choices.explanation: The provider can specify the shared content and consumer, without copying data to separate storage.

choices.text: Periodically copy the sales data to S3 with UNLOAD, and have the consumer read it as an external table.
choices.explanation: Changes between scheduled copies are not reflected immediately, and this creates an additional copy that the requirements prohibit.

choices.text: On the consumer side, have an administrator associate the authorized datashare with the target consumer namespace and create a database for use.
choices.explanation: The consumer can select the target compute environment and query the data without distributing the central cluster's administrative credentials.

choices.text: Have analysts log in directly to the provider's database.
choices.explanation: This would use the central team's compute capacity and would not meet the requirement to process queries on the consumer's cluster.

choices.text: Use the same ARN for the encryption keys of both clusters; the datashare will then be registered automatically on both sides.
choices.explanation: Encryption is a prerequisite, but it does not replace provider authorization and consumer association.

source.label: Amazon Redshift — アカウントをまたぐデータ共有

learning.reason: The provider adds selected data to a datashare and authorizes the consumer account. The consumer administrator then associates the authorized share with the target namespace.
learning.concept: Cross-account datasharing requires provider authorization and consumer association. Both sides must be encrypted, but they do not need to use the same key.

category: コスト最適化
title: Reuse Existing Query Results Only for the Scheduled Dashboard
prompt: In one Athena workgroup, a scheduled dashboard that runs the same deterministic SELECT can tolerate aggregates up to 30 minutes old. A monthly close process that uses the same SELECT always needs the latest data. Both use the same catalog, database, and S3 result settings, and no managed setting on the target table prevents result reuse. Which approach reduces scan costs for the scheduled run?

choices.text: Set result reuse to 30 minutes for both queries and assume Athena detects data updates.
choices.explanation: Within the reuse period, you cannot rely on Athena to detect source updates, so the close process could receive stale results.

choices.text: Specify 30-minute result reuse only for the scheduled dashboard run, and run the monthly close normally each time.
choices.explanation: Only the scheduled run can reuse an eligible result in the same workgroup, while the close process can rescan the data.

choices.text: Put the scheduled and close queries in separate workgroups, then reuse the close process's latest result from the scheduled run.
choices.explanation: Result reuse does not work across workgroups.

choices.text: Override the S3 output location for each scheduled query and assume results are shared when the SQL is identical.
choices.explanation: Overriding the result settings at runtime does not meet the conditions for result reuse.

source.label: Amazon Athena — クエリ結果の再利用条件

learning.reason: Enable result reuse only for the scheduled dashboard run and set the maximum result age to 30 minutes. Do not enable reuse for the close process; it should read the source data again.
learning.concept: Athena does not check for source changes while a result is within its reuse period. When the same SQL serves multiple purposes, set freshness requirements for each use.

sourceLabel: Amazon Athena — Query result reuse conditions

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Trust CI Tokens Issued Only for One Production Branch
prompt: Assume a GitHub Actions workflow into an AWS deployment role. The only allowed source is the main branch of the portal repository in the workplace organization; GitHub Environments and custom subject formats are not used. Do not issue long-term keys, and reject other repositories using the same GitHub issuer or other branches of the same repository. Which AWS-side trust configuration should you use?

choices.text: Set only aud to sts.amazonaws.com and trust the GitHub issuer as a whole for the role.
choices.explanation: aud identifies the intended audience, but does not restrict the organization, repository, or branch.

choices.text: Allow all repositories and refs in the workplace organization through sub, and grant the role only minimal permissions.
choices.explanation: Limiting the role's permissions does not prevent another repository or branch from assuming the role.

choices.text: Register GitHub as a SAML provider and add a repository-name condition to AssumeRoleWithSAML.
choices.explanation: The workflow issues an OIDC token, which cannot be used to assume a role through a SAML assertion.

choices.text: Allow web identity role assumption from GitHub OIDC; require aud to equal sts.amazonaws.com and sub to exactly match repo:workplace/portal:ref:refs/heads/main.
choices.explanation: This restricts both the intended token audience and the repository and branch that can assume the role.

source.label: AWS IAM — GitHub OIDCのロール信頼ポリシー

learning.reason: Allow AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity from the GitHub OIDC provider, with aud restricted to sts.amazonaws.com and sub restricted to the specified value for the main branch.
learning.concept: Registering an OIDC provider identifies the issuer. The role must also evaluate the issuer's claims to determine which workload can assume that role.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM — GitHub OIDC role trust policy

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Deny ordinary HTTP access while preserving audit log delivery
prompt: An internal audit S3 bucket denies HTTP requests from employee roles and automated processing roles. It already allows audit log delivery for narrowly specified service principals, and that delivery must not be blocked when service-to-service calls omit forwarding-related authorization context. The exception must apply only to AWS service principals, and no new permissions may be added. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Add only an Allow conditioned on aws:SecureTransport being true, and leave the existing IAM permissions unchanged.
choices.explanation: A separate permission might allow HTTP, so this does not create an explicit denial.

choices.text: In the same Deny, require both aws:SecureTransport=false and aws:PrincipalIsAWSService=false.
choices.explanation: This denies HTTP from non-service principals and excludes AWS service principals from that Deny.

choices.text: Add a Deny that applies uniformly to services and people whenever aws:SecureTransport is absent.
choices.explanation: This could also deny legitimate service delivery when context is omitted.

choices.text: Add an Allow for all S3 operations whenever aws:PrincipalIsAWSService=true, without regard to the existing scope.
choices.explanation: This goes beyond excluding service principals from the Deny and grants new operation permissions.

source.label: Amazon S3 — 条件キーとサービスプリンシパル

learning.reason: Require both aws:SecureTransport=false and aws:PrincipalIsAWSService=false as conditions for the explicit Deny. Keep the existing service permission in a separate statement.
learning.concept: A Deny with network-related conditions can affect service-to-service calls. Narrowing a Deny’s scope does not independently grant permissions.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Condition keys and service principals

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restrict mount paths by IAM role on the same EFS file system
prompt: Two EC2 services in the same account need to read and write to separate directories on one EFS file system. Each service has a dedicated IAM role, and no other EFS client permissions are granted. The team wants to allow connections only through access points for the specified directories, without distinguishing clients by source IP. Choose two required controls.

choices.text: Create an access point for each service with its corresponding directory as the root, and mount using IAM authentication.
choices.explanation: This makes each access point’s path and the client principal evaluated by IAM explicit.

choices.text: Allow only DescribeFileSystems, an EFS API action, for each service’s IAM role.
choices.explanation: Read permission for a management API does not let an NFS client mount and write files.

choices.text: In the file system policy, restrict each role’s ClientMount and ClientWrite permissions to the corresponding AccessPointArn condition.
choices.explanation: Each role can perform the permitted NFS operations only through its assigned access point.

choices.text: Use only the mount target security groups to select each role’s root directory.
choices.explanation: Security groups control connection access; they do not assign visible NFS directories or IAM principals.

choices.text: Allow only ClientRootAccess in the policy and omit the access point requirement.
choices.explanation: ClientRootAccess does not replace mount and write permissions or restrict the path by service.

source.label: Amazon EFS — IAMポリシーでのアクセスポイント制御

learning.reason: Set up access points that specify each service’s root directory. Allow ClientMount and ClientWrite for each IAM role under the corresponding AccessPointArn condition, and use IAM authentication with the EFS mount helper.
learning.concept: An access point can specify the root exposed to an application. IAM authorizes the principal, while POSIX permissions also govern file operations in the directory.

sourceLabel: Amazon EFS — Access point control with IAM policies

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Enable IAM permissions for the same-account KMS key
prompt: The policy for an existing customer managed KMS key allows operations only to a central administration role and contains no statement delegating key-use permissions to IAM policies in the same account. An application role has already been allowed to use Decrypt on the target key by IAM, but decryption is denied. The central team does not want to list individual application roles in the key policy; it wants each IAM policy to grant only the permitted operations going forward. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Only add a Decrypt Allow to the application role, without changing the key policy.
choices.explanation: The key does not enable delegation to IAM, so adding more IAM permissions does not resolve the issue.

choices.text: Create a new KMS alias for every application that uses decryption.
choices.explanation: Adding aliases does not change the policy or delegation scope of the referenced key.

choices.text: Enable delegation of key-use permissions to IAM policies for the account in the key policy, and limit each application role’s IAM permissions to the required operations.
choices.explanation: The key policy allows IAM to grant permissions, while each role’s IAM policy manages the actions it may perform.

choices.text: List a role ARN in the key policy whenever a new application role is added.
choices.explanation: Explicit grants are possible, but this does not meet the requirement to manage application access through IAM policies alone.

source.label: AWS KMS — キーポリシーからIAMによる認可を可能にする

learning.reason: Add a statement to the key policy that enables delegation to IAM policies in the account for the relevant key operations. Grant the actual usage permissions in each IAM policy.
learning.concept: When IAM policies grant KMS operations, first check whether the target key allows delegation to IAM. The requirements can differ from one key to another, even within the same account.

sourceLabel: AWS KMS — Enable IAM authorization through the key policy

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Query external audit logs alongside AWS events in Security Lake
prompt: The organization’s Amazon Security Lake contains native AWS logs. It also wants to ingest raw JSON logs from an on-premises audit appliance so subscribers can query them using the same event classification. An adapter for transforming the external logs can be operated. Choose two required measures when sending data under the same event classification to a custom source.

choices.text: Send the JSON directly to the custom source, assuming Security Lake will convert any audit format to OCSF.
choices.explanation: A custom source must be converted to OCSF and a supported format before it is sent.

choices.text: Use the adapter to convert events to the corresponding OCSF class and schema, then output them as Parquet objects.
choices.explanation: This meets the requirements for subscribers to query data in a common format.

choices.text: Reuse the native S3 access log prefix for the external JSON and load it into the same table.
choices.explanation: External logs must use the write destination and data format assigned to the custom source.

choices.text: Use the registered custom source’s write role to deliver data to its assigned destination, partitioned by Region, account, and event date.
choices.explanation: Data can be cataloged using the specified permissions and partitioning.

choices.text: Assume that enabling AWS Glue crawler type inference will normalize raw JSON to OCSF field names without transforming it.
choices.explanation: A crawler discovers schemas and partitions; it does not convert arbitrary fields to OCSF.

source.label: Amazon Security Lake — カスタムソースの取り込み要件

learning.reason: Normalize the external source to OCSF and format it as Parquet with the source-side adapter. Deliver the data to the S3 prefix assigned to the custom source using the required partitions and permissions.
learning.concept: Security Lake manages transformation for supported native sources. For external raw data, the writer must meet the ingestion format and schema requirements.

sourceLabel: Amazon Security Lake — Custom source ingestion requirements

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Recover only the accidentally deleted rows while preserving new transactions
prompt: An operator error at 10:12 deleted some contract rows from an RDS for PostgreSQL database. Legitimate transactions have continued both before and after the deletion. 10:11 is within the RDS restore window and is earlier than the latest restorable time. You need to recover the deleted rows while keeping normal writes to the original database and its connection endpoint. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Create a separate instance from the latest restorable time after the deletion and retrieve the deleted rows.
choices.explanation: At a point after the deletion, the rows you need to recover are already gone.

choices.text: Perform a point-in-time recovery to just before the deletion, create a separate instance, verify the target rows, and merge them into production.
choices.explanation: The original production database can continue operating while only the missing rows are recovered.

choices.text: Create a complete restore from just before the deletion and immediately redirect all applications to it.
choices.explanation: This reverses the deletion, but loses legitimate transactions made after the restore point.

choices.text: Add a read replica to the production database after the deletion, promote it, and retrieve the rows that existed before the deletion.
choices.explanation: A newly added replica is not a restore target for an arbitrary point in the past.

source.label: Amazon RDS — 指定時点への復元

learning.reason: Choose a point just before the deletion and restore it to a separate instance. Verify the target rows there, then return only the necessary rows to the original database after checking consistency.
learning.concept: RDS point-in-time recovery creates a new instance; it does not roll back the original database in place. Plan separately for extracting the data and applying it to production.

sourceLabel: Amazon RDS — Restore to a specified point in time

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Determine the restore point available from a cross-account copy of continuous backups
prompt: AWS Backup takes continuous backups of an RDS DB instance and, with a supported copy configuration, stores them once a day in an isolated vault in another account. During a disaster exercise in which the source account is unavailable, you must rely only on the isolated copy to recover the state at 14:37. The most recent copy is a recovery point created at 00:00. Which assessment is accurate?

choices.text: You can specify 14:37 for continuous backup recovery in the isolated account. The copy time does not affect the restore range.
choices.explanation: A destination in another account cannot use the source's original continuous restore range.

choices.text: If you extend the retention period in the isolated vault, transaction logs after 00:00 will also be copied.
choices.explanation: Changing retention does not change the snapshot's point in time or type of protection.

choices.text: For auditing, copy the 00:00 recovery point again within the same isolated vault and set the copy completion time to 14:37.
choices.explanation: The time of the second copy does not change the original data content.

choices.text: You can restore from the available copy at 00:00, but you cannot specify 14:37 from that copy.
choices.explanation: The destination has a periodic snapshot, not the source backup's point-in-time recovery capability.

source.label: AWS Backup — 連続バックアップのコピーと復元

learning.reason: A recovery point copied to another account is a snapshot and does not inherit the source's point-in-time recovery range. With only the isolated copy available, recovery is limited to the copy point that exists there.
learning.concept: Continuous protection applies to the source recovery point. Evaluate the destination's recovery point objective based on the backup type and frequency that are copied.

sourceLabel: AWS Backup — Copying and restoring continuous backups

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Notify on replication delay for individual objects
prompt: Newly arriving audit objects are replicated across Regions between two versioned S3 buckets. Operations needs a configuration with an SLA for replication time, and wants objects that exceed 15 minutes to be sent to an investigative SQS queue with their identifiers. Avoid periodic comparisons of full object inventories. Choose two required settings.

choices.text: Configure S3 Replication Time Control on the existing replication rule.
choices.explanation: This provides an SLA for the replication time of eligible objects and lets you observe delays.

choices.text: Subscribe only to destination ObjectCreated events and treat them as detection of threshold breaches for objects that have not yet arrived.
choices.explanation: A destination object that has not been created cannot emit this notification.

choices.text: Send OperationMissedThreshold from S3 Event Notifications to the investigative SQS queue.
choices.explanation: This lets you receive a notification for an individual replication that exceeded the threshold.

choices.text: Use daily Batch Replication to deliver newly arriving objects.
choices.explanation: It does not provide a 15-minute threshold or an over-threshold event for the ongoing rule.

choices.text: Without RTC, create a CloudWatch alarm only for the aggregate number of objects not yet replicated.
choices.explanation: An aggregate value alone cannot notify you of the identifiers of the objects that exceeded the threshold.

source.label: Amazon S3 — Replication Time Controlの通知

learning.reason: Enable S3 RTC on the ongoing replication rule and subscribe to OperationMissedThreshold notifications. This supports identifying objects that exceed the 15-minute threshold.
learning.concept: Cross-Region replication is asynchronous. The SLA is not a guarantee that every object will be replicated on time, so monitor individual threshold breaches as well.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Replication Time Control notifications

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Distinguish DMS capture-side and apply-side lag before cutover
prompt: AWS DMS is running CDC after a full load. For 20 minutes after a load test, CDCLatencySource has remained steady at around 2 seconds, while CDCLatencyTarget alone has kept increasing beyond 300 seconds. You will cut over production after confirming that writes have caught up on the target. What should you investigate first?

choices.text: Assume capture of source change logs is 300 seconds behind and only increase log retention on the source database.
choices.explanation: CDCLatencySource is low; the high latency observed is on the target side.

choices.text: Immediately restart the task from the full load.
choices.explanation: A restart does not diagnose the apply-side bottleneck and increases the time to cutover.

choices.text: Check target writes, locks, and I/O, as well as the apply-side processing capacity of DMS.
choices.explanation: High target latency with low source latency is grounds to prioritize the apply side.

choices.text: Since the source side is at 2 seconds, conclude that replication has caught up and cut over production.
choices.explanation: Changes may remain unapplied on the target; the source-side state alone does not satisfy the cutover condition.

source.label: AWS DMS — CDCレイテンシーの切り分け

learning.reason: Changes are being captured from the source, but applying them to the target is lagging. Check target database locks, storage performance, write load, and DMS apply processing.
learning.concept: Reading the two CDC latency metrics together helps determine whether to investigate change-log capture or the application of captured data first.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Verifying all files after an incremental transfer, including unchanged files
prompt: Most of the data has been copied from an on-premises NFS file system to EFS. During the final cutover, writes by the application to both locations can be stopped. In the final run, you want DataSync to transfer only the changes and then verify that both sides of the scope match, including existing files that were not copied in this run. You will not use a manifest. Which configuration is required?

choices.text: Use Basic mode to transfer changes, then use POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT to verify all files in scope after the transfer.
choices.explanation: This copies only the changes while also including previously copied files in the final verification.

choices.text: Use ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED in Basic mode to compare only the changes.
choices.explanation: Existing files that are not transferred in this run are not included in the comparison.

choices.text: Switch to Enhanced mode and select POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT.
choices.explanation: Enhanced mode does not support this VerifyMode combination.

choices.text: Transfer the changes and set VerifyMode to NONE.
choices.explanation: Checks are performed during transfer, but there is no post-transfer verification that compares previously transferred files.

source.label: AWS DataSync — 転送と整合性検証モード

learning.reason: Use Basic mode to transfer changes and set VerifyMode to POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT. Stop writes until DataSync has checked all in-scope files on both sides after the transfer.
learning.concept: The transfer scope and the post-transfer verification scope are separate settings. It is difficult to confirm synchronization while writes continue.

sourceLabel: AWS DataSync — Transfer and data consistency verification modes

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Returning changes made on the standby EFS file system to the original
prompt: During an outage, you used a read-only EFS replica, deleted the original replication configuration, and made the standby writable. New data created during that time is on the standby. The original EFS file system has recovered, and both file systems have compatible encryption settings. You can pause writes during cutover. You want to preserve the changes made on the standby before returning to the original Region. Which action is appropriate?

choices.text: Resynchronize from the original EFS to the standby in the same direction used before the outage, assuming that changes on the standby will also be applied to the original automatically.
choices.explanation: EFS replication aligns data in the configured direction, so this direction could overwrite changes made on the standby.

choices.text: Restore mounts to the original EFS, then make the standby a replica again in the direction used before the outage.
choices.explanation: This would resume production use without the latest data being on the original EFS.

choices.text: Create a replication configuration with the standby as the source, then use the original EFS for writes at the same time without checking the synchronization status.
choices.explanation: The replication destination is read-only, and this would not establish whether the data is synchronized.

choices.text: Replicate from the standby EFS to the original EFS. Stop writes, confirm the final synchronization, delete the replication configuration, and then resume service on the original EFS.
choices.explanation: This applies post-outage changes to the original. After deleting the replication configuration, the original can be writable before connections are switched back.

source.label: Amazon EFS — レプリカの利用とフェイルバック

learning.reason: Configure reverse replication with the current standby as the source and the original EFS as the destination. After confirming final synchronization, delete the reverse replication configuration and switch connections back once the original EFS is writable.
learning.concept: Choose as the replication source the side whose data you want to preserve. Returning directly to the pre-outage direction could overwrite the standby with the original's data.

sourceLabel: Amazon EFS — Using a replica and failing back

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Ensuring existing ActiveMQ clients reconnect after an Availability Zone failure
prompt: A critical business application uses ActiveMQ and persistent JMS queues, and the client protocol cannot be changed. You are migrating to managed Amazon MQ. After broker maintenance or a single-AZ failure, clients must reconnect to a broker in another AZ and use the data stored there. The connection settings of the existing JMS library can be changed. Select two required settings.

choices.text: Use a single-instance broker and only increase the number of connection attempts in the JMS client.
choices.explanation: Retries alone do not provide a broker and data in another AZ.

choices.text: Use an Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ deployment option that places two brokers in active/standby mode in separate AZs.
choices.explanation: This configuration can fail over to the standby during maintenance or an AZ failure.

choices.text: Create two independent single-instance brokers and assume that queues with the same name automatically share their contents.
choices.explanation: Independent brokers do not automatically share persistent data, even when their queues have the same name.

choices.text: Pin the JMS client to only one of the wire-level protocol endpoints.
choices.explanation: If the other endpoint becomes active during a failure, the client will not try to connect to it.

choices.text: Specify both provided endpoints as candidates in the client's Failover Transport.
choices.explanation: The client can select the endpoint that is currently active.

source.label: Amazon MQ — ActiveMQブローカーの高可用性

learning.reason: Configure ActiveMQ in a multi-AZ active/standby setup, and include both provided protocol endpoints as connection candidates in the Failover Transport.
learning.concept: Check both broker-side replication or failover and the client-side mechanism for trying the active connection endpoint.

sourceLabel: Amazon MQ — ActiveMQ broker high availability

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Enabling private routes between two existing hubs
prompt: There are existing Transit Gateways in Tokyo and Virginia, and the spoke CIDRs in each environment do not overlap. The route tables used by both Transit Gateways already have routes to the spoke CIDRs in their own Regions. Transit Gateway peering has been approved to allow bidirectional communication between multiple spokes in the two Regions. Which route configuration is required to start forwarding traffic?

choices.text: Enable route propagation for the peering on both Transit Gateways, and add routes for the remote CIDRs only to the spoke VPCs.
choices.explanation: Peering does not automatically propagate remote CIDRs, so the Transit Gateways will not have a next hop.

choices.text: Add a static route for the remote CIDRs to the Tokyo Transit Gateway, where traffic originates, and let return traffic be forwarded automatically in the reverse direction over the same peering.
choices.explanation: Route lookup is also required on the remote side of a peering connection, and routes to the return CIDRs are not created automatically.

choices.text: In each Transit Gateway route table, add a static route for the remote CIDRs with the peering attachment as the next hop, and configure each VPC to route the remote CIDRs to its local Transit Gateway.
choices.explanation: For both outbound and return traffic, the VPCs and Transit Gateways can explicitly select the next hop.

choices.text: Enable propagation of the local spokes on both Transit Gateways, and put only a default route pointing to the Transit Gateway in each VPC.
choices.explanation: Propagating local spokes does not add the remote Transit Gateway's CIDRs as routes through the peering attachment.

source.label: Transit Gateway — ピアリングアタッチメント

learning.reason: In each Transit Gateway, register routes for the remote Region's CIDRs in the route table that receives traffic from the spokes, and direct those routes to the peering attachment. Configure the corresponding routes for remote destinations in the VPCs as well.
learning.concept: Distinguish propagation from VPC attachments to a Transit Gateway from static routes to remote CIDRs through Transit Gateway peering.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Add a New Internal Network to a Split-Tunnel VPN
prompt: AWS Client VPN uses split tunneling, so employees’ general internet traffic exits directly from their homes. You want to make a new internal CIDR reachable from the VPC available only to the existing employee group. The VPC return route and the destination security group are already configured, and the change will be made during a window when connections can be re-established. Which two actions are required on the endpoint?

choices.text: Add 0.0.0.0/0 to the Client VPN endpoint and route the new internal destination through the default route.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to keep general internet traffic local, and adding a default route with split tunneling can cause connectivity issues.

choices.text: Add the target internal CIDR to the Client VPN endpoint route table.
choices.explanation: When clients reconnect, the route for the target destination is distributed, and that traffic is sent through the tunnel.

choices.text: If the internal CIDR is present only in the route table of the VPC target subnet, clients also receive that route.
choices.explanation: Routes are distributed to clients from the Client VPN endpoint route table, not from the VPC subnet route table.

choices.text: Create a Client VPN authorization rule for the new CIDR and limit access to the employee group.
choices.explanation: The endpoint can control which users are allowed to connect to the new CIDR.

choices.text: Apply the authorization rule for the new CIDR to all users and rely on existing VPN connection authentication instead.
choices.explanation: Being authenticated is different from being authorized to access a destination only as a specific group.

source.label: AWS Client VPN — エンドポイントのルート

learning.reason: Add a route for the internal CIDR to the Client VPN route table, then limit the authorization rule for that CIDR to the employee group.
learning.concept: With split tunneling, endpoint routes are added to clients when they connect. Route distribution does not itself grant access to a destination, and changing the table requires connections to be re-established.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Constrain the Route and Access Scope for Secrets Manager
prompt: An application running in private subnets across multiple AZs reads secrets from Secrets Manager using the standard regional hostname. You must not add an outbound default route to the subnets, and calls that use this route must be limited to retrieving the target secret. The application's IAM role also allows retrieval of that secret. Which configuration is best?

choices.text: Configure a Secrets Manager interface endpoint with private DNS, and use the endpoint policy to allow only retrieval of the target secret.
choices.explanation: This preserves the standard hostname while connecting through private IPs, and limits the actions and resources allowed over that route.

choices.text: Disable private DNS for the Secrets Manager interface endpoint and use the endpoint policy to constrain access to the target secret.
choices.explanation: The route can be constrained, but the standard regional hostname will not automatically resolve to the endpoint's private IPs.

choices.text: Create an STS interface endpoint and limit only the role policy to the target secret.
choices.explanation: This provides a private route for obtaining tokens, but it does not carry Secrets Manager API traffic.

choices.text: Configure a Secrets Manager interface endpoint with private DNS and leave the endpoint at its default full-access policy.
choices.explanation: This meets the network requirement, but does not restrict the resources and operations available to other principals using this route.

source.label: AWS Secrets Manager — VPCエンドポイント

learning.reason: Create a Secrets Manager interface endpoint in each AZ and enable private DNS. Use the endpoint policy to limit access to GetSecretValue and the target ARN.
learning.concept: Private DNS directs the SDK's standard hostname to the endpoint inside the VPC. The endpoint policy adds a restriction on the route and is evaluated separately from IAM permissions.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Decouple Analytics While Preserving Capacity After Promotion
prompt: An Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 cluster has a read/write writer and two Serverless readers in different AZs. Reader 1 is the preferred failover target, and you want it to track the writer's capacity as the writer's load increases. Reader 2 is dedicated to reporting, already uses a dedicated endpoint, and must be able to scale down independently even when the writer is busy. Which promotion tiers should you configure?

choices.text: Set Reader 1 to tier 0 and Reader 2 to tier 1.
choices.explanation: Both readers track the writer, so the reporting reader cannot scale down independently of the writer.

choices.text: Set Reader 1 to tier 2 and Reader 2 to tier 3.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes their order, but Reader 1 also sets capacity independently and is not guaranteed to track the writer.

choices.text: Set Reader 1 to tier 2 and Reader 2 to tier 0.
choices.explanation: This makes the reporting reader the first promotion target, and it also tracks the writer's capacity.

choices.text: Set Reader 1 to tier 0 and Reader 2 to tier 2.
choices.explanation: The preferred promotion target tracks the writer's capacity, while the reporting reader can scale independently within the cluster's capacity range.

source.label: Amazon Aurora — Serverlessのスケーリング

learning.reason: Set the failover reader to tier 0 and the reporting reader to tier 2. Serverless readers at tier 0 or 1 track the writer's capacity as a minimum, while those at tier 2 or higher scale independently.
learning.concept: Promotion tiers for Serverless readers affect both failover priority and whether their capacity tracks the writer's.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Connect to a Private REST API by Its Standard Name over Direct Connect
prompt: You want only on-premises servers to connect to an existing API Gateway private REST API over an established Direct Connect connection. The target VPC has an execute-api interface endpoint, and connections using the standard DNS name from within the VPC are working. On premises, you must use the same standard name, and the API must accept only requests that pass through the approved endpoint. Which two changes are required?

choices.text: Use a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint and forward execute-api queries from on-premises DNS.
choices.explanation: This lets on-premises clients use the private DNS response for the standard name provided by the VPC.

choices.text: Configure a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint to receive DNS queries from on premises.
choices.explanation: Outbound endpoints forward queries from the VPC to external networks; they do not receive queries from remote networks into the VPC.

choices.text: Restrict the REST API resource policy to the approved endpoint using aws:SourceVpce.
choices.explanation: The API resource policy can allow only requests that pass through the approved VPCE.

choices.text: Replace the private REST API with a public regional REST API and use WAF to restrict on-premises source IPs.
choices.explanation: Although this can restrict allowed sources, it does not meet the requirement to connect to the existing private API over Direct Connect.

choices.text: Disable private DNS for execute-api and call the API from on premises by using the endpoint-specific name.
choices.explanation: Reachability might still be possible, but this does not meet the requirement for on-premises servers to use the standard name.

source.label: API Gateway — プライベートAPIの呼び出し

learning.reason: Conditionally forward on-premises DNS to a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint, and restrict the REST API resource policy to the approved VPCE.
learning.concept: Direct Connect provides network connectivity, and Resolver resolves the VPC's private DNS name. The resource policy further limits the API to the approved endpoint.

sourceLabel: API Gateway — Invoking a Private API

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Connect order intake directly to a fixed queue
prompt: An authenticated HTTP API must enqueue delivery-creation requests in an existing SQS standard queue, preserving the request body, and return an acceptance response. The operations team fixes the destination queue; clients cannot choose it. Do not change the existing workers or add compute resources between the API and the queue. Which configuration should be combined? Choose two.

choices.text: Map the QueueUrl request header to SQS-SendMessage.
choices.explanation: This passes the URL supplied by the client to the integration instead of fixing the destination URL in the API definition.

choices.text: Specify the queue's HTTPS URL in an HTTP proxy integration and relay the request as is.
choices.explanation: A simple HTTP relay does not perform the SQS operation selection, parameter configuration, and authentication provided by an AWS service integration.

choices.text: In an SQS-SendMessage integration, set QueueUrl to a fixed value and MessageBody to the request body.
choices.explanation: This sends the request body to the existing queue without allowing the requester to choose the queue.

choices.text: Start a worker from a separate EventBridge rule in addition to API Gateway, and have the worker send the message to SQS.
choices.explanation: This requires a new processing path or a change to the worker, and it does not send the message directly to SQS when the request is accepted.

choices.text: Configure an integration role that API Gateway can assume and that allows only sqs:SendMessage on the target queue.
choices.explanation: This limits the permissions the integration uses to call the AWS service to sending messages to the target queue.

source.label: API Gateway — HTTP APIのAWSサービス統合

learning.reason: Configure the HTTP API route with an SQS-SendMessage integration, set the destination URL to a static value, and map the request body to MessageBody. Give API Gateway an execution role with only SendMessage permission on the target queue.
learning.concept: An HTTP API can invoke an AWS service action directly. To fix the delivery path, keep the request body separate from the destination value that callers cannot change.

sourceLabel: API Gateway — AWS service integrations for HTTP APIs

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Distinguish evidence of use from denied attempts
prompt: A CloudTrail trail records the relevant events for the past 90 days. While narrowing permissions for an operations role, the team sees in IAM service last accessed data that there was a recent attempt to access a service, but wants to know whether the API was actually allowed or the attempt failed. Which evidence should the team use?

choices.text: If service last accessed data shows a timestamp, treat the latest recorded call as successful.
choices.explanation: Service last accessed data includes denied attempts, so a timestamp alone does not show whether the call succeeded.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to match the role session and target API, then check the event's error information.
choices.explanation: The record of the actual operation shows whether the call was denied.
