choices.text: Evaluate today's effective policies with the IAM policy simulator and apply the result to calls from the past 90 days.
choices.explanation: This can evaluate authorization under current conditions, but it cannot establish the actual outcome under past policies or request conditions.

choices.text: Retrieve the role's service usage outcomes from the IAM credential report.
choices.explanation: The credential report shows the status of IAM user credentials; it is not evidence of the outcomes of individual API operations made by role sessions.

source.label: IAM — 最終アクセス情報の読み方

learning.reason: Find the target API event made by the relevant role session in CloudTrail and check whether it succeeded or was denied.
learning.concept: IAM service last accessed data helps narrow down candidates, but it includes denied attempts. Use the original audit event to determine whether access was actually granted.

sourceLabel: IAM — How to read last accessed data

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Block only IAM changes that expand permissions in CI
prompt: A team is refining IAM identity-based policies. Before deployment, CI must check that changes to conditions or resource statements do not cause the proposed version to allow actions that the current version did not allow. Which method compares the current and proposed policy documents without requiring the team to enumerate affected APIs or resources for each test?

choices.text: Run ValidatePolicy on the proposed policy alone and allow it if there are no syntax errors or general security findings.
choices.explanation: This can validate the policy, but it does not compare the allowed permissions against the current version.

choices.text: Check only the prohibited APIs listed with CheckAccessNotGranted.
choices.explanation: This checks only the specified targets and cannot evaluate all new access relative to the current version.

choices.text: Compare the proposed and current JSON documents and allow the change if the number of existing Allow statements does not increase.
choices.explanation: A change can expand conditions or resources and increase permissions without adding statements.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer's CheckNoNewAccess to evaluate the proposed policy against the current version as the reference.
choices.explanation: This evaluates permissions to check whether the proposed policy grants access that is absent from the reference version.

source.label: IAM Access Analyzer — カスタムポリシーチェック

learning.reason: Pass the current and proposed versions to IAM Access Analyzer's CheckNoNewAccess and block changes that grant new access.
learning.concept: Syntax and recommendations from ordinary policy validation are different from comparing the permissions a policy grants against a specific reference policy.

sourceLabel: IAM Access Analyzer — Custom policy checks

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Migrate a shared bucket from legacy ACLs to policy management
prompt: Multiple accounts write to an existing central S3 bucket. The bucket ACL currently grants permissions to other accounts, and some sources attach their own ACLs when uploading. The goal is for the central account to own all existing and new objects while continuing approved writes. Which actions are required? Choose two.

choices.text: Allow only the required sources in the bucket policy and remove external grants from the bucket ACL.
choices.explanation: This moves the approved write permissions from ACLs to the policy and meets a prerequisite for switching to Bucket owner enforced.

choices.text: Leave the external grants in the bucket ACL unchanged and switch Object Ownership to Bucket owner enforced.
choices.explanation: The setting change fails if the bucket ACL still grants permissions to other accounts.

choices.text: Set Bucket owner preferred and assume that this disables all object ACLs, including those on existing objects.
choices.explanation: With preferred, ACLs remain enabled, and ownership of all existing objects is not transferred automatically.

choices.text: Bulk-copy the existing files to change their owners, then leave later writes from sources using Object writer.
choices.explanation: Copying can address the existing files, but future cross-account writes will not be owned by the central account.

choices.text: Update sources to omit ACLs or use bucket-owner-full-control, then switch to Bucket owner enforced.
choices.explanation: This avoids write errors from incompatible ACLs and puts all objects under the bucket owner's control.

source.label: Amazon S3 — ACLを無効化する前提条件

learning.reason: Move the necessary ACL permissions to a policy and remove external grants from the bucket ACL. Update sources to omit ACLs or use bucket-owner-full-control, then switch to Bucket owner enforced.
learning.concept: For an existing bucket, first move external permissions from the bucket ACL. After ACLs are disabled, writes that use incompatible ACLs are rejected.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Prerequisites for disabling ACLs

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Apply a Consistent Backup Policy to New Members Without Exceptions
prompt: In the organization’s production OU, back up EC2 instances and EBS volumes with the target tag every day and retain backups for 35 days. Organization-integrated CloudFormation StackSets can deploy a role and a backup vault with the same names to existing and new member accounts. How can you automate account onboarding without allowing member account owners to edit the backup plan independently? Choose two.

choices.text: Restrict backup API calls with an SCP and define the daily schedule and 35-day retention in the SCP.
choices.explanation: An SCP limits available permissions; it cannot distribute an execution schedule or backup plan.

choices.text: Attach an AWS Organizations backup policy to the production OU and inherit a plan that includes the target resources and retention period.
choices.explanation: This distributes common rules to member accounts and reduces the need to maintain independent backup plans in each account.

choices.text: Register a delegated administrator for AWS Backup and create the vault and plan only in that account.
choices.explanation: Central management is useful, but registration alone does not make member accounts inherit the plan or create the required resources.

choices.text: Use StackSets to create the IAM role referenced by the plan and the backup vault in each member account in the target Regions.
choices.explanation: The organization policy does not create IAM roles or vaults, so the required prerequisites must be made available in each account.

choices.text: Use a tag policy to validate backup tags and distribute the retention period through that policy.
choices.explanation: A tag policy can check tag consistency, but it does not define backup schedules or retention periods.

source.label: AWS Organizations — バックアップポリシーの構文と前提

learning.reason: Attach a backup policy to the production OU and configure its Region, tags, role, vault, frequency, and retention. Deploy the role and vault to member accounts separately.
learning.concept: An effective backup policy managed by the organization is inherited by member accounts. The referenced role and vault must be created separately.

sourceLabel: AWS Organizations — Backup Policy Syntax and Prerequisites

category: コスト最適化
title: Maintain Key Permissions While Reducing KMS Calls
prompt: A system writes a large number of small objects to S3 and currently uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key. The KMS key policy includes a condition on object ARNs in the target bucket in its encryption context. Keep existing data readable, preserve access control through S3 policies, and reduce KMS requests for future writes while keeping the same KMS key. Choose two required actions.

choices.text: Keep SSE-KMS and the current key, and apply an S3 Bucket Key to new objects.
choices.explanation: Using a bucket-level key can reduce the required KMS API calls.

choices.text: Keep SSE-KMS, create a new KMS key, and enable automatic KMS key rotation.
choices.explanation: Rotating key material does not reduce the frequency of KMS requests during encryption, and this also fails the requirement to keep the same key.

choices.text: Keep the existing object ARN condition and also allow the target bucket ARN in the encryption context.
choices.explanation: This accepts the context used with Bucket Keys while retaining the existing condition for data encrypted before the change.

choices.text: When enabling the Bucket Key, replace the encryption-context condition with a condition for only the target bucket ARN.
choices.explanation: The new condition would be met, but it would remove the condition needed for objects encrypted using the previous method.

choices.text: Change the bucket’s default encryption to DSSE-KMS and apply the same S3 Bucket Key.
choices.explanation: S3 Bucket Keys are not supported for DSSE-KMS.

source.label: Amazon S3 — S3バケットキーによるSSE-KMSのコスト削減

learning.reason: Enable S3 Bucket Keys for new objects. Allow the target bucket ARN in the KMS key policy’s encryption context while retaining the condition needed to read existing objects.
learning.concept: S3 Bucket Keys use the bucket ARN in the encryption context. Objects already encrypted without a Bucket Key are not rewritten automatically.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Reduce SSE-KMS Costs with S3 Bucket Keys

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Tie DNS Failover to the Health of a Private Database
prompt: A two-Region ordering API has a single standard-resolution CloudWatch metric derived from connectivity checks to a private database. The primary should fail over to the standby through DNS if it cannot reach the database for two minutes, even while the ALB targets remain healthy. The standby has been tested. Which configuration can you use with Route 53 health checks?

choices.text: Enable Evaluate Target Health on the primary alias so that only responses from the ALB targets are evaluated.
choices.explanation: The ALB health information does not include the private database connectivity result, so it cannot detect the stated database failure condition.

choices.text: Specify a high-resolution alarm based on 10-second database connectivity metrics in the Route 53 health check.
choices.explanation: Route 53 health checks that use CloudWatch alarms do not support high-resolution metrics.

choices.text: Specify an M-out-of-N alarm for the database connectivity metric that triggers when any two of five periods breach the threshold.
choices.explanation: This does not test for two consecutive minutes, and Route 53 does not support alarms where M and N differ.

choices.text: In the same account as the health check, create an alarm that evaluates a standard-resolution database connectivity metric once per minute for two consecutive periods, then use it for the primary health check.
choices.explanation: The alarm for a supported single metric lets the database failure affect the health evaluation of the primary record.

source.label: Route 53 — CloudWatchアラームのデータストリーム

learning.reason: In the same account as the health check, create an alarm for the standard-resolution database connectivity metric that detects two consecutive breaching periods, then associate it with the primary failover record.
learning.concept: A health check that specifies a CloudWatch alarm evaluates the alarm’s data stream. The alarm must meet Route 53 requirements, including support for standard-resolution metrics.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Validate a Point-in-Time DynamoDB Restore Before Switching Traffic
prompt: A DynamoDB inventory table must be restored to just before an incorrect bulk update. PITR was enabled before the incident with 35 days of retention, and the desired time is within the restorable range. Keep the post-update data for investigation and use the restored table only after approval. The application also uses DynamoDB Streams for notifications. Which two actions should you take?

choices.text: Use PITR to overwrite the existing table by specifying its current name, preserving the same stream ARN.
choices.explanation: PITR creates a new table; it cannot restore data directly into an existing table.

choices.text: Restore to a table with a different name at the desired time and preserve the original table for investigation.
choices.explanation: This allows you to validate the pre-update state separately from the current state.

choices.text: Configure Streams on the restored table, update consumers to read from the new stream, and switch the application to the new table.
choices.explanation: Reconfiguring the required features on the new table and directing the application and stream consumers to the correct resources enables a controlled cutover.

choices.text: Add a replica Region with Global Tables, which rolls back to the specified restore time regardless of when the replica is added.
choices.explanation: Creating a replica is not a restore operation that selects a past point in time.

choices.text: Disable PITR and enable it again to reset the start of the restorable range to a time before the incident.
choices.explanation: After PITR is disabled and re-enabled, the previous history is not immediately available for restore, so restorable history is lost.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — PITRで新しいテーブルへ復元

learning.reason: Use PITR to restore to a table with a different name. Validate the restored data, then configure the required Streams settings and switch consumers and application references before using the new table.
learning.concept: PITR does not overwrite the source table. Restoring data and reconfiguring connections to the new environment are separate tasks.

sourceLabel: Amazon DynamoDB — Restore to a New Table with PITR

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Planned Migration of MySQL Writes to Another Region
prompt: A planned migration of RDS for MySQL to another Region is required. The encrypted cross-Region read replica in the destination Region is already used for audit reads. A brief write outage is acceptable during the cutover, and every transaction committed before the outage must be migrated. After the migration, the two Regions must not accept independent writes. In what order should the work be performed?

choices.text: Keep writing to the source instance, promote the destination, and then switch the connection endpoint in Route 53.
choices.explanation: Transactions would continue to reach the old instance after replication is detached, leaving updates that are not reflected in the destination.

choices.text: Disable read_only on the destination read replica, move writes to it while replication remains in place, and then promote it.
choices.explanation: Allowing replication and new writes on the destination to coexist could cause unintended overwrites or inconsistencies between the two sides.

choices.text: Stop writes to the source, confirm that the replica has caught up through the final commit, promote the destination, and then switch the connection.
choices.explanation: This completes replication of changes from the source before detaching the replica, so only one instance is used as the system of record.

choices.text: Restore the latest source snapshot in the destination and switch the connection while writes continue on the source after the snapshot was taken.
choices.explanation: There is no step to bring transactions committed after the snapshot into the restored destination.

source.label: Amazon RDS — リードレプリカの独立インスタンスへの昇格

learning.reason: Stop writes to the source, confirm that changes through the final commit have been replicated, and promote the destination replica. Switch the application's write connection after promotion is complete.
learning.concept: Replication to a cross-Region read replica is asynchronous, and promotion detaches it from replication. Stop writes and confirm that the replica has caught up before promotion.

sourceLabel: Amazon RDS — Promoting a Read Replica to Be a Standalone DB Instance

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Apply Every Approved Change in Arrival Order
prompt: Schema changes to a payment platform depend on the immediately preceding intermediate state. In a single CodePipeline, every execution that passes testing and is approved must proceed to production in the order it reached the stage entrance. Subsequent source retrieval and testing may continue while an execution awaits approval, but multiple executions must not modify production concurrently. How should the pipeline be configured without adding a queue or lock outside the pipeline?

choices.text: Set V2 to SUPERSEDED mode and place the approval at the start of the production stage.
choices.explanation: Approval controls progression into that stage, but it does not change the behavior in which a newer execution replaces an older one waiting at the entrance.

choices.text: Set V2 to QUEUED mode and process each change in the same production stage.
choices.explanation: Executions waiting before the production stage proceed in arrival order, and another execution cannot enter while that stage is processing.

choices.text: Set V2 to PARALLEL mode and place a manual approval inside the production stage.
choices.explanation: Approvals occur independently for each execution, and the pipeline does not prevent out-of-order approvals or concurrent executions in the same stage.

choices.text: Keep V1, disable the production stage entrance, and re-enable it when changes may proceed.
choices.explanation: Enabling stage transitions does not guarantee the order of pending releases, and V1 does not support QUEUED mode.

source.label: CodePipeline — 実行モード

learning.reason: Choose QUEUED mode in V2. Later executions do not enter a production stage that is locked by another execution; they wait their turn at the stage entrance.
learning.concept: The entire pipeline does not need to be limited to one execution at a time. A per-stage queue and lock prevent conflicts in the same stage and stop waiting executions from overtaking one another.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Retain Build-Level Test Results for Long-Term Audits
prompt: CodeBuild validates medical-device management software and sends JUnit XML files to an existing report group. Developers view recent results in the CodeBuild reports console. Auditors need to independently reanalyze individual failed test cases from any build from one year ago using BI. Which configuration meets this need without adding an external transfer process for each build?

choices.text: Extend CodeBuild log retention and search the logs for each build's final status.
choices.explanation: Log retention does not affect report expiration, and a final status alone is insufficient to reanalyze individual failed cases.

choices.text: Share the same report group across accounts and open historical reports from the auditor account.
choices.explanation: Sharing reports does not extend their retention period, and expired results cannot be viewed by the recipient account either.

choices.text: Store CodeBuild EventBridge state-change events in S3.
choices.explanation: State-change events contain build information, but not the details of every test case in the JUnit report.

choices.text: Export the report group's raw data to S3 and configure the retention period on the bucket.
choices.explanation: Use CodeBuild reports for recent checks and reanalyze the JUnit XML retained in S3 for historical audits.

source.label: CodeBuild — テストレポート

learning.reason: Export the JUnit files from the report group to S3 and use a storage policy to meet the audit retention period. Use the CodeBuild console for recent checks.
learning.concept: CodeBuild reports have a retention period. The original data files exported to S3 can be retained independently of CodeBuild's expiration period.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Update Nodes Only the Day After the Scheduled Maintenance
prompt: Distribute an internal CA bundle to AWS Systems Manager managed nodes with State Manager on the day after the second Tuesday of each month. Create the association earlier, during a weekday daytime, but do not change any nodes immediately after registration. Which settings should be combined without adding an external scheduler or date-calculation code? Choose two.

choices.text: Set a cron schedule based on the second Tuesday and a one-day schedule offset on the association.
choices.explanation: A base date and relative day count can represent the requirement, even though the following Wednesday is sometimes the second Wednesday and sometimes the third.

choices.text: Set the association to a 30-day rate and count from the previous scheduled date.
choices.explanation: The interval between second Tuesdays varies by month, so a fixed number of days cannot represent the following day.

choices.text: Specify the second Wednesday and do not use a schedule offset.
choices.explanation: When the month begins on a Wednesday, the day after the second Tuesday is the third Wednesday.

choices.text: Register a cron schedule for the second Tuesday and set the maximum number of concurrent executions to one.
choices.explanation: The concurrency limit caps how many targets are changed at once; it does not affect an immediate run on registration or shift the base date.

choices.text: Enable ApplyOnlyAtCronInterval so the association does not start until its scheduled execution time.
choices.explanation: This satisfies the offset's prerequisite and prevents an immediate run when the association is created.

source.label: Systems Manager — アソシエーションの作成

learning.reason: Use a cron expression for the second Tuesday, set ScheduleOffset to one day, and enable ApplyOnlyAtCronInterval.
learning.concept: The State Manager offset is a number of days from the cron schedule's base date. The setting required for the offset also suppresses an immediate run at registration.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Reflecting Uneven Workloads in a Per-Request SLO
prompt: The SLO for a video streaming API requires 99.9% of all requests over the most recent 28 days to complete within 500 milliseconds. During viewing events, traffic is 100 times higher than usual, so the number of affected requests can vary greatly even when latency occurs during the same minute. You use CloudWatch Application Signals to include every request in the denominator and track the error budget consumed. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Use a period-based SLO that evaluates the percentage of one-minute intervals in which p99 latency was at or below 500 milliseconds.
choices.explanation: This gives each minute equal weight, so it does not account for the number of requests affected during busy periods.

choices.text: Set the average latency over 28 days to 500 milliseconds and evaluate a period-based SLO using daily averages.
choices.explanation: An average does not reveal how many requests exceeded the threshold, and each day also receives equal weight.

choices.text: Evaluate a request-based latency SLO over 28 days using a 500-millisecond threshold.
choices.explanation: This counts individual requests that meet the threshold and uses the total request count to calculate SLO attainment and the allowable number of failed requests.

choices.text: Create a request-based SLO for the HTTP error rate and treat every successful HTTP response as good.
choices.explanation: Although the denominator is the number of requests, this misses successful responses that take longer than 500 milliseconds.

source.label: CloudWatch — サービスレベル目標

learning.reason: Configure a request-based latency SLO. Divide the number of requests that meet the threshold by the total number of requests in the evaluation period.
learning.concept: A period-based evaluation counts a high-traffic interval and a low-traffic interval as one interval each. A request-based SLO accounts for the difference in traffic volume between intervals.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Immediately Recording Each Task's Stop Reason
prompt: You operate multiple ECS clusters with both tasks launched as services and one-off Fargate tasks. You need to store each task's identifier and the stop reason reported by ECS in the same process whenever a task transitions to STOPPED, including normal stops during scale-in and failures immediately after startup. How can you avoid periodic polling and adding logs to the containers?

choices.text: Filter for STOPPED ECS Task State Change events and store taskArn, stopCode, and stoppedReason from detail.
choices.explanation: For both service tasks and one-off tasks, the event provides task identifiers and stop information for processing.

choices.text: Store alarm messages when Container Insights task-count metrics decrease.
choices.explanation: A change in task count does not identify individual stopped tasks or their stop reasons; the total may also stay the same when a task is replaced.

choices.text: Receive ECS Deployment State Change events and store the deployment state and reason.
choices.explanation: Deployment-level events do not cover stops of one-off tasks or the termination of each individual task.

choices.text: Detect task stops only with metric filters on errors already present in the application's CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: This misses startup failures that happen before the process runs and normal stops that produce no logs.

source.label: Amazon ECS — タスク状態変更イベント

learning.reason: Filter for STOPPED events from ECS Task State Change in EventBridge and pass them to a process with a write destination. The event provides the task ARN and stop reason.
learning.concept: Task-level state events provide control-plane information, separate from deployment-level progress and output produced inside a container.

sourceLabel: Amazon ECS — Task state change events

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Continuously Streaming Metrics from All Linked Accounts
prompt: The operations team has linked 12 accounts in the same Region to a CloudWatch monitoring account, and the target namespaces are shared. The team wants to continuously stream EC2 and Lambda metric updates to a central S3 data lake, automatically including metrics for new resources. How can you add a new collection configuration only in the central account? Choose two.

choices.text: Run GetMetricData periodically in the central account and stream known metric identifiers listed in an inventory.
choices.explanation: Specifying only known identifiers does not automatically include time series created by new resources.

choices.text: Specify inclusion filters for AWS/EC2 and AWS/Lambda in a metric stream in the central account.
choices.explanation: Namespace-level inclusion filters can capture matching metrics created later.

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter in the central account to deliver the target namespaces as log events.
choices.explanation: Log delivery settings cannot stream updates stored in CloudWatch Metrics namespaces.

choices.text: Include the linked source accounts in the stream and deliver metrics from the central account's Firehose to S3.
choices.explanation: This streams the target time series from each linked account without requiring delivery configuration in every source account.

choices.text: Share resource dashboards from each source account with the central account.
choices.explanation: Dashboard sharing can provide viewing access, but it does not create continuous delivery to S3.

source.label: CloudWatch — メトリクスストリーム

learning.reason: Create a metric stream in the monitoring account, filter it to the target namespaces, include the linked source accounts, and deliver the stream to S3 through Amazon Data Firehose.
learning.concept: CloudWatch cross-account observability makes metrics available for viewing from a central account. Continuous delivery to S3 requires a separately configured metric stream.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Starting Analysis as Each Partition Is Ready
prompt: Normalize 300 measurement files by manufacturing line, then analyze them in a separate high-memory job. In AWS Batch, the normalization and analysis job definitions are separate. You want analysis for a line to start as soon as normalization for that same line succeeds, without waiting for other lines. How can you use two array jobs and avoid an external orchestrator?

choices.text: Set the analysis job to SEQUENTIAL and submit the normalization and analysis jobs to the same queue.
choices.explanation: This orders the analysis array children relative to one another, but does not make them depend on successful normalization jobs.

choices.text: Wait for the entire parent normalization array job to succeed, then submit the analysis array with no dependencies.
choices.explanation: This ensures the input data is ready, but lines normalized earlier still wait for all lines to finish.

choices.text: Map the same line to the same index in both arrays and set an N_TO_N dependency on the normalization array job ID in the analysis array.
choices.explanation: Each analysis child job can run as soon as normalization for the matching index is complete.

choices.text: Submit the normalization array to a higher-priority queue and the analysis array to a separate, lower-priority queue.
choices.explanation: Queue priority affects job selection but does not make completion of the matching file a prerequisite.

source.label: AWS Batch — アレイジョブ

learning.reason: Assign each line to the same index in both arrays and make the analysis array depend on the normalization array job ID with an N_TO_N dependency.
learning.concept: N_TO_N associates child jobs with the same index in two arrays. This preserves the stage order for each line while allowing different lines to run in parallel.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Retrying a Failed Record in a Stream
prompt: A Lambda function processes DynamoDB Streams updates and receives records numbered 201–205 from the same shard in one batch. Writes for 201 and 202 succeed, 203 fails temporarily, and 204 and 205 are also processed before the function returns. You want to reduce how often all records are reprocessed while correctly accounting for the retry scope within a shard. Which combination of change and expectation is correct?

choices.text: Add code that returns a partial batch response, leave the Lambda configuration at its default, and expect records from 203 onward to be retried.
choices.explanation: In addition to returning the appropriate value from the function, you must enable partial batch failure reporting in the event source mapping.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return the sequence number for 203. Be prepared for records from 203 onward to run again.
choices.explanation: Lambda uses the lowest failed sequence number as the checkpoint and retries records starting from that record.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return the sequence number for 203. Expect 204 and 205 not to run again.
choices.explanation: For DynamoDB Streams, records at and after the failed record can be retried, including later records that already succeeded.

choices.text: Enable only BisectBatchOnFunctionError and return partial success JSON without throwing an exception.
choices.explanation: This setting alone does not interpret the returned failed sequence number, and no function error is reported to trigger batch splitting.

source.label: AWS Lambda — DynamoDBの部分バッチ応答

learning.reason: Enable partial batch responses in the event source mapping and return 203 as the failed record. Because retries start at 203, make subsequent processing idempotent as well.
learning.concept: For partial failures in a stream, retries start at the first failed record. The retry scope differs from message-level partial success with SQS.

sourceLabel: AWS Lambda — Partial batch responses for DynamoDB

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Investigating a Brief Wait by Tracing It to the Lock Holder
prompt: Aurora PostgreSQL experiences transaction latency for only a few minutes at month-end. Average CPU utilization is low, and the locks have already cleared by the time you investigate. To prepare for the next occurrence, you want to collect the blocking relationships between sessions and the related SQL during the incident, then examine them in the CloudWatch console after it has passed. How can you do this without adding a continuously connected monitoring agent?

choices.text: Use Standard mode in Database Insights to display DB load by wait event, then open the lock tree from the graph.
choices.explanation: This can display the load breakdown, but lock tree analysis requires Advanced mode.

choices.text: Set RDS Enhanced Monitoring to a one-second interval and infer wait relationships from OS process CPU and memory.
choices.explanation: This provides OS process statistics but does not show lock relationships between transactions.

choices.text: Display CloudWatch DB connection counts and deadlock counts on the same dashboard.
choices.explanation: These metrics show trends in counts but cannot reconstruct which session blocked another.

choices.text: Enable Advanced mode in CloudWatch Database Insights before the next occurrence, then open lock analysis for the relevant time on the DB instance after that occurrence.
choices.explanation: It displays database-native lock waits hierarchically so you can investigate the holding and waiting sessions.

source.label: CloudWatch Database Insights — PostgreSQLのロック分析

learning.reason: Enable Advanced mode in Database Insights before the next occurrence. After it happens, use the lock snapshots collected during that incident to examine the lock tree for the relevant period.
learning.concept: Aggregated lock-wait metrics indicate the type of load. Use lock analysis to inspect the hierarchy of blocking and waiting sessions.

sourceLabel: CloudWatch Database Insights — PostgreSQL lock analysis

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Speeding Up Cross-Account Log Searches for New Events
prompt: Ten application accounts store JSON in CloudWatch Logs Standard log groups in the same Region. A central monitoring account searches them for the transaction-specific orderCorrelationId using an equality condition. For future logs, you want to reduce the amount of data read, while still being able to search pre-deployment logs with a separate query. How can you configure this without copying the logs? Select two.

choices.text: Configure a field index policy only in the monitoring account.
choices.explanation: That policy does not apply to the log groups owned by linked source accounts.

choices.text: Configure a field index for orderCorrelationId on the Standard log groups in each source account.
choices.explanation: The account ingesting the logs can index new structured log events.

choices.text: Use filterIndex to search the full time range, including the period before creation, and all historical logs will be indexed automatically.
choices.explanation: Events ingested before the index was created are not indexed retroactively and can be missed by a query restricted to the index.

choices.text: Convert the field value into a metric filter dimension and use Logs Insights to search the same logs.
choices.explanation: Publishing a metric does not create an index for searching the original logs.

choices.text: Use filterIndex for the period after creation when the index is active, and use a regular filter to search the pre-deployment period.
choices.explanation: This uses the index for new logs while allowing separate searches of periods not covered by the index.

source.label: CloudWatch Logs — フィールドインデックス

learning.reason: Index the field in each source account that owns the log group, then use filterIndex for new events. Search the pre-deployment period with a regular filter.
learning.concept: Centralized access to log groups and indexes configured at ingestion in each account are separate concerns. Creating an index does not apply it retroactively to historical logs.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Caching Dependencies Across Build Hosts
prompt: Unit tests and integration tests run in separate CodeBuild projects with the same lockfile, operating system, and runtime. You want both projects to reuse downloaded dependencies without relying on build hosts being reused. If the lockfile contents change, the previous cache must not be restored. How can you do this without passing artifacts through a separate pipeline?

choices.text: Use the same S3 bucket and prefix, cacheNamespace, and cached paths, and include a hash of the lockfile in the key.
choices.explanation: The projects use the same cache when the contents match, and a change to the lockfile produces a different cache.

choices.text: Configure both projects to use local custom caching and specify the same directory path.
choices.explanation: Local contents cannot be shared if the projects are assigned different build hosts.

choices.text: Use the same storage location, namespace, and paths, and specify the same fixed key without using a lockfile hash.
choices.explanation: Because the key remains the same when dependencies change, this does not prevent restoring the old cache.

choices.text: Use the same S3 storage location, key, and paths, but configure a different cacheNamespace for each project.
choices.explanation: Separate namespaces prevent the projects from sharing a cache, even when the key is the same.

source.label: CodeBuild — S3キャッシュ

learning.reason: Configure the same S3 cache, prefix, namespace, and cache paths, and calculate the cache key from the same hash expression in both projects.
learning.concept: Sharing a cache across projects requires matching the storage location, cache namespace, key, and paths. Treat changes to dependency definitions as changes to the key.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Process each notification only once with regional redundancy
prompt: In a single AWS account, account-specific AWS Health notifications are sent from EventBridge rules in the affected Region and a backup Region to the same intake process. Each notification fits on one page. Additional communications about the same event must be retained, while only duplicate copies of the same communication delivered from both Regions should be deduplicated. Which fields should be combined as the key?

choices.text: Use the top-level EventBridge event id and the value in resources.
choices.explanation: The outer EventBridge identifier is not suitable for deduplication across AWS Health backup delivery.

choices.text: Use detail.eventArn alone.
choices.explanation: All communications for the same event would then have the same key, causing communications that should be ingested to be dropped.

choices.text: Concatenate detail.eventArn and detail.communicationId.
choices.explanation: Both fields match in backup deliveries, while distinguishing separate communications for the same event.

choices.text: Concatenate the top-level EventBridge region and detail.communicationId.
choices.explanation: The top-level region reflects the delivery Region, so copies of the same communication would get different keys.

source.label: AWS Health — バックアップ通知

learning.reason: Use both detail.eventArn and detail.communicationId. This groups the two copies of the same communication while giving separate communications for the same event different keys.
learning.concept: AWS Health communication identifiers remain consistent across delivery Regions. Treat the affected event identifier and the individual communication identifier as separate parts of the key.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Stop new invocations near the end of a maintenance window while protecting work in progress
prompt: A Systems Manager maintenance window runs from 1:00 AM to 4:00 AM and starts an Automation task for each managed node. The cutoff is set to 3:00 AM. Invocations started before 3:00 AM must be allowed to finish because interrupting them could leave resources inconsistent, and no invocations for targets that have not started yet may begin after 3:00 AM. Which setting on the registered Automation task meets the requirement?

choices.text: Set CutoffBehavior to CONTINUE_TASK and assume that only invocations already in progress will remain.
choices.explanation: This allows in-progress tasks to continue, but does not select the behavior that stops new invocations for targets that have not started.

choices.text: Set MaxConcurrency to 1 and wait for the same task to finish each target in sequence from 3:00 AM onward.
choices.explanation: Limiting concurrency alone does not prevent the next target from being invoked after the cutoff.

choices.text: Switch to a Run Command task and set CutoffBehavior to CANCEL_TASK.
choices.explanation: For Run Command, this behavior attempts to cancel commands that are already running, contrary to the requirement that they continue.

choices.text: Set CutoffBehavior to CANCEL_TASK on the Automation task.
choices.explanation: This does not stop invocations that have already started; it suppresses only new invocations for targets that have not started.

source.label: Systems Manager — Maintenance Windowタスクのカットオフ

learning.reason: Set the Automation task's cutoff behavior to CANCEL_TASK. Invocations that have started continue, and no new invocations begin.
learning.concept: The behavior of CANCEL_TASK depends on the task type. For Automation, started invocations continue; for Run Command, the service attempts to stop them.

sourceLabel: Systems Manager — Maintenance Window task cutoff

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Continue only processing paths independent of a failed parallel step
prompt: A shared EMR on EC2 cluster runs up to four Spark steps concurrently. Only downstream steps in a failed processing path must be prevented from starting; independent paths should continue. A central orchestrator can be added, and neither the entire cluster nor other paths already running should be stopped. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Set StepConcurrencyLevel to 4, attach CANCEL_AND_WAIT to each step, and submit all paths at once.
choices.explanation: This failure action is not allowed when the concurrency level is greater than 1, and it does not selectively control only dependent steps.

choices.text: Set StepConcurrencyLevel to 4 and submit independent steps with CONTINUE. Have the orchestrator submit each path's downstream steps only after its preceding step succeeds.
choices.explanation: This meets the requirements for concurrent execution and lets the external orchestrator prevent downstream steps in a failed path from being submitted.

choices.text: Set StepConcurrencyLevel to 1 and submit all steps sequentially with CANCEL_AND_WAIT for each path.
choices.explanation: Only one step can run at a time, and a failure could cancel pending steps from other independent paths.

choices.text: Set StepConcurrencyLevel to 4, submit all steps in advance with CONTINUE, and enable cluster termination protection.
choices.explanation: Termination protection does not establish success dependencies between steps, so downstream steps in a failed path could still start.

source.label: Amazon EMR — ステップ並行実行の制約

learning.reason: Use CONTINUE as the failure action for concurrent steps, and have the orchestrator verify that each path's preceding step succeeded before submitting its downstream steps.
learning.concept: When StepConcurrencyLevel is greater than 1, steps cannot be added with a failure action other than CONTINUE. The decision to stop only dependent steps after a failure must be made externally.

sourceLabel: Amazon EMR — Concurrent step execution constraints

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Monitor post-replacement degradation and roll back
prompt: When updating an image-processing platform with CloudFormation, queue routing and worker configuration are switched at the same time. After all updated resources have been created, if either of two monitoring conditions enters ALARM within 15 minutes, the entire stack update must be rolled back automatically. The monitoring alarms have already been created outside the stack. How should this be configured without adding external processing?

choices.text: Add both alarm ARNs to the stack update's rollback configuration and set the monitoring period to 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation evaluates the alarms after the resources are in place and rolls back the update if either enters ALARM.

choices.text: Set both alarm ARNs and set the monitoring period to 0 minutes, while setting each alarm's evaluation period to 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: Extending an alarm's evaluation period does not extend the time CloudFormation monitors after the resources are in place.

choices.text: Set a 15-minute monitoring period for the stack update and use the alarms only for SNS notifications.
choices.explanation: This can wait for old resources to be cleaned up, but without configuring rollback triggers, notifications alone do not cause an automatic rollback.

choices.text: Create a change set and check both CloudWatch alarms before making the change set execute.
choices.explanation: A change set helps review the proposed changes, but it does not automatically monitor alarms after the update is applied.

source.label: CloudFormation — ロールバックトリガー

learning.reason: Specify both alarms as rollback triggers for the stack update and set a 15-minute monitoring period after the updated resources are in place.
learning.concept: CloudFormation monitors during the update and for the specified period afterward. If a configured alarm enters ALARM during that period, CloudFormation rolls back the entire stack operation. A monitoring period alone does not configure an automatic rollback condition.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Provision temporary video-processing storage, including image usage
prompt: An Amazon ECS Fargate task running Linux converts video. The compressed and unpacked container images together use 28 GiB. Temporary output and working files require up to an additional 80 GiB; both are present at the same time, and other application files are included in this estimate. The data does not need to be retained after the task ends or shared with other tasks. Choose the smallest configuration that meets the requirements.

choices.text: Set ephemeralStorage to 80 GiB on Linux platform version 1.4.0 or later.
choices.explanation: The working files alone require 80 GiB, and this does not include the 28 GiB needed for the images.

choices.text: Set ephemeralStorage to 100 GiB on Linux platform version 1.4.0 or later, and allocate separate space for the compressed image.
choices.explanation: The compressed and unpacked images occupy the same storage area, so 100 GiB is 8 GiB short.

choices.text: On Linux platform version 1.3.0, configure 108 GiB of shared ephemeralStorage for the images and working files.
choices.explanation: Increasing the capacity through this task definition is supported only on Linux platform version 1.4.0 or later.

choices.text: Set ephemeralStorage to 108 GiB in the task definition on Linux platform version 1.4.0 or later.
choices.explanation: This provides the total capacity needed for both the images and working files in the same task.

source.label: Amazon ECS — Fargateの一時ストレージ

learning.reason: Specify 108 GiB of ephemeral storage in the task definition on Linux platform version 1.4.0 or later. 108 GiB is within the configurable range.
learning.concept: Fargate container images use the same ephemeral storage as working files. Include image usage when estimating capacity, not just the space used by the process.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Prioritize AZ distribution while allowing temporary imbalance
prompt: An EKS cluster has nodes in three Availability Zones (AZs) and runs a stateless API. Under normal conditions, you want Pods from the same Deployment to be distributed as evenly as possible across AZs. During an update, however, if one AZ runs out of capacity, new Pods must still be placed in an AZ with available capacity, even if that results in an imbalance. Which configuration is best?

choices.text: Use topology.kubernetes.io/zone as the key, set maxSkew to 1, and set whenUnsatisfiable to DoNotSchedule.
choices.explanation: This encourages distribution across AZs, but prevents placement when strict balance cannot be achieved despite capacity being available.

choices.text: Use kubernetes.io/hostname as the key, set maxSkew to 1, and set whenUnsatisfiable to ScheduleAnyway.
choices.explanation: This encourages distribution across nodes, but does not directly prevent concentration in an AZ that has more nodes.

choices.text: Use topology.kubernetes.io/zone as the key, set maxSkew to 1, and set whenUnsatisfiable to ScheduleAnyway.
choices.explanation: This prioritizes placement that reduces AZ imbalance while allowing placement to continue when strict conditions cannot be met.

choices.text: Set required node affinity for a specific AZ on every Pod in the Deployment.
choices.explanation: This always pins Pods to one AZ, so it meets neither the normal distribution goal nor the requirement to place Pods when that AZ has no capacity.

source.label: Amazon EKS — 可用性に向けたPodの分散

learning.reason: Use topologySpreadConstraints to select the Deployment's Pods and apply a soft constraint that limits imbalance across AZ labels.
learning.concept: ScheduleAnyway prefers nodes that improve distribution. With a required placement constraint, Pods can remain pending when the distribution condition cannot be met.

sourceLabel: Amazon EKS — Pod distribution for availability

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Commit an order and inventory update together to prevent overselling
prompt: In DynamoDB in the same account and Region, decrement one item in an inventory table and create a new order ID in another table. Even when requests run concurrently, if inventory is insufficient or the order ID already exists, neither write should occur. Which configuration meets the requirement without a compensating process?

choices.text: Use TransactWriteItems with a ConditionCheck and an unconditional Update on the same inventory item, plus a conditional Put for the order.
choices.explanation: Multiple actions in one transaction cannot operate on the same item, so DynamoDB rejects this combination.

choices.text: Include a conditional Update that rejects insufficient inventory and a conditional Put that rejects an existing order ID in TransactWriteItems.
choices.explanation: The conditions and writes for each item are evaluated together, and the entire transaction can fail if either condition is not met.

choices.text: Use BatchWriteItem to issue conditional Put operations for both the inventory and order items, then retry only the failed items.
choices.explanation: BatchWriteItem does not support condition expressions on individual writes and does not provide atomicity for the batch.

choices.text: Use TransactGetItems to check inventory and the order, then send two independent writes based on the results.
choices.explanation: Another request could occur between the reads and the subsequent writes. The two writes are not atomic as a group.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — トランザクションAPI

learning.reason: In one TransactWriteItems call, apply a conditional Update to inventory and a conditional Put to the order that succeeds only if the ID does not already exist.
learning.concept: TransactWriteItems makes operations across multiple tables succeed or fail together. Put the condition for an item in its corresponding update action; do not add a second action for the same item.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Archive only expired-item deletions in the originating Region
prompt: Sessions are deleted by TTL in a two-Region DynamoDB global table. User-initiated deletions must not be written to an audit S3 bucket; archive only old data deleted by TTL. Do not change the application's deletion paths. Choose two required settings.

choices.text: In both Regions, configure the stream to include the item image from before deletion in its output.
choices.explanation: This makes the pre-deletion record available regardless of which Region processes the TTL deletion.

choices.text: Monitor only the stream in the primary Region, and use userIdentity to identify TTL deletions replicated from the replica.
choices.explanation: A deletion event in the replica does not have the userIdentity that identifies the original TTL processing.

choices.text: Filter for REMOVE events in both Regions and unconditionally save them to the audit bucket.
choices.explanation: REMOVE does not distinguish TTL deletions from application deletions, so this would include records that should not be archived.

choices.text: In each Region's event source, filter for deletions performed by the DynamoDB service and save the old image.
choices.explanation: This targets service-deleted events only in the Region where TTL actually runs.

choices.text: Periodically scan for items whose expiration time is earlier than the current time, and archive them when found.
choices.explanation: An expiration time does not prove why or whether deletion occurred, and periodic scans also add load.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — TTL削除とStreams

learning.reason: Use streams that provide the old image in each Region, and filter for the original service deletion caused by TTL using userIdentity. Record the old image in S3 so redelivery does not create duplicate cases.
learning.concept: The original TTL deletion event carries an identifier for the DynamoDB service, but that marker is not available on a deletion replicated to another Region.

sourceLabel: Amazon DynamoDB — TTL deletions and Streams

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Creating Writable Validation Databases in the Same Region
prompt: You need to create a separate cluster from an Aurora cluster containing several terabytes of data so a small number of validation teams can make changes. The data they read must contain only data approved for validation. The source cluster has an instance, and deployment can be in the same Region and account. Choose a method that prevents writes from reaching other validation teams or production and avoids copying all storage initially.

choices.text: Create Aurora clones and have each team connect to its own independent cluster.
choices.explanation: With copy-on-write, only changed pages are kept separate, so a small number of clones can avoid an initial full copy.

choices.text: Add an Aurora Replica to the production cluster and have the validation teams use that reader.
choices.explanation: A reader that uses the same cluster storage does not provide an independent write environment.

choices.text: Copy a full snapshot of the production cluster to another Region, then restore one for each team.
choices.explanation: This provides isolation, but requires a full copy and a cross-Region step that is unnecessary here.

choices.text: Create a custom endpoint for each team on the production cluster and have them connect to the writer.
choices.explanation: Separating connection destinations does not prevent changes from being applied to the same cluster.

source.label: Amazon Aurora — DBクラスターのクローン

learning.reason: Create a separate clone for each validation team, using Aurora copy-on-write.
learning.concept: Copy-on-write shares the initial data pages and keeps modified pages separate. The validation and production environments do not write to the same database.

sourceLabel: Amazon Aurora — Cloning a DB cluster

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Measure User Impact Before Enforcing Risk Controls
prompt: Employees sign in to an Amazon Cognito user pool with a username and password. No external IdP is used. During an initial pilot, users should continue to sign in as usual while you review the risks detected by the service. Then, only high-risk sign-ins should be rejected, while the existing flow remains unchanged for low-risk sign-ins. How should you configure this without changing the authentication application?

choices.text: Use the Plus plan and select Audit-only, then configure high-risk sign-ins to be blocked while still in Audit-only mode.
choices.explanation: Audit-only records evaluations but does not enforce blocking.

choices.text: Keep the current plan, require MFA for all users, and have operators determine risk from the logs.
choices.explanation: This applies a blanket change to all users and does not provide either a pilot or automatic risk-based enforcement.

choices.text: Use the Plus plan and start in Audit-only. After validation, switch to Full function and block high-risk responses.
choices.explanation: This separates the period when you observe risk detections from the period when controls are enforced automatically based on risk.

choices.text: Use the Plus plan and enable Full function with high-risk blocking from the start, then estimate impact from the logs afterward.
choices.explanation: Users identified as high risk would be affected during the audit period.

source.label: Amazon Cognito — 脅威対策

learning.reason: Enable threat protection with the Plus plan and review detected risks in Audit-only mode. After validation, switch to Full function and configure blocking based on risk level.
learning.concept: Audit-only records risk assessments. Full function enforces the response configured for the selected risk level.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Use KMS APIs with Keys Dedicated to CloudHSM
prompt: For document encryption subject to regulatory requirements, an existing application must continue using the AWS KMS API for symmetric encryption. The key material must be generated and retained in an AWS CloudHSM cluster dedicated to your organization and must never leave it in plaintext. Choose a design that lets you use the key as an AWS KMS key while ensuring the HSM's availability through operations.

choices.text: Import key material generated by your organization into a standard KMS key, without using a CloudHSM cluster.
choices.explanation: Although you can import key material into KMS, this does not meet the requirement to retain the material in a dedicated CloudHSM and perform cryptographic operations there.

choices.text: Create a standard symmetric AWS KMS key and use its key policy to allow operations only for the application role.
choices.explanation: You can restrict who uses the KMS API, but the key material is not kept in your organization's CloudHSM cluster.

choices.text: Use PKCS #11 in CloudHSM to operate on keys directly and switch the application's cryptographic operations.
choices.explanation: This meets the key-management requirements but violates the constraint that the existing application continue using the KMS API.

choices.text: Create a symmetric KMS key in an AWS CloudHSM key store connected to a CloudHSM cluster, and maintain the cluster.
choices.explanation: This combines the KMS interface with key material generated and retained in dedicated HSMs.

source.label: AWS KMS — CloudHSMキーストアでキーを作成

learning.reason: Create a symmetric KMS key in a custom key store connected to a dedicated CloudHSM cluster, and operate the cluster.
learning.concept: AWS KMS performs cryptographic operations using CloudHSM. If the key store loses its connection, cryptographic operations with that key are unavailable.

sourceLabel: AWS KMS — Create a key in a CloudHSM key store

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Control S3 Network Paths and Permissions by Application
prompt: A shared S3 bucket in one account is used by applications from different teams, each through its own VPC endpoint. You want each application to read its assigned prefix from its approved application VPC and to manage each application's access policy independently. You want to avoid adding application-specific conditions to the shared bucket policy whenever an application is added or its permissions change. Users who write data directly to the bucket are managed separately, and applications must not read through direct bucket access. Which design should you use?

choices.text: Create a single access point for public network connections on the bucket, then add conditions for each application's IAM role to the bucket policy.
choices.explanation: This relies on one central policy to maintain application conditions, rather than allowing policy management by application.

choices.text: Use an access point for each VPC and allow the relevant prefix. Configure the bucket and endpoint policies so application reads must use the specified access point.
choices.explanation: This lets you manage network conditions and prefix permissions by application, with a path separate from direct access.

choices.text: Create an access point for each application, and allow only the access point ARN in each endpoint policy.
choices.explanation: Requests through the endpoint will not work unless the endpoint policy also allows access to the underlying bucket.

choices.text: Assign a dedicated prefix to each application and use only S3 object ACLs to restrict the source and actions, without access points.
choices.explanation: Object ACLs cannot condition access on the source VPC and do not provide a dedicated network entry point.

source.label: Amazon S3 — VPCに制限したアクセスポイント

learning.reason: Provide a VPC-restricted access point for each application and use separate policies to allow the required reads. The bucket policy should deny direct application reads and allow reads through the specified access point.
learning.concept: An access point policy cannot override restrictions on the bucket. The VPC endpoint policy must allow access to both the access point and the underlying bucket.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Separate audit aggregation from rule distribution
prompt: You need to centrally view existing AWS Config configuration data and compliance results from multiple AWS accounts and Regions. You also need to automatically deploy a new set of audit rules to the in-scope accounts in the organization. Config is enabled in the target Regions, and organization integration and the required permissions are already configured. Select two approaches that meet the requirements.

choices.text: In the audit account, create an AWS Config aggregator that aggregates data from the target organization and Regions.
choices.explanation: This lets you review configuration data and compliance results without signing in to each member account.

choices.text: Register the rule set with the aggregator in the audit account and have it write the rules automatically to the aggregated accounts.
choices.explanation: An aggregator is read-only and does not deploy rules to the accounts it aggregates.

choices.text: Create an organization trail in CloudTrail and use only the CloudTrail Event history page to view the latest Config compliance status.
choices.explanation: This can audit API operations, but it does not aggregate Config evaluation results.

choices.text: Describe the Config rule conditions and remediation actions in an AWS Organizations SCP, avoiding deployment to Config.
choices.explanation: An SCP sets permission guardrails for member accounts; it does not create a Config rule set.

choices.text: Deploy an organization conformance pack in the target Regions, specifying exclusions for accounts that are out of scope.
choices.explanation: This manages a shared evaluation configuration separately from aggregating audit results.

source.label: AWS Config — 複数アカウント・リージョンの集約

learning.reason: Use a central Config aggregator to view configuration and compliance status, and use an organization conformance pack separately to deploy rules.
learning.concept: An aggregator is a read-only view of existing data. Organization deployment features are responsible for distributing rules and remediation.

sourceLabel: AWS Config — Aggregating across multiple accounts and Regions

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Detect an increase in write management API calls as an abnormal baseline change
prompt: The organization trail currently records only read management events. The audit team wants to detect when the volume of API calls that can actually change IAM or EC2 resources rises above normal. S3 data operations are out of scope, and per-API fixed thresholds are not to be maintained. How should the CloudTrail configuration be changed?

choices.text: Keep recording read management events and enable only the API call rate in CloudTrail Insights.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail must record write management events for Insights on management API call rates.

choices.text: Enable write management events and configure only API error rate Insights.
choices.explanation: This detects the frequency of errors; it does not measure an increase in write management API call volume, including successful calls.

choices.text: Record S3 data events and inspect the API call rate for data events.
choices.explanation: This observes operations on content; it does not measure IAM or EC2 management operations.

choices.text: Record write management events and configure CloudTrail Insights for management event API call rates.
choices.explanation: This can detect abnormal changes in normal write API call volume without configuring fixed thresholds.

source.label: AWS CloudTrail — Insightsイベント

learning.reason: Record write management events in the trail and enable CloudTrail Insights to analyze management event API call rates.
learning.concept: Management event API call rates are determined from write management events. Monitoring abnormal API error rates differs from detecting unusual call volume regardless of whether operations succeed.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Apply approved exceptions to findings before routing notifications
prompt: In Security Hub CSPM, a specific control has an approved exception for development accounts only. Match the control using its stable control ID, and mark the applicable findings as suppressed in CSPM. Send only other high-severity, actionable findings to the existing ticket workflow. Which settings should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Apply a CSPM automation rule to all accounts using only the configuration name string.
choices.explanation: This would also apply to findings in accounts such as production that are outside the approved exception, and it would not match by stable ID.

choices.text: Use a CSPM automation rule to set findings to SUPPRESSED when both the development account and control ID match.
choices.explanation: The rule limits the exception using both conditions and can update the finding workflow.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to select high-severity, unsuppressed findings after the CSPM update and send them to the ticket workflow.
choices.explanation: The notification target can be determined from finding data that includes the applied exception.

choices.text: Use an EventBridge input transformer to change only the exception's workflow string.
choices.explanation: This can change the payload being sent, but it does not change the finding workflow in CSPM.

choices.text: Disable the control across the organization and send notifications based only on severity from then on.
choices.explanation: The control would stop producing findings in accounts without an approved exception as well.

source.label: AWS Security Hub CSPM — 検出結果の自動処理

learning.reason: Use a CSPM automation rule to match the development account and control ID, then set the workflow status to SUPPRESSED. An EventBridge rule receiving the updated findings can narrow down which ones go to the ticket workflow.
learning.concept: CSPM automation rules update finding fields. EventBridge evaluates the updated data afterward and triggers external processing.

sourceLabel: AWS Security Hub CSPM — Automated finding processing

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Skip distributing raw shared log files to enable SQL analysis
prompt: Amazon Security Lake in a central account collects VPC Flow Logs in the same Region. An analyst in another account needs to query them with Athena. Limit access to the specified source and subscriber, and query newly appended data without operating data file copies or delivery notifications. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Register the specified source with query access in Lake Formation, create a resource link to the shared table in the analysis account, and query it with Athena.
choices.explanation: This shares the target table and lets the analyst query updates to the central data without copying data files.

choices.text: Create a subscriber with data access for S3 and, by receiving only S3 new-object notifications, use the shared table from Athena.
choices.explanation: This provides access to raw data and notifications, but that configuration does not include sharing Lake Formation tables for Athena.

choices.text: Add Security Lake to the analysis account and periodically ingest replicated objects from the central bucket.
choices.explanation: This maintains a data copy in another account and does not meet the requirement to share new central data as it is added.

choices.text: Have the analysis team assume the VPC Flow Logs delivery role and run SQL with permission to store logs in the central bucket.
choices.explanation: A log delivery permission does not configure subscriber permissions or a catalog for reading the target table.

source.label: Amazon Security Lake — クエリアクセスのサブスクライバー

learning.reason: Create a query-access subscriber in the same Region for the specified source, then use Athena in the analysis account after receiving the Lake Formation table share.
learning.concept: Security Lake distinguishes access to data objects from query access that uses a catalog. Query access uses Lake Formation cross-account sharing.

sourceLabel: Amazon Security Lake — Query access subscribers

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restrict the IAM token target and database user
prompt: For the read-only user reports on an RDS for PostgreSQL instance with IAM database authentication enabled, only the EC2 instance profile role should be able to connect over TLS without managing a password. The role must not be usable to connect as any other database user. Which two settings are required?

choices.text: Allow only rds:DescribeDBInstances on the execution role, specifying the standard RDS DB instance ARN.
choices.explanation: This grants permission to view instance configuration; it does not grant permission to connect as a database user.

choices.text: Allow rds-db:connect on the execution role, specifying the DB instance resource ID and reports.
choices.explanation: Both the target instance and the database user name can be specified.

choices.text: Allow rds-db:connect for all database users on the execution role, and hard-code reports in the client code.
choices.explanation: Hard-coding a default in the program does not restrict the role's permission to connect as other users.

choices.text: Grant rds_iam to reports in PostgreSQL, and configure the required data-reading permissions in the database.
choices.explanation: The database user can then connect using IAM authentication, while SQL permissions after connection can still be limited to what is required.

choices.text: Keep password authentication only for reports in PostgreSQL, and pass the IAM connection token as the password.
choices.explanation: A PostgreSQL user using IAM authentication needs rds_iam; simply substituting the token does not enable IAM authentication.

source.label: Amazon RDS — IAMデータベースアクセスのポリシー

learning.reason: Grant the PostgreSQL rds_iam role to reports, and grant the EC2 execution role rds-db:connect scoped to the DB resource ID and reports.
learning.concept: Permission to connect to a database through IAM and permission to perform operations such as SELECT within PostgreSQL are managed separately.

sourceLabel: Amazon RDS — IAM database access policies

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Manage authorization policies independently for each contracted company
prompt: A B2B SaaS application uses different Cedar policies to decide whether each company can use the same API. The impact of a policy change approved by one company's administrator must be limited to that company's policy store. The backend can identify the authenticated tenant using trusted information. Which configuration should be used with Amazon Verified Permissions?

choices.text: Put a shared Cedar policy for all companies in one policy store, and update the shared policy when it changes.
choices.explanation: Updating a shared policy could affect authorization for multiple companies. This does not provide tenant-specific management boundaries.

choices.text: Manage user capabilities with IAM policies and treat each document in the SaaS application as an AWS IAM action.
choices.explanation: Permissions for AWS APIs and application-specific authorization are separate; this approach cannot evaluate company-specific Cedar policies.

choices.text: Create a policy store for each tenant, and have the backend choose the evaluation target based on its mapping of verified tenants to stores.
choices.explanation: This preserves company-level policy management and limits authorization evaluation to the relevant store.

choices.text: Use a different Cedar schema name for each company, but evaluate all companies' policies in a single shared store.
choices.explanation: Different names alone do not make the policy management boundary independent for each company.

source.label: Amazon Verified Permissions — 認可モデルの設計

learning.reason: Separate policy stores by company and have the application request an authorization decision from the store corresponding to the tenant it has verified.
learning.concept: A policy store is the management boundary for policies, templates, and schemas. With separate stores for each company, a policy change in one store does not directly affect evaluations in another.

sourceLabel: Amazon Verified Permissions — Designing an authorization model

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Manage zone-sharing authorization as single-use
prompt: A DNS management account owns a Route 53 private hosted zone that must be associated with 20 VPCs owned by another account. Route 53 Profiles are not used. The DNS administrator must authorize each target VPC and leave no authorization after the association is established, while keeping the association in place. Each VPC owner also has permission to perform their part. In what order should the steps be performed?

choices.text: The zone owner creates one authorization for the target account, and the VPC owner uses it to associate all 20 VPCs.
choices.explanation: Association authorization is required for each VPC, not just once per account.

choices.text: Peer all VPCs with the zone account and enable DNS resolution for the peering connections.
choices.explanation: DNS resolution settings for VPC peering do not make the other account's private hosted zone an associated zone for each VPC.

choices.text: The zone owner authorizes each VPC, the VPC owner creates the association, and then the authorization alone is deleted.
choices.explanation: This separates each party's responsibilities and leaves no unused authorization while preserving the established association.

choices.text: Instead of deleting the authorization, the zone owner has the VPC owner disassociate the VPC from the zone.
choices.explanation: Disassociation removes the DNS access path; its effect differs from deleting only the authorization.

source.label: Route 53 — アカウント間のプライベートホストゾーン関連付け

learning.reason: The zone owner authorizes the association for each VPC, and the owner of the target VPC creates the association. After it succeeds, the zone owner deletes that authorization.
learning.concept: Association authorization and the actual association are independent. Deleting the authorization preserves an established association and DNS resolution.

sourceLabel: Route 53 — Associating private hosted zones across accounts

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Consolidate DNS forwarding from VPCs to on-premises DNS
prompt: A network account in the same Region has a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint that can reach on-premises DNS, along with a forwarding rule for corp.example. You want VPCs in the development OU in your organization to resolve the same names. You must avoid adding endpoints and make the rule visible in new accounts. Sharing within the organization is enabled in AWS RAM. Which two actions are required?

choices.text: Share only the outbound endpoint directly with the development OU, without sharing the forwarding rule.
choices.explanation: The forwarding rule that references the endpoint is the resource that member VPCs use.

choices.text: Share the existing corp.example forwarding rule with the development OU using AWS RAM.
choices.explanation: Accounts in the OU can use the central rule without updating individual account IDs.

choices.text: Create a corp.example private hosted zone in each VPC and register the same IP addresses as the central forwarding rule.
choices.explanation: Registering records in a hosted zone does not dynamically forward queries for all of corp.example to the existing DNS server.

choices.text: In each development account, associate the shared forwarding rule with the target VPC.
choices.explanation: The VPC's Resolver then forwards queries for the target name according to the shared rule.

choices.text: Set the development VPC's DHCP options to specify the private IP address of the central outbound endpoint.
choices.explanation: An outbound endpoint provides an egress path to external DNS; it is not used to receive queries from the development VPC in this configuration.

source.label: Route 53 Resolver — 転送ルールの管理

learning.reason: Share the central rule with the development OU. In each member account, associate the shared rule with the VPCs that need to resolve the names.
learning.concept: The outbound endpoint referenced by the rule is shared indirectly. Even when a rule is shared, it must still be associated with the VPC that will use it.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Route a public HTTP API only to a private listener
prompt: An existing API Gateway HTTP API must remain public while forwarding requests to an internal Application Load Balancer in the same AWS account. The ALB runs in private subnets, and its HTTPS listener routes requests to multiple services based on the path. The HTTP API's public stage is named prod, but the ALB expects paths without that prefix. How can you reuse the ALB's routing without making the ALB public?

choices.text: Use an HTTP proxy integration with a VPC Link, specify the HTTPS listener ARN and TLS settings, and remove the stage name from the path sent to the backend.
choices.explanation: The private connection reaches the listener, and path mapping can pass the value expected by the ALB's path rules.

choices.text: Create an HTTP proxy integration using a VPC Link and specify the service's ALB target group ARN.
choices.explanation: An integration targeting the ALB requires the listener ARN. A target group also cannot use the rules on the existing listener.

choices.text: Set the internal ALB's HTTPS URL as the standard public HTTP proxy integration, without using a VPC Link.
choices.explanation: A public HTTP integration cannot provide a private network path to an internal ALB.

choices.text: Use an API Gateway HTTP API AWS Cloud Map private integration and register task IPs separately from the ALB.
choices.explanation: This can connect through direct service discovery, but it does not reuse the existing ALB listener rules.
