source.label: API Gateway — HTTP APIのプライベート統合

learning.reason: Use a VPC Link to integrate with the ALB's HTTPS listener ARN and specify TLS settings. Use parameter mapping to override the path with the original request path.
learning.concept: Whether clients can reach the API and how API Gateway connects to the backend are configured separately.

sourceLabel: API Gateway — HTTP API private integrations

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Reserve concurrency for critical processing and cap notifications
prompt: Two Lambda functions in the same AWS account and Region need these settings: order finalization must be protected from other functions' load with up to 200 concurrent executions, and the function that notifies an external vendor must be capped at 500 concurrent executions. The account limit is 1,000, and no other concurrency is reserved. Initialization time is not a requirement. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Reserve 200 only for order finalization, and let notifications use unreserved concurrency without a cap.
choices.explanation: This protects the order finalization allocation, but notifications can exceed 500 concurrent executions by using the unreserved pool.

choices.text: Reserve 500 only for notifications, and make order finalization share the unreserved pool with other functions.
choices.explanation: Notifications have a cap, but no dedicated allocation of 200 is secured for order finalization.

choices.text: Configure 200 and 500 provisioned concurrency for order finalization and notifications, respectively.
choices.explanation: Requests above the initialized capacity can use the standard pool, so this does not enforce a 500-execution cap for notifications.

choices.text: Set reserved concurrency to 200 for order finalization and 500 for notifications.
choices.explanation: This allocates dedicated capacity and sets a cap for each function. Their combined reserved concurrency also fits within the available account limit.

source.label: AWS Lambda — 予約済み同時実行

learning.reason: Set reserved concurrency to 200 for order finalization and 500 for notifications. Reserved concurrency is dedicated to a function and also caps its concurrency.
learning.concept: Reserved concurrency can both keep capacity unavailable to other functions and prevent a function from using too much.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Manage S3 access scope through employee groups
prompt: An internal application manages users in IAM Identity Center directory groups. In an S3 data lake, users need direct access with temporary credentials to prefixes assigned to their groups. You do not want to create an IAM role for each user, and the application can propagate user information through a trusted mechanism. Choose two steps that meet these requirements.

choices.text: Specify directory group display names directly as AWS principal values in each bucket policy.
choices.explanation: Directory group display names cannot be specified as AWS principal ARNs in a bucket policy.

choices.text: Associate an Access Grants instance with IAM Identity Center and register an IAM role for issuing temporary permissions for the relevant location.
choices.explanation: Access Grants can identify directory principals and issue credentials for the relevant data.

choices.text: Have all users assume the same execution role for the entire bucket and distinguish destinations only in the application UI.
choices.explanation: The temporary credentials would not reflect group-specific data permissions, so direct access could not be restricted to the required scope.

choices.text: Create an S3 access point for each prefix and set the IAM Identity Center group ID directly as the access point principal.
choices.explanation: Access points can isolate network or data access, but a directory group ID cannot be specified directly as an IAM principal.

choices.text: Create grants that associate each relevant group with its prefixes and operations, then have the application obtain temporary credentials in the user's context.
choices.explanation: Temporary permissions for direct reads and writes can be scoped to the relevant data according to the user's group membership.

source.label: Amazon S3 — Access Grantsの仕組み

learning.reason: Associate an S3 Access Grants instance with IAM Identity Center, then register the relevant S3 locations and access role. Create group-level grants, and have the application obtain temporary credentials in the user's context.
learning.concept: S3 Access Grants uses a location role to issue temporary credentials. Each grant can associate a directory identity with an S3 location and operations.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — How Access Grants works

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restrict certificates to server use on the same issuing CA
prompt: The same AWS Private CA is used for several internal purposes. A delegated role must be allowed to issue only TLS server end-entity certificates using this CA. The same role must not be able to issue client-authentication certificates or subordinate CA certificates. How should the IAM policy for the issuance operation be designed?

choices.text: Allow only acm-pca:IssueCertificate for the target CA, without restricting the template.
choices.explanation: This limits which CA can be used, but it may also allow issuance with other templates on the same CA.

choices.text: Allow acm-pca:IssueCertificate for the target CA only when acm-pca:TemplateArn specifies the designated server-authentication template.
choices.explanation: The policy can constrain both the issuing CA and the issuance template available to the role.

choices.text: Allow only acm-pca:GetCertificate for the target CA and check the certificate name when retrieving it.
choices.explanation: Permission to retrieve an issued certificate does not allow a new certificate to be issued.

choices.text: Tag the target CA for standard server use and allow acm-pca:IssueCertificate only when the tag matches.
choices.explanation: A tag can help identify the CA's intended use, but it does not evaluate which template is specified for that CA.

source.label: AWS Private CA — 証明書テンプレートとIAM条件

learning.reason: Allow acm-pca:IssueCertificate for the target CA and limit acm-pca:TemplateArn to the server-authentication end-entity template.
learning.concept: Specifying the CA resource controls which CA can be used. A TemplateArn condition also restricts which issuance templates can be used on that CA.

sourceLabel: AWS Private CA — Certificate templates and IAM conditions

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Bulk update of assigned audit permissions
prompt: An employee group has the same audit permission set assigned across 80 accounts in IAM Identity Center. Apply an approved policy change to the permission set through the API and propagate it to the roles created in each account. Do not change the account assignments or users. Select two actions required to do this.

choices.text: Set the approved policy on the existing permission set with PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet.
choices.explanation: This centrally updates the permission definition referenced by the existing assignments.

choices.text: Add an individual IAM policy directly to the automatically created role in each of the 80 accounts.
choices.explanation: This does not update the central permission definition, and the direct change could be lost when permissions are reprovisioned from the permission set.

choices.text: Create a new assignment of the same group to the current permission set.
choices.explanation: Reassigning is unnecessary when keeping existing assignments, and it serves a different purpose from distributing a policy change through the API.

choices.text: Apply the update to the existing assignments with ProvisionPermissionSet and confirm that provisioning is complete.
choices.explanation: This distributes the central update to the roles in the accounts that already have assignments.

choices.text: Attach an SCP listing the new audit permissions and skip updating the permission set.
choices.explanation: An SCP sets an upper bound on permissions; it does not directly grant new actions to existing audit roles.

source.label: IAM Identity Center — 許可セットのインラインポリシー更新

learning.reason: Use PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet to update the existing permission set, then use ProvisionPermissionSet to apply the change to accounts that already have assignments.
learning.concept: A permission set is the central permission definition. Applying an inline policy change made through the API to an environment with existing assignments also requires provisioning.

sourceLabel: IAM Identity Center — Update an inline policy for a permission set

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Validate a consistent request body across multiple Content-Types
prompt: A partner-facing API Gateway REST API accepts the same JSON structure as application/json and under a partner-specific Content-Type. Existing clients cannot change their headers. If any required body field or type is invalid, or a required query parameter is missing, reject the request before invoking Lambda. How should you configure this without registering a model for each Content-Type?

choices.text: Create a model only for application/json and enable body and parameter validation.
choices.explanation: There is no matching model for the other Content-Type, so the request body from those clients is not validated.

choices.text: Set a model for $default and use a validator that checks only required parameters.
choices.explanation: Even with a model, body validation is disabled, so required fields and types are not evaluated.

choices.text: Enable body validation for $default and check for the query parameter in Lambda code.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to reject requests with a missing parameter before invoking Lambda.

choices.text: Set a body model for $default and validate both the body and required query parameters.
choices.explanation: This checks the body and request parameters before sending the request to the integration, regardless of the partner-specific header.

source.label: API Gateway — REST APIの要求検証

learning.reason: Choose a validator that checks both the body and required parameters, and set $default as the Content-Type for the JSON Schema model on the relevant method.
learning.concept: A body model is associated with a Content-Type. Use $default to validate requests against the same schema even when no model matches their Content-Type. Required-parameter validation checks that a parameter is present and non-empty.

sourceLabel: API Gateway — REST API request validation

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Preserve per-order ordering and distinguish retries from separate events
prompt: Order confirmation events are processed independently by inventory, billing, and shipping systems. The sender publishes them in confirmation order for each order. Preserve the order of events for the same order in each system, and prevent duplicate delivery of the same event when the sender retries within 5 minutes. Different events can have the same body; their attributes and unique event IDs distinguish them. Do not change existing event bodies. Select two required settings.

choices.text: Set the order ID as the MessageDeduplicationId for every event for that order.
choices.explanation: Different events would then have the same ID, so events sent close together could be suppressed as duplicates.

choices.text: Deliver from one SNS FIFO topic to a separate SQS FIFO queue for each processing system.
choices.explanation: Each system receives all events from its own queue and can preserve ordering within that system.

choices.text: Use content-based deduplication in SNS FIFO to identify events by combining their bodies and attributes.
choices.explanation: The standard body hash does not include attributes, so it cannot distinguish different events with the same body.

choices.text: Aggregate events from SNS Standard into one SQS FIFO queue and have the three systems compete to consume from it.
choices.explanation: This does not give each system every event, and it cannot guarantee FIFO delivery from publishing through consumption.

choices.text: Set the order ID as the MessageGroupId and the event ID as the MessageDeduplicationId, reusing both for retries of the same event.
choices.explanation: This preserves ordering per order and distinguishes retries of the same event from different events with identical bodies.

source.label: Amazon SNS — FIFOトピックの重複排除

learning.reason: Deliver from SNS FIFO to an SQS FIFO queue for each processing system. Use the order ID as the MessageGroupId and keep the unique event ID as the MessageDeduplicationId on retries.
learning.concept: MessageGroupId controls ordering within the same order. Content-based deduplication uses a hash of the body and does not include message attributes.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Replay outage-period events only to the corrected processing rule
prompt: Order events are published to an EventBridge custom event bus. An archive has been collecting events since before the outage, and it retains the events from the affected period. You corrected an aggregation rule and want to replay the events from during the outage, but must not send duplicate emails through notification rules on the same event bus. How can you do this without building additional replay logic in the application?

choices.text: Specify a temporary, separate event bus as the replay destination instead of the original bus.
choices.explanation: A replay can be sent only to the event bus from which the archive was created.

choices.text: Replay to the original bus, specifying the affected time period and only the corrected aggregation rule.
choices.explanation: This selects only the retained events in scope and limits delivery to the aggregation rule.

choices.text: Replay to all rules on the original bus and suppress email using only the archive's ingestion filter.
choices.explanation: The archive's ingestion conditions cannot separate which rules receive replayed events.

choices.text: Delete and recreate the aggregation rule with the same name, then wait for past events to be delivered again.
choices.explanation: Creating a rule handles future events; it does not automatically replay events retained in an archive.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge — イベントのリプレイ

learning.reason: Replay the archive to the original event bus, specifying only the outage period and the aggregation rule.
learning.concept: An archive can be replayed only to its original event bus. You can limit the replay to selected rules so the same events are not sent to targets of other rules.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Use PostgreSQL failover candidates for reads
prompt: Run Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL across three Availability Zones in the same Region. Read traffic increases during certain periods, so you want to use two instances for reads under normal conditions and automatically promote one of the read instances in the same configuration if the writer fails. Provide read clients with a single managed endpoint. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use the writer in an RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster and two readers in separate Availability Zones, and direct reads to the reader endpoint.
choices.explanation: Reads can be distributed to the readers under normal conditions, and a reader is promoted if the writer fails.

choices.text: Use a standard Multi-AZ DB instance and add its synchronous standby to a read-only endpoint.
choices.explanation: The standby does not accept read traffic.

choices.text: Create two independent read replicas from a Single-AZ DB instance and designate both as automatic promotion targets.
choices.explanation: A different read replica can be promoted manually, but it is not an automatic failover target within the configuration.

choices.text: Add two RDS Proxies to a Single-AZ DB instance and distribute read connections between them.
choices.explanation: Adding proxies does not create independent read instances or failover targets.

source.label: Amazon RDS — Multi-AZ DBクラスター

learning.reason: Create an RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster. Direct normal read connections to the reader endpoint and write connections to the writer endpoint.
learning.concept: RDS Multi-AZ DB instances and Multi-AZ DB clusters are different. In a DB cluster, two read instances handle read traffic and serve as promotion candidates.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Exclude future readers from analytics connections
prompt: In Aurora PostgreSQL, you want monthly analytics connections to go only to the two current high-memory readers. Do not include general-purpose readers added automatically in the future, and remove a designated analytics reader from analytics connections if it is promoted to writer. The analytics application uses one DNS name. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create a READER-type custom endpoint and add only the current general-purpose readers to its exclusion list.
choices.explanation: Future general-purpose readers that are not named in the exclusion list can be included if their role matches.

choices.text: Create an ANY-type custom endpoint and add the two high-memory instances to a static list.
choices.explanation: The static list limits membership, but ANY does not exclude a member based on its role if it is promoted to writer.

choices.text: Create a READER-type custom endpoint and add only the two high-memory instances to a static list.
choices.explanation: This does not automatically include added readers, and a member promoted to writer is excluded from read connections.

choices.text: Use the cluster’s default reader endpoint and give the two high-memory instances higher promotion priorities.
choices.explanation: Promotion priority does not provide fixed membership for analytics readers.

source.label: Amazon Aurora — カスタムエンドポイントの考慮事項

learning.reason: Use the API or CLI to create a READER-type custom endpoint and specify a static list containing the two high-memory instances.
learning.concept: Instances added later are not automatically included in a static list. With a READER-type endpoint, an instance is excluded if its role changes to writer.

sourceLabel: Amazon Aurora — Considerations for custom endpoints

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Connect two Regions over a dedicated connection and limit advertised routes
prompt: You have a dedicated Direct Connect connection on premises, and Transit Gateways in Tokyo and Virginia each aggregate multiple VPCs. Advertise only the approved, nonoverlapping application CIDRs for each Region to on-premises over BGP. Keep the existing regional Transit Gateways and do not add a separate connection for each Region. How should you configure this? Choose two.

choices.text: Connect a transit VIF to a Direct Connect gateway and associate the Transit Gateways in both Regions, which have different ASNs.
choices.explanation: The dedicated connection can be shared to reach the VPCs attached to each Transit Gateway.

choices.text: Connect a public VIF to the Direct Connect gateway and advertise the application CIDRs of the Transit Gateways.
choices.explanation: A public VIF does not provide connectivity to private Transit Gateways.

choices.text: For each Transit Gateway association, configure the allowed prefixes that are nonoverlapping and should be advertised to on-premises.
choices.explanation: The allowed CIDRs can be advertised for each association.

choices.text: Set the same 0.0.0.0/0 prefix on both associations and have the Direct Connect gateway combine the identical routes.
choices.explanation: Allowed prefixes for multiple Transit Gateways associated with the same Direct Connect gateway cannot overlap.

choices.text: Associate a private VIF directly with the Transit Gateway in each Region.
choices.explanation: Connectivity to a Transit Gateway uses a Direct Connect gateway and a transit VIF.

source.label: AWS Direct Connect — Transit Gatewayとの関連付け

learning.reason: Connect one transit VIF from the dedicated connection to a Direct Connect gateway, then associate both Transit Gateways. For each association, configure the nonoverlapping prefixes that are allowed to be advertised.
learning.concept: A Direct Connect gateway can advertise allowed prefixes specified for each association to on-premises. Use a different ASN for each Transit Gateway.

sourceLabel: AWS Direct Connect — Transit Gateway associations

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Separate continuous and push-time scans in one registry
prompt: The same private ECR registry contains production and development repositories. For eligible images, production must continuously detect newly disclosed vulnerabilities, while development must be scanned only when images are pushed. Keep push-time scanning enabled across the registry, and select only production repositories with an additional filter. Which settings should you use?

choices.text: Set SCAN_ON_PUSH for both the registry-wide and production filters in enhanced scanning, and give production higher priority.
choices.explanation: Even with overlapping filters, both settings specify push-time scanning, so continuous scanning for newly disclosed vulnerabilities is not configured.

choices.text: Use basic scanning’s push-time setting across the registry, and configure production to be reevaluated continuously within that same setting.
choices.explanation: Enhanced scanning is required to apply continuous scanning to repositories.

choices.text: Configure registry-wide SCAN_ON_PUSH and production-only CONTINUOUS_SCAN in enhanced scanning.
choices.explanation: Continuous scanning takes precedence for overlapping production repositories, while development can remain push-time only.

choices.text: Set CONTINUOUS_SCAN for all repositories and SCAN_ON_PUSH for production in enhanced scanning.
choices.explanation: Continuous scanning applies registry-wide, so development is not limited to push-time scans.

source.label: Amazon ECR — スキャン対象のフィルター

learning.reason: In enhanced scanning, specify SCAN_ON_PUSH for all repositories and CONTINUOUS_SCAN for production repositories. When both match a production repository, continuous scanning takes precedence.
learning.concept: ECR enhanced scanning integrates with Amazon Inspector and uses repository filters to distinguish push-time scanning from continuous evaluation.

sourceLabel: Amazon ECR — Filters for image scanning

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Rejecting unapproved ZIP packages when updating a production function
prompt: A pipeline signs AWS Lambda ZIP packages with AWS Signer. Going forward, updates to ZIP packages that are unsigned or use an unapproved signing profile must be rejected. Code already registered must continue running until the next update. How can allowed signatures be enforced when updating the Lambda function?

choices.text: Configure an approved signing profile version and set the validation failure policy to Warn.
choices.explanation: Warn records validation failures, but deployment continues.

choices.text: Sign packages in CI and do not assign a new code signing configuration to the function.
choices.explanation: This produces signed artifacts, but does not enforce signature validation in the function's update path.

choices.text: Log the hash of the account that created the signing profile and use a CloudWatch alarm for post-deployment review.
choices.explanation: This does not reject updates in advance based on signature validation, so it cannot prevent deployment of unapproved code.

choices.text: Configure the signing profile versions to allow and assign a code signing configuration with Enforce to the production function.
choices.explanation: Only future updates using an approved signature are allowed; the current code can continue running until the next update.

source.label: AWS Lambda — コード署名の検証

learning.reason: Register the approved AWS Signer signing profile versions in a code signing configuration, set the validation failure policy to Enforce, and assign that configuration to the function.
learning.concept: Represent approved publishers with signing profile versions and use Enforce to reject deployments that fail validation. Existing code continues running until the next update.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Allowing one distribution to read an SSE-KMS S3 origin
prompt: CloudFront serves a general purpose S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS using a customer managed KMS key. An S3 website endpoint is not needed, and direct public reads are prohibited. CloudFront must connect to S3 with signed requests, and S3 and KMS must allow origin reads only for a specific distribution. Select two required actions.

choices.text: Specify the S3 website endpoint as the origin and attach an OAC to it.
choices.explanation: An S3 website endpoint is a custom origin and cannot use OAC.

choices.text: Specify the regular S3 bucket endpoint as the origin and configure OAC to always sign requests.
choices.explanation: CloudFront can then send signed requests to the private bucket.

choices.text: Allow the distribution in the bucket policy only, without adding an allowance for CloudFront to the existing KMS key policy.
choices.explanation: Allowing S3 reads is not enough if CloudFront cannot decrypt the SSE-KMS objects.

choices.text: Issue signed URLs to CloudFront viewers and keep public reads enabled on the bucket.
choices.explanation: Controlling viewer access does not prevent users from reading directly from S3.

choices.text: Allow the CloudFront service principal to read from S3 and decrypt with KMS, restricting both permissions to the specific distribution ARN.
choices.explanation: This grants the origin operations needed by an individual distribution.

source.label: Amazon CloudFront — S3オリジンへのアクセス制限

learning.reason: Attach OAC and sign requests to the S3 origin. In the bucket and KMS key policies, allow the CloudFront service principal only for the specific distribution.
learning.concept: Reading SSE-KMS objects requires both S3 read permission and KMS decrypt permission. The OAC connection and the permissions in each policy are separate requirements.

sourceLabel: Amazon CloudFront — Restricting access to an S3 origin

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Auditing IAM credentials with two types of records
prompt: An audit team must inventory whether IAM users in an account have console passwords, whether they use MFA, their regular access keys, and long term credentials for specific services. The operators want to use the IAM credential report CSV. How should they combine the CSV with additional investigation?

choices.text: Generate only the credential report and identify service specific long term credentials from the access key columns.
choices.explanation: Service specific credentials are not included in this CSV.

choices.text: Use the credential report to check MFA and regular credentials, and use the applicable user listing API to check service specific credentials.
choices.explanation: This separates the standard report fields from an inventory of credential types the report does not include.

choices.text: Retrieve IAM last accessed information and use only the time of access to a service to enumerate registered credentials.
choices.explanation: This observes service access attempts; it does not inventory MFA settings or registered credentials.

choices.text: Read only management events from a period in CloudTrail and assume users with no matching operation records have no credentials.
choices.explanation: This can miss credentials created before the period and does not reliably show current registrations.

source.label: AWS IAM — 認証情報レポート

learning.reason: Use the credential report for user password, MFA, and regular access key status. Retrieve service specific credentials separately through the relevant IAM listing API.
learning.concept: The IAM credential report summarizes management status for many IAM users, but it is not a complete inventory of service specific credentials.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Separating copy permissions from restore permissions in the central vault
prompt: A recovery point is copied from a production account to a vault in a central backup account within the same AWS Organizations. The resource and key support cross account copies, and the source IAM permissions are already configured. The central account's operations role performs restores, and the production role must not restore a recovery point directly from the central account. What should be configured on the destination vault?

choices.text: Allow only backup:CopyIntoBackupVault for approved source accounts in the destination vault, and perform restores with a central IAM role.
choices.explanation: This accepts copies into the central account and keeps restore operations within the central account's permissions boundary.

choices.text: Allow only backup:StartCopyJob for approved source accounts in the destination vault.
choices.explanation: The destination side permission for accepting a copy is backup:CopyIntoBackupVault.

choices.text: Allow backup:StartRestoreJob for approved source accounts in the destination vault, and use that permission instead of copy authorization.
choices.explanation: A restore action does not authorize copying to the destination and cannot be used as this type of cross account vault permission.

choices.text: Enable only Vault Lock on the destination vault and accept copies from every source account in the same way.
choices.explanation: Vault Lock controls retention; an access policy specifies which other accounts can copy into the vault.

source.label: AWS Backup — アカウント間でのバックアップコピー

learning.reason: In the destination vault access policy, allow only backup:CopyIntoBackupVault from approved source accounts. Configure restore permissions for the central account's role.
learning.concept: Cross account acceptance by a vault authorizes copying recovery points. It does not authorize direct restores across accounts.

sourceLabel: AWS Backup — Copying backups across accounts

category: コスト最適化
title: Allocate commitment charges to the usage period, not the purchase date
prompt: You are comparing the monthly effective costs of two configurations in Cost Explorer. Some accounts prepaid for EC2 Reservations and Savings Plans, and the usage occurred in other accounts. For the comparison, allocate the commitment’s upfront and recurring charges over its term, and include the applicable discounts applied on the bill. You do not need to compare costs by the accounting payment date on the AWS bill. Which metric should you use?

source.label: AWS Cost Explorer — 高度なコスト表示

learning.reason: Choose Net amortized costs. It allocates upfront and recurring commitment charges over the applicable period and includes applicable discounts in the cost comparison.
learning.concept: Amortized costs spread a one-time purchase charge over its term, avoiding a spike around the payment date. Net metrics reflect applicable discounts.

choices.text: Choose Unblended costs.
choices.explanation: This lets you compare usage charges individually, but it does not amortize commitment payments over the commitment term.

choices.text: Choose Net unblended costs.
choices.explanation: This reflects applicable discounts, but it does not amortize upfront and recurring commitment charges.

choices.text: Choose Amortized costs.
choices.explanation: This allocates commitment charges over time, but Net amortized costs are the appropriate metric for an amortized comparison that reflects discounts.

choices.text: Choose Net amortized costs.
choices.explanation: This reflects the applicable discounts and allocates upfront and recurring commitment charges over time.

sourceLabel: AWS Cost Explorer — Advanced cost views

category: コスト最適化
title: Keep a quarterly peak in the rightsizing analysis
prompt: An EC2 business system runs continuously, and 70 days of CloudWatch data are available. Load has been low over the last 30 days, but a quarter-end workload caused a peak 70 days ago. Include that past quarter-end workload in Compute Optimizer’s analysis, and use paid enhanced metrics only for the relevant workloads. Which configuration should you use?

source.label: AWS Compute Optimizer — ライトサイジングの推奨設定

learning.reason: Enable enhanced infrastructure metrics in the recommendation preferences for the relevant EC2 instances and choose a 93-day lookback.
learning.concept: The recommendation lookback period determines how much collected data is analyzed. Recommendations are based on metrics that are actually available; a setting cannot create data that was never collected.

choices.text: Enable enhanced infrastructure metrics in the recommendation preferences for the relevant EC2 instances, and use a 93-day lookback period.
choices.explanation: The 70-day-old observation for the relevant resources falls within the recommendation lookback period.

choices.text: Keep enhanced metrics disabled and choose a 32-day lookback period to account for the past quarter-end workload.
choices.explanation: A 32-day lookback does not include data from 70 days ago.

choices.text: Change the CloudWatch dashboard to show 93 days, and leave Compute Optimizer at its default 14-day lookback.
choices.explanation: The dashboard display range does not change the period Compute Optimizer analyzes.

choices.text: Only increase the CPU headroom in the recommendation preferences and keep the default lookback period.
choices.explanation: Changing the headroom does not include metrics from the past quarter-end period in the analysis.

sourceLabel: AWS Compute Optimizer — Rightsizing recommendation preferences

category: コスト最適化
title: Separate storage costs from requester-side retrieval costs
prompt: A research institution stores analytics data in an S3 general purpose bucket. The institution will continue to pay storage charges, while user organizations in other AWS accounts should pay for successful read requests and data transfer. Each user organization signs requests with its own AWS credentials, and read access has already been granted. How should this be configured? Select TWO.

source.label: Amazon S3 — リクエスタ支払い

learning.reason: Enable Requester Pays on the bucket. Authorized users must send authenticated requests that specify the payer and accept the charges.
learning.concept: Requester Pays changes how charges are assigned; it does not grant access. It shifts request and transfer charges to the requester, while storage charges remain with the bucket owner.

choices.text: Add each user organization’s IAM roles to the bucket policy again so that charges are automatically transferred to those organizations.
choices.explanation: Access permissions and the party responsible for S3 charges are configured separately.

choices.text: Enable Requester Pays on the bucket.
choices.explanation: This assigns charges for successful covered requests and data transfer to the requester while leaving storage charges with the bucket owner.

choices.text: Allow public anonymous access to connect directly to S3 and assign retrieval charges to the requester.
choices.explanation: Requester Pays requires authenticated requests and cannot be used to charge anonymous access.

choices.text: Have authenticated users include the RequestPayer parameter in their requests.
choices.explanation: The signature identifies the requester, and the parameter indicates that the requester accepts the applicable charges.

choices.text: Share S3 Storage Lens with users outside the organization and configure it to change the billing destination for data transfer from the same bucket.
choices.explanation: Storage Lens aggregates usage data; it does not change who is billed for data transfer.

category: コスト最適化
title: Account for added cache charges when deciding whether to deploy
prompt: CloudFront caches in multiple Regions are making duplicate requests to the origin for the same video. In a trial, Origin Shield reduced monthly origin requests from 12 million to 3 million, and billable Origin Shield requests were estimated at 14 million per month. Under this contract, the variable rate is $30 per million origin requests and $8 per million Origin Shield requests. Assuming all other costs stay the same, what is the monthly difference?

source.label: Amazon CloudFront — Origin Shield

learning.reason: The 9 million fewer origin requests save $270. Subtract the $112 added charge for Origin Shield, for a net monthly reduction of $158.
learning.concept: For an additional caching layer, measure separately the origin load it offsets and the new charges for that cache layer.

choices.text: A $270 monthly reduction.
choices.explanation: This counts only the reduction in origin costs and does not subtract the stated Origin Shield charges.

choices.text: A $112 monthly increase.
choices.explanation: This counts only the added Origin Shield charges and does not account for the reduction in origin costs.

choices.text: A $158 monthly reduction.
choices.explanation: This is the $270 reduction in origin costs minus the $112 in Origin Shield charges.

choices.text: A $382 monthly reduction.
choices.explanation: The added $112 charge must be subtracted from the savings, not added to them.

category: コスト最適化
title: Include Unused Reserved Capacity in the Budget
prompt: An organization reserves an On-Demand Capacity Reservation for 30 instances with the same attributes so that it can launch 30 On-Demand EC2 instances in a specific Availability Zone. During one hour, 20 instances use the reservation and the remaining 10 slots go unused. No discounts apply. How should the charges for the reservation and the 20 instances using it be estimated for this hour?

source.label: Amazon EC2 — 容量予約の請求

learning.reason: The On-Demand usage for the 20 instances and the charges for the 10 unused reserved slots both apply. Do not count the reservation charge twice for the instances using it.
learning.concept: An On-Demand Capacity Reservation secures capacity. Unused slots incur the same instance charges, so slots that are no longer needed continue to add to cost if left reserved.

choices.text: Only the 20 instances that were used are charged; unused reserved capacity has no cost.
choices.explanation: The 10 unused but reserved slots are also charged at the On-Demand rate.

choices.text: Charge for the 20 instances in use and the 10 unused slots; do not add the instances using the reservation a second time.
choices.explanation: Account for the running instances covered by the reservation and the capacity that was reserved but left unused.

choices.text: Charge for all 30 reserved instances, then add the full cost of the 20 instances launched within the reservation.
choices.explanation: This double-counts the instances whose usage matches the reservation.

choices.text: Charge only for the 10 unused slots; the 20 instances launched using the reservation are free.
choices.explanation: Running instances also incur usage charges.

category: コスト最適化
title: Avoid Double-Counting Savings for the Same Resource
prompt: For a test EC2 instance scheduled for shutdown, Cost Optimization Hub recommends resizing it to save $200 per month or deleting it to save $350 per month, based on the same assumptions. Neither action affects other charges, and both are feasible. How should the aggregate achievable monthly savings for this resource be estimated?

source.label: AWS Cost Optimization Hub — 削減機会の集約

learning.reason: The deletion recommendation yields greater savings than the mutually exclusive resize recommendation for the same resource, so count only $350 per month.
learning.concept: Simply adding multiple recommendations can count the same cost reduction twice. Identify alternative actions before aggregating their estimated savings.

choices.text: Use $350 per month as the estimated savings for the resource.
choices.explanation: Deleting the same resource is an alternative to resizing it, not an additional source of savings. For budgeting, use the higher estimate.

choices.text: Add $200 and $350 to get $550 per month.
choices.explanation: The deleted instance cannot also yield additional resizing savings, so this double-counts savings from the same baseline.

choices.text: Subtract $200 from $350 and count only $150 per month toward the total.
choices.explanation: Both recommendations estimate savings from the same current configuration; their difference is not the achievable total.

choices.text: Use only the lower estimate, $200 per month, as the value Cost Optimization Hub would aggregate.
choices.explanation: When aggregating mutually exclusive recommendations, use the strategy with the larger savings.

sourceLabel: AWS Cost Optimization Hub — Aggregating Savings Opportunities

category: コスト最適化
title: Evaluate the Rate Change Alongside Actual Runtime
prompt: An x86_64 Lambda function processes images. The team wants to lower its unit rate by switching to arm64, but a layer used by the function contains native libraries. The team must maintain the same quality and processing-time limit and explain the cost difference before switching. Which actions should it take? Select TWO.

source.label: AWS Lambda — 命令セットアーキテクチャ

learning.reason: Make the function and native dependencies compatible with arm64, then test both architectures using the same inputs and compare execution charges using measured billed duration and memory alongside architecture-specific rates.
learning.concept: Choosing arm64 or x86_64 affects both pricing and runtime characteristics. The unit-rate difference alone does not establish actual cost or performance.

choices.text: Change only the function setting to arm64 and keep using the existing binaries in the x86_64 layer.
choices.explanation: The instruction sets differ, so native libraries that are incompatible with arm64 cannot be used.

choices.text: If the arm64 unit rate is lower, assume costs will fall by the same percentage without measuring billed duration.
choices.explanation: Runtime may change, so the unit rate alone does not determine the percentage reduction in execution cost.

choices.text: Prepare an arm64-compatible function and native dependencies, and build the layer for the same architecture.
choices.explanation: This ensures the function and dependency binaries can run on the target architecture.

choices.text: Increase reserved concurrency so x86_64 instructions can run in an arm64 environment.
choices.explanation: Changing the number of concurrent executions does not change library architecture compatibility.

choices.text: Run the same set of inputs on both architectures, compare the results, latency, and billed duration, and calculate the execution cost.
choices.explanation: This evaluates actual usage together with the pricing difference while checking the quality and performance requirements.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Move Index Writes to the Standby Search Domain
prompt: Cross-cluster replication is configured between OpenSearch Service domains, and searches are running against a follower in another Region. Writes in the source Region have stopped, and the follower has been confirmed to have caught up with the latest changes. After failover, writes must go to the follower's existing index, and replication with the source index must end. Which operation should be performed?

source.label: Amazon OpenSearch Service — クロスクラスター複製

learning.reason: Stop replication completely on the follower and confirm that it has become a regular index before redirecting writes.
learning.concept: A pause leaves the follower relationship in place. Stopping replication ends following, and the same replication relationship cannot be resumed.

choices.text: Pause replication on the follower and immediately write to that index.
choices.explanation: Pausing replication does not end the follower state or make the index a regular index.

choices.text: Change the application's endpoint to the follower domain to move both reads and writes.
choices.explanation: Changing the endpoint does not change the read-only status of the follower index.

choices.text: Fully stop replication for the index on the follower, then direct writes to it after it becomes a regular index.
choices.explanation: Ending the replication relationship allows the index, which already has synchronized data, to be updated.

choices.text: Change the follower's connection permissions to read-only and wait for replication to resume from the leader.
choices.explanation: This does not convert the index into a regular index that accepts writes.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Restore backups with approval independent of the primary organization
prompt: Business backups are in a logically air-gapped vault in the primary AWS organization. To prepare for a situation in which administrative operations in the primary organization become unavailable, you want to obtain temporary restore access from a separate recovery organization after multiple approvals. The recovery organization, IAM Identity Center, and approvers are already in place. Integration between the two organizations can be configured in advance. Which restore design should you choose?

source.label: AWS Backup — 論理エアギャップボールトの複数承認

learning.reason: Share the recovery organization's approval team in advance and associate it in the vault-owning account. When needed, request approval from the recovery account and restore through a restore access vault after approval is granted.
learning.concept: A restore access vault is an access point for viewing the original recovery points. It is not a vault that stores another copy of the recovery points.

choices.text: Share the approval team from the separate organization through AWS RAM and associate it with the vault on the primary side in advance. The recovery account creates a restore access vault after obtaining multiple approvals.
choices.explanation: This prepares an approval path that does not require administrative operations in the primary organization and allows restoration from an authorized recovery account.

choices.text: Do not create an approval team; have the primary account create a new standard AWS RAM share after the incident occurs.
choices.explanation: This depends on administrative operations in the primary organization and does not provide a path to obtain access through multiple approvals.

choices.text: Configure only Vault Lock on the original vault in the primary account, and have the recovery account access it by specifying the same vault name.
choices.explanation: Vault Lock protects retention, but it does not provide an approval process that grants access to a separate recovery organization.

choices.text: Create a standard vault with the same name in the recovery account and consider the backups to have been shared.
choices.explanation: The original recovery points do not appear in a vault merely because it has the same name, and this provides no approval-based access to the original vault.

sourceLabel: AWS Backup — Multi-party approval for logically air-gapped vaults

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Cut over to a restored file server using the existing share name
prompt: A Windows application uses a share hosted on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server through a custom DNS alias and requires Kerberos authentication. A new file system was restored from a backup into the same Active Directory. The backup alias is also associated with the new file system. Before cutover, writes to the old share will be stopped, and the old file system will be retained for investigation. Choose TWO additional cutover steps.

source.label: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server — DNSエイリアスの関連付け

learning.reason: Move the SPNs for the same alias from the old side to the computer object of the new file system, and change the DNS CNAME to the restored file system's default DNS name.
learning.concept: An alias can be retained during restoration. Actual name resolution and the Kerberos service identity must both be switched through the DNS record and the Active Directory SPN.

choices.text: When the alias appears on the new system, assume that the CNAME and the Kerberos authentication target were changed automatically.
choices.explanation: Associating an alias with FSx does not update customer-managed DNS records or Active Directory SPNs.

choices.text: Move the alias SPNs to the AD computer object of the restored file system.
choices.explanation: This binds Kerberos authentication for the same share name to the restored destination and avoids duplicate SPNs.

choices.text: Register duplicate SPNs for the same alias on both the old and new file systems.
choices.explanation: The authentication target for the same service name would no longer be unique, so Kerberos authentication after cutover cannot be guaranteed.

choices.text: Update the alias CNAME to point to the default DNS name of the new file system.
choices.explanation: This lets the application continue using the same name while reaching the new file system.

choices.text: Provide users only with the DNS name of the old file system.
choices.explanation: This satisfies neither cutover to the restored destination nor continued use of the existing custom alias.

sourceLabel: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server — Associating DNS aliases

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Use another Region without splitting artifact storage ownership
prompt: A tools account in Tokyo manages CodePipeline and uses artifacts built in Tokyo in a CodeDeploy action in Osaka within the same account. The pipeline is defined with CloudFormation, and the tools account manages the artifact buckets and encryption keys. How should this be configured without adding custom transfer processing to the build?

source.label: AWS CodePipeline — クロスリージョンアクション

learning.reason: Configure stores for Tokyo and Osaka in artifactStores, and specify Osaka as the Region for the Osaka action. The bucket and key for the Osaka store must be in Osaka.
learning.concept: CodePipeline automatically copies input artifacts for cross-Region actions into the Region of the action. Configure a store for each Region that contains actions.

choices.text: Specify one artifactStore in Tokyo and change only the Region of the deployment action to Osaka.
choices.explanation: An action in another Region requires an artifactStores configuration for that Region.

choices.text: Place buckets in Tokyo and Osaka, but use the Tokyo KMS key for the Osaka store.
choices.explanation: The bucket and KMS key that encrypt artifacts must be in the same Region as the cross-Region action.

choices.text: Register Tokyo and Osaka in artifactStores, and place the Osaka bucket and key in Osaka in the same tools account.
choices.explanation: This uses CodePipeline artifact copying to make the input available in the Region where the action exists.

choices.text: Use only the Tokyo artifactStore and replicate to Osaka with S3 Replication so that the Osaka action detects it automatically.
choices.explanation: Even with replication, the required Osaka artifact store is not registered in the pipeline definition.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Reflect secret updates in the database password
prompt: The MasterUserPassword of an RDS instance created with CloudFormation references a Secrets Manager secret without specifying a version. An administrator changed only the value in Secrets Manager, but the old password remained valid for RDS. Automatic rotation is not configured. Choose the appropriate explanation for the future configuration.

source.label: AWS CloudFormation — Secrets Managerの動的参照

learning.reason: A dynamic reference is retrieved when CloudFormation creates or updates the resource containing it. To keep the DB and secret synchronized, configure rotation that also updates the DB credentials.
learning.concept: An unversioned dynamic reference resolves the current value during an update, but a secret-change event does not automatically propagate to the resource.

choices.text: An unversioned dynamic reference is continuously monitored by RDS, so wait for propagation to finish.
choices.explanation: An existing DB does not monitor changes to the referenced value; waiting does not update the password.

choices.text: The value is retrieved again when the DB resource containing the reference is updated. In the future, configure Secrets Manager rotation that also updates the DB password.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes resolving the reference value from the mechanism that updates the password on the database side.

choices.text: Pin the current value to a version ID so that RDS obtains the next secret change.
choices.explanation: A pinned reference does not follow a new version, and changing only the secret does not update the resource.

choices.text: Change the tag of another resource unrelated to the DB in the stack so that the DB dynamic reference is always resolved again.
choices.explanation: A change that does not update the resource containing the reference provides no guarantee that the DB password will be updated.

sourceLabel: AWS CloudFormation — Secrets Manager dynamic references

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Review an emergency change before restoring the template value
prompt: During incident response, an operator temporarily changed a setting explicitly declared in a CloudFormation-managed resource. The resource type and property support drift-aware change sets. You want to review the proposed changes that restore the template's declared value before applying them, and, if an update to another resource fails, return to the state immediately before the update while preserving that temporary change. Which option should you choose?

source.label: AWS CloudFormation — ドリフトを考慮した変更セット

learning.reason: A drift-aware change set compares against current values, so you can review and apply the restoration. If it fails, it returns to the actual state from before application.
learning.concept: A standard change set compares the last deployed settings with the new template. Drift-aware change sets also use the values currently in effect.

choices.text: Run Detect drift on the stack and rely on the detection operation alone to restore the template value.
choices.explanation: Drift detection identifies differences between current and expected values; it does not modify resources.

choices.text: Pass the unchanged template to a standard change set and assume the manually changed setting will always appear in the diff.
choices.explanation: A comparison against the template alone may not include a manually changed property if its declared value has not changed.

choices.text: Change the template's declared value to match the temporary value and adopt the current setting as the new source of truth.
choices.explanation: This may adopt the current value, but it does not meet the requirement to restore the original declared value.

choices.text: Generate a drift-aware change set, review the changes from the actual value back to the declared value, and execute it.
choices.explanation: For supported resources, the plan includes actual values and can restore the actual pre-update state if the update fails.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Compare display delays on users' devices
prompt: The response times of an e-commerce site's API servers are stable, but users report that the purchase page takes a long time to display in a particular mobile browser. You want to measure a sample of real users who have given consent and compare the distributions of resource loading and page display by page and browser. Synthetic traffic alone is unlikely to reproduce the issue. What is the best approach?

source.label: CloudWatch RUM — ウェブアプリのモニター

learning.reason: Instrument clients with CloudWatch RUM, enable performance telemetry, and configure the required session sampling. Compare the measurements by browser and page.
learning.concept: Synthetic monitoring repeatedly follows a configured path. RUM captures load times and errors on users' actual devices.

choices.text: Instrument actual clients with CloudWatch RUM and sample performance telemetry for the pages in scope.
choices.explanation: This lets you compare real-user processing times by device, browser, and page.

choices.text: Run the purchase flow every minute in a standard CloudWatch Synthetics browser and treat its response-time distribution as representative of all users.
choices.explanation: This provides repeatable monitoring, but it does not measure real devices and networks.

choices.text: Check the ALB TargetResponseTime metric for the relevant paths and treat it as the browser's full page-load time.
choices.explanation: Target response time does not include browser rendering or the timing of static-resource loads.

choices.text: Sample only downstream backend calls with X-Ray.
choices.explanation: This can show backend dependencies, but it cannot provide the distribution of client-side page-load times.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Separate audit scans from the production patch window
prompt: Patch managed EC2 instances in production OUs across two Regions using Systems Manager. Select targets by workload tag and check compliance daily, but apply patches and allow reboots only on weekends. You want to maintain the configuration at the organizational-unit level rather than register executions account by account. Which configuration should you use?

source.label: AWS Systems Manager — Quick Setupのパッチポリシー

learning.reason: Deploy a Quick Setup patch policy to the target OUs and Regions, select targets by workload tag, and set separate schedules for scanning and installation.
learning.concept: A scan checks compliance against the baseline. Configure application and reboot settings with installation so you can control the maintenance window.

choices.text: Enable daily patch scans in Quick Setup host management and rely on that same configuration to install patches automatically on weekends.
choices.explanation: Enabling compliance scans does not create a weekend installation policy.

choices.text: Schedule daily scans in Quick Setup and use the scan's reboot option to apply patches only on Saturdays.
choices.explanation: A scan does not install patches. You need a separate installation schedule.

choices.text: Deploy a Quick Setup patch policy to the production OUs and configure daily scans and weekend installations separately.
choices.explanation: This lets you configure target selection and both schedules at the organizational-unit level, limiting when patches are applied.

choices.text: Set only the patch baseline approval delay and scan and install patches every day at the same time.
choices.explanation: Approval rules determine which patches are eligible; they do not establish a weekend installation schedule.

sourceLabel: AWS Systems Manager — Quick Setup patch policy

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Design separate paths for new logs and historical logs
prompt: Aggregate CloudWatch Logs from multiple accounts and Regions in AWS Organizations. Auditors will search future logs from a central log group. In addition, the logs from the 30 days before central aggregation begins must remain available in an auditable destination. Assuming the behavior of the organization's centralization feature, which operating approach should you choose?

source.label: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — アカウントとリージョンをまたぐ集約

learning.reason: Use centralization rules for logs ingested after creation, and separately export the previous 30 days from the sources.
learning.concept: Centralization rules process newly ingested logs. Existing source events require a separate historical migration plan.

choices.text: Creating a centralization rule copies the entire retention period of logs already present in each source for the first time.
choices.explanation: Centralization processes only data ingested after the rule is created.

choices.text: Create a cross-account observability link and use it to copy logs into the central log group.
choices.explanation: Being able to view data through a shared link is different from having a copy in the central log group.

choices.text: Add a subscription filter and assume that it will deliver all events created before the filter was added, in sequence.
choices.explanation: A new delivery path does not replay existing events from before it was configured.

choices.text: Use CloudWatch Logs centralization rules for new logs, and separately export the specified period of historical logs from the sources for audit retention.
choices.explanation: This handles newly ingested logs and existing history separately, meeting both requirements.

sourceLabel: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — Cross-account and cross-Region centralization

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Automating quota requests for new and existing accounts
prompt: A technical team in an AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled must request specified values for adjustable service quotas in the Tokyo Region for all 20 existing accounts and all accounts created in the future. The team must also track the approval outcomes. How should it use the organization features in Service Quotas and handle existing accounts? Choose two.

source.label: Service Quotas — 組織用のクォータ引き上げテンプレート

learning.reason: Associate a template with the organization for new accounts. Check current values in existing accounts, and submit an increase request for each account where the current value is insufficient.
learning.concept: A template automatically creates requests for new accounts. Requests and approvals are separate, and updating a template does not submit requests retroactively for existing accounts.

choices.text: Associate a quota request template containing the required increases with the organization.
choices.explanation: This can automatically submit the specified increase requests for newly created accounts.

choices.text: Assume that quotas in existing accounts are updated automatically when the template is saved, and do not submit increase requests for them.
choices.explanation: The template does not apply retroactively to existing accounts, so some accounts may remain below the required values.

choices.text: Apply an AWS Organizations SCP to allow quota values above the current limits.
choices.explanation: An SCP controls which API operations are allowed; it does not change quotas.

choices.text: Create CloudWatch alarms for quota usage and treat an alert as proof that an increase request has been submitted.
choices.explanation: An alarm notifies the team about usage but does not submit an increase request.

choices.text: Check the current values in existing accounts and explicitly request increases in the accounts and Region where values are insufficient.
choices.explanation: This identifies and addresses shortfalls in existing accounts, separately from the template's scope, and lets the team track the outcomes.

sourceLabel: Service Quotas — Quota increase request templates for organizations

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Launch capacity before the daily increase in demand
prompt: A delivery platform runs on an EC2 Auto Scaling group. The opening time itself varies by day of the week, and the increase in load can be predicted from records of the past two weeks. Nodes take 12 minutes to be ready to handle requests. The current target tracking policy must remain in place. The team first wants to assess forecast accuracy without changing capacity, then start preparing capacity before the forecast time. The group's maximum capacity must not change. Which approach is appropriate?

source.label: 予測スケーリングの仕組み

learning.reason: Use forecast-only mode to compare hourly forecasts with actuals. When moving to production, enable scale-out based on forecasts and set a lead time.
learning.concept: SchedulingBufferTime, which starts instances earlier, is separate from instance warmup, which accounts for metric effects while instances are being added. Predictive scaling does not scale in based on forecasts, so retain target tracking.

choices.text: Enable forecasting and scaling, and lengthen the default instance warmup during the initial assessment. After moving to production, set warmup to 12 minutes.
choices.explanation: A longer warmup does not suppress the initial capacity changes based on forecasts, and it does not itself move scaling actions earlier.

choices.text: Register scheduled actions for each day of the week based on recent observations, and leave increases and decreases around those times to target tracking.
choices.explanation: Fixed-time control is possible, but this does not meet the requirement to evaluate forecast-based capacity predictions that adapt to observed data before moving to production.

choices.text: Compare forecasts with actuals in forecast-only mode, then switch to forecasting and scaling when moving to production. Specify a lead time of at least 12 minutes, and choose a setting that does not raise maximum capacity.
choices.explanation: Use ForecastOnly and ForecastAndScale for the two phases. SchedulingBufferTime starts capacity earlier, while maximum capacity remains unchanged even when the forecast exceeds it.

choices.text: Keep forecast-only mode and target tracking in production, and lower the target tracking target to start instances earlier.
choices.explanation: This does not start instances based on the forecast before the load appears in the metric. Lowering the target can also increase capacity during periods of low demand.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Record the same source revision in approvals and build artifacts
prompt: In a V2 pipeline that uses a GitHub connection in CodePipeline, later commits can arrive while a release approval is pending. The team wants the commit ID captured by that pipeline execution in both a manifest created by CodeBuild and the link on the approval screen. The source ZIP does not contain .git, and no additional stores or processing can be added. Which approach meets both requirements?

source.label: CodePipelineアクションの変数

learning.reason: The source action's output variable CommitId identifies the revision captured by that action and can be passed to later action settings using a namespace.
learning.concept: Input artifacts carry build outputs, while output variables expose metadata from the same execution for use in later action settings. Configure a namespace separately from the artifact name.

choices.text: Have CodeBuild retrieve the source branch's HEAD, and use the same branch in the approval link.
choices.explanation: The branch may advance while approval is pending, so this does not refer to the revision captured by that execution.

choices.text: Set a namespace on the source action, then expand its CommitId in the CodeBuild environment variables and the manual approval review URL.
choices.explanation: Both settings can refer to the source output of the same pipeline execution, so the approval link can be pinned to a specific commit.

choices.text: Set the reserved PipelineExecutionId in the CodeBuild environment variables and approval URL.
choices.explanation: This identifies the pipeline execution, but it is not a VCS commit ID and cannot be used to construct a commit details URL.

choices.text: Leave the upstream action unchanged, use CODEBUILD_RESOLVED_SOURCE_VERSION in CodeBuild, and reference a variable with the same name in the variables namespace in the approval URL.
choices.explanation: A build environment variable is not automatically exposed as a pipeline-level variable, so the approval configuration cannot reference it directly.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Track only delivery failures for scheduled, time-limited jobs
prompt: At each contract's renewal time, EventBridge Scheduler must start an existing Step Functions state machine once. Renewal times differ by contract. The team wants completed schedules to be cleaned up automatically without ongoing manual work, and it wants to inspect later the input for a StartExecution call that could not be delivered even after Scheduler retries. Errors after the workflow starts are handled by existing monitoring. Which two settings should be configured?

source.label: EventBridge Schedulerのスケジュール自動削除

learning.reason: Use a one-time schedule that is deleted after completion, and record delivery failures to the target in Scheduler's dead-letter queue.
learning.concept: A Scheduler delivery failure and a failure within a workflow that started occur at different boundaries. Delivery retries and the DLQ apply while invoking the target.

choices.text: Create an at expression for each contract and set the action after completion to DELETE.
choices.explanation: This avoids having to manually delete schedules created for a single invocation after they complete.

choices.text: Set each contract's renewal time as EndDate and set the action after completion to NONE.
choices.explanation: An at schedule does not evaluate EndDate. With NONE, the resource remains after completion.

choices.text: Use a Catch in the state machine being started to record the input when delivery fails.
choices.explanation: If the invocation never reaches the state machine, execution does not start and its Catch is not reached.

choices.text: Configure a retry policy and a standard SQS DLQ on the Scheduler target, and grant the execution role permission to send messages.
choices.explanation: After retries are exhausted, Scheduler sends the details of the undelivered event to the queue.

choices.text: Store Step Functions execution status change events with a separate EventBridge rule to capture target execution results.
choices.explanation: This can capture the status of executions that started, but not the input for a StartExecution call that was never delivered and therefore created no execution.

sourceLabel: Automatic deletion of EventBridge Scheduler schedules

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Keep Running Monitoring Stacks After an OU Move
prompt: A service-managed CloudFormation StackSet deploys monitoring stacks to an operations OU. When an account is moved to a migration OU, you want the stack already created in that account to keep running as is and to be excluded from future central updates. Automatic deployment to accounts added to the operations OU in the future must remain enabled. Individual accounts cannot perform manual operations. Which approach is appropriate?

source.label: StackSetsの自動デプロイと削除時の動作

learning.reason: With the removal setting that retains existing stacks, the stack in an account removed from the OU is detached from the StackSet. Automatic deployment to new accounts remains enabled.
learning.concept: Automatic account onboarding and offboarding is configured at the StackSet level. Retaining individual resources is different from retaining the stack itself.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy: Retain on every resource in the stack and apply the default behavior when the account leaves.
choices.explanation: Even if individual resources can be retained when a stack is deleted, the existing stack will not remain as a detached management unit.

choices.text: Enable termination protection on the target stack and move the OU while the default deletion is blocked.
choices.explanation: This prevents deletion; it does not configure the stack to be cleanly detached from the StackSet during the move and removed from future management.

choices.text: Disable automatic deployment and keep the current stack instances in the target OU.
choices.explanation: Accounts added to the OU in the future will no longer receive automatic deployments.

choices.text: Keep automatic deployment enabled, change the removal behavior to Retain stacks, and move the account.
choices.explanation: The stack and its resources remain in place, and only the association with the central StackSet is removed.

sourceLabel: Automatic deployment and removal behavior for StackSets

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Register Only Nodes Whose Initialization Is Confirmed
prompt: An EC2 Auto Scaling group associated with an ALB target group launches nodes from an updated AMI. At startup, each node retrieves a cache and runs an application self-test. Retrieval takes between a few minutes and 20 minutes, and the HTTP port responds before initialization is complete. You must prevent target registration until initialization is confirmed and replace nodes that do not receive a callback. Let Auto Scaling continue managing existing registrations and capacity adjustments. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: Auto Scalingグループでのライフサイクルフック

learning.reason: A launch lifecycle hook can hold an instance before automatic registration. Proceed with CONTINUE only on success, and use ABANDON on timeout so Auto Scaling can launch a replacement node.
learning.concept: Health checks control traffic after registration. A launch lifecycle hook checks readiness before registration itself.

choices.text: Pause at a launch lifecycle hook and send CONTINUE after initialization. Set the hook's default result to ABANDON.
choices.explanation: While paused, the instance does not proceed to target registration; if no response arrives, its launch is abandoned.

choices.text: Pause at a launch lifecycle hook and send CONTINUE after initialization. Also set the hook's default result to CONTINUE.
choices.explanation: If no callback arrives, the instance proceeds to registration after the timeout.

choices.text: Change the ALB health check to a path that confirms initialization and extend the health check grace period.
choices.explanation: This can limit traffic before initialization, but target registration itself occurs before initialization has been confirmed.

choices.text: Instead, use instance refresh checkpoints and set Auto Scaling's default warmup to 20 minutes for each batch.
choices.explanation: This can control the pace of an instance refresh, but it cannot gate registration based on per-node confirmation and does not apply to ordinary scale-out.

sourceLabel: Lifecycle hooks for Auto Scaling groups

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Validate Configuration Syntax and References Before Deployment
prompt: You deploy free-form JSON that describes destination routing with AWS AppConfig. Before deployment begins across the environment, you want to verify required keys and weight types, and confirm that every destination code is valid in the management team's DynamoDB registry. You want to maintain the syntax rules as a JSON Schema. Which two configurations should you choose?

source.label: AppConfigの設定プロファイルのバリデーター

learning.reason: The same free-form configuration profile can use declarative syntax validation and semantic validation against external data.
learning.concept: AppConfig validation occurs before deployment. Gradual deployment and automatic rollback on alarms can also help address issues that emerge after deployment starts.

choices.text: Configure a CloudWatch alarm for the AppConfig environment and roll back if an invalid destination is observed at the first deployment target.
choices.explanation: Detection occurs after deployment begins, so this does not meet the requirement to validate references before deployment.

choices.text: Register a JSON Schema validator with the configuration profile and define the required keys and value types.
choices.explanation: This declaratively validates the syntax of a free-form configuration.

choices.text: Define the DynamoDB table as an external reference in JSON Schema and use schema reference resolution to query the registry.
choices.explanation: JSON Schema references point to other schema definitions; they do not make runtime queries to DynamoDB.

choices.text: After retrieving the configuration, add a hook from the AppConfig Agent to the application to require each host to query DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: Validating on each host after retrieval cannot stop an invalid configuration before deployment begins.

choices.text: Add a Lambda validator to the configuration profile to compare destinations with the registry and fail validation if any are invalid.
choices.explanation: Lambda can query DynamoDB programmatically, and AppConfig applies validation as part of starting a deployment.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Identify Anomalies in a Changing EC2 Fleet by Instance
prompt: The number of EC2 workers that collect memory utilization with the CloudWatch Agent frequently changes. Even if the average is normal, you want an alert with the instance ID when a particular worker exceeds a threshold. The dashboard must show a separate time series for every worker. How can you avoid creating alarms again for each new instance while keeping the dashboard display?

source.label: CloudWatch Metrics Insightsの複数時系列アラーム

learning.reason: Metrics Insights can generate and evaluate a time series for each instance ID. The query automatically includes new instances, and state changes for individual series that exceed the threshold can drive notifications.
learning.concept: The dashboard's SEARCH expression and the alarm's evaluation data can be selected independently. A multi-time-series alarm uses GROUP BY to define the aggregation dimension and ORDER BY to define the evaluation order.

choices.text: Set the SEARCH expression used by the dashboard directly as the metric-math alarm and notify on state changes.
choices.explanation: SEARCH can select series for a graph, but it is not supported as an input to a CloudWatch metric-math alarm.

choices.text: Use Metrics Insights without grouping to return the MAX across all workers, then create a single time-series alarm.
choices.explanation: This detects an anomalous maximum, but aggregation loses the instance ID, so it cannot notify you which individual worker was affected.

choices.text: Use Metrics Insights grouped by InstanceId and evaluate a multi-time-series alarm in descending utilization order. Use EventBridge to notify on contributor state-change events.
choices.explanation: The alarm evaluates each series and can emit events for state changes associated with the affected workers.

choices.text: Combine the metric alarms for each instance ID into a composite alarm, OR-ing the individual alarms currently configured.
choices.explanation: Individual thresholds can be retained, but the individual alarms and composite conditions must be updated as instances are added or removed.

category: コスト最適化
title: Apply an existing DB reservation discount when moving to Multi-AZ
prompt: An account has a size-flexible Reserved DB Instance for a Single-AZ db.t4g.large running RDS for PostgreSQL in a particular account and Region. Performance testing has confirmed that the workload can run on one primary db.t4g.medium and one standby of the same family. There are no other running instances, and the deployment will be changed to a Multi-AZ DB instance during the remaining reservation term. Which statement about the instance-hour discount is correct?

source.label: Amazon RDSのサイズ柔軟性と正規化単位

learning.reason: A Single-AZ large provides four normalized units per hour. The two medium instances in a Multi-AZ DB instance configuration consume four units per hour in total, so the existing discount covers them all.
learning.concept: Reserved DB Instances apply discounts to eligible usage. For engines that support size flexibility, convert the number and size of instances to normalized units, and verify matches such as engine, instance family, and Region.

choices.text: The discount applies only to the primary medium instance, so a separate medium reservation is required for the standby.
