choices.explanation: Size-flexible reservations can apply to both Single-AZ and Multi-AZ usage. Even with the standby included, the usage fits within the four normalized units covered by the reservation.

choices.text: Two Multi-AZ medium instances in the same family and engine use the same number of normalized units as one Single-AZ large instance, so the existing reservation covers the instance hours for the entire deployment.
choices.explanation: Each medium uses two units per hour, while a large uses four. The reservation does not apply to separate charges such as storage.

choices.text: Changing to Multi-AZ changes the deployment type, so the discount no longer applies at all.
choices.explanation: For this PostgreSQL reservation, size flexibility applies to both deployment types.

choices.text: The existing reservation also covers all instance hours if the workload is split across three Single-AZ medium instances in the same family.
choices.explanation: Three Single-AZ medium instances use six units per hour. The existing reservation cannot cover usage above four units.

sourceLabel: Amazon RDS size flexibility and normalized units

category: コスト最適化
title: Limit additional charges to upload paths that improve transfer times
prompt: A photo intake system uploads directly from browsers to a single S3 bucket. In some remote locations, uploads through the standard Regional endpoint miss the required transfer time even when multipart uploads are parallelized; clients near the same Region meet the target. Objects are processed immediately in the same bucket, and the solution must not increase storage in another Region. Which approach improves the inbound network path while limiting additional charges?

source.label: Amazon S3料金のTransfer Acceleration項目

learning.reason: The same bucket can be accessed through both Regional and Accelerate endpoints. Switching only remote clients that need the improvement to the accelerated path, based on measured results, limits its use.
learning.concept: Evaluate Transfer Acceleration charges separately from standard data transfer charges. If AWS determines that an upload to the accelerated endpoint was not faster than the standard path, the acceleration charge for that upload is waived.

choices.text: Standardize on the Regional endpoint and multipart uploads for all clients. Because there are no additional charges, address the remote path by retrying parts.
choices.explanation: Parts can be retried or uploaded in parallel, but that does not change the network path from a remote location to the Region.

choices.text: Create an S3 bucket in each location and use S3 replication to consolidate the objects into the existing bucket.
choices.explanation: This can shorten the distance to an entry point, but it requires additional storage and replication and does not meet the requirement to write to the original bucket immediately.

choices.text: Put a cache-enabled CloudFront distribution in front of S3 and reduce Internet upload traffic through cache hits on PUT requests.
choices.explanation: CloudFront does not cache PUT requests, so it cannot reuse object uploads.

choices.text: Enable Transfer Acceleration for the target bucket and compare results by location. Use the Accelerate endpoint only for clients whose standard path misses the transfer target and whose accelerated path meets it.
choices.explanation: Measure the benefit in each location and limit use of a path that may incur additional charges to where it is needed. No acceleration fee is charged for an upload that AWS determines was not accelerated.

sourceLabel: Transfer Acceleration line item in Amazon S3 pricing

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Recover a deleted volume without relying on an earlier snapshot
prompt: Data on stateful EC2 workers is protected with periodic snapshots. If an EBS data volume is accidentally deleted, the goal is to recover the volume as it was at deletion, including changes since the previous backup, for three days after deletion. In the Region, all EBS volumes must be covered, and a minimum seven-day waiting period must be enforced for changing or deleting the recovery rule. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: EBS Recycle Bin保持ルールの作成

learning.reason: When enabled, a Region-level rule for deleted volumes allows covered EBS volumes to be restored during the retention period. A rule lock enforces the waiting period after an unlock request.
learning.concept: Deleted EBS volumes and EBS snapshots are distinct resource types. A Region-level rule for volumes can have a retention period of up to seven days and an unlock waiting period of 7–30 days.

choices.text: Create a Region-level EBS_VOLUME retention rule for three days and configure a rule lock with a seven-day unlock waiting period.
choices.explanation: This retains covered volumes after deletion. After an unlock request, the rule cannot be changed or deleted until the waiting period has elapsed.

choices.text: Create a Region-level EBS_SNAPSHOT retention rule for three days and configure a rule lock with a seven-day unlock waiting period.
choices.explanation: This targets deleted snapshots. It does not retain the EBS volume data as it existed at deletion.

choices.text: Configure a tag-level EBS_VOLUME rule for three days, have an organizational automation process apply the target tag, and then lock the rule.
choices.explanation: Tag-level rules are supported, but Recycle Bin rule locks are not supported for them, and resources without the tag would not be protected.

choices.text: Set AWS Backup Vault Lock on the storage location for periodic snapshots and restore from the latest recovery point after deletion.
choices.explanation: This protects stored backups, but does not guarantee retention of changes made between the latest snapshot and deletion.

sourceLabel: Create an EBS Recycle Bin retention rule

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Allow Kubernetes API access only from the corporate network
prompt: EKS operators can route from the corporate network to the cluster VPC through Direct Connect and a Transit Gateway. CI runners are also in the same VPC. Assume the corporate network and CI can resolve the name of the private Kubernetes API. The cluster must allow kubectl access for authenticated operators and CI while eliminating any Kubernetes API endpoint that is reachable from the Internet. Nodes must continue to retrieve images from external registries through NAT. Which design meets these requirements?

source.label: Amazon EKS cluster endpoint access ガイド

learning.reason: With private access only, the Kubernetes API is reachable from the VPC and connected networks. Restrict source access with the cluster security group.
learning.concept: The AWS API for the EKS service and the Kubernetes API for an individual cluster are separate endpoints. Disabling the latter's public access does not change the NAT route nodes use to retrieve images.

choices.text: Keep public access enabled and restrict the public CIDRs to the fixed corporate Internet egress addresses and the VPC NAT addresses.
choices.explanation: Source restrictions can be applied to the public endpoint, but this does not eliminate an Internet-reachable endpoint.

choices.text: Enable only private access for the Kubernetes API and allow HTTPS from the corporate network and CI in the cluster security group.
choices.explanation: This uses the existing private routes, disables the public endpoint, and preserves kubectl connectivity.

choices.text: Add an interface VPC endpoint for the EKS service API and change kubectl to connect through it.
choices.explanation: That endpoint is for the AWS API used to manage EKS; it does not provide the Kubernetes API for an individual cluster.

choices.text: Keep public access enabled for the Kubernetes API and use the cluster security group to exclude HTTPS sources other than the corporate network and CI.
choices.explanation: The cluster security group controls the private endpoint and does not apply to access through the public endpoint.

sourceLabel: Amazon EKS cluster endpoint access guide

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Move the cluster while keeping its shared data disk
prompt: A commercial cluster application running on Windows Server is being migrated to EC2. The vendor-supported configuration uses two Windows Nitro instances in the same Availability Zone that share one data block device. Each node has a separate boot disk, and the application's clustering mechanism controls write ordering. You do not want to detach and reattach the shared device to the standby node after a host failure. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: Amazon EBS Multi-Attach ガイド

learning.reason: For sharing the same EBS data volume between Windows Nitro instances, use io2 Multi-Attach. Keep a separate boot volume for each instance.
learning.concept: Multi-Attach shares a block device with instances in the same Availability Zone. The application or cluster file system must coordinate writes. Backups are still needed to protect against underlying infrastructure failures.

choices.text: Attach an io2 data volume to both Windows instances with Multi-Attach.
choices.explanation: io2 is supported for this Windows use case. The instances can keep separate boot disks while attaching the same data volume at the same time.

choices.text: Attach an io1 data volume to both Windows instances with Multi-Attach.
choices.explanation: io1 Multi-Attach is available for Linux, but it does not support this Windows configuration.

choices.text: Provide a shared disk as SMB using an FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ configuration.
choices.explanation: This provides shared files over SMB. It cannot be attached as the shared block device required here.

choices.text: Create a separate EBS data volume for each node from an io2 snapshot.
choices.explanation: Separate volumes do not share writes after restoration, so the standby node cannot access the latest state of the shared device.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Rewind the same cluster to just before an incorrect update
prompt: An incorrect update was applied to every record in an Aurora MySQL cluster, and writes have been stopped. A safe recovery point is within the actual backtrack window. There are no valid changes after that point, and temporary database unavailability is acceptable. How should you rewind the same cluster to just before the incorrect update without creating a new cluster or changing the existing connection target?

source.label: Amazon Aurora Backtrack ガイド

learning.reason: With backtracking enabled, Aurora MySQL can rewind an existing cluster to a specified point within the eligible period. Account for the interruption during recovery.
learning.concept: Both Backtrack and point-in-time restore work with past points in time. Choose based on whether recovery should modify the original cluster or create a new one. Aurora selects a consistent time close to the requested time, so verify the time actually applied.

choices.text: Restore the cluster to just before the incorrect update using point-in-time recovery, and leave the application pointed at the existing cluster endpoint.
choices.explanation: Point-in-time recovery creates a new cluster. Applications using the existing endpoint would not use the restored cluster.

choices.text: Use Aurora Backtrack to rewind the existing cluster to a known safe time, then verify the actual recovery point and data before resuming writes.
choices.explanation: The cluster can be rewound in place when the recovery time is within the enabled window.

choices.text: Promote an Aurora Replica in the same cluster that does not have sufficient lag.
choices.explanation: Replicas in the same cluster use shared storage. Promoting one does not restore an earlier state.

choices.text: Restore the most recent manual DB cluster snapshot over the same cluster identifier.
choices.explanation: Restoring a snapshot creates a new cluster. It does not overwrite the running target in place.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Privately expose a Pod TCP service to on-premises clients
prompt: EKS Pods using AWS Load Balancer Controller and Amazon VPC CNI receive transaction data over a TCP protocol other than HTTP. Users are limited to the cluster VPC and the corporate network through Direct Connect, and they need one stable DNS name. Pods receive IP addresses from VPC subnets, and the Pods themselves must be registered as targets according to their lifecycle. Forwarding through NodePort is prohibited; traffic must be sent directly to each Pod IP. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: Amazon EKS Network Load Balancing ガイド

learning.reason: Use a LoadBalancer Service that creates an internal NLB, with a TCP listener and IP targets. Pod IPs are registered as targets, and users can connect through the internal NLB DNS name.
learning.concept: When selecting an external load balancer for an EKS Service, evaluate the protocol, exposure scope, and target type separately.

choices.text: Create an Ingress for an internal ALB, with IP targets and a TCP listener.
choices.explanation: IP targets can connect to Pods, but an ALB does not support a general-purpose TCP listener and cannot forward the required protocol.

choices.text: Create a LoadBalancer Service for an internal NLB, with a TCP listener and instance targets.
choices.explanation: It can forward TCP, but instance targets register nodes, and traffic is forwarded through NodePort.

choices.text: Create a ClusterIP Service and publish its virtual IP on the cluster network through on-premises DNS.
choices.explanation: ClusterIP is an internal service IP. It does not function as a load balancer directly usable from the VPC and on-premises network.

choices.text: Create a LoadBalancer Service for an internal NLB, with a TCP listener and IP targets.
choices.explanation: This keeps access on private routes and forwards TCP traffic to registered Pod targets.

sourceLabel: Amazon EKS Network Load Balancing Guide

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Speed up image-processing scratch objects within one AZ
prompt: An image-processing cluster pinned to one Availability Zone makes millions of PUT and GET requests through the S3 API for intermediate batch data. If the scratch data is lost, it can be reprocessed from the originals, and outputs are stored in existing S3 Standard. Which configuration can reduce and stabilize access time for the scratch data without rewriting the application to use a file system API?

source.label: Amazon S3 Express One Zone directory buckets ガイド

learning.reason: An S3 Express One Zone directory bucket in the same Availability Zone is suited to low-latency S3 object operations.
learning.concept: Directory buckets use zonal endpoints and supported APIs. For a single-AZ scratch area, maintain a separate copy of the originals or a way to reprocess them.

choices.text: Configure a directory bucket with S3 Express One Zone in the same Availability Zone as the processing cluster.
choices.explanation: This preserves the S3 API and provides a low-latency scratch area within the Availability Zone.

choices.text: Keep a general purpose bucket in S3 Standard and enable S3 Transfer Acceleration.
choices.explanation: This feature improves transfers over distant internet paths; it does not optimize object operations from processing in the same Availability Zone.

choices.text: Use S3 One Zone-IA for a general purpose bucket and specify a zonal endpoint in the same Availability Zone as the processing cluster.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA is for infrequent access and does not provide the zonal endpoint or dedicated low-latency processing of a directory bucket.

choices.text: Associate FSx for Lustre with the existing source bucket and mount the inputs and scratch directory as a file system on the processing cluster.
choices.explanation: This supports high-performance file processing, but it does not meet the requirement to use the native S3 API for scratch data.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 Express One Zone Directory Buckets Guide

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Keeping up with irregular EFS throughput demand
prompt: A group of containers uses Regional EFS over NFS from multiple AZs. During a batch job that runs every few weeks at an unpredictable time, metrics show that burst credits are depleted and throughput drops. Normal usage is low, and you want to avoid committing to fixed capacity for peaks, making manual changes before a batch, or reducing resilience to an AZ failure. Which configuration should you use?

source.label: Amazon EFS throughput modes ガイド

learning.reason: With Elastic Throughput, throughput scales with demand. You do not need to specify throughput in advance or rely on accumulating burst credits.
learning.concept: The EFS throughput mode is configured separately from the file system's Regional resilience. When burst demand is unpredictable, compare charges based on the amount of data processed with the fixed charges for peak capacity.

choices.text: Keep Bursting Throughput on Regional EFS and increase the number of containers based on CPU utilization during the batch.
choices.explanation: Adding workers does not increase EFS's accumulated credits or burst limit.

choices.text: Keep Regional EFS and switch to Elastic Throughput.
choices.explanation: This preserves the Regional configuration and adjusts throughput to match the requested workload.

choices.text: Keep Regional EFS and set Provisioned Throughput continuously to match the largest batch observed in the past.
choices.explanation: You can set the required performance, but you must manage a fixed peak and may incur the fixed charge even when demand is low.

choices.text: Set up EFS One Zone with Elastic Throughput and replace the existing Regional EFS.
choices.explanation: This meets the throughput requirement, but stores data in a single AZ and does not preserve Regional resilience.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Scaling database capacity for temporary read spikes only
prompt: In a provisioned Aurora MySQL cluster, the writer's write load is steady, but the average CPU utilization across the reader fleet rises during an advertising campaign. At that time, as user sessions increase, the application opens new read connections. Keep the existing failover replicas, and automatically remove only the replicas added for the spike after the load falls. Which design avoids routing queries to individual replica IDs?

source.label: Amazon Aurora Auto Scaling ガイド

learning.reason: Aurora Auto Scaling adjusts the number of replicas. Target tracking on average CPU utilization changes that number, while the built-in reader endpoint distributes new connections.
learning.concept: The reader endpoint distributes connections, not individual SQL statements. Aurora Auto Scaling scales in replicas that it added.

choices.text: Convert the existing writer to Aurora Serverless v2 so its capacity changes automatically, and direct all reads to the writer endpoint.
choices.explanation: This adjusts writer capacity rather than the number of read replicas, and it sends normal read traffic back to the writer.

choices.text: Create enough Aurora Replicas in advance for the peak and register them with a custom endpoint for the reader role.
choices.explanation: This provides a single connection target, but replica creation and removal remain fixed operations.

choices.text: Use target tracking in Aurora Auto Scaling to set a target for average replica CPU utilization, and use the built-in reader endpoint for reads.
choices.explanation: New connections are distributed to replicas added automatically in response to read load, and Auto Scaling can remove the replicas it added when scaling in.

choices.text: Connect to the RDS Proxy read-only endpoint, including the existing replicas, and increase the connection pool's maximum size.
choices.explanation: Connections can be pooled, but this does not target-track the number of replicas. Raising the connection limit alone also does not resolve excessive CPU utilization caused by query load.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Preventing policies that allow overly broad sharing
prompt: In a central Secrets Manager setup, resource policies allow individual sharing with specified accounts. A single policy grants operators permission to call PutResourcePolicy. You want AWS to reject saving a policy that allows overly broad access, even when the call follows the normal approval path, while preserving this delegation. Apply the same control when operators use the AWS CLI directly, and do not rely on automatic remediation after the policy is attached. What should you design?

choices.text: Create a procedure in which an approved Lambda function calls ValidateResourcePolicy, and grant operators unconditional PutResourcePolicy permission.
choices.explanation: Validation is performed, but permissions cannot enforce that direct writes go through the validation step.

choices.text: Restrict GetSecretValue permission for the secret to a specific VPC endpoint, and allow PutResourcePolicy unconditionally.
choices.explanation: This can restrict the retrieval path, but it does not prevent registering a broadly shared policy.

choices.text: Invoke an AWS Lambda function from CloudTrail PutResourcePolicy events to delete resource policies detected as public.
choices.explanation: This acts after the policy is saved, so a policy that allows overly broad access is attached at least temporarily.

choices.text: Add a condition requiring secretsmanager:BlockPublicPolicy to be true to the PutResourcePolicy permission, and set BlockPublicPolicy to true in requests.
choices.explanation: This limits writes to those that include the service-side check for broad access.

source.label: Secrets Managerのリソースポリシーの保護

learning.reason: Require secretsmanager:BlockPublicPolicy to be true in the operators' PutResourcePolicy permission, and set BlockPublicPolicy to true in each call. A write that skips the broad-access check will not be allowed.
learning.concept: BlockPublicPolicy validates resource policies attached directly to a secret. Manage read-side IAM permissions, KMS key policies, and the validity of individual sharing arrangements separately.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Connecting to certified API endpoints
prompt: A company uses AWS SDKs in multiple Regions. For audit purposes, TLS connections to the relevant AWS service APIs must use AWS endpoints with cryptographic modules validated under FIPS 140. Support varies by service and Region, and falling back to a standard endpoint when a combination is unsupported is not allowed. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable dual-stack for every SDK client and allow HTTPS only.
choices.explanation: Dual-stack and HTTPS do not ensure selection of a FIPS-compliant endpoint.

choices.text: Check FIPS endpoint support for each service and Region. Enable FIPS endpoint selection in the SDK, and reject use when it is unsupported.
choices.explanation: This specifies the required type of TLS termination and does not create a path to bypass the requirement using a standard endpoint.

choices.text: Specify a FIPS endpoint in the SDK, and reconnect to the standard endpoint in the same Region if it cannot be reached.
choices.explanation: The fallback path for unsupported cases violates the FIPS-only requirement.

choices.text: Encrypt the data handled through the APIs with a KMS customer managed key and keep the current standard API endpoints.
choices.explanation: This controls encryption of data at rest but does not change the TLS modules used by the SDK's network endpoint.

source.label: AWS SDKのFIPSおよびデュアルスタックエンドポイント

learning.reason: Check FIPS support for the relevant service and Region, and use the SDK's FIPS endpoint setting where supported. Do not allow access for unsupported combinations.
learning.concept: Dual-stack concerns IPv4 and IPv6 reachability. Check the property required at the TLS termination of the AWS API separately from data encryption with KMS.

sourceLabel: FIPS and dual-stack endpoints in AWS SDKs

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Providing short-term credentials to an external process with an enterprise PKI
prompt: An on-premises backup service calls AWS APIs regularly. Its execution hosts have X.509 certificates issued by the enterprise’s backup intermediate CA. The service must use existing IAM role permissions without storing long-term AWS access keys. The account also contains another team’s IAM Roles Anywhere trust anchor, and certificates issued by that CA must not be able to obtain credentials for the backup role. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a backup trust anchor and profile, and make the IAM role trust policy require only that the caller be in the same AWS account.
choices.explanation: An account condition does not distinguish another trust anchor in the same account. The profile alone cannot bind the target role to a particular trust anchor.

choices.text: Register the internal CA’s public certificate as an IAM OIDC provider and pass the host’s X.509 certificate to AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.
choices.explanation: This API requires a token from a trusted OIDC issuer. An X.509 certificate by itself is not that token.

choices.text: Create a backup trust anchor from the CA and specify the role in the profile. Have the role trust Roles Anywhere and restrict it to that anchor with aws:SourceArn.
choices.explanation: The certificate is validated against the enterprise PKI, and the target role accepts short-term credentials only through the permitted trust anchor.

choices.text: Create a backup anchor and profile, and restrict only S3 actions in the identity policy to the host’s source IP address.
choices.explanation: This can constrain S3 operations made with the credentials, but it does not prevent credentials for the role from being obtained through another CA.

source.label: IAM Roles Anywhereの信頼モデル

learning.reason: Create a trust anchor representing the backup CA and select the backup IAM role in the profile. In the role’s trust policy, restrict the permitted trust anchor ARN.
learning.concept: Roles Anywhere validates trusted certificates and returns short-term IAM role credentials. The role’s aws:SourceArn condition can distinguish multiple trust anchors in the same AWS account.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Point-in-time recovery in another Region without a running standby database
prompt: A single-instance RDS for PostgreSQL DB has automated backups enabled. For disaster recovery, the team wants to be able to restore it at a time within the restorable period in a supported Region in the same account. There is no budget to keep a DB running continuously in the alternate Region, and waiting for a new DB to be restored is acceptable. Recovery must be possible using only the data stored on the alternate side, even if the DB in the original Region cannot be accessed. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: Amazon RDSの自動バックアップのクロスリージョン複製

learning.reason: RDS native cross-Region automated backup replication transfers snapshots and transaction logs. A new instance can be created from a replicated backup in the alternate Region at a specified time within the restorable period.
learning.concept: Using replicated backups avoids continuously running a standby DB. The restorable time depends on log replication, and recovery time includes creating a new instance.

choices.text: Create and copy a daily snapshot from the automated backups, then restore in the alternate Region from the most recent copy.
choices.explanation: A copied snapshot can be restored to its point in time, but the team cannot choose a time between snapshots.

choices.text: Create a cross-Region read replica in the alternate Region and promote it during an outage, specifying the required recovery time.
choices.explanation: This requires a running DB, and promotion carries forward the current replication state. It does not restore to a specified point in time.

choices.text: Enable RDS cross-Region automated backup replication, then select the replicated automated backup and specify a time in the alternate Region.
choices.explanation: Snapshots and transaction logs are replicated. After checking the restorable period on the replica side, the team can perform point-in-time recovery from the alternate Region.

choices.text: Copy AWS Backup continuous backups to the alternate Region and specify any time when restoring from the copied recovery point.
choices.explanation: A copied recovery point is a snapshot and does not support the same point-in-time recovery as the original continuous backup.

sourceLabel: Cross-Region replication of Amazon RDS automated backups

category: コスト最適化
title: Estimating NAT charges by Availability Zone and traffic path
prompt: A team will consolidate the NAT Gateways it currently has, one in each of three AZs, into Regional NAT Gateway automatic mode. Workers in each AZ run on weekdays, while on holidays they remain in only one AZ. Most worker traffic goes to S3 in the same Region, and they also connect to an external license server. The team wants to bypass NAT for S3 traffic while retaining external connectivity. Which combination of post-migration estimate and routing is correct?

source.label: Amazon VPCのリージョンNATの料金

learning.reason: Regional NAT hourly charges are based on the AZs in which NAT is configured, not the number of endpoints. Associating an S3 gateway endpoint with the workers’ route tables keeps same-Region S3 traffic from being processed by NAT.
learning.concept: In automatic mode, AZ removal may not happen at the same time workers stop. Estimate charges by checking the AZs where NAT is actually configured and the bytes it processes.

choices.text: Estimate hourly charges for each AZ in which NAT is actually configured. Associate an S3 gateway endpoint with the workers’ route tables, and keep the default route for external destinations pointed at NAT.
choices.explanation: Hourly charges track the number of active AZs. S3 traffic uses the more specific endpoint route, while external traffic continues through NAT.

choices.text: Because Regional NAT Gateway is one resource, estimate one hourly charge regardless of the number of AZs. Send S3 traffic to a gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: The gateway endpoint avoids NAT processing for S3, but NAT hourly charges apply per configured AZ.

choices.text: Estimate hourly charges for each AZ with NAT configured. Keep the route for same-Region S3 traffic because it incurs no NAT data processing charge.
choices.explanation: Being in the same Region as S3 does not exempt data that actually passes through NAT from processing charges.

choices.text: Estimate hourly charges only for AZs that actually have traffic through Regional NAT. Send S3 traffic to a gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: Hourly charges apply to configured AZs even when traffic is zero. Scaling down the AZs can take time.

category: コスト最適化
title: Comparing hourly costs after excluding an expiring commitment
prompt: Some of the organization’s shared Compute Savings Plans expire in 45 days. Finance wants to use the previous eight weeks of hourly demand to compare two different hourly commitments, excluding the expiring plans. How can it compare remaining On-Demand spend, coverage, and utilization across the organization without making a purchase?

source.label: Savings Plans Purchase Analyzerの設定

learning.reason: Use Purchase Analyzer in the payer account and exclude plans that are due to expire. Run separate analyses for the different custom commitments to compare all three metrics over the same observation period.
learning.concept: The analysis applies commitments to usage in each historical hour. For commitments consumed hourly, choosing a purchase amount from a simple period average can leave unused commitment during demand troughs.

choices.text: Use monthly amortized costs in Cost Explorer and apply each candidate’s discount rate to average spend in prior months.
choices.explanation: This can provide a rough comparison of purchase amounts, but it does not reproduce hourly utilization or remaining On-Demand spend.

choices.text: Open Purchase Analyzer in the payer account and exclude the plans that are due to expire. Analyze each of the two custom commitments separately using the same observation period and payment terms.
choices.explanation: Without making a purchase, the tool can model remaining spend, coverage, and utilization against hourly historical usage.

choices.text: Use member-account filters in the coverage report and aggregate current plan utilization by team to decide how much to replace.
choices.explanation: The coverage report describes current application of plans. It does not model two commitments under an assumption that the expiring plans are excluded.

choices.text: Refresh the organization-level Savings Plans recommendations and compare the first and second recommendations.
choices.explanation: Generating recommendations is a different operation from modeling two specified amounts under the same assumptions.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Reclaiming an unused resource only when initial creation fails
prompt: Whenever CloudFormation creates a new stack, it creates an empty S3 bucket before any other resources. If the initial creation rolls back because a later resource fails, you want the empty bucket reclaimed too. After the stack has operated successfully, business data must remain in the bucket even if you remove it from the template or delete the stack. The bucket is empty during initial creation, and you do not want to delete it with an external script. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: CloudFormationのDeletionPolicy

learning.reason: RetainExceptOnCreate deletes a resource if the operation that first created it rolls back, and retains it for the other covered operations.
learning.concept: DeletionPolicy determines what happens to resources when a stack is deleted or resources are removed from a template. UpdateReplacePolicy determines what happens to an old resource that is replaced during an update.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy to Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy to Delete.
choices.explanation: A standard Retain policy also keeps the bucket when the initial creation rolls back. Changing the replacement policy does not change that behavior.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy to Delete and enable bucket versioning.
choices.explanation: This deletes an empty bucket created initially, but it also fails to retain the bucket when an empty bucket is later deleted or removed from the stack. Versioning does not provide a retention guarantee.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy to RetainExceptOnCreate on the bucket.
choices.explanation: This reclaims the bucket only when initial creation fails, while retaining it on a later stack deletion or removal from the template.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain on the bucket and leave DeletionPolicy at its default.
choices.explanation: This retains the old physical resource when it is replaced. It does not apply when the bucket is removed from the template or the stack is deleted.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Validating a new task at the earliest point before sending production traffic
prompt: An ECS service managed by CodeDeploy has production and test ALB listeners. You want to route only the test listener to the new task set and validate orders using fixed inputs. Run the validation in the first hook available immediately after switching the test listener, and notify CodeDeploy of any failure so it does not change the production listener. Which configuration should you choose?

source.label: ECSのCodeDeployライフサイクル

learning.reason: AfterAllowTestTraffic follows AllowTestTraffic. The validation Lambda can use the test listener and then return success or failure for the lifecycle hook to CodeDeploy.
learning.concept: In an ECS deployment with CodeDeploy, installing new tasks, directing test traffic, and switching production traffic are separate steps. Check when the endpoint needed for testing is routed to the new tasks.

choices.text: Configure a validation Lambda function in AfterInstall and validate orders through the test listener.
choices.explanation: The new task is installed, but routing through the test listener has not yet been changed to the new task set.

choices.text: Configure a validation Lambda function in BeforeAllowTraffic and validate orders through the test listener.
choices.explanation: Validation is possible before the production switch, but this hook comes after AfterAllowTestTraffic and is not the first hook available after the test listener switches.

choices.text: Configure a validation Lambda function in AfterAllowTraffic and use CodeDeploy automatic rollback based on the result.
choices.explanation: Rollback on failure can be configured, but by this point the production listener has already switched to the new task set.

choices.text: Configure a validation Lambda function in AfterAllowTestTraffic, send requests to the test listener, and return the result as the hook status.
choices.explanation: Immediately after the test listener switches, you can validate only the new task set and control whether the deployment proceeds to the next stage.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Reprocessing only historical runs while preserving scheduled progress
prompt: A daily AWS Glue job processes new S3 partitions and has job bookmarks enabled. You need to rerun only a specific, consecutive set of three past runs with a corrected transformation and validate the differences without touching the current output. The next scheduled run must continue from the current bookmark. You have recorded the run IDs, and the reprocessing can finish before the next scheduled run. Which two actions should you take?

source.label: AWS Glueのジョブブックマーク

learning.reason: Use Pause mode and set from to the run ID immediately before the target runs and to to the ID of the last target run. Write the rerun output to a separate S3 prefix.
learning.concept: Job bookmarks track input progress. Reprocessing historical data does not cause Glue to automatically delete or replace target output.

choices.text: Roll back the bookmark to the run ID immediately before the three target runs, then process the historical data using normal Enable mode.
choices.explanation: This changes the state used by subsequent scheduled runs and may process data newer than the selected three runs.

choices.text: Set the bookmark to Pause and specify the run ID immediately before the three runs as job-bookmark-from and the ID of the third run as job-bookmark-to.
choices.explanation: This specifies the processed range to rerun without updating the latest bookmark state.

choices.text: Reset the bookmark, rerun the job using the normal output location, and wait for Glue to erase the saved output.
choices.explanation: This does not limit processing to the target range, and job bookmarks do not erase existing target data.

choices.text: Specify the latest successful run ID, launch the job in Enable mode, and provide the three historical partitions as input.
choices.explanation: The job determines incremental input from its current progress. This does not select a historical run range while preserving the current state.

choices.text: Set the rerun output to a separate S3 prefix reserved for validation, then compare it with the current output.
choices.explanation: This prevents results from reprocessing historical input from being mixed into the current target.

category: コスト最適化
title: Measuring additional CPU charges for short-lived T3 instances
prompt: You scale out T3 Unlimited workers with EC2 Auto Scaling, use all available CPU for about an hour each time, and then terminate them. The bill includes a separate charge in addition to instance hours. You want to determine whether T3 or a non-burstable option is cheaper per job while meeting the processing time limit. Which analysis is appropriate?

source.label: EC2 Unlimitedの追加CPUクレジット

learning.reason: When an instance terminates, surplus credits cannot be repaid through later periods of low CPU usage. Compare actual costs, including additional CPU charges, and completion times for the same workload.
learning.concept: Additional charges are determined by credits earned and consumed, repayment of surplus credits, and when the instance stops or terminates—not simply by instantaneous CPU utilization. CPUSurplusCreditsCharged helps investigate billed surplus credits.

choices.text: Review CPUSurplusCreditsCharged and the bill, then compare the cost and completion time of the same job against a non-burstable instance that can sustain the required CPU usage, including surplus credit charges.
choices.explanation: Unpaid surplus credits can be charged when short-lived instances stop or terminate, so combine billing data with measurements for the actual workload.

choices.text: Compare only the displayed hourly instance rates for T3. If a job runs for less than 24 hours, Unlimited incurs no additional CPU charges.
choices.explanation: Unrepaid surplus credits are charged on stop or termination, so running for less than 24 hours does not avoid additional charges.

choices.text: Switch to T3 Standard and decide based only on the On-Demand hourly rate, assuming performance stays above baseline.
choices.explanation: In Standard mode, performance is limited to baseline after credits are depleted. Completion time can change, so it must be checked against the requirement.

choices.text: Compare each instance's peak CPU value and choose the least expensive option based only on average monthly CPU utilization if the peaks are equal.
choices.explanation: Aggregate metrics can miss the short instance lifetime and settlement of surplus credits. Check completion time and cost per job separately.

category: コスト最適化
title: Avoiding Account-Level Minimum Charges for Variable Streams
prompt: You run Kinesis Data Streams in one account and Region. A small number of streams occasionally scale up, but during normal operation, the aggregate throughput across all streams is no more than 2 MiB/s for ingestion and no more than 2 MiB/s for retrieval. You want to avoid manually adjusting shard counts. There are few dedicated enhanced fan-out consumers, and load testing has shown that existing streams do not need additional warm throughput. How can you avoid adding a minimum commitment to ongoing usage?

source.label: Kinesis Data Streamsのキャパシティーモード

learning.reason: Choose On-demand Standard to retain automatic scaling without a Region-level minimum commitment for ingestion or retrieval.
learning.concept: On-demand Advantage aggregates all on-demand streams in the account and Region and has a minimum level for both ingestion and retrieval. Choosing it solely for temporary peaks can leave costs during low-usage periods.

choices.text: Enable On-demand Advantage and leave only the low-load streams on On-demand Standard in the same Region to avoid the minimum commitment.
choices.explanation: The Advantage setting applies to all on-demand streams in the account and Region. You cannot avoid the minimum commitment by leaving only selected streams on Standard.

choices.text: Use On-demand Standard, with its standard usage-based charges and stream-hour charges.
choices.explanation: This keeps automatic shard scaling without adding Advantage's minimum commitments for ingestion and retrieval.

choices.text: Move all streams to provisioned capacity, set the shard count for normal conditions, and have them scale automatically like on-demand streams when load increases.
choices.explanation: With provisioned capacity, you set the shard count. On-demand's automatic scaling does not apply as-is.

choices.text: Use On-demand Advantage, disable only the retrieval minimum commitment, and reserve capacity only for ingestion.
choices.explanation: The minimum levels for ingestion and retrieval apply separately; you cannot disable only the retrieval minimum.

category: コスト最適化
title: Stop New Launches in a Development Account Only After Approval
prompt: In a development AWS Organizations member account, notify Finance when actual monthly EC2 charges exceed a threshold. After approval, prevent ordinary IAM principals in the account from launching new EC2 instances, while keeping already running instances and existing access intact. Do not affect budgets or workloads in other accounts, and do not add another execution service. Which combination should you choose?

source.label: AWS Budgetsアクションの設定

learning.reason: A budget in the management account can conditionally apply an SCP that denies EC2 launches to the development member account. Choose manual approval so the SCP is applied only to that account after approval.
learning.concept: Budget actions are based on billing data; they do not impose an immediate usage limit. An action that stops existing instances differs from an SCP that denies new operations.

choices.text: Create a budget in the development account and use a budget action there to apply an SCP that denies launches to that same account.
choices.explanation: A member account can create a budget, but a budget action that applies an SCP must be run from the management account.

choices.text: In the management account, set an actual-spend action to require manual approval, then stop running instances in the development account.
choices.explanation: This stops existing compute resources. It does not meet the requirement to restrict only new launches.

choices.text: In the management account, create a budget scoped to the target member's EC2 charges. When actual charges exceed the threshold, use an action requiring manual approval to apply an SCP that denies launches only in that member account.
choices.explanation: This combines approval, limiting the action to the target account, and preventing new EC2 launches without stopping instances that are already running.

choices.text: In the management account, automatically approve an actual-spend action and notify Finance when an SCP denying launches is applied to the target account.
choices.explanation: Workloads can keep running, but the restriction takes effect before Finance approves it.

category: コスト最適化
title: Avoid Adding Compute Nodes Just to Store Growing Historical Data
prompt: Historical data is growing in a provisioned Redshift DC2 cluster. Analyses usually cover only the most recent few days, and load tests show spare CPU and concurrency capacity. Auditors still need to query older history in the same internal tables; moving it to external tables is not allowed. How can you keep using provisioned capacity while reducing the cost of adding compute nodes solely to increase storage?

source.label: Amazon Redshiftのノードタイプとマネージドストレージ

learning.reason: With Redshift managed storage on RA3, compute-node count can match query processing needs while managed storage scales with the data volume.
learning.concept: Account for the requirement to keep data in internal tables. Distinguish storage attached to DC2 nodes, RA3's decoupled storage, and data queried as external tables.

choices.text: Add DC2 nodes to make room for the history and reduce the number of concurrent slots on the query side.
choices.explanation: This retains the history, but both compute-node count and compute costs increase whenever storage runs short.

choices.text: Keep recent history in internal tables, export older years to S3, and move them to Redshift Spectrum external tables.
choices.explanation: The history remains queryable with SQL, but older data is no longer in internal tables.

choices.text: Keep DC2 and enable concurrency scaling, using the additional cluster's storage as the permanent location for historical data.
choices.explanation: Concurrency scaling adds temporary compute capacity; it does not separate permanent storage for DC2 internal tables.

choices.text: Migrate to RA3 with Redshift managed storage, and size the compute nodes according to measured query performance.
choices.explanation: This lets you keep internal tables while sizing managed storage separately from compute nodes.

sourceLabel: Amazon Redshift node types and managed storage

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Distribute Encrypted AMIs as Copies Owned by the Using Accounts
prompt: EC2 Image Builder in a dedicated image account creates encrypted AMIs. With each update, distribute them to specified Regions in other accounts, where the receiving accounts must have copies they own. A design that relies on the source account's AMI registration to launch EC2 instances is not acceptable. Both sides manage KMS keys. Which two settings should you configure?

source.label: Image BuilderのクロスアカウントAMI配布

learning.reason: Specify the receiving accounts as distribution targets and configure a distribution role and the necessary KMS access in each receiving account.
learning.concept: A copy created during distribution differs from sharing permission to launch the source AMI. For encrypted copies, check the roles and KMS key policies together.

choices.text: In the distribution settings, grant the receiving account launch permission on the source AMI only.
choices.explanation: Launch permissions do not change AMI ownership or create a local copy owned by the receiving account.

choices.text: Periodically update the AMI ID so each receiving account's launch template refers to the AMI owned by the source account.
choices.explanation: The AMI can be used to launch instances, but the design still depends on an AMI owned by the source account and does not create a receiving-account copy.

choices.text: Specify the receiving account IDs and corresponding Regions as targets in the distribution settings.
choices.explanation: This configures AMI copies to be distributed to the target accounts rather than merely sharing launch permission.

choices.text: Set up the Image Builder cross-account distribution role in the receiving accounts, and grant the KMS permissions needed to use the source key and encrypt the copies in the destination.
choices.explanation: The role that performs the AMI copy and access to the relevant keys are required.

choices.text: Create one distribution role in the source account and omit roles in the receiving accounts.
choices.explanation: The receiving-side role needed for Image Builder to create copies at each distribution target would be missing.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Switch to the failure path when an external worker stops reporting progress
prompt: A Step Functions Standard workflow sends work to SQS. A worker in the same account may process the work for up to two hours, and can report progress every 30 seconds after starting. The workflow must not continue as soon as the SQS send succeeds; it must take the failure path if progress stops for 60 seconds, and it must enforce an overall time limit even if reports continue. Which configuration should you use?

source.label: Step Functionsのコールバック統合

learning.reason: Include the task token in the work request, then have the worker send heartbeats and the completion result. Configure the heartbeat interval and overall task timeout separately.
learning.concept: SendTaskHeartbeat resets the heartbeat timeout. It does not extend the task's overall TimeoutSeconds. Distinguish completion of the integration from completion of the external work.

choices.text: Send the message using the standard SQS SendMessage integration, and set the queue visibility timeout to 60 seconds and message retention to two hours.
choices.explanation: A successful queue send does not indicate that the worker has reported progress. This configuration also does not make the workflow wait for the work to complete.

choices.text: Use the SQS waitForTaskToken integration, and have the worker call SendTaskHeartbeat and return the result on completion. Set HeartbeatSeconds to 60 and TimeoutSeconds to 7,200, and handle the timeout on the failure path.
choices.explanation: This configuration evaluates missed progress and the task's maximum duration separately, and lets the workflow wait for the result after handing off the work to SQS.

choices.text: Use waitForTaskToken with only TimeoutSeconds, and have the worker call SendTaskSuccess when the work is complete.
choices.explanation: The workflow can wait for completion, but without heartbeats it cannot detect within 60 seconds that the worker has stopped.

choices.text: Use waitForTaskToken with TimeoutSeconds set to 60, and have the worker call SendTaskHeartbeat with each report to extend the workflow's total duration to two hours.
choices.explanation: A heartbeat does not extend TimeoutSeconds. Even normal processing would time out after about 60 seconds.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Catch up one new subscription from history through the present
prompt: Delivery events are published to an SNS FIFO topic. Archiving has been enabled for 30 days. You need to deliver events from 10:00 yesterday through the present, in order, to only a new aggregation service that uses SQS FIFO, and then continue delivering new events without interruption. Do not republish events from the publisher, and do not replay messages to existing subscriptions. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: SNS FIFOの購読単位リプレイ

learning.reason: Set StartingPoint on the new subscription and omit EndingPoint. It can catch up from history through the present and continue delivery to the same subscription afterward.
learning.concept: Replay is not a way to republish messages from a topic to all subscriptions. A fixed end point can make that subscription process messages through the specified period and then pause; that differs from catching up and continuously receiving new messages.

choices.text: Set ReplayPolicy on only the new subscription, set StartingPoint to 10:00 yesterday, and omit EndingPoint.
choices.explanation: Only the new subscription receives the historical events. It also evaluates messages published during catch-up so it can reach the present.

choices.text: Set both the start time and the current time in the new subscription's ReplayPolicy, and make no changes after processing through the end point.
choices.explanation: This processes messages through the fixed end point, but the subscription pauses afterward instead of automatically continuing with new notifications.

choices.text: Change the topic's ArchivePolicy retention period to one day and wait for the new subscription to retrieve the previous day's history automatically.
choices.explanation: ArchivePolicy controls retention at the topic level; it does not specify that a new subscription should start a replay.

choices.text: Configure a dead-letter queue for the new subscription and start redrive on that queue to ingest events from 10:00 yesterday.
choices.explanation: The new subscription had no delivery failures at that time, so its dead-letter queue will not contain those historical events.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Shift some new connections away for planned maintenance
prompt: A standard Global Accelerator has endpoint groups in Tokyo and Virginia. During planned maintenance in Tokyo, you want only about one-quarter of the new TCP connections that would normally be directed to Tokyo to continue going to Tokyo. Preserve established sessions, health checks, and the endpoint proportions within each Region. Which action is appropriate?

choices.text: Set only the traffic dial for the Tokyo endpoint group to 25%.
choices.explanation: This adjusts the share of new connections that would have gone to Tokyo without disconnecting clients that are already connected.

choices.text: Reduce the weight of every endpoint in the Tokyo group to one-quarter of its current value.
choices.explanation: The relative allocation within the Tokyo group remains the same, so this does not set the desired share of new connections assigned to Tokyo.

choices.text: Set the Tokyo and Virginia traffic dials to 25% and 75%, respectively, to apply those proportions to traffic from all listeners.
choices.explanation: The dial is not based on a single pool shared by all listeners. This would also change the existing allocation of new connections directed to Virginia.

choices.text: Create separate accelerators for Tokyo and Virginia, configure weighted Route 53 records, and then begin planned maintenance.
choices.explanation: This requires changing the client entry point and relying on DNS resolution, and cannot adjust only the connections that the original accelerator would have directed to Tokyo.

source.label: AWS Global Accelerator traffic dials

learning.reason: An endpoint group's traffic dial uses as its baseline the new traffic that would otherwise be directed to that group. Existing connections and health checks are preserved.
learning.concept: A group's traffic dial controls traffic at the Region level; endpoint weights control the allocation within a group.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Monitor a public port separately from an EC2 listener port
prompt: With a standard Global Accelerator, client TCP connections must use port 443. Each endpoint is an EC2 instance, and both the application and health check listen only on port 8443. Keep the client port and application unchanged, and open only the required ports in each EC2 security group. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a public listener on port 443 and a health check on port 8443, without configuring a port override.
choices.explanation: The health check reaches the correct port, but client connections are sent to port 443, where the application is not listening.

choices.text: Keep the public listener on port 443 and configure an override from port 443 to port 8443. Also set the health check port to 8443, and allow connections to port 8443 in the EC2 security groups from the required source.
choices.explanation: This maps the client entry port to the application's actual port and separately sets the health check to the application's listener port.

choices.text: Configure an override from port 443 to port 8443, but leave the health check on port 443.
choices.explanation: The endpoint port override does not change the health check configuration. Port 443 is not open on the EC2 instances for the check.

choices.text: Change the public listener to port 8443 and tell clients to connect over TCP 443. Run the health check on port 8443.
choices.explanation: The accelerator will not accept connections on port 443, so this does not meet the client connection requirement.

source.label: AWS Global Accelerator port overrides

learning.reason: Configure a listener port override to send client connections to port 8443. Because the EC2 health check does not follow the override, specify port 8443 separately in the endpoint group.
learning.concept: The public listener, endpoint destination port, and health check port are separate settings. The EC2 security group must allow the required source and port for the actual destination.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Prioritize a forwarding exception for one VPC while retaining shared DNS
prompt: A shared Route 53 Profile is associated with multiple VPCs at priority 100. It forwards names under corp.example.com to shared DNS. In just one VPC, dev.corp.example.com must be forwarded to a different DNS server by an exception profile. No rule is directly associated with the target VPC. Keep both profile associations and avoid affecting the other VPCs. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Keep the shared profile at 100 and set the exception profile to 200. Because dev.corp.example.com is more specific, the exception profile will be selected.
choices.explanation: For multiple profiles associated with the same VPC, selection stops at the profile with priority 100 when it matches first.

choices.text: Keep the shared profile at 100 and set the exception profile to 50.
choices.explanation: Prioritizing the lower number is the right idea, but 50 is outside the permitted range.

choices.text: Change only the shared profile association for the target VPC to 200, then add the exception profile at 100.
choices.explanation: The exception profile is evaluated first in the target VPC. Names that do not match it are handled by the shared profile, and associations in other VPCs remain unchanged.

choices.text: Associate both the shared and exception profiles at priority 100, and use the specificity of the forwarding destination to determine evaluation order.
choices.explanation: Multiple associations in one VPC must have distinct priorities.

source.label: Route 53 Profile とVPCの関連付け

learning.reason: Profiles are evaluated in the same VPC starting with the lowest numeric priority. Once a match is found in the higher-priority profile, a more specific domain in a later profile is not considered.
learning.concept: Profile priority is specified per association with each VPC, in the range 100 to 9900. Distinguish selection among profiles from the later stage of comparing the selected settings with settings directly associated with the VPC.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Route traffic using both the hostname and contract tier
prompt: On an internal ALB, all requests for partner.example.com are sent to the standard target group by an existing hostname rule. Requests for this host should go to a dedicated group only when an authenticated upstream service has set the X-Contract-Tier header to gold. Preserve the destination for requests that match only one condition, and do not change the application. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Keep the existing hostname rule and add a dedicated rule with both the hostname and custom-header conditions after it.
choices.explanation: The standard rule matches first, so requests with the gold header never reach the later rule.

choices.text: Add a dedicated rule that matches only the gold header before the existing hostname rule.
choices.explanation: Requests for other hosts with gold specified would also match the dedicated rule.

choices.text: Create separate rules for the hostname and the gold header, and configure both to forward to the dedicated group.
choices.explanation: Two separate rules do not form a logical AND. Requests matching either condition alone would reach the dedicated group.

choices.text: Put the hostname and gold-header conditions in the same rule, give it higher priority than the existing hostname rule, and forward to the dedicated group.
choices.explanation: The dedicated rule applies only when both conditions match; otherwise, the existing rule handles the request.

source.label: Application Load Balancer listener rule condition types

learning.reason: Set the hostname and custom header as separate conditions in the same rule, and evaluate it first. Only requests matching both conditions go to the dedicated group.
learning.concept: An ALB evaluates rules in ascending order of priority number and applies the action for the first matching rule. Distinguish multiple conditions in one rule from matches in separate rules.

sourceLabel: Application Load Balancer listener rule condition types

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Retain connection reuse when initializing PostgreSQL sessions
prompt: An API that uses RDS for PostgreSQL through RDS Proxy has grown, and many database connections are observed to be pinned to sessions. Every client for this API issues the same time-zone SET statement once immediately after connecting. The API does not depend on long-running transactions or temporary tables. Without changing the database settings of other applications that bypass the proxy, how can you retain the API's initial setting and reuse backend connections between transactions?

choices.text: Move the common SET statement to the proxy's initialization query and remove the same SET statement issued by clients immediately after connecting.
choices.explanation: This applies the common value to the API's backend connections while reducing pinning caused by each client's SET statement.

choices.text: Keep the client SET statement and enable EXCLUDE_VARIABLE_SETS in the proxy.
choices.explanation: This session pinning filter is not supported for PostgreSQL.

choices.text: Change the time zone in the database's shared parameter group and remove the client SET statement.
choices.explanation: This would also affect applications that do not use the proxy, so it would not meet the requirement for an API-specific value.

choices.text: Increase the connection pool's maximum connection count and keep the client SET statement.
choices.explanation: Increasing the number of available connections does not remove the pinning of individual connections or the resulting barrier to reuse.

source.label: Amazon RDS Proxy のsession pinning回避

learning.reason: Moving the common SET statement to the proxy's initialization query applies it when backend connections are created. Removing the per-client SET avoids interfering with reuse between transactions.
learning.concept: In RDS Proxy for PostgreSQL, a client setting a session variable can cause pinning. Applying the same initial value to every connection is a case that can be separated from individual client-side settings.

sourceLabel: Avoiding session pinning with Amazon RDS Proxy

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Forward the Host received on an 8443 listener unchanged
prompt: An internal ALB uses an HTTPS listener on port 8443. Clients for multiple tenants send Host without a port number, while a packaged application rejects Host values that include a port number. ALB rules route traffic successfully based on the received hostname. Keep the existing rules, application, and listener port, and forward the received Host unchanged for every tenant. What should you do?

choices.text: Change only the target group's forwarding port to 443.
choices.explanation: The default Host modification depends on the ALB listener port, not the target port.

choices.text: Set the ALB attribute routing.http.preserve_host_header.enabled to true.
choices.explanation: The ALB forwards the received Host header to the target without changing its value.

choices.text: Add 8443 to the Host matching condition in each tenant's existing rule.
choices.explanation: This changes the value being matched; it does not configure header preservation when forwarding.

choices.text: Replace the ALB with an NLB using TLS pass-through and retain the same host-based listener rules.
choices.explanation: TCP forwarding does not rewrite the header, but an NLB cannot handle ALB Layer 7 host-based conditions in the same way.

source.label: Application Load Balancer host header preservation

learning.reason: Enabling Host header preservation on the ALB prevents changes such as adding a nonstandard listener port. The rules can continue to evaluate the hostname as received.
learning.concept: The incoming header evaluated by a listener rule and the handling of the header forwarded from the ALB to a target are configured separately.

sourceLabel: Application Load Balancer host header preservation

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Route reconnecting clients to the same endpoint
prompt: You are exposing a TCP service across multiple Regions with a standard Global Accelerator. You want a client's brief reconnects to reach the same endpoint when the source IP and destination accelerator IP are unchanged, even if the source port changes, provided the edge location and set of endpoint candidates remain unchanged. The TCP client does not use cookies. Which setting meets this requirement?

choices.text: Set the traffic dial to 100% for every Region.
choices.explanation: This preserves traffic distribution to healthy Regions but does not configure affinity that is independent of the source port.

choices.text: Set the same weight for every endpoint in the group.
choices.explanation: This adjusts relative traffic distribution; it does not pin reconnects from the same source to one endpoint.

choices.text: Set the listener's client affinity to NONE.
choices.explanation: With the five-tuple, a source-port change can result in a different endpoint being selected.

choices.text: Set the listener's client affinity to SOURCE_IP.
choices.explanation: Because endpoint selection uses the source and destination IP addresses, changing the source port does not change the endpoint along the assumed path.

source.label: AWS Global Accelerator client affinity

learning.reason: With SOURCE_IP configured on the listener, endpoint selection uses the source and destination IP addresses. The port number can change when a client reconnects without being included in this calculation.
learning.concept: The default, NONE, selects a connection using the combination of source address and port, destination address and port, and protocol. If the edge location changes and the new edge selects a different Region, affinity is not guaranteed even when the IP addresses are unchanged.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Assessing EC2 instances without agent management by volume eligibility
prompt: Two Linux EC2 instances in the same Region are protected by Amazon Inspector. Both are running, their operating systems and file systems are supported targets for agentless scanning, neither is managed by Systems Manager, and neither has an exclusion tag. The first instance has a total of 600 GB across its EBS volumes, and the second has a total of 1,300 GB. Each instance uses three volumes. If you use Hybrid scanning without changing the application configuration or volumes, how should you assess coverage?

choices.text: Hybrid scanning does not scan either instance unless it is managed by Systems Manager.
choices.explanation: An instance that is not managed by Systems Manager can still be assessed agentlessly if it meets the eligibility requirements.

choices.text: Both instances are scanned if each volume on the second instance is 1,200 GB or smaller.
choices.explanation: The capacity limit applies to the total volume size attached to an instance, not to each individual volume.

choices.text: The first instance can be assessed agentlessly. The second exceeds the total-capacity requirement and is ineligible for the same method.
choices.explanation: The 600 GB instance meets the requirement, while the 1,300 GB instance does not meet the total-capacity limit.

choices.text: Specify only the smallest volume on the second instance as an Amazon Inspector assessment target and treat that as an assessment of the entire instance.
choices.explanation: Eligibility is determined across all attached volumes; specifying only part of them does not make this a whole-instance assessment.

source.label: Amazon InspectorのEC2スキャンと対象条件

learning.reason: Hybrid scanning uses EBS snapshots for eligible instances that are not managed by Systems Manager. Because eligibility includes a total capacity limit of 1,200 GB, the 1,300 GB instance needs another protection approach.
learning.concept: Agentless coverage is not determined solely by whether Systems Manager management is required. Check the supported operating system, running state, number of volumes and their total capacity, and exclusion settings.

sourceLabel: Amazon Inspector EC2 scanning and eligibility requirements

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Run a daily audit evaluation separately from change events
prompt: AWS Config records configuration history. A custom audit rule is a Lambda function that evaluates the account-wide inventory rather than changes to individual EC2 instances. Under the audit policy, running the check every 24 hours is sufficient; it does not need to be invoked whenever configuration changes. Preserve the existing configuration history, and do not add another scheduler. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Use ScheduledNotification as the only trigger and set MaximumExecutionFrequency to TwentyFour_Hours.
choices.explanation: This runs a daily evaluation independently of configuration-change events and preserves the recorded configuration history.

choices.text: Use only ConfigurationItemChangeNotification and set the configuration recorder to continuous recording.
choices.explanation: This invokes Lambda when configuration changes and does not schedule a periodic check on days without changes.

choices.text: Configure both ScheduledNotification and ConfigurationItemChangeNotification.
choices.explanation: In addition to the daily evaluation, Lambda would also be invoked whenever configuration changes.

choices.text: Change only the configuration recorder to daily recording and keep the rule's change-triggered setting.
choices.explanation: Changing the recording interval affects the granularity of existing history. The rule trigger also would not provide a daily account-wide check.

source.label: AWS ConfigのカスタムLambdaルールのトリガー

learning.reason: Configure the custom Lambda rule to run only on a periodic basis. Set the ScheduledNotification frequency to TwentyFour_Hours and maintain the configuration recorder separately.
learning.concept: Recording configuration history and scheduling compliance evaluations are separate concerns. For periodic rule evaluations, specify a supported frequency.

sourceLabel: AWS Config custom Lambda rule triggers

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Delegate a role only to authorized accounts in an OU and its child OUs
prompt: Allow only authorized IAM roles in accounts belonging to the Payments OU in AWS Organizations, or to its descendant OUs, to assume an IAM role in a central services account. Exclude other departments in the organization and accounts outside the organization. You do not want to update an account allowlist in the trust policy as accounts move. In addition to identifying the caller role, which condition should you add to the trust policy?

choices.text: Require aws:PrincipalOrgID to match the organization ID.
choices.explanation: This also matches other departments in the same organization, so it does not restrict access to the Payments OU hierarchy.

choices.text: Require aws:PrincipalOrgPaths to exactly match a path ending at the Payments OU.
choices.explanation: A descendant OU adds another OU to the path, so it would not match exactly.

choices.text: Check whether aws:ResourceOrgPaths is under Payments.
choices.explanation: The condition must check the organization placement of the requesting principal, not the account that owns the target role.

choices.text: Match aws:PrincipalOrgPaths using ForAnyValue:StringLike, with a wildcard after the organization path through the Payments OU to include descendants.
choices.explanation: This uses the account's organization path, includes descendant OUs, and follows changes in account placement.

source.label: IAMの組織パス条件キー

learning.reason: Use the Organizations path for the account containing the caller principal. Match values that start with the organization path through the Payments OU by using ForAnyValue:StringLike.
learning.concept: aws:PrincipalOrgPaths is a multivalued condition key that lets you select principals by organization ID, root, and OU path. The caller must also have permission to use sts:AssumeRole, and the role must trust that caller.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Automatically deploy agents only to designated EKS clusters
prompt: You are introducing GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring to EKS. The clusters are in the same account and Region, and the security team monitors only clusters registered for audit. New clusters must remain out of scope until approved; after a cluster is approved, GuardDuty should manage agent updates. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable automatic EKS agent configuration and tag only approved clusters with GuardDutyManaged=true.
choices.explanation: When automatic management is enabled globally, clusters without the tag are included by default.

choices.text: Keep Runtime Monitoring enabled but disable automatic agent configuration globally. Tag approved EKS clusters with GuardDutyManaged=true.
choices.explanation: The tag limits coverage to approved clusters and lets GuardDuty manage deployment and updates.

choices.text: Keep Runtime Monitoring disabled and tag approved EKS clusters with GuardDutyManaged=true.
choices.explanation: A cluster tag alone does not satisfy the requirement to enable Runtime Monitoring.

choices.text: Enable only EKS control plane audit logs on approved clusters.
choices.explanation: This captures API audit logs but does not configure agent-based monitoring of workload runtime behavior.

source.label: GuardDutyのEKSエージェントの自動管理

learning.reason: Enable Runtime Monitoring, but do not enable automatic agent configuration for all EKS clusters. Tag approved clusters with GuardDutyManaged=true so GuardDuty manages deployment and updates for those clusters.
learning.concept: Account-level feature enablement and the scope of agent management for individual clusters are configured separately. Tag management differs between global coverage and coverage limited to approved clusters.

sourceLabel: Automatic management of the GuardDuty EKS agent

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Exclude specific buckets from automated discovery
prompt: A Macie administrator account operates automated sensitive data discovery for S3 in one Region of the organization. A change in a vendor contract means that two legal department buckets must be excluded from future automated analyses. Other buckets owned by the same member account must continue to be analyzed, and the sensitivity scores already collected for the legal department buckets must remain available for audit. How can this be done?

choices.text: Disable automated discovery for the member account and move all of its buckets to individual jobs.
choices.explanation: This also removes the member account's other buckets from automated discovery, disrupting ongoing coverage.

choices.text: Create a discovery job covering all S3 data for the same member account and exclude the legal department buckets. Leave existing automated discovery unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the job scope does not stop the separate automated discovery process from continuing to consider the legal department buckets.

choices.text: In the administrator account, open the automated discovery settings for the Region and add the two buckets to the exclusion list.
choices.explanation: This excludes only the selected buckets from future analyses while preserving scores and statistics already recorded.

choices.text: Reduce the set of managed data identifiers used by automated discovery across the organization.
choices.explanation: This controls which data types are detected; it does not exclude specific buckets from automated discovery.

source.label: Macieの自動機密データ検出の対象設定

learning.reason: In the administrator account, add the two specific buckets to the exclusion list for automated discovery in the relevant Region. They will be excluded from future cycles while existing statistics remain.
learning.concept: Automated discovery scope settings and individual sensitive data discovery jobs are separate features. The exclusion list updates the analysis scope while retaining other buckets.

sourceLabel: Configuring the scope of Macie automated sensitive data discovery

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Remove inherited controls from only the account that moved between OUs
prompt: In a Control Tower environment with automatic enrollment disabled, a member account was moved between OUs. A detective control from the source OU remains on the account and appears as inheritance drift.
