The control must remain on the other accounts in the source OU, and only the residual control on the moved account should be removed. How can this be done while also preventing the same issue on future moves?

choices.text: Re-register the destination OU and reset the residual detective control with ResetEnabledControl.
choices.explanation: Re-registration and reset address configuration drift; they do not resolve inheritance drift for the moved account.

choices.text: Disable the control in the source OU and recreate it separately for the members that still need it.
choices.explanation: This changes protection for the entire source OU instead of addressing only the account that moved.

choices.text: Enable automatic enrollment and wait for it to remove the residual controls from the account that has already moved.
choices.explanation: Controls left behind by a move that occurred before automatic enrollment was enabled are not removed automatically.

choices.text: On the moved account, retrieve the identifiers of the enabled controls in inheritance drift and disable only those controls by identifier. Enable automatic enrollment to prepare for future moves.
choices.explanation: This handles the residual controls on the target account, and automatic enrollment ensures controls are handled appropriately during future moves.

source.label: Control Towerのコントロール継承ドリフト

learning.reason: Identify the enabled controls in inheritance drift on the moved account and disable them by identifier. Enable landing zone automatic enrollment to prepare for future moves.
learning.concept: Resetting configuration drift does not remove controls left behind by the source OU. Automatic enrollment applies to future moves.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Keep the former database for inspection after switchover
prompt: An RDS for MySQL Blue/Green switchover succeeds, and the business application resumes writing to the new database through the production endpoint it used before the switchover. The migration team wants to retain the original database for inspection and determine whether updates made to the new database have also been applied to the old one. Assuming no changes are made to the old environment, which statement is correct?

choices.text: The production endpoint continues to point to the old database. The old database remains a read/write primary that propagates changes to the new database.
choices.explanation: After switchover, the new database takes over the production endpoint. The original database is given a different name.

choices.text: The new database takes over the existing production endpoint. The old database is renamed and becomes read-only, and writes to the new database after switchover are not automatically replicated back.
choices.explanation: The old environment remains available for investigation but does not become a reverse replica that reflects the latest state.

choices.text: The old database remains read-only and catches up through reverse replication from the new database.
choices.explanation: Switchover does not configure reverse replication. Changes do not reach the old environment merely because it is retained.

choices.text: RDS automatically deletes the old database after the switch to prevent it from interfering with rollback.
choices.explanation: The old database is retained under a renamed identifier and can be handled separately when no longer needed.

source.label: RDS Blue/Green切り替え後の状態

learning.reason: The new environment takes over the existing production identifier and endpoint. The renamed old environment remains read-only, and writes to the new environment are not synchronized back in reverse.
learning.concept: Retaining the old environment after switchover and failing back with the updates incorporated are separate requirements. Simply making the old environment writable again would not incorporate updates made to the new database.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Returning the latest production data from AWS to on premises
prompt: During an on-premises outage, AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery was used to launch EC2 production recovery instances, and DNS was switched over. Transactions have continued to be accepted in this AWS environment for several days. A replacement server that meets the disk capacity requirements is available at the original site, and a brief period is available to stop the last writes. Which method returns operations to the regular site without losing the latest data in AWS?

choices.text: Replicate back from the AWS recovery instances to on premises. After confirming that writes have stopped and the final synchronization is complete, finalize failback in DRS. Verify startup and operation at the original site before switching DNS back.
choices.explanation: This makes the current write destination the source, preserving transactions accepted in AWS so operations can be switched back.

choices.text: Resume normal data replication from the original servers to AWS, then switch DNS to the original site as soon as replication catches up.
choices.explanation: The changes made in production are in AWS. Replication is in the wrong direction, so the latest business data will not be returned to the original site.

choices.text: Replicate a drill instance that was verified before the outage to on premises, then switch DNS back.
choices.explanation: A drill instance is a copy from the time of testing and does not contain the latest transactions accepted by the actual recovery instances.

choices.text: Restore a snapshot of the production recovery instances from before the outage and move it to on premises.
choices.explanation: Transactions completed in AWS after the outage are not included in an older snapshot.

source.label: Elastic Disaster Recoveryのオンプレミスへのフェイルバック

learning.reason: Replicate from the production recovery instances in AWS. Stop writes and confirm synchronization, finalize failback, and start the instances; then verify operation before switching traffic back.
learning.concept: A drill instance is separate from a production recovery instance. DRS helps restore data, but switching users to the destination is an operational task.

sourceLabel: Elastic Disaster Recovery failback to on premises

category: コスト最適化
title: Reassessing historical cost allocation tags missing from billing
prompt: Finance needs project-level costs from January onward for a report requested in December. The Project tag has been continuously set on resources since April, but the payer account activated it as a cost allocation tag only in October. Guessing historical tag values is not allowed. What can be recovered in AWS billing data, and what action should be taken?

source.label: コスト配分タグのバックフィル

learning.reason: Request a backfill of the current activation state to January from the management account. Values in the history can be used from April onward, but no values are created for January through March, when the tag was absent.
learning.concept: Assigning a tag to a resource and activating it as a cost allocation tag for billing are separate actions. Backfill reflects activation state for up to 12 months; it does not reconstruct tag values that did not exist at the time.

choices.text: Reopen Cost Explorer using the activated cost allocation tag. Report values will update automatically back to April, when the tag was added.
choices.explanation: Making the tag active now does not perform the steps needed to recalculate historical allocation data.

choices.text: Save the Project tag again on the resources with its current value, thereby applying that value to costs from January onward.
choices.explanation: Updating the current tag value does not create tag values for periods when the tag had not been set.

choices.text: Request backfill separately in each member account and deactivate the tag in the management account.
choices.explanation: Backfill is requested from the management account. Backfilling a disabled state would remove the allocation values being sought.

choices.text: Request a tag backfill from January in the management account. Report costs by project from April onward, when tag values exist, and leave January through March unallocated.
choices.explanation: Cost allocation tag activation can be backfilled, but tag values are limited to what was set at the time.

category: コスト最適化
title: Controlling read costs for an analytics index only
prompt: An on-demand DynamoDB table has a GSI that is read only by an analytics service. Reads during backfill were the main cause of a cost increase. Analytics can tolerate temporary throttling, but the write capacity of the production base table and GSI must not be changed. Which service-side approach can help control normal costs without imposing a strict per-second cap?

source.label: DynamoDBオンデマンドの最大スループット

learning.reason: Setting an on-demand maximum read throughput only on the analytics GSI can limit analytics spikes without changing the base table or write maximums.
learning.concept: On-demand maximum throughput can be configured separately for each table and GSI, and for reads and writes. Bursting can temporarily exceed the configured value, so it is not a strict billing cap.

choices.text: Set the on-demand maximum read throughput only for the analytics GSI and monitor throttling.
choices.explanation: This lets you target analytics without changing GSI writes or the base table settings.

choices.text: Set the on-demand maximum read throughput on the base table and assume the same value is automatically applied to related GSIs.
choices.explanation: GSI settings are separate, and limiting the base table's maximum reads would restrict production reads.

choices.text: Set only the maximum write throughput for the analytics GSI.
choices.explanation: This does not limit analytics reads. If index writes fall behind, writes to the source table may also be affected.

choices.text: Switch the table to provisioned capacity and operate only the GSI with low read capacity.
choices.explanation: This could constrain GSI reads, but it changes the base table's on-demand operating mode.

category: コスト最適化
title: Reducing allocated costs to match Spark processing waves
prompt: A batch Spark job using AWS Glue 4.0 G.1X workers needs many workers only for certain stages. Many of the fixed workers provisioned for peak demand are idle during other stages. You want to evaluate cost differences using measured usage while keeping the current maximum worker count and the goals for scheduled start and completion. Which configuration should you test?

source.label: AWS GlueのAuto Scaling

learning.reason: With Auto Scaling, you can set the maximum worker count and adjust the allocated workers to the needs of each Spark stage. Compare DPUSeconds and completion time for each batch run.
learning.concept: DPUSeconds measures compute resources actually used in an Auto Scaling run. Do not estimate on the assumption that all workers at the maximum count run throughout the entire execution.

choices.text: Fix the worker count at a small number suited to typical stages and assume the deadline will still be met during peaks.
choices.explanation: This may reduce steady-state cost, but it does not preserve the number of workers available during peaks.

choices.text: Switch to the Glue Flex execution class and judge by unit price alone, without considering the effect of start delays or variable allocation.
choices.explanation: Flex requires flexibility in start time or execution duration. Those factors must be checked when the job has scheduled start and completion requirements.

choices.text: Enable Glue Auto Scaling and set the current fixed count as the maximum. Measure DPUSeconds and completion time for each run, then compare them with fixed-worker runs.
choices.explanation: This preserves the maximum and lets you evaluate compute usage when only the workers needed at each stage are allocated.

choices.text: Keep the fixed count and reduce only the number of Spark partitions used by the job, assuming charges for unused workers will disappear.
choices.explanation: Changing parallelism does not reduce the fixed worker allocation. Idle capacity is not automatically removed from charges.

category: コスト最適化
title: Reduce Iceberg snapshot files while preserving the audit window
prompt: Frequent updates have accumulated snapshots in an Iceberg table managed by the Glue Data Catalog, increasing S3 storage costs. Audits must continue to use points in time from the most recent 30 days. You want a managed way to reduce data files used only by snapshots older than 30 days, without accidentally deleting files that are still referenced. Which setting is appropriate?

source.label: Glue Icebergテーブルのスナップショット保持

learning.reason: Set the retention policy to at least 30 days and use the snapshot retention optimizer to clean up expired snapshots and associated files that are no longer referenced by any remaining snapshot.
learning.concept: Data files referenced by manifests cannot be deleted based only on object creation time. Distinguish removing snapshot metadata from deleting the underlying data that is no longer needed.

choices.text: Use S3 Lifecycle to expire all data files 30 days after object creation.
choices.explanation: This could also delete older files referenced by the current table or by snapshots that must be retained.

choices.text: Enable the snapshot retention optimizer in Glue with a 30-day retention period, and enable deletion of unneeded files when snapshots expire.
choices.explanation: This reduces storage costs for unneeded data files while retaining snapshots within the retention period.

choices.text: Enable compaction alone to combine small files, and treat the files from old snapshots as deleted.
choices.explanation: Compaction optimizes file layout. It does not remove history because files needed by old snapshots remain available.

choices.text: Use the snapshot retention optimizer to clean up history after 30 days, but disable deletion of the data files themselves.
choices.explanation: Cleaning up metadata leaves the data files in S3, so it does not reduce the storage costs targeted here.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Move management of live resources without recreating them
prompt: A single CloudFormation stack manages a queue and resources for another purpose. You want to move the queue to an existing separate stack while preserving its messages and physical ID. The resource is eligible for stack refactoring; neither stack has a stack policy, and other resources will remain in the source stack. In the same change effort, you also want to update the queue's visibility timeout. How can you proceed without first manually detaching the queue from existing IaC management?

source.label: CloudFormationのスタックリファクタリング

learning.reason: Apply the queue configuration change in a regular stack update. Then provide the source and destination templates and any required mappings for refactoring without changing that configuration.
learning.concept: Stack refactoring is limited to reorganizing existing resources. Keep configuration changes and new resource creation out of the same operation, and review the preview to confirm the move.

choices.text: Add the queue to the destination template with the new visibility timeout, and apply both changes in the same refactoring operation.
choices.explanation: The queue can be moved, but a configuration change cannot be included in the refactoring operation.

choices.text: Change the visibility timeout in a regular stack update and confirm it, then move the queue with CloudFormation stack refactoring while keeping that configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: This handles the configuration update and the change in management stack as separate operations.

choices.text: Set Retain on the queue in the source stack, remove it from that stack, and import it separately into the destination stack.
choices.explanation: The resource can be retained, but this requires manually removing it from the source stack's management and importing it.

choices.text: Run a regular stack creation change set in the destination and specify the same name as the queue in the source stack.
choices.explanation: A regular creation operation does not adopt an existing queue with the same name. This could cause a name conflict or changes to the physical resource.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Pin and switch deployment targets with a label
prompt: You use old and new versions of a single String parameter in Systems Manager Parameter Store in test and production. Each time the production client reads the setting, it should retrieve the selected version. Registering a later version for testing must not change the production value. After approval, apply the version to production; if it causes a problem, quickly revert to the preceding version. Which method avoids adding parameter names or changing the reference used by clients each time?

source.label: Systems Manager Parameter Storeのラベル

learning.reason: GetParameter accepts a name and label. Attach the production label to an approved version, and move the label during promotion or rollback without changing the client reference.
learning.concept: A label points to one parameter version at a time, but it can be moved to another version. A retrieval that does not specify a version uses the latest version.

choices.text: Have production retrieve the parameter using only its name, and record the approved version number in the parameter description after testing.
choices.explanation: The description does not control which version is retrieved. Registering a later version changes the result for name-only retrieval.

choices.text: Have production specify the approved version number directly, and edit the version number in every client during each promotion and rollback.
choices.explanation: This separates candidate registration from production use, but requires changing the production clients' references every time.

choices.text: Label only the new candidate, while production retrieves the latest version by name.
choices.explanation: Whether the candidate has a label does not change the behavior of retrieval by name alone.

choices.text: Have production retrieve the parameter using its name and the production label. On approval, move the label to the candidate version; to revert, move it back to the preceding version.
choices.explanation: Registering a new version does not move the label, so the same reference can select a trusted version.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Restore management by isolating a failed nested resource
prompt: A production CloudFormation stack with nested stacks is in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED. The ID of the original scaling target was deleted through an external procedure and cannot be restored during the current incident response. Only this one resource in a child stack failed during rollback; the other resources can be rolled back. First, return the parent to an operable state. Reconcile the stack with the actual resources before subsequent updates. Which procedure is appropriate?

source.label: CloudFormationの更新ロールバックの続行

learning.reason: In the continue operation, specify only the child resource whose rollback failed, using the nested stack name and logical ID. Wait to perform a regular update until the post-skip state has been reconciled with the actual resources.
learning.concept: ResourcesToSkip is an exception for continuing a failed rollback. The resource is treated as updated, but its actual state is not restored to match the original configuration.

choices.text: Run a regular change set on the parent and immediately apply the new template for the failed update.
choices.explanation: A regular update cannot be started in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state; recovery from the failed rollback must come first.

choices.text: Continue rollback and specify every resource in the child stack, including those that rolled back successfully, to skip them all.
choices.explanation: Resources whose state does not differ because of a rollback failure cannot be specified. Unnecessary skips can increase inconsistency.

choices.text: Continue the parent's rollback and skip only the resource that failed rollback, identifying it by the child stack name and logical ID. Reconcile the configuration with the actual resource before the next update.
choices.explanation: This lets the other resources roll back while excluding only the resource that cannot be restored, and allows the inconsistency to be corrected before another update.

choices.text: Retry the parent's rollback without specifying any resources, and wait for the failed resource to be ignored automatically as if it had been skipped.
choices.explanation: The missing identifier has not been restored, so continuing may fail on the same resource. Failed resources are not skipped automatically.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Run independent checks in parallel while gating only the dependent build
prompt: In a single CodeBuild batch, run API contract generation, integration validation that starts after generation completes, and a license check that does not depend on either task. Each task runs in a different environment. Do not make the license check wait for generation, and do not add a wait loop to the application scripts. Which configuration should you choose?

source.label: CodeBuildバッチのbuildspec

learning.reason: In a build-graph, you can specify contract generation as a depend-on for integration validation. A task with no dependency can be scheduled independently.
learning.concept: build-list runs independent tasks in parallel, while build-matrix expands combinations of settings. Use a graph to express dependencies when you need to control the order in which tasks start.

choices.text: Use build-graph, set depend-on for contract generation only on integration validation, and leave the license check without dependencies.
choices.explanation: Declare only the required prerequisite so the unrelated check does not wait for generation to finish.

choices.text: List generation, validation, and the license check in that order in build-list, and use the listed order as the condition for starting integration validation.
choices.explanation: Tasks in the list run in parallel. Their listed order does not create dependencies.

choices.text: Put each environment in build-matrix and set the generation variable only for the first environment.
choices.explanation: This can expand combinations of environments, but it does not specify that integration validation must wait for generation to finish.

choices.text: Run everything in sequence in the phases of a single regular build, starting the license check after integration validation.
choices.explanation: This also delays the independent check, and does not meet the requirement for a parallel batch with separate execution environments.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Search assets in multiple Regions from a single view
prompt: Every Region in use in a single AWS account has an AWS Resource Explorer user-owned local index. Starting in Tokyo, an operator wants to search for assets with a target tag in other Regions from one view. Do not build a client that searches each Region and concatenates the results. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: Resource Explorerのアグリゲーターインデックス

learning.reason: Promote the user-owned index in Tokyo to an aggregator, then create a view in Tokyo that filters for the target assets. Information from other Regions' local indexes is replicated to the aggregator.
learning.concept: An account can have one aggregator. The Region containing a view determines the search scope, and replication can take time.

choices.text: Create a local view in Tokyo and search for the consistent tag. This automatically searches the other Regions too.
choices.explanation: A view that uses a local index is limited to searches in that Region. Tags do not expand its scope.

choices.text: Convert every Region into a separate aggregator and keep the local view in Tokyo.
choices.explanation: An account can have only one aggregator.

choices.text: Put the aggregator in another Region and specify the same tag filter only in the local view in Tokyo.
choices.explanation: A view used for cross-Region searches must be in the aggregator's Region.

choices.text: Promote the user-owned index in Tokyo to an aggregator and create a view there that filters for the target assets.
choices.explanation: Replicas of local indexes from other Regions can be searched from Tokyo.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Forward logs using normalized field names at ingestion
prompt: An application sends new logs to a CloudWatch Logs Standard log group. In several legacy formats, the original severity field has different names, but an enabled log transformer produces the normalized field level. Use a subscription to send only new events whose normalized level is ERROR to an external consumer; do not have the consumer parse each original format separately. Which configuration is required?

source.label: CloudWatch Logsのサブスクリプションフィルター

learning.reason: In a log group with an enabled transformer, set applyOnTransformedLogs to true and filter on the transformed field level.
learning.concept: Original and transformed logs can have different available fields. Configure which version the subscription filter evaluates for forwarding new logs.

choices.text: Keep the transformer enabled, but use a filter against the original events to check whether level is ERROR.
choices.explanation: The original events do not have the normalized level field, so the filter cannot find the expected match.

choices.text: Set applyOnTransformedLogs to true on the subscription and filter for level equal to ERROR.
choices.explanation: This evaluates the subscription filter against normalized events.

choices.text: Use a metric filter to count occurrences of level ERROR, then forward that metric as a Logs subscription.
choices.explanation: A metric filter produces a count; it does not deliver the matching log events.

choices.text: Update the log group to disable transformation of new logs, then use a log group filter to read only the normalized level.
choices.explanation: With transformation disabled, new events do not have the normalized field being tested.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Allow one brief spike and notify on two intermittent breaches
prompt: CloudWatch receives one service latency datapoint per minute. Notify when two of the latest three 1-minute values exceed the threshold, even if a normal value occurs between them. Do not notify for just one spike or for an increase only in the 3-minute average. Assume the evaluation data points arrive without gaps. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: CloudWatchアラームの評価

learning.reason: Set the period to 1 minute, EvaluationPeriods to 3, and DatapointsToAlarm to 2. With M out of N, breaching datapoints do not have to be adjacent.
learning.concept: Specify the statistic period, the number of datapoints to evaluate, and the number that must breach the threshold separately. Aggregating into one long period loses the count of individual breaches.

choices.text: Set the period to 1 minute, EvaluationPeriods to 2, and DatapointsToAlarm to 2.
choices.explanation: This requires two consecutive datapoints, so it will not notify when a normal datapoint occurs between the breaches.

choices.text: Set the period to 3 minutes, with one evaluation period and one breaching datapoint required, and evaluate the 3-minute average.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate whether two individual 1-minute values breached the threshold.

choices.text: Set the period to 1 minute, EvaluationPeriods to 3, and DatapointsToAlarm to 2.
choices.explanation: This detects when any two of the latest three datapoints breach the threshold.

choices.text: Set the period to 1 minute, EvaluationPeriods to 3, and DatapointsToAlarm to 1.
choices.explanation: A single anomalous datapoint triggers a notification, so an isolated spike is not excluded.

category: コスト最適化
title: Queue builds that exceed reserved capacity
prompt: A CodeBuild reserved fleet maintains a fixed number of machines. Large bursts of additional builds occur around scheduled builds, but the additional builds can wait to start. Keep the number of reserved machines unchanged and prevent charges outside the fleet when all machines are in use. Which approach avoids manually re-registering build requests?

source.label: CodeBuild予約済みフリートのオーバーフロー

learning.reason: With Queue overflow, builds wait until reserved machines are available. They do not start on separate on-demand compute resources when the fleet is at capacity.
learning.concept: Reserved fleet capacity is always provisioned. The overflow setting determines whether builds can wait or start sooner at additional on-demand cost.

choices.text: Set overflow to Queue so builds wait until reserved machines become available.
choices.explanation: This handles the wait without using on-demand machines outside the fleet.

choices.text: Set overflow to On-demand and only increase the timeout for waiting builds.
choices.explanation: When no capacity is available, builds overflow to on-demand and incur separate charges. A timeout setting does not change how capacity is allocated.

choices.text: Move all builds to on-demand and keep the number of reserved machines unchanged.
choices.explanation: This adds on-demand build charges to the existing reservation cost and does not meet the requested operating model.

choices.text: Permanently add enough reserved machines for the expected peak to eliminate build waits.
choices.explanation: This can reduce work outside the fleet, but the additional reservations incur charges and do not meet the requirement to keep peak workloads within the existing capacity.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Distribute writes across shards while preserving order per order
prompt: A Kinesis Data Streams producer uses one customer ID as the partition key for thousands of independent orders from a single customer, concentrating writes on one shard. No individual order exceeds a shard's write limit. Within each order, the producer continues using PutRecord and waits for the previous event to succeed before sending the next. Events are processed without sorting them by timestamp in the consumer. How should the producer change how it publishes events?

choices.text: Use a unique order ID as the key, but change sending to PutRecords and resend failed records after the successful ones.
choices.explanation: This avoids concentrating writes on one key, but resending records after a partial batch failure can change event order within an order.

choices.text: Append a random value to the customer ID for each event to distribute writes across shards.
choices.explanation: Events from the same order can go to different shards, so order within an order cannot be preserved.

choices.text: Keep the customer ID as the partition key and only increase the number of shards.
choices.explanation: The same key hashes to one shard range, so adding shards does not eliminate the concentration for that customer.

choices.text: Use a fixed key combining the customer ID and order ID, and send each order's PutRecord calls in sequence with the previous successful sequence number.
choices.explanation: This distributes writes by order while keeping events for the same order on the same key and accepting them in sequence.

source.label: KinesisのパーティションキーとPutRecordでの順序

learning.reason: Use the same partition key for all events in an order, and vary the key across orders. Passing the previous sequence number to PutRecord preserves ordering while hashes for different orders are distributed.
learning.concept: Check shard count and key distribution separately. Splitting a single key can lose business-level ordering. Retrying after a partial PutRecords failure also does not provide the same ordering guarantee.

sourceLabel: Kinesis partition keys and ordering with PutRecord

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Use an access point alias only for object requests
prompt: Team-specific access points have been created for a general purpose S3 bucket in the same Region. The existing SDK reads the destinations for GetObject and PutObject from a bucket-name field in a configuration file, and its input validation rejects ARNs. Change only the configuration value to route requests through an access point, and allow only objects for the target access point in the IAM policy. Which combination is appropriate?

choices.text: Keep the original bucket name for GetObject and PutObject, and change only the IAM Resource to the access point ARN.
choices.explanation: Requests sent to the original bucket name do not go through the access point. A policy alone cannot change the request route.

choices.text: Pass the access point alias in the bucket field for the relevant operations, and specify the object ARN under the access point in the IAM policy.
choices.explanation: This changes the access point through a bucket-compatible SDK value and uses a supported resource syntax in IAM.

choices.text: Use the same access point alias in both the SDK and the IAM Resource.
choices.explanation: An alias that can be used in the data plane cannot be used as the resource notation in an IAM policy.

choices.text: Keep the original name in the configuration file and change only the SDK access Region.
choices.explanation: The access point route is not selected by using the same bucket name.

source.label: S3アクセスポイントのARNとエイリアス

learning.reason: For supported object operations, an access point alias can be used in the bucket field. In the IAM policy's Resource, specify the access point ARN for the target objects rather than the alias.
learning.concept: A bucket-compatible value used for data-plane requests is distinct from the resource identifier used in policy evaluation. Do not reuse the alias in bucket configuration APIs.

sourceLabel: S3 access point ARNs and aliases

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Preserve per-customer ordering without blocking other customers
prompt: A FIFO queue and Lambda process customer billing events. All events are sent with the same MessageGroupId, so unrelated customers also wait while one customer's processing is retried. Preserve ordering within each customer and deduplication specific to each event. What is the smallest change that allows processing across customers to run concurrently while keeping one queue?

choices.text: Move to a Standard queue, retain event IDs, and assume that ordering per customer is guaranteed by send order.
choices.explanation: A Standard queue can deliver messages out of order, so downstream processing cannot rely on it to preserve order within a customer.

choices.text: Keep the same group ID and change MessageDeduplicationId to the customer ID.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the groups, and distinct events from the same customer could be treated as duplicates.

choices.text: Change MessageGroupId to the customer ID and retain a distinct MessageDeduplicationId for each event.
choices.explanation: This preserves ordering and deduplication within each customer while allowing other customer groups to be processed concurrently.

choices.text: Keep the same group ID, shorten the visibility timeout, and increase Lambda concurrency.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the waiting messages into independent groups. A shorter timeout can cause the same event to be processed again more often.

source.label: SQS FIFOのメッセージグループの動作

learning.reason: Using the customer ID as the MessageGroupId keeps messages for that customer ordered while allowing other groups to be processed independently.
learning.concept: The group ID defines ordering and concurrency boundaries. The deduplication ID suppresses duplicate submissions of the same message; it does not change the group.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Restricting service callers even when their VPCs are connected
prompt: A VPC Lattice service network in a shared management account is already associated with multiple VPCs and HTTP services in the organization. The network administrator wants all services to accept only signed requests from within the organization, while an administrator for an individual service wants to allow calls only from a batch role in one of the associated VPCs. The workloads are in another account, and the routes and VPC associations must remain in place. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Set both authentication types to AWS_IAM and require organization membership at the network level. At the service level, allow the batch role, and also allow it to invoke the target service in its IAM policy.
choices.explanation: This aligns the organization, service, and caller constraints.

choices.text: Set only the network to AWS_IAM and allow requests from within the organization. Set the target service's authentication type to NONE.
choices.explanation: The network constraint remains in effect, but the service does not restrict callers to the batch role.

choices.text: Set only the target service to AWS_IAM and allow the batch role, without configuring a common authentication policy for the network.
choices.explanation: This can provide service-specific authentication, but not the shared constraint for the entire network.

choices.text: Use the security group attached to the VPC association to allow the batch role's ARN.
choices.explanation: Security group network conditions cannot evaluate the IAM role that issued a request.

source.label: VPC Latticeの認証ポリシー評価

learning.reason: Set both authentication types to AWS_IAM, then evaluate the organization condition at the network level and the specific role condition at the service level. For cross-account calls, also configure the caller's IAM policy and sign the request.
learning.concept: VPC and service associations provide reachability. Authorization is evaluated through the network, service, and principal policies.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Assessing encryption behavior when an external key store is disconnected
prompt: A regulated processing platform protects data keys using a key in an AWS KMS external key store. During a planned exercise, the connection between the key store and its proxy is disconnected. You want to determine what happens to new KMS cryptographic operations and to requests from an integrated service that already has a decrypted data key. The application has no implemented fallback to another key. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: KMS automatically switches cryptographic API calls to a standard key with the same name as the external key's alias, and the integrated service continues operating.
choices.explanation: External keys are required for KMS cryptographic operations. There is no automatic switch to a standard key.

choices.text: Once the connection is lost, new KMS cryptographic API calls and all requests from services that already hold plaintext data keys fail at the same time.
choices.explanation: Processing that reuses a data key already available locally without calling KMS does not necessarily stop immediately.

choices.text: New KMS cryptographic operations using that key fail. Processing can continue in a service that already holds a valid plaintext data key until it needs KMS again.
choices.explanation: Calls to KMS cryptographic APIs fail, while reuse of a data key does not share the same failure boundary.

choices.text: Only the generation of new data keys fails; KMS can still decrypt existing encrypted data keys while the connection is down.
choices.explanation: Decrypting an existing encrypted data key also requires the external key.

source.label: KMS外部キーストアの接続と切断

learning.reason: While disconnected, new KMS cryptographic operations using that KMS key fail. If an integrated service is reusing a plaintext data key that is already available, the impact may not appear until the key is needed from KMS again.
learning.concept: Distinguish the availability of KMS cryptographic APIs from the processing state of services that use envelope encryption. KMS does not automatically replace an external key with a standard KMS key.

sourceLabel: KMS external key store connection and disconnection

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Maintaining CloudFront certificate renewal after a DNS migration
prompt: A DNS-validated public certificate issued by ACM and used by CloudFront contains two hostnames with different parent domains owned by the company. The company is moving its public DNS to another provider but wants to keep delivery and automatic ACM certificate renewal working. You can manage CloudFront and ACM settings and edit both public DNS zones. What change should you make?

choices.text: Move only the CNAME that points to CloudFront to the new provider; do not move the ACM validation CNAMEs because initial issuance is complete.
choices.explanation: Name resolution for delivery may continue, but the records ACM needs for DNS validation during a later renewal will be missing.

choices.text: Publish the ACM CNAME for only one hostname; do not create one for the other because both names are on the same certificate.
choices.explanation: Automatic renewal cannot be maintained if the required record for each name is not available.

choices.text: Move both ACM validation CNAMEs to a private hosted zone and keep only CloudFront name resolution in public DNS.
choices.explanation: DNS validation for renewal requires the CNAMEs to be verifiable in public DNS.

choices.text: Keep the certificate in use by CloudFront, move both ACM validation CNAMEs specified for the certificate to the new public DNS, and verify that they resolve publicly.
choices.explanation: The certificate remains in use, and DNS validation for each hostname can be checked again at renewal.

source.label: ACMのDNS検証済み証明書の更新

learning.reason: Keep the certificate in use by CloudFront and maintain the required ACM validation CNAME for each hostname in the new public DNS.
learning.concept: For public certificate renewal, verify both that the certificate is in use and that its validation records are publicly reachable. The DNS record pointing to the delivery endpoint is separate from the CNAME ACM uses to verify domain ownership.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Avoiding duplicate IAM configuration history while continuing regional audits
prompt: An AWS Config aggregator receives data from three Regions. You want to preserve each Region's resource history while recording global IAM users and roles in only one recorder to avoid duplicate records. The aggregation Region is one where Config support began in February 2022 or later, while some source Regions were supported earlier. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Choose one Region that was supported before February 2022 to record the global IAM resource types, and exclude those types from the other recorders.
choices.explanation: This records them once in a supported Region while preserving the other Regions' histories.

choices.text: Enable global IAM recording only in the aggregation Region and assume it will be recorded regardless of when Config support began there.
choices.explanation: Recording global IAM resource types is not available in Regions where AWS Config support began in February 2022 or later.

choices.text: Enable global IAM recording in every recorder and rely on the aggregated view to deduplicate identical ARNs, assuming recording costs will be incurred only once.
choices.explanation: Deduplicating the display does not prevent records from being collected in multiple places.

choices.text: Disable global IAM recording in all Regions and change the aggregator's Region to one Region, assuming IAM history will be generated automatically.
choices.explanation: An aggregator does not create configuration history for resources that are not being recorded.

source.label: AWS Configのグローバルリソース記録

learning.reason: Record global IAM resources in one Region that has supported this for longer, and exclude them from other recorders while preserving each Region's regional history.
learning.concept: Do not confuse the Regions that can record legacy global IAM resources with the home Region rules later introduced for other global resource types. An aggregator collects data from existing recorders.

sourceLabel: AWS Config recording of global resources

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Centralizing bidirectional finding updates in the home Region
prompt: A team already uses Security Hub CSPM in three Regions. Without changing its existing standards, the team wants to investigate future findings and workflow status updates in a home Region while reviewing earlier findings over time. Some older findings created just before linking do not appear in the home Region. If the team does not want to operate a manual forwarding pipeline, which configuration and expectation are correct?

choices.text: Reassign the standards in central configuration across all Regions; this copies the entire finding history to the home Region immediately.
choices.explanation: Standard deployment and replication of findings or updates are separate. The entire history is not replicated immediately.

choices.text: Configure cross-Region aggregation by specifying the home Region and linked Regions. Review findings and updates made after linking, and check unupdated existing findings in their source Regions.
choices.explanation: Use aggregation for new findings and updates, without assuming that unupdated historical findings are replicated automatically and immediately.

choices.text: Add every Region to a Config aggregator so that Security Hub CSPM finding workflow statuses are replicated.
choices.explanation: Aggregating AWS Config configuration and compliance data does not synchronize Security Hub CSPM finding history or updates.

choices.text: Disable CSPM in every Region and enable it only in the home Region; findings will arrive without enabling the linked Regions.
choices.explanation: Cross-Region aggregation does not replace existing Region-by-Region collection.

source.label: Security Hub CSPMのクロスリージョン集約

learning.reason: Specify the home and linked Regions in a finding aggregator. New findings and updates made afterward are replicated. Existing findings might not be replicated to the home Region until they are updated.
learning.concept: Finding aggregation is separate from central configuration of standards. Security Hub CSPM must be enabled in the Regions being aggregated.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Reflecting external IdP permissions in trusted access tokens
prompt: A Lite-plan Cognito user pool uses an external SAML IdP and can use the V1_0 pre-token generation trigger. An existing management API authorizes requests using cognito:groups in an access token after validating its signature and issuer, among other checks. The company’s authorization ledger can be looked up using Cognito’s stable user ID, and users cannot edit the ledger. Without changing plans, how should operational groups be assigned in the token only when the ledger’s department is on an allowlist?

choices.text: Map SAML attributes to ordinary custom attributes and assume users are automatically added to user-pool groups with matching names.
choices.explanation: Attribute mapping alone does not automatically assign a user to a Cognito group.

choices.text: Put all departments in one user-pool group and let the API rely on the browser’s decision when displaying the UI.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for API authorization based on token groups or restrict access on the server to allowed departments.

choices.text: Put the department in a different custom claim before token generation, while leaving the existing API to check only cognito:groups.
choices.explanation: The operational group will not appear in the claim that the existing API uses for authorization.

choices.text: Use a V1_0 Pre token generation Lambda to look up the authorization ledger and specify the operational group for allowed users with groupOverrideDetails.
choices.explanation: The operational group can be set at token issuance based on the trusted authorization ledger, and will appear in the access-token group claim the existing API checks.

source.label: Cognitoのトークン生成前トリガー

learning.reason: In the Pre token generation Lambda, look up the authorization ledger associated with the stable user ID. Set the operational group in the response’s groupOverrideDetails only when the department is on the allowlist.
learning.concept: Attribute mapping and Cognito group assignment are separate. In V1_0, group overrides are reflected in the access token’s cognito:groups claim. Adding arbitrary claims to an access token uses a different event version.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Delegating decryption while fixing only required context fields
prompt: A data-processing workload uses a symmetric KMS key and needs to delegate scoped decryption permissions to a batch role. Limit decryption to data whose encryption context includes tenant=finance. Additional fields such as doc-id, specified during encryption, vary by file and are also specified during decryption. The role has no other decryption grants. How can this be delegated without changing the key policy?

choices.text: Create a Decrypt grant with EncryptionContextEquals specifying only tenant=finance.
choices.explanation: If the request includes additional fields such as doc-id, it will not meet the grant’s exact-match condition.

choices.text: Create a KMS alias containing the text tenant=finance and configure a Decrypt grant without conditions.
choices.explanation: An alias does not validate context and does not exclude requests to decrypt ciphertext encrypted for a different tenant.

choices.text: Set EncryptionContextSubset on a Decrypt grant and specify tenant=finance as the required key-value pair.
choices.explanation: This requires the request to include the required field while allowing the other fields added during encryption.

choices.text: Set EncryptionContextSubset only on a GenerateDataKey grant.
choices.explanation: This allows an operation to obtain new data keys; it does not grant the Decrypt permission the batch role needs.

source.label: KMSグラントの暗号化コンテキスト制約

learning.reason: In the grant that delegates only Decrypt, specify tenant=finance in EncryptionContextSubset to require that pair in the request. A valid encryption context that includes additional pairs is also allowed.
learning.concept: Subset matches the context required by the grant; it does not relax the exact-context requirement for decrypting the ciphertext. Equals requires the entire request context to match the grant constraint.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Collecting events from additional accounts in an existing audit platform
prompt: An organization has used CloudTrail Lake since before it stopped accepting new customers. Some existing member accounts currently have account-level event data stores. The organization wants to aggregate all-Region management events from its growing membership into a single audit store, using CloudTrail Lake, which continues to be available to existing customers. How can it do this without adding a data store for every new member?

choices.text: Convert the audit member’s account-level data store to multi-Region.
choices.explanation: This expands Region coverage but does not expand the store’s account scope to the entire organization.

choices.text: Create an organization event data store that collects all-Region management events across the organization.
choices.explanation: The management account or a delegated administrator can configure this, so new members do not need to be added individually.

choices.text: Save an all-Region organization trail to S3 and assume the existing account-level event data store in the same account will continuously ingest the S3 objects.
choices.explanation: Delivering an organization trail to S3 does not expand an existing account-level event data store’s ongoing collection scope.

choices.text: Extend retention for existing members’ event data stores and assume new members’ events will be recorded under the same historical identifiers.
choices.explanation: Retention controls how long data is kept; it does not collect management events from other accounts.

source.label: CloudTrail Lakeの提供範囲と組織データストア

learning.reason: The organization’s management account or a delegated administrator configures an organization event data store. Selecting all Regions and management events enables collection at the organization level, including from new members.
learning.concept: An existing account’s individual event data store continuing to work is different from automatically ingesting new members. An organization store is needed to manage collection for members added after new-customer onboarding ended.

sourceLabel: CloudTrail Lake availability and organization data stores

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Record the result after completing a three-hour restore validation
prompt: AWS Backup restore testing already restores to an isolated RDS environment every day. Add application testing after the restore completes. The test can take up to 3 hours after the completion event, and the restored database must remain available during that time. Make the result visible on the AWS Backup restore job, and let AWS Backup delete the resource after validation. Which two settings should you configure?

choices.text: Set StartWindowHours to 4 in the restore testing plan to allow a four-hour testing period after the restore.
choices.explanation: The start window is the period during which the test job can start. It does not control the post-restore validation period.

choices.text: Set a 4-hour validation window in the restore testing selection for the resource.
choices.explanation: This sets how long the restored resource remains available, so the window stays open even if testing takes up to 3 hours.

choices.text: Extend the retention period of the source backup by 4 days and assume the same retention period applies to the test environment.
choices.explanation: Changing the lifetime of the recovery point does not change how long the restore testing environment remains before cleanup.

choices.text: Apply a backup tag directly to the restored database and use the tag as the restore job's validation result.
choices.explanation: A tag does not change the validation status of an AWS Backup restore job.

choices.text: Start the test workflow from the completion event, then call PutRestoreValidationResult with the restore job ID after testing is complete.
choices.explanation: The application validation result can be recorded against the corresponding restore job.

source.label: AWS Backupの復元テストの検証

learning.reason: Set a validation window long enough in the restore testing selection. Run validation after the restore completes, then report the result to AWS Backup using the same restore job identifier.
learning.concept: A successful restore job and an application validation result are separate. Changing backup retention does not change the validation time available for a temporarily restored environment.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Roll back to a known configuration when business metrics degrade during an AMI refresh
prompt: An EC2 Auto Scaling group is undergoing an instance refresh to update its AMI. It currently runs the configuration from launch template version 41, and the new AMI is in version 42. Business error rates can rise even when EC2 health checks pass. If the corresponding CloudWatch alarm enters ALARM during the refresh, you want to automatically return to the original configuration. The AMI uses a fixed ID. Which procedure is appropriate?

choices.text: Update the group to version 42 first, then request automatic rollback in a refresh that omits the desired configuration.
choices.explanation: Automatic rollback cannot be used in a refresh that does not specify a desired configuration. Changing the group configuration first also makes the rollback target unclear.

choices.text: Keep the group's launch template reference set to $Latest and add only the CloudWatch alarm to the refresh.
choices.explanation: A launch template reference that is not pinned to a version cannot return to a previous version. The automatic rollback setting is also missing.

choices.text: Set the desired configuration to version 42 and enable automatic rollback, but do not pass the alarm to the refresh; rely only on EC2 health checks.
choices.explanation: For a business issue that does not fail health checks, an alarm that is not associated with the refresh will not cause the refresh to fail.

choices.text: Keep the current group pinned to version 41 and specify version 42 as the desired configuration for the refresh. Associate the business error-rate alarm and enable automatic rollback.
choices.explanation: This provides a pinned rollback target and lets the refresh return replaced instances to the original configuration when the alarm enters ALARM.

source.label: EC2 Auto Scalingの手動と自動ロールバック

learning.reason: Keep the current group pinned to version 41 and set version 42 as the refresh's desired configuration. Include the CloudWatch alarm and enable automatic rollback.
learning.concept: Rollback requires a configuration to return to. Check the constraints that apply when using $Default or $Latest for a launch template, or when a refresh does not specify a desired configuration.

sourceLabel: Manual and automatic rollback in EC2 Auto Scaling

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Resume PostgreSQL change capture from the correct point after preloading
prompt: Migrate from PostgreSQL to another database. The initial data has already been loaded through a separate path from a consistent snapshot, and the PostgreSQL LSN corresponding to that point was recorded. The appropriate logical replication slot has been created, and the required WAL is retained. How can you use DMS to capture only changes from this point without recreating the target tables?

choices.text: Run full load and CDC in the same task, recreating the target tables before starting CDC.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid recreating the initial data.

choices.text: Use a CDC-only task, specify the UTC time of the initial load, and let DMS convert it to the corresponding PostgreSQL LSN.
choices.explanation: For PostgreSQL, DMS does not support starting by converting a time to an LSN.

choices.text: Set up a CDC-only task and use the source replication slot and the recorded native start LSN.
choices.explanation: This captures changes from the appropriate point in the retained WAL without repeating the initial load.

choices.text: Create a CDC-only task and capture changes only from the time the task starts, without using the recorded LSN.
choices.explanation: Changes between the initial data point and task startup would not be migrated.

source.label: AWS DMSでの継続レプリケーションの開始位置

learning.reason: Use a CDC-only task with the source's logical replication slot and the native start LSN. Apply changes after the point represented by the data already loaded.
learning.concept: Specify the CDC starting point in the form required by the source engine. DMS for PostgreSQL does not support converting a specified time to an LSN to start CDC.

sourceLabel: Starting point for ongoing replication with AWS DMS

category: コスト最適化
title: Stop charges for parts of failed uploads only
prompt: Use S3 multipart uploads for browser-based video uploads. Uploads are accumulating without completing because of network disconnections. Allow up to 7 days from initiation for a resumable upload, then automatically clean up only old, incomplete parts under the video prefix. Do not change the retention of completed videos in the same location. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: S3の未完了マルチパートの自動中止

learning.reason: For the video prefix, set the lifecycle action AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload to 7 days after initiation. It does not apply to completed objects.
learning.concept: Storage for incomplete parts is separate from the expiration of successfully completed objects. Parts consume storage until the upload is completed or the incomplete upload is aborted.

choices.text: Set a 7-day expiration for current objects under the video prefix.
choices.explanation: This expires current objects, changing the retention of completed videos, and does not abort incomplete parts.

choices.text: Enable versioning and expire only noncurrent versions after 7 days.
choices.explanation: Parts from an incomplete upload are not noncurrent versions.

choices.text: Create a lifecycle rule for the video prefix that aborts incomplete multipart uploads more than 7 days after initiation.
choices.explanation: This cleans up incomplete parts while leaving completed objects under the same prefix outside the rule's scope.

choices.text: Configure a transition to S3 Glacier after 7 days for the video prefix.
choices.explanation: A storage class transition applies to completed objects; it does not delete incomplete upload parts.

sourceLabel: Automatically aborting incomplete multipart uploads in S3

category: コスト最適化
title: Keep Lambda capacity ready only during known demand windows
prompt: A business Lambda function is invoked through its production alias. On weekdays, a burst of traffic arrives at exactly 9:00 a.m., and the first request must not incur initialization latency. Slow cold starts are acceptable overnight, and the goal is to reduce the cost of keeping peak-level capacity available during low-demand periods. If the function and invocation path must remain unchanged, which configuration should you choose?

source.label: Lambdaのプロビジョンド同時実行とスケーリング

learning.reason: Increase provisioned concurrency for the production alias in advance, allowing time for initialization to complete. Use Application Auto Scaling schedules to lower the configured amount after the peak.
learning.concept: Reserved concurrency reserves account concurrency capacity. Use provisioned concurrency to initialize execution environments in advance, and plan for the time needed for allocation to complete.

choices.text: Increase only reserved concurrency for the morning period and assume the execution environments will also be initialized.
choices.explanation: Reserved concurrency reserves concurrency capacity, but it does not initialize execution environments by itself.

choices.text: Increase provisioned concurrency for the production alias to the planned capacity before the start time. After the period ends, use a schedule to lower the limit.
choices.explanation: This prepares execution environments before peak traffic begins and reduces the cost of preallocated capacity during low-demand periods.

choices.text: Configure only utilization-based target tracking and wait for capacity to increase after the first request arrives at 9:00 a.m.
choices.explanation: Capacity increases after demand is detected, so this does not ensure that preinitialized capacity is available for the first request.

choices.text: Configure provisioned concurrency on a separate development alias and continue invoking the production alias as before.
choices.explanation: Provisioned capacity on an alias that is not used for invocation does not preinitialize the production alias.

category: コスト最適化
title: Estimate short-task costs from before the container starts
prompt: An ECS on Fargate Linux task takes 30 seconds to pull its image, and the task runs for 45 seconds after the pull completes. The same CPU and memory settings are specified each time, and ephemeral storage is set to 50 GB. The operating system, architecture, and Region are fixed. Excluding data transfer and other charges, how should you estimate charges for Fargate compute resources and additional ephemeral storage?

source.label: AWS Fargateの料金と計測区間

learning.reason: For Linux, billing is measured from the start of the image pull through task completion, subject to a one-minute minimum. Here the duration is 75 seconds, and 30 GB of the configured 50 GB is above the included 20 GB and is subject to the additional ephemeral-storage charge.
learning.concept: Billing covers more than the application's processing time within the task. Calculate charges using the configured CPU and memory, and include additional ephemeral storage.

choices.text: The business workload runs for 45 seconds, so charge for 45 seconds of compute resources and treat all 50 GB as free.
choices.explanation: This omits image-pull time and the minimum billing duration, and ephemeral storage above the included amount is chargeable.

choices.text: Apply the one-minute minimum to the 45-second task runtime, for 60 seconds, and charge for all 50 GB of ephemeral storage.
choices.explanation: The measured interval starts when the image pull starts, so it is 75 seconds. Also, the included 20 GB is not subject to the additional storage charge.

choices.text: Estimate 75 seconds of compute resources. Add storage charges only for the number of bytes actually used.
choices.explanation: Additional storage charges are based on the configured capacity; actual usage alone does not determine the charge.

choices.text: Use the 75 seconds from the start of the image pull to task completion as the compute billing duration, based on the specified CPU and memory. Add the 30 GB of ephemeral storage above the included amount.
choices.explanation: This accounts for the duration of a Linux task that exceeds one minute and for configured storage capacity above the included amount.

sourceLabel: AWS Fargate pricing and billing duration

category: コスト最適化
title: Reduce compute charges while pausing a development database
prompt: An on-demand RDS for PostgreSQL development DB instance is not a read replica and has no replicas. It will not be used at all for four days during a holiday. After the holiday, the team wants to use the same endpoint and data and avoid rebuilding the instance from a snapshot. What is the appropriate decision about charges during the idle period?

source.label: Amazon RDS DBインスタンスの一時停止

learning.reason: Stopping the instance and restarting it after the holiday preserves the original configuration and endpoint. DB instance-hour charges stop, but storage and other applicable charges remain.
learning.concept: Do not treat an RDS stop as indefinite storage. After seven consecutive days stopped, the DB instance starts automatically, so account for this limit in longer-term cost estimates.

choices.text: Stop the DB instance and start it again after the holiday. DB instance-hours are not charged during the stopped period, while provisioned storage and chargeable backups remain.
choices.explanation: For a four-day period, the instance can be restarted before the automatic restart after seven days, and the same DB can continue to be used.

choices.text: Stop the DB instance and eliminate all charges, including storage and backups, for 30 days.
choices.explanation: Storage charges continue while the DB instance is stopped, and it automatically starts again after seven days of being stopped.

choices.text: Delete the DB instance and retain a final snapshot. After the holiday, restart the same DB instance that existed before it was stopped.
choices.explanation: A deleted DB instance cannot be restarted. You would need to restore a new DB instance from the snapshot.

choices.text: Leave the DB instance running and block connections from the VPC. Instance-hours are not charged while there are no requests.
choices.explanation: DB instance-hour charges depend on whether the DB instance is running, not on whether users send requests.

sourceLabel: Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Choose a successful execution to roll back from the current configuration version
prompt: A deployment stage in CodePipeline V2 failed. The team wants to roll back the stage manually and reuse the variables and artifacts from a successful execution. The candidates are a successful execution from an older pipeline configuration version, a standard successful execution from the current configuration version, a successful rollback execution from the current configuration version, and the failed execution. Which execution can be selected without rebuilding?

source.label: CodePipelineのステージロールバック

learning.reason: Select a standard successful execution of the target stage under the current pipeline configuration version. CodePipeline creates a new rollback execution that reuses that execution's variables and artifacts.
learning.concept: The eligible target is a successful stage execution. Earlier pipeline configuration versions and executions that are themselves rollback executions are not eligible.

choices.text: A standard execution in which the target stage succeeded under an older pipeline configuration version.
choices.explanation: You cannot roll back a stage to an execution started under an earlier configuration version.

choices.text: A standard execution in which the target stage succeeded under the current pipeline configuration version.
choices.explanation: This is a successful execution for the target stage under the current configuration version, and it is not itself a rollback execution.

choices.text: A rollback execution in which the target stage succeeded under the current pipeline configuration version.
choices.explanation: Even if it succeeded, an execution ID for a rollback execution cannot be selected as the target.

choices.text: Select the currently failed execution and have CodePipeline automatically rebuild the earlier artifacts from its pre-failure variables.
choices.explanation: A rollback requires a successful target execution; it is not intended to reuse artifacts from the currently failed execution.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Store large parallel worker outputs without aggregating them in the parent
prompt: In a Step Functions Distributed Map, each worker's result is small, but combining all the results would exceed 256 KiB. The parent only needs to pass the result location to the next step, and the results, including worker failures, must be reviewable in S3. Buckets are available both in the account and Region that host the state machine and in a separate audit account. How can this be done without changing the worker implementations?

source.label: Step Functions Distributed MapのResultWriter

learning.reason: Use ResultWriter to export the Map Run results to S3 in the same account and Region. The Map state's output can pass the S3 destination information to the next step.
learning.concept: Reading the input dataset and exporting child workflow results are separate configurations. Including all results in the default return value can exceed the parent payload limit.

choices.text: Specify the audit bucket in ItemReader and have the child results automatically written to the same destination.
choices.explanation: ItemReader is used to read the data to process. It does not define result exports.

choices.text: Use ResultWriter to write directly to the audit bucket in another account. Rely on the bucket policy alone to remove the restriction.
choices.explanation: ResultWriter exports require a bucket in the same account and Region as the state machine.

choices.text: Use ResultWriter to write to a bucket in the same account and Region as the state machine, and have the parent receive the destination information.
choices.explanation: The results can be accessed in S3 without aggregating all child outputs into the parent's payload.

choices.text: Lower the Map's MaxConcurrency and combine all results in the parent after each execution completes successfully.
choices.explanation: Limiting concurrency does not reduce the size of the output once it is combined.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Exclude a planned outage from training while retaining normal seasonality
prompt: Monitor the traffic volume of a payment API in CloudWatch. Traffic is seasonal, with different patterns on weekdays and holidays, and is gradually increasing, so a fixed threshold is not stable. A planned outage last week is not part of the normal seasonal pattern, and you do not want the anomaly detection model to learn from it. However, you do not want future scheduled outages to be automatically excluded from notifications. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: CloudWatchの異常検出アラーム

learning.reason: Use a metric anomaly detection model and set the planned outage's dates as a training exclusion range. The alarm continues to evaluate using the anomaly detection band.
learning.concept: An exclusion range selects the history the model trains on. It is different from a scheduled suppression of alarm actions or a setting that ignores future metric data.

choices.text: Use a fixed threshold for a standard alarm, setting it to the average immediately before and after last week's planned outage.
choices.explanation: A fixed threshold does not model the seasonality and upward trend, and it does not provide a setting to exclude the planned outage from training.

choices.text: Configure only the alarm's treatment of the metrics from last week's planned outage as missing data.
choices.explanation: Missing-data treatment controls evaluation when input data is absent; it does not change the training range for data that was actually received.

choices.text: Temporarily disable the anomaly detection alarm's actions so the data from last week's planned outage is excluded from the model.
choices.explanation: Disabling actions affects notifications but does not select which historical data the model trains on.

choices.text: Add last week's planned outage to the anomaly detection model's training exclusion ranges and use an alarm based on the band.
choices.explanation: The model can learn seasonality without the exceptional period, while future evaluation and notifications remain enabled.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Tag only S3 object versions fixed at a specified point in time
prompt: In an S3 bucket with versioning enabled, add an audit tag to several million specific versions that currently have no tags. The audit team has finalized the targets in a CSV, and new current versions must not be touched even if they are added during processing. Mechanically collect whether processing succeeded for each target. Which two settings should you use?

source.label: S3 Batch Operationsのマニフェストと完了レポート

learning.reason: Use a CSV with the bucket, key, and VersionId in every row. Specify the object tagging operation and write a completion report for all tasks to S3.
learning.concept: The manifest fixes the targets. If a version is not specified, the current version could be selected when the job runs, so explicitly identify the target version and audit the results. S3 Batch Operations object tagging replaces the entire tag set.

choices.text: Specify the bucket name, key, and target VersionId in every row of the manifest.
choices.explanation: This targets the versions selected by the audit, regardless of changes to the current version.

choices.text: Omit VersionId and use the current version only for objects that should receive the audit tag.
choices.explanation: Without VersionId, processing cannot precisely target the fixed versions, including noncurrent versions.

choices.text: Specify object tagging in S3 Batch Operations and enable a completion report for all tasks.
choices.explanation: This lets you check success or failure for each target.

choices.text: Enable only S3 Inventory and treat the completion of the inventory CSV as confirmation that each target has been tagged.
choices.explanation: Inventory creates a listing; it does not perform tagging or record task results.

choices.text: Configure a failure-only completion report and assume that targets not listed in it have individual success records available.
choices.explanation: A failure-only report does not include individual success rows, so it cannot record the outcome for every target as the audit team requires.

sourceLabel: S3 Batch Operations Manifest and Completion Report

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Keep the incident state visible while delaying only notifications during maintenance
prompt: A CloudWatch composite alarm displays the actual incident state on a dashboard. While a separate maintenance alarm is in ALARM, only notification actions should be suppressed. The incident state may be reflected up to one minute before maintenance is detected, and actions should remain suppressed for two minutes after maintenance ends. The incident alarm itself must remain in ALARM. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: CloudWatch複合アラームのアクション抑止

learning.reason: Specify the maintenance alarm as ActionsSuppressor. Set WaitPeriod for the delay when an incident is detected first and ExtensionPeriod for the delay after the maintenance alarm leaves ALARM.
learning.concept: Suppression affects the composite alarm's actions. Adding the maintenance state to the alarm's expression changes the incident state displayed.

choices.text: Add a condition that the maintenance alarm is OK to the composite alarm's expression, making the composite alarm OK during maintenance.
choices.explanation: This avoids notifications, but the composite alarm cannot display ALARM during maintenance even if an incident is actually occurring.

choices.text: Set the maintenance alarm as the ActionsSuppressor, with a WaitPeriod of 60 seconds and an ExtensionPeriod of 120 seconds.
choices.explanation: This allows time for maintenance detection and extends suppression after maintenance ends. The composite alarm's state is still evaluated using its original expression.

choices.text: Set the maintenance alarm as the ActionsSuppressor, with a WaitPeriod of 120 seconds and an ExtensionPeriod of 0 seconds.
choices.explanation: This does not configure the required two-minute suppression after maintenance ends.

choices.text: Change the incident metric alarm's evaluation period to two minutes and keep the existing notification actions.
choices.explanation: This changes the incident detection interval but does not suppress only notifications based on maintenance state.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Deliver messages without losing those meant for other workers
prompt: A single SQS queue contains a mix of billing and shipping JSON messages. A new billing Lambda must process only billing messages, while shipping events must reach the existing shipping worker without loss. The publisher can be changed to send each message only once to a new SNS topic, and the body’s `type` field will remain. A design in which a poller discards a shipping message it has received is not acceptable. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: LambdaイベントフィルタリングとSQS

learning.reason: To avoid removing nonmatching messages from the shared SQS queue, use SNS body filtering at delivery time and send billing and shipping messages to their respective SQS queues.
learning.concept: An SQS Lambda event source filter deletes events that do not match; it does not retain them for another consumer. When workers need independent processing, separate subscriptions before they receive the messages.

choices.text: Keep sharing the existing SQS queue and configure an event source filter for the billing Lambda so it is invoked only when `type` is billing.
choices.explanation: A shipping message received by the poller does not match the filter and is deleted, so it may never reach the shipping worker.
