choices.text: Publish to one SNS topic and send every message to the same SQS queue without filters. Have each billing and shipping Lambda treat irrelevant events as successfully processed.
choices.explanation: Once either consumer receives a message from the shared queue and succeeds, the other consumer is not guaranteed to receive it.

choices.text: Use separate SNS subscriptions for the billing and shipping SQS queues, set `FilterPolicyScope` to `MessageBody`, and route messages by `type`.
choices.explanation: Messages are routed before a worker receives them, so messages intended for another group are not deleted.

choices.text: Keep sharing the existing SQS queue and configure the billing Lambda’s filter to send nonmatching shipping messages to a DLQ.
choices.explanation: A nonmatch is deleted by event source filtering; it is not an invocation failure and is not sent to a DLQ.

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Move to the organization’s standard management role while preserving application permissions
prompt: The organization manages its EC2 instances with Systems Manager Default Host Management Configuration. The default management role is configured in the target Region, and all instances use IMDSv2 and a compatible version of the SSM Agent. Existing instance profiles contain permissions used by applications, as well as permission for `ssm:UpdateInstanceInformation`. What should be done so the Agent uses the default management role while application permissions are preserved?

source.label: Systems ManagerによるEC2権限の設定

learning.reason: The Agent gives precedence to permissions in the instance profile. Remove the profile’s grant of `ssm:UpdateInstanceInformation` while retaining the permissions the application needs.
learning.concept: IMDSv2 and a compatible Agent are prerequisites. Enabling Default Host Management Configuration alone may not move the Agent from existing profile permissions to the new management role.

choices.text: Keep the application permissions and remove the permission granting `ssm:UpdateInstanceInformation` from the instance profile.
choices.explanation: This removes the condition that causes the instance profile’s management permissions to take precedence, while preserving the application permissions.

choices.text: Add `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` to the current profile so the Agent prefers the default management role.
choices.explanation: The profile still grants `UpdateInstanceInformation`, so the Agent does not switch to the default management role.

choices.text: Remove all instance profiles and wait for the default management role to inherit the existing application permissions automatically.
choices.explanation: The default management role does not inherit existing application permissions.

choices.text: Disable IMDSv2 and revert to IMDSv1 to encourage detection of the default management role.
choices.explanation: IMDSv2 is a prerequisite for using the default management configuration.

sourceLabel: Configuring EC2 permissions for Systems Manager

category: 運用上の優秀性・自動化
title: Track the published version actually used in execution history
prompt: A Standard Step Functions state machine has versions 11 and 12 published, and the production alias is assigned to both. Production clients still call `StartExecution` with the unqualified state machine ARN. Operators want alias-based traffic distribution to apply and want to identify the alias and selected published version for each execution in its history. Which change and expectation are correct?

source.label: Step Functions実行へのバージョンとエイリアスの関連付け

learning.reason: Specify the production alias ARN in `StartExecution`. The version selected by the alias distribution and the alias used are associated with the execution.
learning.concept: An unqualified ARN uses the latest revision. Even if that definition is also included in a published version, a run started without a qualifier is not associated with that version.

choices.text: Continue using the unqualified ARN; naming the alias `prod` will apply traffic distribution to every call.
choices.explanation: Naming an alias does not apply it automatically. The call must use an ARN qualified with the alias.

choices.text: Use the unqualified ARN. If the latest revision matches published version 12, the history will automatically associate the execution with the alias and version 12.
choices.explanation: Even when the latest revision has the same definition as a published version, the execution is not associated with that alias or published version.

choices.text: Specify the ARN for published version 12. The production alias weights will still apply, and both identifiers will be recorded for the execution.
choices.explanation: A version ARN pins the version; alias-based traffic distribution and association do not apply.

choices.text: Specify the ARN qualified with the production alias. The execution will be associated with the alias called and the published version selected by its distribution.
choices.explanation: This uses the production alias distribution and lets operators identify the version actually used for the execution.

sourceLabel: Associating versions and aliases with Step Functions executions

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Preserve a one-off task’s block volume and pass its data to another task
prompt: Run a one-off conversion task on Amazon ECS on EC2. The task creates a block volume from an existing EBS snapshot and writes results to it. Keep the volume for audit purposes after the task stops. Later, provide the same point-in-time data to an independent validation task using the same ECS managed EBS configuration. There is no need to attach the volume while it is in use to multiple tasks. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Use an ECS service to create EBS volumes for its tasks. Set `deleteOnTermination` to false under the service and reassign a used volume to a new task.
choices.explanation: EBS volumes for service-managed tasks are deleted when the task ends. Managed configurations also cannot reconnect an existing EBS volume.

choices.text: Delete EBS when the one-off task stops. Use the container’s writable layer as the source of the same data for the validation task.
choices.explanation: There is no persistent block storage for the stopped task’s changes, so the EBS results needed for validation cannot be preserved.

choices.text: Keep the EBS volume from the one-off task and pass its retained volume ID to the validation task’s managed EBS configuration to attach that same volume.
choices.explanation: The volume can be retained, but managed EBS does not support configuring a direct attachment of an existing volume.

choices.text: Set `deleteOnTermination` to false for the one-off task. After it stops, create a snapshot of the retained EBS volume and create a new EBS volume for the validation task from that snapshot.
choices.explanation: This preserves the original results and lets an independent task start with the same point-in-time data.

source.label: ECSタスクでのEBSボリュームと保持

learning.reason: Set `deleteOnTermination` to false for the one-off task to retain the EBS volume. Create a snapshot of that volume after the task stops, then create a new volume for the validation task.
learning.concept: EBS volumes for ECS service-managed tasks are not retained after termination. ECS managed configurations do not reconnect an existing volume; create a new one from a snapshot.

sourceLabel: EBS volumes and retention for ECS tasks

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Statically assigning shared files to Fargate Pods
prompt: Run all EKS Pods on Fargate. You want to use an existing Regional EFS file system so Pods can read and write the same files even if they move to different Availability Zones. An operator can prepare a PersistentVolume in advance, but you cannot move the nodes to EC2. The application writes through the file system. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Use a StorageClass that specifies the existing EFS file system and dynamically creates all access points for PVCs on Fargate.
choices.explanation: Dynamic persistent volume provisioning is not supported for Fargate Pods.

choices.text: Create a static PersistentVolume that references the existing Regional EFS file system, and mount it in the Pod through a PersistentVolumeClaim.
choices.explanation: A pre-provisioned file system meets the sharing and persistence requirements. Static provisioning can be used with Fargate.

choices.text: Use the EBS CSI driver to provide each Pod with a ReadWriteOnce volume, then have multiple Availability Zones write to the same volume at the same time.
choices.explanation: EBS is Availability Zone-scoped block storage, and EBS volumes are not available to Fargate Pods in this configuration.

choices.text: Increase Fargate ephemeral storage and specify the same mount path for every Pod.
choices.explanation: Using the same path does not share storage across Pods or preserve data when a Pod is replaced.

source.label: EKS Fargateの永続ボリューム

learning.reason: Prepare a static PersistentVolume for the existing Regional EFS file system and assign it to the Pod. Fargate can mount EFS, but it does not support dynamic persistent volume provisioning.
learning.concept: Support for mounting a storage system is separate from the ability to provision storage dynamically when a PVC is created. Check which CSI storage provisioning methods are available with Fargate.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Connecting an apex domain to a regional API's production stage
prompt: Make a Tokyo API Gateway REST API available over IPv4 at example.com, the apex of a Route 53 public hosted zone. An ACM certificate for example.com already exists in Tokyo, and users should receive a URL that does not include a stage name. Do not use API edge optimization or fixed IP addresses. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Associate a Regional custom domain with the production stage, then create a CNAME at the zone apex to the custom domain's Regional target.
choices.explanation: The custom domain mapping is appropriate, but Route 53 does not allow a CNAME at the zone apex.

choices.text: Register the IP address resolved from the API's execute-api endpoint at that time in an A record in the public hosted zone.
choices.explanation: This design pins the managed API's IP address. It also lacks a custom domain and stage mapping, so it does not meet the requirements.

choices.text: Create a Regional custom domain using the certificate in Tokyo, and map an empty base path to the production stage. At the zone apex, configure an A Alias to the Regional target.
choices.explanation: This uses the existing certificate and API mapping, and routes the zone apex to a supported AWS target.

choices.text: Create an edge-optimized domain using the certificate in Tokyo, and create an A Alias to the CloudFront target.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for a Regional API, and edge-optimized domains have a different certificate Region requirement.

source.label: API Gatewayのリージョンカスタムドメイン

learning.reason: Create a Regional custom domain in API Gateway and map an empty base path to the production stage. The Route 53 A Alias at the zone apex points to the Regional target for that custom domain.
learning.concept: The default invoke URL and the DNS target for a custom domain are different. Although a CNAME cannot be used at the zone apex, an Alias can point to a supported AWS target.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Making local decisions during an outage and sending results later
prompt: Factory sensors must continue detecting anomalies on equipment at the site within seconds, even when the internet connection is lost. Results to be sent must be temporarily stored on disk, retained across a restart of the device service, and sent to AWS Kinesis Data Streams when connectivity returns. How should you implement this without adding a custom queue server?

choices.text: Run local detection in a Greengrass component and export a file-persisted stream from the stream manager to Kinesis.
choices.explanation: This enables immediate detection on the device and saves results locally during an outage until they can be exported after connectivity returns.

choices.text: Keep sensors connected to IoT Core at all times, use an IoT rule to send data to Kinesis, and detect anomalies in AWS.
choices.explanation: AWS cannot receive events while connectivity is lost, so this cannot sustain immediate detection at the site.

choices.text: Use only an in-memory Greengrass stream and assume that the data to be retained will remain available after a process restart.
choices.explanation: Local detection can continue, but data held only in memory will not survive a restart.

choices.text: Send data directly from sensors to Kinesis and extend the retention period for data Kinesis has already received.
choices.explanation: This does not store data before it reaches Kinesis or provide local detection while the network is unavailable.

source.label: AWS IoT Greengrassのストリームマネージャー

learning.reason: Run a component on the Greengrass core device to detect anomalies locally and save results in a file-persisted stream. Configure the stream manager to export the stream to Kinesis Data Streams.
learning.concept: Separating local processing from cloud delivery allows detection to continue during an outage. Set retention and storage limits for the stream based on device capacity and expected outage duration.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Validating JWTs from an existing IdP without an additional authorization function
prompt: Implement a simple public HTTP endpoint with Lambda. You want to validate JWTs signed with RS256 by the enterprise's external OIDC provider and require scopes for each route. Do not migrate to Cognito, use API keys per client, or use a custom authorization Lambda. Caching and usage plans are not required. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Configure standard API keys and a usage plan for a REST API, and pass the external JWT as the API key value.
choices.explanation: An API key in a usage plan is not an authorizer that validates a JWT's signature, issuer, or scopes.

choices.text: Configure the enterprise OIDC issuer and audience in an HTTP API JWT authorizer, and configure scopes and a Lambda proxy integration for each route.
choices.explanation: This validates JWTs issued by the external provider in their existing form and applies scopes at the route level.

choices.text: Add a custom Lambda authorizer to a REST API and implement scope validation in it.
choices.explanation: This can implement authorization, but it violates the requirement to avoid a separate authorization function.

choices.text: Configure IAM authorization for a REST API and send the OIDC bearer token as an AWS-signed request without modification.
choices.explanation: Sending an external JWT alone does not make the request an AWS-signed request required for IAM authorization.

source.label: API GatewayのHTTP APIとREST API

learning.reason: Use a Lambda proxy integration with an HTTP API, apply a JWT authorizer configured with the existing issuer to each route, and specify the required scopes on the route.
learning.concept: Check the feature differences between HTTP APIs and REST APIs. Choose the identity issuer and authorizer type independently of the Lambda integration used by the backend.

sourceLabel: API Gateway HTTP APIs and REST APIs

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Diagnose why a record in a parent zone does not resolve
prompt: Private hosted zones for corp.example.com and payments.corp.example.com are associated with the same VPC. The parent zone has an A record for api.payments.corp.example.com, but the child zone has no record with that name. There are no conflicting Resolver rules or caches. What result occurs when the name is queried, and how can the name be resolved while retaining the child zone?

choices.text: The A record in the parent zone is returned. If a record is later added to the child zone, the two responses alternate.
choices.explanation: The more specific child zone is selected first. Responses from the two zones are not combined or alternated.

choices.text: NXDOMAIN is returned only if neither the parent nor child has a record. Re-create the record in the parent zone.
choices.explanation: Resolver does not fall back to the parent zone when a record is absent from the child zone.

choices.text: NXDOMAIN is returned because the child zone has no target record. Create the A record for api in the child zone.
choices.explanation: Placing the record in the selected namespace makes it resolvable from the VPC.

choices.text: There is no response from the child zone, so register an A record with the same name in a public hosted zone.
choices.explanation: When a matching private hosted zone exists, missing records are not forwarded to public DNS for resolution.

source.label: Route 53の重複するプライベートホストゾーン

learning.reason: The more specific child zone is selected. If it lacks the record, the result is NXDOMAIN; therefore, place the target record in the child zone to resolve it.
learning.concept: Resolver does not search parent zones sequentially as alternatives. It selects the namespace of the most specific matching zone.

sourceLabel: Overlapping private hosted zones in Route 53

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Move day-to-day audit operations while retaining the trail
prompt: Audit account A in AWS Organizations created an organization trail that records management events for all members as a CloudTrail delegated administrator. Move day-to-day operations to another audit account, B, without changing access permissions or delivery destinations. An administrator of the organization management account can perform the work. How can the same trail be retained after A is deregistered?

choices.text: Have audit account B create an IAM role with administrator permissions and take over the trail without changing the CloudTrail organization delegation.
choices.explanation: IAM permissions within an account alone do not make it a CloudTrail delegated administrator for the organization.

choices.text: Have the management account register B as a CloudTrail delegated administrator and deregister A. Manage the organization trail using the same identifier.
choices.explanation: Deregistering a delegated administrator does not change ownership of, or delete, an existing organization trail.

choices.text: Before A is deregistered, transfer ownership of the organization trail to B and replace its ARN.
choices.explanation: The management account owns the organization trail; no operation is needed to transfer ownership from the creating delegated administrator to another delegated administrator.

choices.text: Create a new organization trail for B, deregister A, and switch over on the assumption that A's trail will disappear.
choices.explanation: Deregistering A does not automatically delete the trail. Re-creating it cannot retain the same trail identifier.

source.label: CloudTrailの組織委任管理者と所有権

learning.reason: The management account registers B as the CloudTrail delegated administrator and deregisters A. Because the management account always owns the organization trail, the trail remains after the delegation for its creator, A, is removed.
learning.concept: Operational delegation and resource ownership are distinct for CloudTrail organization trails. Moving organization delegation does not require re-creating the trail.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Enable the target account for the STS Region as well
prompt: A service already runs in an opt-in Region for account A. It will AssumeRole into an IAM role in account B, and credential acquisition must be limited to STS in that Region. The required IAM policies are configured, but B has not yet enabled that Region. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Because only account A has opted in, simply use a Regional endpoint in the SDK.
choices.explanation: Target account B must also be able to use STS operations in that Region.

choices.text: Opt in B, but continue using the global STS endpoint in the SDK.
choices.explanation: Enabling the target account alone does not fix the request destination to the specified Region's STS endpoint.

choices.text: Create a new IAM role with the same name in B so STS can be used in that Region without enabling the Region.
choices.explanation: Re-creating the role does not enable the Region.

choices.text: Enable the Region in B as well, and configure the SDK's AssumeRole destination as the STS endpoint for that Region.
choices.explanation: This satisfies both the target-account prerequisite and the required destination for credential requests.

source.label: リージョンごとのAWS STSの管理

learning.reason: Use the STS endpoint for the relevant Region from the SDK, and enable the opt-in Region in B, which owns the target role. For manually enabled Regions, the target account must also be able to use STS in that Region.
learning.concept: Distinguish the STS request destination from the account that owns the temporary credentials generated by AssumeRole. This is not an operation to re-create the IAM role in a Region.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Update the trusted SAML signing key using the same provider ARN
prompt: An external IdP will update its signing key for SAML assertions to AWS on the company's planned schedule. Authorized IdP metadata containing the new signing certificate has been distributed. The IdP entity ID and attribute contract are unchanged, and trust policies for many IAM roles reference the same SAML provider ARN. Which approach aligns with the signing transition without updating the roles' trust policies?

choices.text: Replace the metadata for the existing SAML provider by using UpdateSAMLProvider, coordinating it with the signing transition on the IdP side.
choices.explanation: This updates the trusted public information for the same provider.

choices.text: Create a separate SAML provider with a new name and assume that existing roles automatically select the new ARN based on the same IdP entity ID.
choices.explanation: The roles' trust policies reference the existing provider ARN and do not automatically switch to a new ARN.

choices.text: Leave the SAML provider unchanged and add the fingerprint of the new signing certificate to conditions in each role trust policy.
choices.explanation: Role conditions alone cannot update the IdP public information used to validate SAML assertion signatures.

choices.text: Only add an IAM-side private key used to decrypt encrypted SAML assertions, assuming that the new IdP signing certificate will then be trusted.
choices.explanation: A key for decrypting received assertions and a public certificate for validating IdP signatures serve different purposes.

source.label: IAMのSAML IDプロバイダー管理

learning.reason: Update the existing IAM SAML provider with the new metadata. Coordinate the order with the IdP signing change and confirm that new assertions are accepted by AWS.
learning.concept: Update the IdP's public signing information in SAML metadata. Because the provider ARN is retained, each referencing role does not need to be changed to a new ARN.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Enforce a seven-day maximum at the issuing CA and distribute short-lived TLS certificates
prompt: An internal mesh issues certificates with a five-day validity period every day. The team wants the CA’s mode—not client-side input validation—to enforce that issuance fails if an operator mistakenly requests a validity period of eight days or more. Issuance can be automated in-house, and ACM-managed certificates are not required. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a general-purpose CA and specify five days in the Private CA API, assuming the CA will automatically reject any issuance request for eight days or more.
choices.explanation: The short-lived mode’s limit does not apply to a general-purpose CA. Simply requesting five days does not enforce the limit through the CA’s mode.

choices.text: Create a short-lived mode CA and obtain certificates through ACM-managed issuance.
choices.explanation: ACM cannot issue certificates from a short-lived mode CA.

choices.text: Set up a short-lived mode Private CA and issue five-day certificates through the Private CA issuance API.
choices.explanation: This mode can issue the required five-day certificates and rejects validity periods above its seven-day limit.

choices.text: Set the CRL update interval to seven days on a general-purpose CA and assume the same period will apply to issued certificates.
choices.explanation: A CRL schedule does not limit the validity period of individual certificates.

source.label: AWS Private CAの短命証明書モード

learning.reason: A CA in short-lived certificate mode is limited to issuing certificates with a validity period of seven days or less. Issue five-day certificates through the Private CA issuance API.
learning.concept: A general-purpose CA can also issue short-lived certificates, but its mode does not enforce a seven-day maximum. ACM cannot issue ACM-managed certificates from a short-lived mode CA.

sourceLabel: AWS Private CA short-lived certificate mode

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Replace an external CA certificate without changing the ALB reference
prompt: An ALB references the ARN of an RSA 2048-bit certificate issued by an external CA and imported into ACM. The external CA has provided the next certificate under the same usage conditions and with the same key type and size, along with the matching private key and certificate chain. How can the certificate be renewed before it expires without editing the ALB listener?

choices.text: Import the new certificate for the first time without specifying an ARN, then wait for the ALB to switch automatically to the new ARN based on the shared domain name.
choices.explanation: This creates a new ARN. A matching domain name alone does not change the association with the existing ALB.

choices.text: Specify the existing certificate ARN and reimport the new certificate, matching private key, and certificate chain into ACM.
choices.explanation: Reimporting updates the existing ARN, so the association with the ALB that uses that ARN can be maintained.

choices.text: Keep the common name and create an ACM validation record in public DNS so ACM automatically renews the imported external certificate.
choices.explanation: A DNS record does not make an imported external CA certificate eligible for ACM managed renewal.

choices.text: Prepare a new certificate with an elliptic-curve key and reimport it under the same ARN to replace the RSA key.
choices.explanation: Reimporting cannot change the key type or size.

source.label: ACMの証明書再インポート

learning.reason: Reimport the new certificate, matching private key, and required chain by specifying the existing certificate ARN. The ARN and its association with AWS services are maintained.
learning.concept: Imported certificates are not eligible for ACM managed renewal. Reimporting under the same ARN is subject to restrictions, including the key type and size.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Protect an owned bucket from external IAM principals across an OU
prompt: An S3 bucket owned by a business OU in AWS Organizations has a bucket policy managed by a member account. Even if someone mistakenly grants access directly to an IAM role in an external account, the organization wants to deny that role’s GetObject access across the entire OU. The external account is not part of the organization, and the organization does not want to change each bucket individually. Assume that required service delivery is permitted separately. Which control is appropriate?

choices.text: Restrict s3:GetObject with an SCP on the business OU, assuming the same SCP applies to IAM principals in external accounts.
choices.explanation: Principals in external accounts are not subject to the business OU’s SCP.

choices.text: Apply a tag policy to the business OU that defines permitted bucket tags, and use tag presence to deny reads by the external role.
choices.explanation: Tag policies standardize tags. A tag policy alone does not deny access to GetObject.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to detect buckets with external grants and notify the responsible team.
choices.explanation: This can detect the grants, but it does not deny access before external access to the resource is permitted.

choices.text: Apply an RCP to the business OU and deny S3 object reads by the specified external IAM principals.
choices.explanation: An applicable RCP deny stops access even when the target bucket’s resource policy allows it.

source.label: AWS Organizationsのリソースコントロールポリシー

learning.reason: Apply an RCP to the OU that owns the target S3 resources and deny reads by external IAM principals that meet the conditions. A deny takes precedence over an allow in an individual resource policy.
learning.concept: An RCP sets an upper bound on permissions to access resources in scope. An SCP controls permissions for principals on the organization-member side and does not impose the same limit on external IAM principals.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Decrypt the same ciphertext while separating permissions by Region
prompt: Related multi-Region keys using key material generated by AWS KMS were created in Tokyo and the disaster recovery Region. Testing confirms that ciphertext created in Tokyo can be decrypted in the disaster recovery Region. However, only the local recovery role should be permitted to use the disaster recovery key; the Tokyo application role must not be allowed. How should you assess the effect of changing grants or key policies in Tokyo?

choices.text: Configure the key policy and grants individually on the disaster recovery key. Changes to grants or the key policy in Tokyo are not synchronized automatically.
choices.explanation: This preserves the shared-key-material behavior while allowing permissions to be separated by Region.

choices.text: Set the key policy in Tokyo and rely on it to synchronize automatically to every replica, then add a grant on the disaster recovery key to exclude the Tokyo role.
choices.explanation: Key policies are not synchronized automatically. Grants authorize access; they do not turn an allow in another policy into a deny.

choices.text: Create a grant for the recovery role in Tokyo so it can decrypt with every replica that has the same key ID.
choices.explanation: Related keys have different ARNs, and one grant does not apply to every key.

choices.text: Replace the related disaster recovery key with a regular single-Region key to separate authorization, while still decrypting Tokyo ciphertext as is.
choices.explanation: An unrelated key does not share the key material, so this does not satisfy the assumption that the copied ciphertext can be decrypted as is.

source.label: KMSマルチリージョンキーのアクセス制御

learning.reason: Related keys share key material. Authorization is independent for each key, so configure the disaster recovery key’s policy or grants to authorize the recovery role as appropriate.
learning.concept: Synchronizing multi-Region key material does not synchronize authorization data. A grant applies to the KMS key for which it was created.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Allow only management sessions whose activity can be recorded
prompt: Operators use Session Manager to maintain EC2 instances, and the input and output of every interactive session must be collected in CloudWatch Logs. The administrator’s interactive actions must be auditable, not just network activity. If connections must be restricted to those that meet the audit requirement, which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Store management events, including StartSession, in CloudTrail and rely on CloudTrail alone to retain session terminal output.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail’s API auditing captures management actions such as starting a session, but not shell terminal output.

choices.text: Add a CloudWatch Logs destination to the Session Manager settings and assume that this necessarily records the input and output of every permitted session type.
choices.explanation: Unless session types are restricted to those that can be recorded, some sessions may have auditable start events but no recorded terminal input or output.

choices.text: Configure the logging permissions and destination, and use IAM to allow only interactive sessions over recordable standard streams.
choices.explanation: This combines the logging configuration with enforcement of a session type that can be audited.

choices.text: Record connection traffic with VPC Flow Logs and use the stored network logs to inspect shell input and output.
choices.explanation: Flow Logs store network metadata; they do not record terminal activity.

source.label: Session Managerのセッションログ

learning.reason: Enable session logging to CloudWatch Logs and configure the permissions it requires. Limit the IAM permissions for audited users to session types that use recordable standard streams.
learning.concept: CloudTrail management events show API operations such as starting a session. To capture session input and output, configure a session type that Session Manager can record.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Converge connections that remain in the old Region after a DNS switch
prompt: A service with WebSocket clients runs in two Regions behind Route 53 failover records. New DNS queries already return the DR side, but some established connections on the old side continue running and do not perform name resolution again. If the clients and the application on the old side can be changed in a planned manner, which approach can reduce this mismatch?

choices.text: Only shorten the Route 53 DNS TTL. Assume that existing WebSockets will move to the new address as soon as the TTL expires.
choices.explanation: The TTL controls DNS caching. An established WebSocket does not move just because DNS is updated.

choices.text: Increase the frequency of WebSocket heartbeats on the client and keep the same TCP connection alive.
choices.explanation: This can monitor an existing connection, but it does not trigger a new DNS lookup or reconnect to the DR side.

choices.text: Terminate connections in the old-side application, then have clients reuse the old-side IP address recorded during the initial connection.
choices.explanation: Even after reconnecting, pinning the old-side IP bypasses DNS, which now returns the DR side.

choices.text: During a planned switch, terminate old-side connections after a defined period. On reconnect, have clients use the hostname and refresh the result in accordance with DNS cache expiration.
choices.explanation: This accounts for both the lifetime of network connections and the DNS switch.

source.label: Route 53 DNSとクライアントキャッシュの復旧設計

learning.reason: DNS changes the result of new name lookups. Design application behavior to terminate established WebSockets after a defined lifetime and to resolve DNS again when reconnecting.
learning.concept: DNS cache duration and TCP connection lifetime are independent. Account for any remaining DNS cache time during reconnection.

sourceLabel: Route 53 DNS and client-cache recovery design

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Inspect data in the same file system before restoring it to the shared volume
prompt: Some files were accidentally deleted from a production Amazon FSx for OpenZFS volume. Other valid updates have been made since the deletion, so the entire production volume cannot be rolled back to an earlier point in time. The latest snapshot is available and can be retained during testing. Which approach lets you inspect the affected files on another writable volume and restore only the files you need without making a full copy at the outset?

choices.text: Create a clone volume from the snapshot, inspect its contents at a separate validation path, and then copy only the required files to production.
choices.explanation: This allows inspection without rolling back the entire current production volume or making a full copy.

choices.text: Immediately restore the production volume from the snapshot and check at the current path whether the required data is present.
choices.explanation: This would also affect valid writes accepted after the deletion.

choices.text: Restore the latest snapshot as a full copy, but assume that no full data copy occurs because only a separate volume is created.
choices.explanation: A full copy creates a complete replica that does not depend on the source snapshot.

choices.text: Change the production volume to read-only and expose its current state through a separate mount.
choices.explanation: Files that are already missing cannot be inspected by mounting the current state again.

source.label: FSx for OpenZFSのクローンとフルコピー

learning.reason: Create a clone in the same file system from the latest snapshot. It shares the initial data while providing an independent writable area, so you can restore only the files you have verified.
learning.concept: A clone depends on its source snapshot. Choose between a clone that shares the initial blocks and a full copy that duplicates all data to create an independent volume.

sourceLabel: FSx for OpenZFS clones and full copies

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Test replica promotion across multiple shards with a managed operation
prompt: An ElastiCache for Valkey cluster-mode enabled test environment has 18 shards, each with a replica in a different Availability Zone. The application uses the configuration endpoint. You want to test managed promotion one shard at a time and measure client recovery, without substituting a restore from backup. Which plan is appropriate?

choices.text: Run TestFailover on all 18 shards in sequence within the same rolling 24-hour period.
choices.explanation: Even when run sequentially, there is a limit on how many shards can be tested in a rolling 24-hour period.

choices.text: Run TestFailover for each selected shard and check events and reconnections. Split the tests across time windows so that no more than 15 shards are tested in any rolling 24-hour period.
choices.explanation: This tests managed promotion for each shard while observing the usage limit.

choices.text: Restore a separate cluster from a snapshot of each shard and assume that clients of the original cluster will automatically switch to the new cluster nodes.
choices.explanation: Restoring a separate cluster does not test replica promotion and reconnection in the same cluster.

choices.text: Remove all replicas from each target shard before running TestFailover, then verify that the primary is promoted to a replica in another Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: Without a replica to promote, the condition of failing over to an existing replica in another Availability Zone is not met.

source.label: ElastiCacheのMulti-AZとテストフェイルオーバー

learning.reason: Run TestFailover on each target shard and verify promotion and reconnection. Divide the tests across time windows to stay within the limit of 15 shards in any rolling 24-hour period.
learning.concept: TestFailover exercises a managed failover for a selected shard. This differs from testing by restoring a backup or manually changing the fixed node to which an application connects.

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Start downstream processing when archived objects become available
prompt: Temporarily restore a specified subset of millions of objects in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, using S3 Inventory to define the scope. The application must start processing each object only after it becomes available for retrieval. You do not want to enqueue objects merely because restore requests were submitted. Which configuration is appropriate if individual restore requests must not be submitted manually?

choices.text: Create a restore job using a manifest, then start GetObject for all targets when the batch completion report is generated.
choices.explanation: The batch completion report does not wait until all the actual data is available.

choices.text: Create a restore job and start reading the target objects when receiving ObjectRestore:Post events.
choices.explanation: Post signals that a restore request has started; it does not mean the object is available from the archive.

choices.text: Start a Batch Operations restore from a manifest. Trigger retrieval processing for each object on ObjectRestore:Completed.
choices.explanation: This submits many restore requests together and lets downstream processing run as each individual restore completes.

choices.text: When the S3 Inventory report is updated, assume that all targets in restore jobs created before that time are available.
choices.explanation: The time an inventory report is generated does not indicate that each object's restore has completed.

source.label: S3 Batch Operationsでのアーカイブ復元

learning.reason: Start the requests with a Batch Operations restore job that uses a manifest. Begin application processing when an ObjectRestore:Completed event arrives for each object.
learning.concept: Completion of a restore job records the result of starting restore requests for the target objects. The actual data becomes available for retrieval when each object's restore completes.

sourceLabel: Archived-object restoration with S3 Batch Operations

category: レジリエンス・移行・事業継続
title: Restore an S3 backup copied to another Region
prompt: An S3 bucket in Tokyo is protected with AWS Backup, and its recovery point has been copied to Osaka. For a disaster-recovery exercise in which you cannot operate in Tokyo, you want to restore only four specified objects using the copy in Osaka. The original objects are encrypted with a customer managed KMS key in Tokyo, and ACLs are not included in the backup. SSE-S3 is allowed at the restore destination. Which two actions should you take?

source.label: AWS BackupのS3復元とクロスリージョンコピー

learning.reason: Restore selected items from the Osaka copy to a versioning-enabled bucket in Osaka. Choose SSE-S3 instead of reusing the original key.
learning.concept: An AWS Backup S3 restore job runs in the Region containing the recovery point used. Restoring from a cross-Region copy requires specifying a different encryption method from the original.

choices.text: Use the Tokyo bucket as the restore destination and restore the objects directly from the Osaka copy to Tokyo in another Region.
choices.explanation: An S3 restore must be performed in the Region where the original recovery point or its copy exists.

choices.text: Select the Osaka copy and restore the four objects at item level to a versioning-enabled bucket in Osaka.
choices.explanation: You can select the specified number of S3 objects and restore them in the same Region as the copy.

choices.text: Select the original encryption method and specify the original KMS key used in Tokyo.
choices.explanation: You cannot use the original encryption method when restoring an S3 recovery point copied from another Region.

choices.text: Disable versioning on the Osaka restore destination and register each restored object as the latest version, one at a time.
choices.explanation: The S3 restore destination must have versioning enabled.

choices.text: Specify the permitted SSE-S3 encryption method for the objects being restored.
choices.explanation: For a restore from a copy, you can use a different permitted encryption method instead of specifying the same one used by the copy.

sourceLabel: S3 restores and cross-Region copies with AWS Backup

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Search multiple domains in one request without moving stored data
prompt: The audit domain and production log domain for Amazon OpenSearch Service are in different Regions. Without persistently storing a full copy of the indexes in another Region, auditors must be able to use one domain as the entry point and include both local and remote indexes in a single search request. Both are existing domains that meet the requirements for cross-cluster search. Which configuration is appropriate?

source.label: OpenSearch Serviceのクロスクラスター検索

learning.reason: Request a cross-cluster connection from the entry-point domain to the search domain and approve it in the destination domain. Configure the required domains and fine-grained access permissions, then refer to the search domain with a connection alias.
learning.concept: Cross-cluster search retrieves results at query time. Its purpose differs from replication, which creates persistent follower indexes.

choices.text: Start cross-cluster replication for the production indexes and maintain follower indexes on the audit side.
choices.explanation: This makes the indexes searchable locally from the audit side, but it persistently stores a copy, which does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Configure the same DNS name in front of both domains and have DNS forward a single search request to both domains.
choices.explanation: DNS only resolves names. It does not fan out a search to both domains and combine the results.

choices.text: Create a cross-cluster connection from the audit domain to the production domain, then search permitted indexes as local indexes and remote indexes using a connection alias.
choices.explanation: This lets one search include indexes from both domains while leaving each index in its original location.

choices.text: For every audit, restore a snapshot of the production domain to the audit domain and add it to the local indexes.
choices.explanation: This creates a copy on the audit side at that point in time, rather than searching indexes in place.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Identify PrivateLink clients by endpoint despite overlapping CIDRs
prompt: Several customers connect over TCP to a PrivateLink endpoint service that uses an NLB. Their IP addresses may overlap. On the backend, you must correlate each connection's original IP address with the VPC endpoint it used, while continuing to use ordinary health checks. The backend accepts connections only from the trusted NLB. Which change is appropriate?

source.label: NLBのProxy Protocol v2とPrivateLink

learning.reason: Enable Proxy Protocol v2 on the NLB target group. The backend can obtain the original connection information and VPC endpoint ID from the header, and must also handle health-check headers that lack client information.
learning.concept: For PrivateLink traffic, the source address on the socket is normally the NLB's address. Distinguish preserving the source IP from the connection metadata forwarded by the load balancer.

choices.text: Enable client IP preservation only, then infer the endpoint ID from the socket source address seen by the target.
choices.explanation: For traffic from PrivateLink, client IP preservation alone does not provide the original IP, and the socket IP does not identify the endpoint.

choices.text: Enable Proxy Protocol v2 on the target group. Parse the original connection information and VPC endpoint ID supplied by the NLB, and handle the header on health checks as well.
choices.explanation: This identifies the endpoint for different clients in addition to providing the source IP. Account for the fact that health checks do not contain ordinary client connection information.

choices.text: Have the NLB send HTTP X-Forwarded-For to the TCP targets and assume the NLB adds the endpoint ID to the header.
choices.explanation: NLB TCP forwarding does not add source connection information or the endpoint ID to HTTP headers.

choices.text: Enable per-endpoint acceptance for the service and determine the VPC endpoint ID for each TCP connection from its acceptance status alone.
choices.explanation: Acceptance controls which endpoints may connect. It does not reveal which accepted endpoint made an individual TCP connection.

sourceLabel: NLB Proxy Protocol v2 and PrivateLink

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Keep the default names for public and private APIs from the same VPC
prompt: Applications in one VPC use the default execute-api names for both an existing API Gateway public REST API and a private REST API. The public API is owned by another company, which cannot change it to use a custom domain, and the VPC already has a public internet path. The private API must continue to use the currently authorized interface endpoint. Which configuration lets clients keep using the APIs' default names?

source.label: API Gatewayの公開・非公開既定エンドポイントの両立

learning.reason: With broad private DNS disabled on the interface endpoint, use a Route 53 private hosted zone to direct only the target private API's default name to that endpoint.
learning.concept: Private DNS for execute-api makes default names resolve to the VPC endpoint, including names for public APIs. Narrowing DNS resolution to only the target API lets the public API use the existing public path.

choices.text: Keep private DNS enabled on the interface endpoint and also call the public API's default DNS name through the endpoint.
choices.explanation: The default execute-api names resolve to the VPC endpoint. The public API's default endpoint cannot be called through that path.

choices.text: Disable private DNS on the interface endpoint, create no other records, and assume the two default names will resolve appropriately on their own.
choices.explanation: Without another record, the private API's default name has no DNS mapping to the designated VPC endpoint.

choices.text: Create a private hosted zone for all of execute-api and direct both the public and private APIs to the same interface endpoint.
choices.explanation: This also sends the public API's default name over the private path, so the original DNS conflict remains.

choices.text: Disable private DNS on the interface endpoint, then create a Route 53 private hosted zone for only the private API's default name, with a record pointing to the existing endpoint.
choices.explanation: The private API name resolves to the existing endpoint, while the public API name uses normal public DNS and the existing public path.

sourceLabel: Coexistence of API Gateway public and private default endpoints

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Free up space on a compute file system while keeping file paths
prompt: FSx for Lustre is linked to S3. Large files used for analytics have been exported to S3, and there have been no changes since export. You want to free the FSx data blocks for the next workload while preserving the existing paths and POSIX metadata, so that the files can be read again from their original paths when needed. Which operation is appropriate?

source.label: FSx for Lustreのデータリポジトリタスク

learning.reason: A release task for files already exported to S3 frees their local contents while preserving metadata. When a file is read again, FSx retrieves its contents from S3.
learning.concept: Export stores data in S3; release frees the local contents of linked files. Release does not delete the file names.

choices.text: Run a data repository release task for the exported files at the target paths.
choices.explanation: The files can still be read from the same paths after their data blocks are released, and their contents can be retrieved transparently from S3.

choices.text: Delete the target files in FSx and assume they will be restored automatically when the application next opens the same file paths.
choices.explanation: Deleting files removes their names and metadata. It does not leave the files in a state where their contents can be retrieved from the same paths, as release does.

choices.text: Run only another export task for the target files, then wait for the local blocks of successfully exported files to disappear.
choices.explanation: An export task writes files to S3; a separate operation is needed to release their local blocks.

choices.text: Move the linked S3 objects to Glacier Deep Archive and assume that this will automatically reduce the local FSx data.
choices.explanation: Changing the S3 storage class does not instruct FSx to release its contents. Retrieving archived objects also requires a separate restore.

sourceLabel: FSx for Lustre data repository tasks

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Provide private database TCP connectivity to multiple VPCs
prompt: Multiple business VPCs in the same Region are attached to a shared VPC Lattice service network. They need direct connections to an existing database in another VPC over the database's TCP protocol, from the business VPCs that are authorized to connect. You must avoid peering the database VPC with every business VPC and avoid adding a dedicated load balancer. Select two provider-side configurations that are required.

source.label: Amazon VPC Lattice — リソース設定

learning.reason: The resource gateway provides a path to the database, and associating the resource configuration with the service network makes it available to existing client VPCs.
learning.concept: VPC Lattice resource configurations share TCP resources through a service network. On the provider side, also allow connections from the resource gateway to the database.

choices.text: Create a Lattice service with an HTTP listener and the database as an IP target.
choices.explanation: An HTTP listener is not suitable for relaying the database's native TCP protocol as is.

choices.text: Create a resource gateway in the provider VPC that can reach the database.
choices.explanation: The resource gateway provides an entry point from the service network to the target resource in the provider VPC.

choices.text: Recreate only the existing associations between the service network and each consumer VPC, without specifying the provider resource.
choices.explanation: The VPC associations already exist. This does not define the resource to share or the provider-side gateway.

choices.text: Register the database endpoint and TCP port in a resource configuration, then associate that configuration with the existing service network.
choices.explanation: This adds the database as a destination on the service network so consumers can reach it through that network.

choices.text: Add an NLB target group and operate a separate PrivateLink endpoint service instead of using the existing service network.
choices.explanation: This could be a valid alternative connectivity method, but it requires adding a dedicated load balancer and does not use the existing service network.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Transform a legacy backend response with an API Gateway REST API
prompt: An immutable HTTP service behind an API Gateway REST API returns HTTP 422 with an internal JSON format for invalid input. The existing client contract requires HTTP 400 and a specified JSON format, while HTTP 200 must be preserved for successful requests. Which configuration lets API Gateway transform the response without adding compute resources?

source.label: Amazon API Gateway — REST APIのHTTP統合

learning.reason: With a non-proxy HTTP integration, you can select an integration response for backend HTTP 422 and map its body to the 400 method response.
learning.concept: Method responses define the client contract. Integration responses map backend status codes and bodies to that contract.

choices.text: Keep an HTTP proxy integration, then add a 400 method response and a response mapping template.
choices.explanation: A proxy integration passes the backend response through. It does not let API Gateway select an integration response and rewrite the body.

choices.text: Switch to a non-proxy HTTP integration and use only an integration request template that runs before the backend call.
choices.explanation: An integration request transforms the input sent to the backend. It does not map the returned status code and body.

choices.text: Use a non-proxy HTTP integration and define an integration response that matches HTTP 422. Map it to the 400 method response and transform the JSON with a response template.
choices.explanation: This lets API Gateway transform only the 422 response to the required contract, while preserving a separate mapping for successful responses.

choices.text: Use a non-proxy HTTP integration, define only 400 and 200 method responses, and route every integration response through the same default mapping.
choices.explanation: Defining a 400 method response alone does not add a rule to select 422 and transform its status and body.

sourceLabel: Amazon API Gateway — REST API HTTP integrations

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Append to an Existing S3 Express Object While Reads Continue
prompt: Multiple video-processing workers append processed data to the same object in a directory bucket in S3 Express One Zone. Readers periodically read the content already stored under the same key. Each worker must detect when an append based on a stale size has failed, then obtain the new end position and retry only after confirming a size conflict. Which operation does this without downloading the existing content?

source.label: Amazon S3 — PutObjectの書き込みオフセット

learning.reason: Setting WriteOffsetBytes to the object's current size appends data to the end. If the size does not match, S3 returns InvalidWriteOffset.
learning.concept: The end position is expressed as the current number of bytes. An explicit size mismatch is different from a communication failure with an unknown outcome. Unconditionally resending the same content after the latter can create duplicates.

choices.text: Specify the original object's ETag in If-Match, omit the offset, and use PutObject to write only the new portion.
choices.explanation: Adding an ETag condition does not change the fact that a regular PutObject without an offset replaces the object with only the new portion.

choices.text: Get the current size and specify it as the write offset when using PutObject to write only the new portion. If the request fails with InvalidWriteOffset, check the size again.
choices.explanation: The new data is appended to the existing content only when the specified offset matches the current size. The response identifies the conflict.

choices.text: Assign multipart upload part numbers for the key independently across all workers, and expose parts that have not been completed as the end of the existing object.
choices.explanation: Parts from an incomplete upload are not included in reads of the existing object. Completing an upload is different from appending to an existing key.

choices.text: Specify If-None-Match when using PutObject to write the new portion to the existing key, and resend it at the same offset if the request fails.
choices.explanation: The If-None-Match asterisk condition applies when the key does not yet exist; it is not a condition for appending to an existing key.

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Wait Only for Your Own Update on a Secondary Connection
prompt: An application runs in the secondary Region of an Aurora MySQL Global Database. The application must keep its connection in that Region, while supported update SQL statements execute on the primary. A SELECT immediately afterward in the same session must reflect the application's own update. Avoid a setting that waits for commits from other sessions to be reflected. Which setting should you choose for a supported version?

source.label: Amazon Aurora — Aurora MySQLのグローバル書き込み転送

learning.reason: Use write forwarding from the secondary and set consistency to SESSION. This waits until updates forwarded from that session can be read.
learning.concept: The write destination and the replica consistency needed for subsequent reads are controlled by separate settings.

choices.text: Enable global write forwarding in the secondary and set the read consistency to EVENTUAL.
choices.explanation: Writes are forwarded, but SELECT does not wait for the same session's update to be reflected.

choices.text: Enable global write forwarding in the secondary and set the read consistency to GLOBAL.
choices.explanation: Your own update is visible, but SELECT may also wait for all commits to the primary up to the time the query starts, which is stronger consistency than required.

choices.text: Disable global write forwarding in the secondary and set the read consistency to SESSION.
choices.explanation: The consistency parameter alone does not forward writes to the primary.

choices.text: Enable global write forwarding in the secondary and set the read consistency to SESSION.
choices.explanation: Writes are handled by the primary, while the setting waits for updates from the same session. It does not require waiting for all updates committed by other sessions to be reflected.

sourceLabel: Amazon Aurora — Aurora MySQL global write forwarding

category: クラウドアーキテクチャ
title: Retrieve Only Orders Needing Review by Fulfillment Center
prompt: A DynamoDB orders table uses the order ID as its partition key. For each fulfillment center, retrieve only orders that need additional review, in creation-time order, and display the order ID and total amount. These orders account for only a few percent of all orders, and whether an order needs review is determined by an application state change. Eventual consistency is sufficient. Which design leaves the table's key unchanged and reduces index entries and reads for orders outside the target set?

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — スパースインデックス

learning.reason: A GSI using a key attribute that is present only while an order needs review lets you Query only the target orders for a fulfillment center. Project the total amount into the index.
learning.concept: A GSI omits items without its key attributes. The table's keys are projected automatically, and you can choose additional attributes needed for the listing.

choices.text: Give only orders needing review an index key that identifies the fulfillment center, and create a GSI with that key and the creation time. Project the total amount into the index. Remove the index key when review is complete.
choices.explanation: Only the target orders appear in the GSI, allowing a time-ordered Query for a fulfillment center. The table's order ID can also be included in the results.

choices.text: Create a GSI with the regular fulfillment-center attribute and creation time, register every order in it, and use a filter at Query time to exclude orders by state.
choices.explanation: This can retrieve the list, but it retains index entries for orders outside the target set and reads items before the filter excludes them.

choices.text: Use a local secondary index that keeps order ID as its partition key, and set the fulfillment center as the sort-key condition to Query all orders for a center in one request.
choices.explanation: A local secondary index uses the same partition key as the base table. It cannot group orders with different IDs by fulfillment center in one Query.

choices.text: Use a table Scan with creation time and state specified in ProjectionExpression, and return only orders needing review.
choices.explanation: ProjectionExpression selects which attributes to return. It does not filter items by fulfillment center or state before the Scan reads them.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Distinguish Control Plane API Data Encryption from Node Encryption
prompt: For an EKS cluster running Kubernetes 1.28 or later, audit rules require envelope encryption of ConfigMaps as well as Secrets with a customer-managed KMS key. Node and persistent-volume storage encryption is managed under a separate standard. Which configuration and scope are correct for a new cluster?

source.label: EKSでの全Kubernetes APIデータの暗号化

learning.reason: Specify a customer-managed KMS key in the cluster encryption configuration. This EKS version encrypts API data, including Secrets and ConfigMaps, but that setting does not cover node EBS volumes.
learning.concept: Distinguish the default KMS key for EKS from a customer-managed key that meets customer ownership and audit requirements. Writes to control-plane etcd and workload storage are protected at different layers.

choices.text: Change only the default EBS encryption key to your own key; the same key will then also apply to Secrets and ConfigMaps.
choices.explanation: The EBS setting alone cannot specify the KMS key used by the EKS-managed control plane.

choices.text: Specify a customer-managed key in the cluster's encryption configuration. This covers Kubernetes API data; configure node-side disk encryption separately.
choices.explanation: This meets the audit requirement for key ownership while keeping control-plane and node encryption separate.

choices.text: Omit the encryption configuration and manage the default AWS-owned key with your own key policy.
choices.explanation: An AWS-owned key is not a customer-managed key, and you do not manage its key policy.

choices.text: Specify a KMS key, then add only configmaps to resources to explicitly override the default encryption scope.
choices.explanation: For this version, the Kubernetes API data covered is not selected through resources. This setting also cannot select only ConfigMaps.

sourceLabel: Encrypting all Kubernetes API data in EKS

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Preserve an investigated version after its retention period ends
prompt: An S3 bucket has Object Lock enabled, and one version of an object under audit already has a time-based retention period. The investigation has no set end date, and that version must not be deletable after its retention period expires. New versions of the same key should still be allowed as usual. Which setting is appropriate?

source.label: S3 Object Lockのリーガルホールド

learning.reason: Place a legal hold on the target version. Even after its existing retention period expires, the version remains protected until an authorized person removes the hold.
learning.concept: Time-based retention and legal holds are independent. Object Lock protects the target version; it does not categorically prevent creating another version under the same key.

choices.text: Extend only the retention period to a provisional investigation end date, and do not revisit the date even if the investigation continues.
choices.explanation: Because the end date is unknown, this cannot ensure protection after the provisional date passes.

choices.text: Extend only the bucket's default retention period and assume this automatically extends protection for the existing target version.
choices.explanation: Changing the default retention period does not revise the retention specified for each existing version.

choices.text: Deny all PutObject requests for the target key and assume this also prevents deletion of the specific version that already exists.
choices.explanation: This prevents new versions from being added. Denying write permissions alone does not control deletion of the target version.

choices.text: Place a legal hold on the target object version, then have an authorized person remove it after the investigation ends.
choices.explanation: This preserves the older version regardless of how long the investigation takes, while allowing other versions to be added.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Deliver multiple restricted files without changing their URLs
prompt: A company delivers videos to subscribers through CloudFront. IPv6 is disabled for this distribution. A single authorization must allow access to multiple files under a subscriber prefix in the same distribution, without adding signature information to each URL in the player. Access must expire, and the allowed IPv4 range must be restricted. The origin is protected separately. Which approach authorizes viewers through CloudFront?

source.label: CloudFrontのカスタムポリシー付き署名付きCookie

learning.reason: Issue signed cookies with a custom policy that specifies the resource scope, expiration, and IPv4 condition. Use a trusted key group on the applicable cache behavior to validate the signatures.
learning.concept: Signed cookies can control access to multiple files while keeping their existing URLs. A custom policy can specify a resource scope and IP condition. OAC protects access to the origin, which is a different direction of access control.

choices.text: Issue a signed URL for each file and require the player to include the signature query string in every request.
choices.explanation: This protects the files but violates the requirement to avoid adding signature information to each URL.

choices.text: Use signed cookies with a canned policy to specify the entire subscriber prefix and the IPv4 condition.
choices.explanation: A canned policy cannot include a source IP address condition.

choices.text: Specify the target prefix, expiration, and allowed IPv4 range in a custom policy, then issue signed cookies associated with a trusted key group.
choices.explanation: CloudFront can evaluate the viewer conditions without changing the URLs for the multiple files.

choices.text: Configure OAC for delivery and serve content without validating cookies or signatures on the viewer side.
choices.explanation: OAC controls access from CloudFront to the origin. It does not determine whether a subscriber's browser may access the content.

sourceLabel: CloudFront signed cookies with a custom policy

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Add an accounting-only condition to shared device requirements for internal apps
prompt: Several internal web applications are being consolidated behind AWS Verified Access. Every application requires authenticated users from the corporate IdP and compliance information from a device management service. The accounting application additionally requires users to belong to the accounting group. Which design avoids duplicating the shared conditions for each application?

source.label: Verified Accessの信頼プロバイダーとポリシー

learning.reason: Configure the instance to obtain user and device trust data. Evaluate shared conditions in the group policy, then add the accounting-group condition in the accounting endpoint policy.
learning.concept: Verified Access evaluates requests using group and individual endpoint policies. A network source alone does not evaluate a user's group membership or device status.

choices.text: Configure IdP and device trust providers, put the shared conditions in the group policy, and add the accounting-group condition to the accounting endpoint.
choices.explanation: This applies the shared conditions to all applications while adding a restriction only to accounting.

choices.text: Put the shared conditions only on the accounting endpoint and allow all users in the group policy.
choices.explanation: The other applications would not enforce the shared user and device conditions.

choices.text: Set the corporate source IP range in the applications' VPC security groups and treat it as identifying device compliance and accounting-group membership.
choices.explanation: An IP condition cannot evaluate group membership or compliance information from the device management service.

choices.text: Configure the IdP and device providers, but have the accounting endpoint use only the shared policy.
choices.explanation: Non-accounting users who satisfy the shared allow policy could also access accounting.

sourceLabel: Verified Access trust providers and policies

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Update client trust before changing the certificate authority
prompt: An existing RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance is used by TLS clients that validate the server certificate. The current root CA must be changed to a new CA while certificate validation is maintained. Several DB engine versions are in use, and the need for a restart must be determined in advance to avoid downtime. Which sequence should be used?

source.label: RDSのSSL/TLS証明書のローテーション

learning.reason: First update clients so they can trust the new CA. Check SupportsCertificateRotationWithoutRestart for the target engine version to plan when to change the CA.
learning.concept: Client preparation differs when RDS renews a server certificate under the same root CA versus when the root CA itself changes.

choices.text: Switch the DB to the new CA first, then update the trust stores only for clients whose TLS connections fail.
choices.explanation: Clients that trust only the old root will fail validation. The order needs to be reversed.

choices.text: Distribute the new CA to clients while they continue to trust the existing CA. Check SupportsCertificateRotationWithoutRestart for each engine version and plan the DB CA switch.
choices.explanation: Clients can validate both old and new certificates during migration, and the restart requirement can be handled for each version.

choices.text: Assume existing trust stores will automatically trust the new CA after the root changes, and apply the change immediately to all versions.
choices.explanation: This differs from renewing a server certificate under the same root and ignores engine-specific restart requirements.

choices.text: Disable certificate validation and use encryption alone before switching the CA.
choices.explanation: Although the TLS connection would be encrypted, this would not meet the requirement to keep validating the server certificate.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Fixing only the certificate between CloudFront and an HTTPS origin
prompt: A customer can connect to CloudFront over TLS at www.example.com, but receives a 502 when CloudFront connects to a custom origin. The configured origin name is origin.example.net, and the viewer's Host header is not forwarded in origin requests. The origin currently presents a certificate that includes only www.example.com. Which change preserves the origin name and the delivery URL while keeping HTTPS on both connections?

source.label: Amazon CloudFront — 502とカスタムオリジンのTLS

learning.reason: Change the origin-side certificate to a trusted certificate that includes origin.example.net, the name CloudFront validates.
learning.concept: CloudFront validates certificates separately for the TLS connection from the viewer to CloudFront and the connection from CloudFront to the origin.

choices.text: Add a certificate that includes origin.example.net as the CloudFront viewer certificate, and leave the certificate presented by the origin unchanged.
choices.explanation: This failure involves validation of the certificate presented by the origin. Changing the viewer certificate does not fix it.

choices.text: Have the origin present a certificate that includes origin.example.net and the required intermediate certificates. Keep the CloudFront viewer certificate unchanged.
choices.explanation: This aligns the name and trust chain validated for the TLS connection to the origin while preserving the viewer TLS connection, which is already working.

choices.text: Replace the DNS record for origin.example.net with a different record type pointing to the same server, and leave the certificate unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the DNS record type does not resolve the mismatch between the name CloudFront validates and the certificate.

choices.text: Reissue the same www.example.com certificate for the origin from a different trusted certificate authority, and assume that name validation against the origin name will then succeed.
choices.explanation: Even if the issuer is trusted, name validation fails if the certificate does not include the required origin name.

sourceLabel: Amazon CloudFront — 502 Errors and TLS for Custom Origins

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Detecting threats to S3 objects while retaining audit records long term
prompt: An organization wants managed detection of suspicious authenticated object access to its private S3 buckets across multiple accounts and Regions. Regardless of whether any findings are generated, it must be able to centrally search, for one year, the read and write object API operations supported by CloudTrail for the covered buckets. The current organization trail records management events only. Which two changes are required?

source.label: Amazon GuardDuty — S3 Protection

learning.reason: Enable S3 Protection in the covered Regions to detect suspicious access. In the organization trail, select S3 read and write data events for the covered buckets and retain them for the required period.
learning.concept: GuardDuty findings do not provide comprehensive retention of the original events. CloudTrail management events alone do not provide object-level auditing.

choices.text: Enable S3 Protection in GuardDuty for the covered accounts and Regions.
choices.explanation: S3 data events for covered buckets in those Regions are analyzed for signs of threats.

choices.text: Retain the existing management-events-only organization trail for one year and assume that it also includes GetObject and PutObject.
choices.explanation: The object API operations in question are data events and are not recorded by a trail limited to management events.

choices.text: Add read and write data events for the covered S3 buckets to the organization trail's event selectors, and retain the centralized logs for one year.
choices.explanation: This records the required events independently of detection results. The retained logs can be searched with tools such as Athena.

choices.text: Retain GuardDuty's S3 findings for one year and use them as the audit log for all covered object API operations.
choices.explanation: Findings report events identified by the analysis; they do not retain the original records for operations that were not detected.

choices.text: Save S3 Inventory daily and identify who read each object from changes in the inventory.
choices.explanation: Inventory reports object listings. It does not identify the principal that read an object or the API call.

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Keeping existing logs decryptable with a key dedicated to a log group
prompt: CloudWatch Logs log group A is encrypted with KMS key K1. New logs must use a dedicated key, K2, and the permissions granted to the CloudWatch Logs service for K2 must be limited to log group A's ARN. Logs already encrypted with K1 must remain readable during their retention period. Which two measures are required?

source.label: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — KMSキーによるログ暗号化

learning.reason: Associate K2 with the log group while restricting it through the encryption context containing the log group ARN. Keep K1 available for as long as logs encrypted with it must be decrypted.
learning.concept: kms:ViaService identifies calls made through a service. The log group ARN in the encryption context provides the log-group-specific restriction.

choices.text: Condition K2's permissions only on kms:ViaService for CloudWatch Logs in the Region, without distinguishing the log group.
choices.explanation: Restricting use to calls through the service does not limit permission to log group A among the log groups in that Region.

choices.text: In K2's permissions for the CloudWatch Logs service, restrict kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn to A and associate K2 with A.
choices.explanation: The KMS permission granted to the service can be scoped to the log group that CloudWatch Logs identifies in the encryption context.

choices.text: Disable K1 and assume that associating K2 with A switches existing logs to K2 for decryption.
choices.explanation: Associating a different key does not re-encrypt existing data. Making K1 unavailable would prevent access to the existing logs.

choices.text: Restrict K2's permissions to an alias for a key whose name contains the log group name, without validating the encryption context.
choices.explanation: An alias names a key; it does not establish which log group is using the key for this purpose.

choices.text: Keep CloudWatch Logs' required access to K1 for decryption while logs encrypted with K1 remain.
