choices.explanation: Existing logs remain encrypted with K1. K1 must remain usable to read them during their retention period.

sourceLabel: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — Encrypting Log Data with KMS Keys

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Establishing DNSSEC trust with an externally managed parent zone
prompt: An organization will enable DNSSEC for a public child zone delegated in Route 53. Another provider manages the parent zone, and the organization must be able to validate trust between the parent and child. The KMS key used for the child zone must be owned by the organization. Which two measures enable DNSSEC while preserving the existing NS delegation?

source.label: Amazon Route 53 — DNSSECのKMSキー要件

learning.reason: Configure the Route 53 KSK with a KMS key that meets the requirements, sign the child zone, and register the corresponding DS record in the parent zone.
learning.concept: Even if a child zone has signed records, the DS record in the parent zone establishes trust in the corresponding key for the child zone.

choices.text: Create a symmetric KMS key in the same Region as the parent provider and use it for the Route 53 KSK.
choices.explanation: The KMS key specified for Route 53 must be an asymmetric ECC_NIST_P256 signing key in Northern Virginia.

choices.text: Place a DS record only in the child zone, and ask the parent provider only to preserve the existing NS delegation.
choices.explanation: The DS record that conveys trust from the parent to the child must be in the parent zone.

choices.text: Create an asymmetric ECC_NIST_P256 signing KMS key in us-east-1, grant the required permissions to the Route 53 DNSSEC service, and configure the KSK.
choices.explanation: This satisfies the key Region, specification, and signing permissions required by the Route 53 KSK.

choices.text: Sign the child zone and verify its responses, then provide the DS information shown by Route 53 to the parent provider for registration in the parent zone.
choices.explanation: A signed DS record in the parent identifies the corresponding public key for the child zone and adds a trust relationship to the existing NS delegation.

choices.text: Instead of enabling DNSSEC in Route 53, register the public key of the HTTPS certificate used by the child zone as the DS record in the parent zone.
choices.explanation: The public key of the HTTPS certificate is not the DS information corresponding to this child zone's DNSSEC KSK.

sourceLabel: Amazon Route 53 — DNSSEC KMS Key Requirements

category: セキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Aligning external IdP group assignments and sign-in
prompt: A company wants to connect an external IdP to IAM Identity Center and centrally manage users and groups across multiple AWS accounts as employees join, leave, or change roles. A test user has already been synchronized through SCIM with an employee ID as the Username, but the SAML Subject NameID sends an email address, so the user cannot sign in to Identity Center. The existing assignment approach for permission sets and target accounts must be preserved. Which configuration should be used?

source.label: AWS IAM Identity Center — 外部IdPからのSCIM

learning.reason: Provision the users and groups through SCIM, and make the SAML NameID match the SCIM Username. Assign accounts and permission sets to the synchronized groups.
learning.concept: SCIM synchronizes the directory, while SAML identifies the user at sign-in. Keep the identity consistent across both and manage assignments in Identity Center.

choices.text: Synchronize users and groups through SCIM. Set the SAML NameID to the same employee ID used as the SCIM Username, then assign the target permission sets to the synchronized groups.
choices.explanation: This uses the same attribute to identify the user. Changes in group membership are reflected in the groups that have assignments through SCIM synchronization.

choices.text: Keep the email address as the SAML NameID and the employee ID as the SCIM Username, then register the email address as the name of the permission set.
choices.explanation: A permission set's display name does not configure how a SAML subject is matched to a synchronized user.

choices.text: Stop using SCIM and assume that sending group names in SAML will automatically create users and groups at sign-in.
choices.explanation: SAML sign-in alone cannot provision users or groups in Identity Center.

choices.text: Enable only SCIM group synchronization without synchronizing individual users, then manually assign different IAM roles for each account.
choices.explanation: This does not fix the mismatch in user identification and abandons the requirement to manage existing assignments centrally in Identity Center.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM Identity Center — SCIM from an external IdP
